name: En'Rage Models Practice
description: Our practice sessions are dynamic and empowering, designed to build confidence, enhance runway skills, and foster creativity in a supportive environment. Each session begins with a warm-up to prepare our models for the physical and mental demands of the runway. Models are then guided through a series of runway walks, where they practice posture, poise, and movement in a variety of styles that challenge traditional norms of fashion and modeling. Throughout the practice, we focus on perfecting choreography for upcoming shows, allowing models to develop their unique flair while staying in sync with the group’s overall performance. Our experienced runway coaches provide individual feedback to ensure that each model feels confident in expressing their own style, aligning with our mission of self-empowerment and diversity. In addition to runway practice, we also incorporate photoshoot preparation, helping models become comfortable in front of the camera, and working on their poses and expressions. Music is played to set the tone, and we regularly rotate different fashion themes to keep practices fresh and engaging. Each session concludes with a debrief, where we emphasize the importance of mutual support and encouragement, celebrating personal growth and teamwork. En'Rage Models practices are more than just rehearsals—they are an opportunity for our members to develop their self-esteem, push creative boundaries, and prepare for the high-energy experience of the runway.

description: The East Coast Asian American Student Union (ECAASU) is an intercollegiate network of students and young professionals whose mission is to inspire, educate, and empower those interested in Asian/Asian American issues. ECAASU’s advocacy work is conducted through outreach to students and organizations across the country and educating individuals on becoming agents of change. Triangle-Area Asian American Student Conference (TAASCON) is an annual student-led, student-run conference between UNC, NCSU, and Duke dedicated to celebrating and empowering the Asian American community The theme for ECAASU Conference 2026 is CURRENTS, with sub-themes of Migration, Headlines, and Resistance. “Currents” is inspired by our understanding of change. Migrant narratives moving across countries, evolving in diverse enclaves, and managing ever-changing political regimes exemplify the dynamism in Asian-American communities. “Currents” also evokes the current political climate of fascism, fragmentation, and polarization. Their annual conference is taking place from March 27-29, 2026 at Duke University at Durham, North Carolina. If you are interested in attending as part of the University of Maryland's delegation, please contact AASU's Vice Presidents of External Affairs, Hana and Divya, at hlee1241@terpmail.umd.edu and dbhat1@terpmail.umd.edu.

description: Unity Gala is the culminating celebration of the University of Maryland’s recognition of APIDA Heritage Month in April. Information about RSVPs will be posted later on our Instagram @umcpaasu. The mission of the annual Unity Gala is to eliminate cultural barriers between various APIDA student groups on campus, fostering a sense of unity and understanding to mark the end of Asian Pacific Islander Desi American Heritage Month at the University of Maryland, College Park (UMCP). In the wake of troubling global and national events creating divisions within our community, this gala strives to create a safe space and welcoming platform for the exchange of ideas, identities, and cultures. We will invite performers from various student organizations to showcase their cultural heritage through dance, music, comedy, and singing performances.

name: 2023 NASA SUITS Challenge Interest Meeting
description: NASA SUITS (Spacesuit User Interface Technologies for Students) challenges students to design and create spacesuit information displays within augmented reality (AR) environments. The XR Club is looking for individuals with a wide range of experiences and skill sets who are motivated and inspired to help us bring our proposal to life! This 10-page proposal would be for an AR software application for a commercial device, e.g., Microsoft HoloLens 2 or Magic Leap, for moonwalks, due on November 1st. If we were to be selected, we will get the opportunity to develop our software, be mentored by NASA experts, and test our devices in an analog mock EVA scenario at the NASA Johnson Space Center in May 2023 where we will showcase their work to NASA, university and industry partners, and participate in student and NASA speaker panels. description: Getting started with XR development can be intimidating if you don't know where to start. Even deciding on the best software tools or finding the correct versions to download is often confusing in this rapidly evolving space. In this workshop, we'll get you set up with the Unity real-time 3D development platform, which powers over 60% of the world’s VR and AR content, as well as the code editors and other tools necessary to build applications for various XR platforms so that you're ready to get started with learning how to create your own apps at one of our future workshops! description: An online information session will be held for START's Master of Professional Studies (MPS) in Security and Terrorism Studies and Graduate Certificate in Terrorism Analysis at 6:00 p.m. ET on Tuesday, October 25, 2022. This event is free and open to the public, but registration is required. The MPS in Security and Terrorism Studies prepares students to examine the complex social, political, economic, and psychological underpinnings of terrorist and other asymmetric security threats. Students are exposed to the theoretical and methodological skills necessary to pursue advanced research opportunities, or be successful in a professional role where analysis and critical thinking are paramount. The program is appropriate for individuals interested in (and/or currently) working in fields related to intelligence analysis, national security analysis, or analysis of other relevant topic areas, and individuals interested in (and/or currently) conducting scholarly research on terrorism and security. This program is entirely online, delivered in a synchronous format using multiple online platforms provided by the University of Maryland, College Park, and offered through the University of Maryland's Graduate School. name: Mapping Your Career: Career Exploration for ARHU Students
organization: University Career Center & The Presidents Promise
description: Figuring out your career path can be confusing, especially for Arts and Humanities majors who gain numerous transferable skills and competencies in demand in various industries. You may wonder what the best career is for you. This workshop will help you identify themes and connections between your academic, professional, and life experiences and discuss how they might guide your time at UMD and beyond. In this session, we will: Create a “Wandering Map” (from You Majored in What?, by Kate Brooks), which is a way of visually (graphically) thinking about your interests, strengths, skills, achievements, and values. This is a physical tool that you will get to take home. Analyze patterns/themes and discover meaningful connections between past experiences. Discuss and reflect as a group and share suggestions for further exploration. Learn about additional career center resources related to career exploration. Questions? Contact Caroline Bodnar, cbodnar@umd.edu RSVP

name: March for Science
description: The March for Science is a celebration of science. It's not about scientists or politicians; it is about the very real role that science plays in each of our lives and the need to respect and encourage research that gives us insight into the world. Nevertheless, the march has generated a great deal of conversation around whether or not scientists should involve themselves in politics. In the face of an alarming trend toward discrediting scientific consensus and restricting scientific discovery, we might ask instead: can we afford not to speak out in its defense? The March for Science, which is supported by the American Association for the Advancement of Science, the American Geophysical Union, the American Physical Society and 25 other organizations of scientists, will be holding a teach-in and rally on the National Mall in Washington DC on April 22, 2017. For more information on details of the march click here: https://www.marchforscience.com

name: Mosaic Retreat Core Group Facilitator Application Deadline
description: MOSAIC Diversity and Leadership Retreat 2015 Core Group Facilitator (CGF) Interest Form Interest forms are due by 10:00AM on December 1, 2014. CGFs will be selected and notified via email by December 8, 2014. If you have any questions please email: Yvette Lerma at ylerma@umd.edu Apply to be a core group facilitator at ter.ps/MosaicCGF Program Description: The MOSAIC: Diversity & Leadership Retreat is a weekend experience focused on exploring the relationships between diversity and leadership. The retreat is an intra-departmental collaboration within the Adele H. Stamp Student Union – Center for Campus Life between the Multicultural Involvement & Community Advocacy Office [MICA] and the Leadership & Community Service-Learning unit. The retreat was established to augment student leadership developmental programs by engaging emerging leaders in concepts related to the Social Change Model of Leadership, particularly aspects of the model that engage self-exploration and civility. Interactive sessions and group discussions are designed to create an environment for individuals to examine who they are and how it influences their understanding of and approach to leadership. Goals of the retreat include developing a stronger sense of self-awareness, understanding identity and social inequity, examining how identity influences leadership, and engaging in practical conversations on implementation of these concepts for individuals and for the University community. Core Group Facilitator Role: Core group facilitators (CGFs) are a critical component of MOSAIC. CGFs consist of graduate students and undergraduate students. Through participating in the retreat as a CGF, you will have the opportunity to interact with and help shape the learning of current and future campus leaders and to think about complex issues relates to diversity and leadership. Through this event, you will have an opportunity to see students learn about themselves, better understand identity and social inequality, and how to engage in socially responsible leadership within their communities. Additional Details: Transportation, room and board will be provided to you Facilitators should expect to co-facilitate learning for a small group of 6 to 7 students. Retreat participants will stay in their same small group throughout the retreat. In order to support our core-group facilitators in their role, we believe it is important that they have an understanding, knowledge, and awareness of the complexities around diversity and leadership, the social change model of leadership, and how to effectively facilitate learning for students. As such, all CGFs must be able to attend the CGF trainings from 5:00-8:00pm on the following 3 Wednesday’s: January 28th, February 4th, and February 11th, 2015. Attendance at the MOSAIC kick-off on Friday, February 20th is an important beginning to the MOSAIC experience and your attendance is important to the program design. Plus, there will be delicious food! MOSAIC takes place all day Saturday, February 21st – Sunday, February 22nd, 2015. Facilitators are also welcomed to apply to the MOSAIC Initiative, a semester long program focused on examining how aspects of identity impact leadership for social change. We will explore strategies for creating positive change while considering the complex dynamics of addressing systems of power, privilege, and oppression.

name: TerpService Days - A Wider Circle
description: A Wider Circle has the mission to end poverty, and the amazing thing about this organization is that they do not say no to anyone! AWC provides education and job preparedness, long-term support programs, and basic provision items. Volunteers will be part of A Wider Circle's Neighbor-to-Neighbor program, which furnishes the homes of about 20 families each day. Anyone in need can find help in the form of home furnishings, appropriate outfits for work, toys and games for kids, and much more, all at no cost to the clients. If volunteers are able to move furniture, they can load clients' vehicles as well as restock the warehouse. There are also plenty of tasks for non-loaders including sorting and organizing donations and assisting clients in choosing items. A Wider Circle does require volunteers to wear closed-toed shoes, sleeved shirts, long shorts, and only "family friendly" messages on their clothing. Volunteers should also dress in layer for the weather and bring a reusable water bottle. Work gloves will be provided by TerpService TerpService Days are one-time days of service targeted at the broad campus community. Students with significant or no experience in service-learning are welcome to participate. Student groups also enjoy participating in the service days. http://thestamp.umd.edu/leadership_community_service-learning/programs/terpservice

name: Basetrack Creative Dialouges
description: BASETRACK Live is a multimedia theatre piece designed to raise public awareness of the impact of war on the service members who served in Iraq and Afghanistan. We must encourage a complicated but necessary discussion that recognizes and respects the role of our military, but looks unflinchingly at the legacy of war. How can artists contribute to realizing that goal? What does it take to create a dialogue that is meaningful and poetic, honest and provocative, that addresses such a complicated subject? Join this group of veterans and artists as we embed ourselves in that complicated conversation about war, art, trauma and memory.

description: LSF's Tutoring Program provides free academic assistance to underserved Washington metropolitan area students to ensure their academic success. LSF is looking for volunteers ages 16 and up interested in working one-on-one with students on Saturday mornings from 9:30 to 12pm in Riverdale, MD. LSP is also opening a new Wheaton, MD location (address TBD)! LSF staff provides lesson plans and guidance, so all tutors have to bring is enthusiasm and dedication. To get involved, tutors must make an account at latinostudentfund.volunteerhub.com and they will reach out.

name: Camp PALS Volunteer opportunity
description: Volunteer to be a Counselor for the PALS program Camp PALS this summer. PALS is a nonprofit organization that provides one week long summer camp opportunities for teens and young adults with Down syndrome and their peers at 14 college campuses across the country. This is a one-week experience from 9am-5pm. Listed below are some details about Camp PALS: Here are some details about Camp PALS: - They offer 14 week long sleep-away camps across the country, including Camp PALS Georgetown, Chicago, and North Carolina! - Volunteer counselors are paired one-to-one with a camper to provide an opportunity to build -meaningful friendships through trips and activities - Looking for volunteers ages 16-30 who are welcoming, genuine, passionate, supportive, and fun which are all the values of the program. - No experience with Down syndrome or the disability community is necessary! They encourage groups of applicants to apply together to share the camp experience. If you are interested please visit the website at palsprograms.org/volunteer or check out their social media pages on Facebook or YouTube channel to get a look at what the PALS experience is like. PALS is an amazing opportunity to give back to the community, gain invaluable leadership skills, and make friends that will last a lifetime! There are no costs for volunteers at PALS, and applicants can apply for travel costs to be covered as well. We are looking for male applicants at this point in our season. Females are welcome to apply but will likely be placed on a waitlist. The dates for each of our 15 camps is different based on their locations, but the dates for Baltimore are July 7-13 at UMBC, and Georgetown is July 28-August 3 at Georgetown University.

name: Intersections of Illicit Trafficking and Counterfeit Parts Workshop
description: On Thursday, October 28 at 10:30 a.m. ET, START and the Center of Advanced Life Cycle Engineering (CALCE) will co-host the Intersections of Illicit Trafficking and Counterfeit Parts Workshop, sponsored by the National Science Foundation (NSF). This event is free and open to the public, but RSVPs are required. If you have any questions, please email the START events team at start-events@umd.edu. This project focuses on the disruption of the supply chains for counterfeit hardware used in critical systems. “Critical systems,” in the context of this project are defined as systems associated with human safety (e.g. transportation, medical), the delivery of critical services (infrastructure, energy generation), important humanitarian and military missions, and global economic stability. These systems are costly to procure, are generally expected to have a long service life, and as a result, they must be supported for long periods of time. But counterfeit parts manufacturing is only a single thread of a larger tapestry. While the world’s largest firms have cracked down on illicit and illegal labor practices, illicit and illegal labor remains a key part of innumerable supply chains. Narcotics production is a hazardous criminal enterprise, but increased professionalization and the availability of quality parts and chemical precursors from China have allowed narcotrafficking cartels to manufacture massive quantities of fentanyl. Weapons traffickers and criminal entities now use additive manufacturing for weapons development and modifications. Trafficking of wildlife, agricultural products, and animal parts present various serious concerns including the introduction of invasive species to the spread, and novel development, of viruses. Often, these differing types of criminal behavior are siloed, but as transnational criminal entities continue to replicate neoliberal business practices, they are agglomerating into polycrime entities. These polycrime entities bridge different lines of the trafficking business. Humans are trafficked for forced or illegal labor. People have been trafficked and forced to serve as caretakers of illegal cannabis plants. Mexican drug cartels have purchased 3D printers and hired engineers to develop weapons modifications, uparmor vehicles, and develop manufacturing techniques that increase the potency of various narcotics. This workshop seeks to bring together social scientists, engineers, law enforcement, policymakers, and industry to push us out of our comfort zones to build connections and identify gaps. Individual sessions will focus on modalities of trafficking: arms trafficking and construction, wildlife trafficking, labor trafficking, and narcotics manufacturing and trafficking. The conference will end with a convocation meant to sum up the presentations and serve as an opportunity for the wider group to discuss new-found connections and overlapping priorities.

name: Fandango for Butterflies (And Coyotes) (USA)
description: “El fandango emigró, y yo emigré con el fandango.” Immigrants from Mexico, Honduras and the Dominican Republic living in New York City without “papeles” band together inside a community sanctuary for a fandango—a celebration brought to life by live music, dance and performance. They shelter-in-place as they wait for Immigrations and Customs Enforcement (ICE) raids to pass and for a family member making the dangerous trek to the U.S. As the fandango plays on, fear and anxiety sink in—fear of family separation, fear of having made the wrong decision and fear for those making the perilous journey across the border. But as threats loom dangerously close, strangers become family, fear becomes strength and sorrow becomes joy. Conceived by Chilean-Costa Rican playwright Andrea Thome in partnership with En Garde Arts, Fandango for Butterflies (and Coyotes) was shaped by the unheard voices of many undocumented immigrants. While at The Clarice in 2021-22, artists from the ensemble will host a dinner conversation with UndocuTerps, a student organization that supports immigrant and undocumented student life at the University of Maryland. By bringing to life true stories that transcend social boundaries, En Garde Arts produces bold experiences that break barriers and inspire audiences and creatives alike, including School of Theatre, Dance, and Performance Studies and School of Music students and College Park Scholars, who will continue experiencing the company’s work up-close this season in workshops and lectures, just as they did in the 2020-21 season. In 2021-22, the company will also perform a live fandango for families in Langley Park, Maryland, as part of The Clarice’s popular Family Art Day series. This event will be performed in The Clarice Courtyard, the lawn area behind The Clarice. The artists will be on an outdoor stage, and chairs will be provided for the audience. Audience members are invited to use the front entrance of The Clarice, and can then find the courtyard by travelling up the grand staircase or taking the elevator to Floor 2. Ushers will be present to assist you and answer questions. Based on current UMD campus guidelines and Prince George’s County guidelines for outdoor events, the artists will not wear masks during the performance. The audience will also not be required to wear masks while seated during the performance. These guidelines are subject to change, and you will receive the most up to date COVID-19 Health and Safety rules in an email prior to your event. Health + Safety There may be COVID safety policies such as mask requirements in place when you attend this event. Please see our health & safety page for the most up to date information about attendance!

name: Las Cantoras Album Release Party (Venezuela)
description: Between 1960 and 1980, Venezuelan architect and folklorist Oswaldo Lares recorded more than 1,000 tracks of rural songs throughout his native Venezuela. In the forthcoming album Las Cantoras, Venezuelan Afro-soul artist Betsayda Machado collaborates with Lares to curate a compilation of these archival recordings featuring female singers. Through this unique collaboration, the two will release a rarely seen side of Venezuela. This virtual album release party includes dynamic conversation and album teasers of Las Cantoras. The album is produced in collaboration with Guillermo Lares, Odelia Artists founder Juan Souki and The Arts Center at NYU Abu Dhabi. name: Terri Lyne Carrington & Social Science (USA)
description: For nearly four decades, Grammy award winner and National Endowment for the Arts Jazz Master Terri Lyne Carrington has been on the front lines of creating a new form of jazz—one without patriarchy. Her work as a drummer and bandleader has earned her a Doris Duke Artist Award and three Grammys, including Best Jazz Vocal Album for “The Mosaic Project,” which exclusively featured female musicians. In 2018, she founded the Berklee Institute of Jazz and Gender Justice to address a long history of inequality and sexual harassment. In late 2019, Carrington released “Waiting Game,” her seventh album as a bandleader and first with her new group, Social Science. The album leaps through an ebullient mix of improvised instrumental suites, electroacoustic textures and pointed social commentary. With pianist Aaron Parks and guitarist Matt Stevens, she guides a band built on kinetic energy and unbound curiosity. In the 2020-21 season, Carrington led a Jazz Clinic for students in the UMD School of Music’s Jazz Studies Division that focused on a lack of gender equity within the jazz community. She also participated in The Clarice’s popular Black Women in the Arts series alongside flutist/composer Nicole Mitchell and singer/songwriter Dianne Reeves. Behind the kit, Carrington is a commanding instrumentalist; as a bandleader, she is nothing less than the future of a more equitable jazz. Health + Safety There may be COVID safety policies such as mask requirements in place when you attend this event. Please see our health & safety page for the most up to date information about attendance!

description: Known for their flamboyant and dynamic style, Harlem Quartet advances diversity in classical music while engaging audiences with underperformed repertoire. From their 2009 performance for former President and First Lady Barack and Michelle Obama to a highly successful South African tour, the quartet performs around the world with such distinguished artists as Itzhak Perlman, Ida Kavafian, Jeremy Denk, Chick Corea and, as in this program, Aldo López-Gavilán. A Cuban piano virtuoso and brother of quartet member Ilmar Gavilán, López-Gavilán is praised for both his classical and jazz technique. He wrote his first composition at age five, and in this program, we hear five of his exuberant works. Harlem Quartet is committed to diverse programming, a collaborative approach and an ongoing commitment to educational residency and outreach. In 2021-22, the quartet will perform livestreamed performances for K-12 students across Prince George’s County Public Schools. In addition, the quartet will appear as part of The Clarice’s Arts Citizenship Talks (ACTnow) series in partnership with UMD’s Latin American and Caribbean Studies Center and will be part of the UMD School of Music’s Renegade series, which features innovative artists of various disciplines. For this event the audience is invited to experience the performance from a new vantage point. Audience seating will be on the Dekelboum stage, on risers where the orchestra typically sits. The musicians will perform on the front of the stage, facing the audience. Seating will be general admission. description: We each take on different roles in our lives– friend, mentor, supporter, leader– but we often forget that we are, above all, human. Nurture your inner child through interactive and collaborative activities and discussion. Snacks will be provided. Diaspora, Distance, and DisconnectThursday, April 21, 5PM @ MICA Cozy Corner (basement level, across from Studio A) This session focuses on the Asian diaspora and distance and disconnect from extended family and broader communities, not only due to physical distance but also cultural and lingual challenges. We will discuss and reflect on our experiences as a form of self-care and healing. Snacks will be provided. BodyCombat Fitness EventThursday, April 28, 7:00-8:15pm @ Eppley Recreational Center - Fitness Room In honor of APIDA Heritage Month, join our special BodyCombat fitness event. In addition to getting a great workout in, we will discuss things related to APIDA heritage and fixed versus growth mindsets in the fitness environment. All are welcome and no previous experience is necessary. Register here.

name: Introduction to the AR Cloud (Persistent and Multi-User AR)
description: In earlier workshops, we covered the basics of developing augmented reality content for your phones, allowing you to detect surfaces and place digital content that blend in realistically with the environment. However, many real-world applications of augmented reality, such as indoor navigation around an airport, in-store advertising, and AR-enhanced museum exhibits, often require more permanent and location-aware digital content that stays in place even while the application is not in use and is accessible to several users with minimal end-user setup. Join the XR Club this Tuesday as we guide you through creating persistent AR experiences utilizing the power of the AR Cloud. Notes:This workshop requires you to bring a computer with a variety of special software tools installed prior to attending the workshop. These tools could take 30 mins or longer to download and install, so you will not have enough time during the workshop to install the software without falling behind. Additionally, it is strongly recommended that you bring a physical mouse. For Android:You will need to have Unity 2021.2 or later installed along with the Android Build Support module and the options for the Android SDK & NDK Tools and OpenJDK. All of these should be installed with the Unity Hub. You will also need to enable developer options and USB debugging on your phone, as described at https://developer.android.com/studio/debug/dev-options#enable For iOS:You will need to have Unity 2021.2 or later installed along with the iOS Build Support module. You will also need to install the latest version of Apple's Xcode IDE, which can be found on the Mac App Store. Once you've done that, add your Apple ID account to your Xcode preferences, as described at https://help.apple.com/xcode/mac/current/#/devaf282080a Note that the Xcode IDE is only available on Macs. If you have a Windows computer, you will still be able to develop AR applications in Unity and export it to an Xcode project, but you will not be able to open that Xcode project and deploy the build to an iOS device for testing As per University guidelines, all attendees of this event will be required to wear KN95 masks. Violators will be denied entry into the event.

name: A Look Back at 2020: Trends from the Global Terrorism Database (GTD)
description: On Wednesday, July 6 at 10:00 a.m. ET, Global Terrorism Database (GTD) Program Manager Dr. Erin Miller will provide an online briefing to discuss the latest findings from the GTD. All are welcome to attend the event, but RSVPs are required. If you have any questions, please email the START events team at start-events@umd.edu. Twenty years after University of Maryland researchers began developing the GTD in 2002, Miller will present trends from the forthcoming publication of new GTD data for 1970 to 2020. Topics will include patterns of terrorism in the United States and around the world during the first year of the COVID-19 pandemic, developments in Afghanistan leading up to the 2021 collapse of the Afghan government and the evolving geographic footprint of Islamic State-related terrorism. Dr. Erin Miller is the program manager for the Global Terrorism Database (GTD) at START headquarters at the University of Maryland. Miller earned a BA in Sociology from the University of Pennsylvania, and an MA and PhD in Criminology and Criminal Justice from the University of Maryland. Her research investigates patterns of decline among terrorist organizations and movements worldwide, using innovative statistical analysis of data from the GTD. She has taught statistics courses at the University of Maryland and delivered invited lectures on the GTD and the implications of research methodology for terrorism research.

description: This workshop was crafted in response to the increasing need + interest in the intersections between activism and the creative arts. Our goal is twofold: to (1) help attendees consider their unique, individual skillsets to support a larger ecosystem of social change on campus/in this nation and to (2) connect artists/creatives of all mediums from UMD's campus in hopes of them building community and coalitions outside of our space, too, to sustain interdisciplinary advocacy via intentional collaboration. name: Alternative Breaks | Spring 2021 Participant Application Open!
description: What does student social justice work look like in a world where our campus is predominantly operating online? How do we connect meaningfully and sustainably with one another in a virtual environment? If you’ve been asking yourself these questions, Alternative Breaks’ adapted programming might be the perfect fit for you. This spring, in the interest of ensuring the health and safety of all our participants and Experience Leaders, Alternative Breaks has created a FREE semester-long fully virtual experience focused on empowering students to learn in community with one another and take action toward just causes. The Alternative Breaks Dialogue Program will consist of intentional and reflective dialogues addressing global social issues. Each team will be diving deeply into a particular social issue area by evaluating resources together, engaging with the topic in individual and global contexts, and seeking an active role in social justice by fostering relationships with local community partners. Participants will engage with a community partner through direct service to turn their knowledge into safe, responsible, and sustainable action. Issue areas will include Environmental Conservation, Education, Ability, Socioeconomic Equity, Health and Wellness, and Food Insecurity. Experience Leaders will be diving deep into a specific aspect of their issue area as they move through the dialogue sessions. These dialogues will take place once a week for 8 weeks between February 15th, 2021 - April 9th, 2021. Each weekly session will be 1.5 hours long, and students must be able to commit to all of the dialogue sessions in their series to participate. Participant applications open Monday, December 7th, 2020! If you have any questions or need more information, email alternativebreaks@umd.edu or check out our website at Alternativebreaks.umd.edu.

name: GRadulting Workshop Series - How do I prepare my taxes?  - for international students
description: Filing Federal and State taxes are confusing for everyone, including graduate students! To help you through this process our offices are hosting a tax workshop for domestic students and another for international students. Get guidance on how to handle common tax issues and bring your questions to the Q&A session. For help with more complex questions, we will share free resources for one-on-one tax support. The Federal Filing deadline is April 15, 2021. speaker: Professor Sam Handwerger, Lecturer and Advisor for TerpTax, UMD Smith's School of Business co-hosts: Graduate Student Legal Aid, The Graduate School, International Student and Scholar Services *** Grad Legal Aid welcomes all GradTerps (and sometimes undergrads) to join us on Tuesdays for the GRadulting Virtual Workshop Series! Whether you are in the U.S. or in your home country, you can count on us for great information to help you navigate the issues and challenges of the adult world. If you are unable to attend, many of our speakers will give us permission to record the workshop so you can view it at your own convenience. We hope to see you there! What is GRadulting? Gradulting is defined as graduate students who are "adulting" -- (v): to carry out one or more of the duties and responsibilities expected of fully developed individuals, such as financial planning, buying a home, negotiating a salary, or estate planning. GradTerps may join our Google Group to receive a weekly reminder of the upcoming workshops.

name: NextLOOK ft. Sinclair Ogaga Emoghene, Pablo Regis & Kate Spanos: Performing Otherness (Ainihi e Alteridade)
description: This new dance and music project examines ainihi (“identity” in Hausa) and alteridade (“otherness” in Portuguese) based on the traditions of Nigeria and Brazil. Multidisciplinary artists Sinclair Ogaga Emoghene, Pablo Regis and Kate Spanos collaborate to look for both universality and cultural specificity in shared movements and rhythms. This work includes new and traditional songs and dances, a carnival-style parade, an audience feedback session and an artist discussion. This event is part of NextLOOK. name: GLAO Lunch and Learn Workshop: Auto Accidents and Personal Injury
description: Join a guest speaker for an inside look at how insurance companies handle automobile accident claims. Learn about how you can lose your case even if the other driver was more at fault than you were, how insurance companies decide what they will pay when your car is declared a total loss, and how to ensure that you get the settlement you deserve when you have suffered personal injuries in an accident what was the other driver’s fault. Get important tips on what to do at the scene of the accident, the relationship between police reports and the insurance settlement process, when it is to your benefit to consult with an attorney, the importance of witnesses, what to do if the driver who hit you doesn’t have insurance…and more. This workshop is hosted by the Graduate Student Legal Aid Office and is open to grad students only. For more information and to register, please visit: www.gradlegalaid.umd.edu. name: Fall Thesis Concert - Ghost Bride & Responsive Wild
description: Responsive Wild Choreography by Krissy Harris Responsive Wild considers and questions notions of womanhood and femininity. Inspired by family history, rock and roll, and physics concepts, Harris investigates these ideas through highly physical, bold and expansive movement. The work is in conversation with feminist theories and reveals a complex interrelationship of the inside/outside body and its potential for energetic expression. Ghost Bride Choreography by Rose Xinran Qi Ghost Bride is based on the Asian tradition of a ghost marriage, when a man dies early in life and his family recruits a young woman to marry him in spirit. Through a combination of movements derived from postmodern dance and classical Chinese dance, this work conveys a story of revolution for women’s rights through time and place. Qi evokes the Chinese feminine form Shenyun (bearing) through breath control in order to communicate the internal emotion behind specific movements.

name: SEE Presents: Outdoor Movie Series
description: As a way to de-stress and have fun leading up to finals season, the outdoor movie series will consist of 3 weeks of Thursday night outdoor movies. The movies will begin with Jurassic Park (4/15), in which a pragmatic paleontologist visiting a theme park is tasked with protecting a couple of kids after a power failure causes the park's cloned dinosaurs to run loose. The following week will feature Soul(4/22), where, after landing the gig of a lifetime, a New York jazz pianist suddenly finds himself trapped in a strange land between Earth and the afterlife. Closing out the series is Ferris Bueller's Day Off (5/6), a comedy where a high school wise guy is determined to have a day off from school in Chicago. The outdoor movies will be socially distanced and COVID friendly! Ticketing and wait list information: The first 36 people to register are guaranteed spots if they arrive by 7:45pm the night of the movie The next 36 students will be put on a waitlist and can come to check in at the night of the event. Waitlist entry will be based on first come first serve, so when students come their names will be taken down as well as their contact information, and they will be told to leave but to stay close by. At 7:45 if anyone has not shown up people on the waitlist will be contacted to attend in the order which they checked in

name: Scholar in Residence: Rabbi Liebtag!
description: Rabbi Menachem Leibtag will be speaking multiple times over the weekend about various Jewish topics. Over the course of the weekend he will speak about the Jewish Bible, rabbinic literature, and Jewish history, as well as how to apply their lessons to our lives. He will speak before the evening prayers, during the communal dinner following prayers, and during the communal lunch on Saturday. Rabbi Leibtag is an internationally acclaimed bible scholar. His vibrant thematic-analytical approach blends the methods of modern academic scholarship with traditional Jewish approaches to the Biblical text. He is best known for his ability to teach students how to study rather than simply read Biblical passages. An alumnus of Yeshivat Har Etzion, Rav Menachem Leibtag '77 headed the Overseas Program at Yeshivat Har Etzion for over a decade, after completing the Hesder Program and academic studies at Machon Lev, the Jerusalem College of Technology. His Tanakh classes at Yeshiva (Orthodox Jewish school), emphasizing biblical theme and structure, have opened his students' eyes to new dimensions within the text, while transmitting a deeper appreciation of Torah values. He was instrumental in creating the Yeshiva's Virtual Beit Midrash (Jewish study hall), which today reaches tens of thousands of readers worldwide, and then initiated the Tanach (Bible) Study Center, his own comprehensive program for the study of Tanach on the Internet. He also teaches at Midreshet Lindenbaum and Yeshivat Sha'alvim.

name: Chuck Wilt/UNA Productions: Grass Is Green
description: Chuck Wilt is the Artistic Director of UNA Productions, a bi-coastal dance company working in California and NYC. An NYU Tisch School of the Arts alumnus, Chuck has been a choreographic fellow for the Alvin Ailey Dance Foundation NDCL, a Dance Initiative Artist In Residence, a recipient of the Rainin Opportunity Fund and an Artist in Residence at the 92nd St. Y, CUNY Dance Initiative, Fusion Japan and Berkeley Ballet Theatre. Wilt’s work has been described as showcasing, “...radical vulnerability [and] eloquent sincerity" with company members that, “... hold our attention with their sensitivity to each other and their meditative focus” (Dance Enthusiast, NYC). The company’s dedication to celebrating individuality and embodying human existence has led to collaborations that honor and explore sexuality and gender and juxtapose connection and isolation. During the 2020-21 season, Wilt zoomed into several dance technique classes in the School of Theatre, Dance, and Performance Studies (TDPS). He also created a new work, Mural, with TDPS students which The Clarice commissioned and premiered during the TDPS Spring Dance Concert. name: Brentano Quartet with Dawn Upshaw
description: Please note: This performance will not be livestreamed. Since forming at The Juilliard School in 1992, The Brentano String Quartet has recorded numerous gold-standard performances of Schubert, Mozart, Beethoven, Brahms and Haydn. Named for the supposed “Immortal Beloved” of a mysterious Beethoven love letter, Brentano has won prestigious awards including the first Cleveland Quartet Award and the Naumburg Chamber Music Award. Described as “brilliant, virtuosic, and still mellow” (Los Angeles Times), these dynamos treat masterpieces with reverence and enthusiasm, rendering performances with equal passion and precision. A crucial note of distinction for Brentano has been a sharp eye for cohesive if counterintuitive programs. The quartet is prone to surprise, often placing the work of relatively unknown composers with the likes of Brahms and Mozart. Their latest project, a monodrama for quartet and voice called Dido Reimagined, was composed by Pulitzer-winning composer Melinda Wagner and librettist Stephanie Fleischmann in collaboration with soprano Dawn Upshaw. MacArthur Foundation and American Academy of Arts & Sciences Fellow and five-time Grammy Award winner, Dawn’s natural warmth and communicative power has earned acclaim across repertoire on operatic and concert stages and has solidified partnerships with many of today’s greatest composers and ensembles, including Gilbert Kalish, the Kronos Quartet and Esa-Pekka Salonen. While visiting The Clarice, Dawn Upshaw will lead a masterclass for School of Music student vocalists, Brentano Quartet will visit the Chamber Music class and host a Composer Colloquium and the ensemble will lead a pre-concert talk. Health + Safety There may be COVID safety policies such as mask requirements in place when you attend this event. Please see our health & safety page for the most up to date information about attendance!

name: Xênia França
description: Brazilian singer Xênia França mixes tenderness and grit, resolve and romance in songs that sprint through samba and drift through soul, nod to electronica and nestle into balladry. Latin Grammy-nominated Xênia is personally and politically charged with songs that demand respect for her and for her time. Backed by a band as deep and dynamic as her voice, França is a live powerhouse, able to challenge and thrill in the space of a single song. Born in the coastal state of Bahia, França relocated to São Paulo to be, as she remembers, her country’s Gisele Bündchen. She discovered her leadership and voice for black roots pride as lead singer of Aláfia, a kaleidoscopic big band that channeled funk, hip-hop and traditional Brazilian sounds into vibrant anthems. Over the years, França has become a beacon of female empowerment, especially among black women. The Clarice's Visiting Artist Series is committed to providing extensive campus and community engagement opportunities that extend academic learning and cultural opportunities. As part of the 2020-21 season, França co-hosted an Arts Citizenship Talk (ACTnow) and presented an artist talk about their new work. Health + Safety There may be COVID safety policies such as mask requirements in place when you attend this event. Please see our health & safety page for the most up to date information about attendance!

name: GSO Large Ensemble Concert
description: (Photo by Ken Rubin) Join the Gamer Symphony Orchestra for its triumphant return to stage at its Fall 2021 concerts! This semester, the performance includes pieces from Pokémon, Mario, Zelda, League of Legends, Frogger, and much more. Don't miss out - tickets go fast: https://theclarice.umd.edu/events/2021/gamer-symphony-orchestra-large-ensemble-concert. If you can't attend in person, this concert will be streamed on our Twitch channel: https://www.twitch.tv/gamersymphonyumd/. The Gamer Symphony Orchestra is a student-run symphonic orchestra at the University of Maryland and the first collegiate ensemble exclusively devoted to performing orchestral arrangements of video game music. Since its establishment in 2005, it has striven to promote video game music as an art form and to continue bringing video game worlds to life through orchestral arrangements - almost all of which are created by its own members. For more information, visit umd.gamersymphony.org.

name: Intro to AR Development (Part II - Interactions and Realism)
description: Description: Join the XR Club this Tuesday for the second part of our AR Development workshop series, where you'll build upon your application from last week in order to place your very own virtual pet into your physical space, interact with it using some common AR touch gestures, and utilize information about the real-world environment in order to make the digital objects fit in realistically. We'll be using the new Unity XR Tech Stack, including AR Foundation, a multi-platform framework that connects you to the core underlying capabilities of both smartphone and headset based AR platforms, and the XR Interaction Toolkit, which allows you to quickly and easily add common AR/VR interactions into your Unity app. No prior experience is necessary; all majors welcome! Pre-requisites: This workshop requires you to bring a computer with a variety of special software tools installed prior to attending the workshop. These tools could take 30 mins or longer to download and install, so you will not have enough time during the workshop to install the software without falling behind. Additionally, it is strongly recommended that you bring a physical mouse. For Android: You will need to have Unity 2020.3 (LTS) or later installed along with the Android Build Support module and the options for the Android SDK & NDK Tools and OpenJDK. All of these should be installed with the Unity Hub. You will also need to enable developer options and USB debugging on your phone, as described at https://developer.android.com/studio/debug/dev-options#enable For iOS: You will need to have Unity 2020.3 (LTS) or later installed along with the iOS Build Support module. You will also need to install the latest version of Apple's Xcode IDE, which can be found on the Mac App Store. Once you've done that, add your Apple ID account to your Xcode preferences, as described at https://help.apple.com/xcode/mac/current/#/devaf282080a Note that the Xcode IDE is only available on Macs. If you have a Windows computer, you will still be able to develop AR applications in Unity and export it to an Xcode project, but you will not be able to open that Xcode project and deploy the build to an iOS device for testing.

name: Naloxone Training
description: The University of Maryland Health Center is designated as an Overdose Response Program (ORP) through the Maryland Department of Health. As part of this designation, we offer overdose response resources to the UMD community, free of charge. One of the most popular resources we offer is Naloxone, an opioid overdose reversal medication. Similarly to how an EpiPen temporarily blocks the life-threatening symptoms of an allergic reaction (i.e. inability to breathe) while emergency medical assistance arrives, Naloxone offers this temporary support for those experiencing an opioid overdose. To get your free Naloxone through the Health Center, all you have to do is attend a brief training, which goes over how to recognize signs of an opioid overdose, instructions for using Naloxone, and what to do as emergency medical assistance makes its way to you and the person in crisis. Trainings are all offered in the Sahet Room of the Health Center, just past the main entrance to the building, and are free to any UMD community member interested in attending! Registration is required for attendance. --- RSVP URL: https://forms.gle/woguGFjSDnYfHs7VA

name: DREAM Gala
organization: Political Latinx United for Movement and Action in Society (P.L.U.M.A.S.)
description: The Dream Gala raises money for the Dream Fund to support undocumented and immigrant students through financial support for needs such as DACA renewals, scholarships, and legal counsel. Our beneficiaries will be undocumented and immigrant students who either have no status or temporary protections such as TPS, student visas, or DACA. During the Gala, we will have students from different communities perform, and we will present highlights of policy and institutional changes nationwide that support immigrants. We will also share the increasing need to advocate for permanent change to our immigration system due to concerns with abuse in detention centers, invalidation of the right to seek asylum, and the uncertain future of protections such as TPS and DACA. This event celebrates the diverse stories of immigration across cultures and decades. We host a space for all community members to come together to help the most vulnerable in the immigrant community, those that are undocumented. We recognize how intricate and unjust the immigration system is and share ways that participants can actively help those that need it most. Through this event, we provide context about the diversity of the undocumented community and its history. By incorporating stories from various cultural backgrounds, we help participants reject the notion that this is a Latinx-exclusive issue, as denying the existence of those beyond our cultural community only alienates them and decreases the resources available to them. By having performers and speakers from a variety of cultures sharing their stories and experiences, we allow for conversations about how other communities are impacted by our broken immigration system. Everyone is welcome, as allies are also incredibly important to this movement.

name: Beekeeping Club Weekly Meeting
description: During the late spring, summer, and early fall, we have meetings to check on our bees. We learn about sustainable beekeeping practices, what to look for and do while taking care of bees. People who show up to this meeting will have to wear bee-safe clothing such as close toed shoes, and preferably pants, though we have full suits and half suits along with gloves provided. Participants will also have to sign a safety waiver which accepts the possibility of bee stings. When it is too cold or rainy, we go to the UMD Greenhouses to complete workshops such as candles, chapstick, and soap using beeswax. Feel free to reach out through our TerpLink page, our email, or the Discord for more information! The Beekeeping Club does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, religion, age, or physical ability. The Mission of The Beekeeping Club is to educate students about bees and beekeeping through hands-on experience and lectures, about harvesting raw products from them in sustainable ways, and about turning those raw products a variety of goods. The Beekeeping Club seeks to offer anyone with a curiosity or passion for bees and beekeeping the ability to participate in beekeeping regardless of their skill level or prior experience and to guide them in learning more about bees and the role beekeeping plays a sustainable world.

name: Walk with an Arborist & Your Baby
organization: University of Maryland Arboretum & Botanical Gardens
description: Walk with an Arborist & Your Baby encourages new parents to connect with each other and with the outdoors in a safe space, both physically and emotionally. Based in the Garden of Reflection & Remembrance at the Memorial Chapel, participants learn about trees and plants while having their newborns along. Parental leave and the welcoming of a new child can be lonely and stressful. By offering a tour specifically for new parents and caregivers, participants can interact as much (or as little) as they wish with other adults and have a focus in order to leave the house. According to the National Institutes of Health, one in seven women will develop postpartum depression and many others will still experience feelings of loneliness and isolation during parental leave. These symptoms can affect all genders, adoptive parents, and all caregivers, not just the birth parent. Things like cost, transportation, and child care can hinder access to alleviating symptoms. The Arboretum aims to make the outdoors and public gardens more accessible to everyone, regardless of where they are in life's journey. Registration is required on the Arboretum website: https://arboretum.umd.edu/maps-tours/walk-arborist-your-baby

name: Know the Code- Alcohol Use harm Reduction
description: Alcohol abuse and misuse is one of the most prevalent problems facing college campuses today. In the past, many universities have targeted their messaging towards encouraging abstinence from drinking; however, efforts are now shifting towards acknowledging the presence of drinking on and around campus and giving students the tools to be safe and smart while drinking. At our event, we will be encouraging students who choose to drink to drink responsibly by providing materials on the dangers of drinking too much, providing resources from the university on safe drinking, and providing elastic drink covers for people to use to protect themselves on a night out. We will also be conducting an activity where students pour what they think is “a shot” of alcohol into a red solo cup; then we will pour the cup into a 1 oz glass to illustrate how hard it can be to know how much you are drinking. We will be conducting our event on Wednesday, April 24th from 12:00 to 3:00 PM in front of the Stamp Student Union. The event should be informative and engaging and it should help keep students on campus much safer. Students under 21 are not permitted to drink however they may be some students under 21 that choose to drink. Providing harm reduction strategies for all students will help create a safer environment for those in the UMD community.

name: En'Rage Models Practice
description: Our practice sessions are dynamic and empowering, designed to build confidence, enhance runway skills, and foster creativity in a supportive environment. Each session begins with a warm-up to prepare our models for the physical and mental demands of the runway. Models are then guided through a series of runway walks, where they practice posture, poise, and movement in a variety of styles that challenge traditional norms of fashion and modeling. Throughout the practice, we focus on perfecting choreography for upcoming shows, allowing models to develop their unique flair while staying in sync with the group’s overall performance. Our experienced runway coaches provide individual feedback to ensure that each model feels confident in expressing their own style, aligning with our mission of self-empowerment and diversity. In addition to runway practice, we also incorporate photoshoot preparation, helping models become comfortable in front of the camera, and working on their poses and expressions. Music is played to set the tone, and we regularly rotate different fashion themes to keep practices fresh and engaging. Each session concludes with a debrief, where we emphasize the importance of mutual support and encouragement, celebrating personal growth and teamwork. En'Rage Models practices are more than just rehearsals—they are an opportunity for our members to develop their self-esteem, push creative boundaries, and prepare for the high-energy experience of the runway.

name: Arduino Workshop
description: Are you curious about the Arduino microcontroller and want to learn more about it? Have you tried learning to use the Arduino on your own but become frustrated? Maybe you're an expert coder who wants to put their software skills to new use. This one hour workshop may be just what you need to make use of this powerful microcontroller tool. You will be introduced to the Arduino software and hardware and see example Arduino projects that will get you started. Sandbox is teaming up with the Terrapin Works Instructional Electronics Shop (IES) staff to host their Intro to Arduino workshop! Get hands-on instruction on how to set up basic circuits and write the program that makes your circuit come to life. If you've never visited Sandbox this is a great opportunity to learn about the tools and technologies available to all students. You will need to bring your laptop and should download and install the Arduino IDE before arriving at the workshop. After the workshop you can stay for an extra 30 minutes to practice what you've learned or come back another day to work on Arduino projects. You'll also be introduced to the Arduino simulator in TinkerCAD.com which allows you to create virtual circuits and write Arduino code that run on your circuit.

name: Walk with an Arborist & Your Baby
organization: University of Maryland Arboretum & Botanical Gardens
description: Walk with an Arborist & Your Baby encourages new parents to connect with each other and with the outdoors in a safe space, both physically and emotionally. Based in the Garden of Reflection & Remembrance at the Memorial Chapel, participants learn about trees and plants while having their newborns along. Registration Link: https://forms.gle/kzY5f3pbiShhUzgq9 Parental leave and the welcoming of a new child can be lonely and stressful. By offering a tour specifically for new parents and caregivers, participants can interact as much (or as little) as they wish with other adults and have a focus in order to leave the house. According to the National Institutes of Health, one in seven women will develop postpartum depression and many others will still experience feelings of loneliness and isolation during parental leave. These symptoms can affect all genders, adoptive parents, and all caregivers, not just the birth parent. Things like cost, transportation, and child care can hinder access to alleviating symptoms. The Arboretum aims to make the outdoors and public gardens more accessible to everyone, regardless of where they are in life's journey.

name: SHAC Campus Health and Wellness Tabling Series
description: The SHAC Campus Health and Wellness Tabling Series is a weekly outreach initiative designed to strengthen student engagement with the University Health Center (UHC). Each week, a SHAC subcommittee—Preventive & Primary Care, Mental & Behavioral Health, Sexual & Reproductive Health, QMIT, or DEI—hosts a themed table in a central campus location. Tabling includes a feedback prompt, educational materials, interactive elements (e.g., surveys or QR codes), and wellness giveaways to encourage participation. The purpose of the series is to raise awareness of campus health resources, gather real-time student feedback, and offer approachable, consistent wellness engagement. It replaces larger, infrequent events with manageable, student-led outreach that better reflects student needs. This initiative supports SHAC’s mission to advise UHC, improve transparency, and promote student-centered health programming on campus.

name: Exploring Black Leadership at the NMAAHC
description: As a part of Black History Month, the MLEAD Program will charter a trip to the National Museum of African American History and Culture. The purpose of this program is to explore Black leadership throughout historical and contemporary contexts by engaging students in experiential and community-based learning. The curriculum will focus on the artifacts and stories in the following exhibits: Reclaiming My Time; Forces for Change; Slavery and Freedom; Making a Way Out of No Way; and more. Participants will be grouped into teams and will have the opportunity to examine how Black figures throughout history made collaborative efforts for collective impact, healing, and liberation. name: En'Rage Models Practice
description: Our practice sessions are dynamic and empowering, designed to build confidence, enhance runway skills, and foster creativity in a supportive environment. Each session begins with a warm-up to prepare our models for the physical and mental demands of the runway. Models are then guided through a series of runway walks, where they practice posture, poise, and movement in a variety of styles that challenge traditional norms of fashion and modeling. Throughout the practice, we focus on perfecting choreography for upcoming shows, allowing models to develop their unique flair while staying in sync with the group’s overall performance. Our experienced runway coaches provide individual feedback to ensure that each model feels confident in expressing their own style, aligning with our mission of self-empowerment and diversity. In addition to runway practice, we also incorporate photoshoot preparation, helping models become comfortable in front of the camera, and working on their poses and expressions. Music is played to set the tone, and we regularly rotate different fashion themes to keep practices fresh and engaging. Each session concludes with a debrief, where we emphasize the importance of mutual support and encouragement, celebrating personal growth and teamwork. En'Rage Models practices are more than just rehearsals—they are an opportunity for our members to develop their self-esteem, push creative boundaries, and prepare for the high-energy experience of the runway.

(Letterboxd)Written and Directed by Quentin TarantinoStarring Leonardo DiCaprio, Brad Pitt, Margot RobbieRuntime: 2 hr 41 minMPAA Rating: RWaves - February 12th, 13th - 8:00p“Let it rush over you…”The epic emotional journey of a suburban African-American family — led by a well-intentioned but domineering father — as they navigate love, forgiveness and coming together in the aftermath of a loss. (Letterboxd)Written and Directed by Trey Edward SchultsStarring Kelvin Harrison Jr., Lucas Hedges, Sterling K. BrownRuntime: 2 hr 15 minMPAA Rating: RKnives Out - February 19th, 20th - 8:00p“Hell, any of them could have done it…”A detective investigates the death of a patriarch of an eccentric, combative family. (IMDB)Written and Directed by Rian JohnsonStarring Daniel Craig, Ana de Armas, Chris EvansRuntime: 2 hr 10 minMPAA Rating: PG-13Parasite (기생충) - February 26th, 27th - 8:00p“Act like you own the place…”All unemployed, Ki-taek’s family takes peculiar interest in the wealthy and glamorous Parks for their livelihood until they get entangled in an unexpected incident. (Letterboxd)Directed by Bong Joon-hoStarring Song Kang-ho, Lee Sun-kyun, Cho Yeo-jeongRuntime: 2 hr 12 minMPAA Rating: RUncut Gems - March 4th, 5th - 8:00p“This is how I win…”Howard Ratner, a charismatic New York City jeweler always on the lookout for the next big score, makes a series of high-stakes bets that could lead to the windfall of a lifetime. (Letterboxd)Directed by Benny Safdie, Josh SafdieStarring Adam Sandler, Julia Fox, Lakeith StanfieldRuntime: 2 hr 15 minMPAA Rating: R*: Indicates screening with movie giveaway.**: Indicated the highest-requested film of the 2019-2020 academic year thus far at UMD, College Park.

name: GRadulting Workshop Series - What HEALTH INSURANCE plan is best for me?
description: How much will it cost me, and what happens if I get sick or hurt? Those questions are at the top of many people’s minds as they look at health plan options. Sure, it’s important to have a plan that fits your budget and has your back – but when you don't even understand the difference between a co-pay and a deductible, it's almost impossible to make a choice. This workshop is designed to help you understand some basic guidelines and terminology so you are prepared to evaluate your options and spend wisely when you’re shopping for health insurance. speakers: Dave Usher, Senior Account Executive, Academic HealthPlans (AHP) & Robyn Kotzker, The UMD Graduate Schoolco-sponsor: The UMD Graduate School General Info about GRadulting Workshops We welcome all GradTerps (and sometimes undergrads) to join us on Tuesdays for the GRadulting Virtual Workshop Series! Whether you are in the U.S. or in your home country, you can count on us for great information to help you navigate the issues and challenges of the adult world. If you are unable to attend, many of our speakers will give us permission to record the workshop so you can view it at your own convenience. We hope to see you there! GradTerps may join our Google Group to receive a weekly reminder of the upcoming workshops.

name: Camp PALS Volunteer opportunity
description: Volunteer to be a Counselor for the PALS program Camp PALS this summer. PALS is a nonprofit organization that provides one week long summer camp opportunities for teens and young adults with Down syndrome and their peers at 14 college campuses across the country. This is a one-week experience from 9am-5pm. Listed below are some details about Camp PALS: Here are some details about Camp PALS: - They offer 14 week long sleep-away camps across the country, including Camp PALS Georgetown, Chicago, and North Carolina! - Volunteer counselors are paired one-to-one with a camper to provide an opportunity to build -meaningful friendships through trips and activities - Looking for volunteers ages 16-30 who are welcoming, genuine, passionate, supportive, and fun which are all the values of the program. - No experience with Down syndrome or the disability community is necessary! They encourage groups of applicants to apply together to share the camp experience. If you are interested please visit the website at palsprograms.org/volunteer or check out their social media pages on Facebook or YouTube channel to get a look at what the PALS experience is like. PALS is an amazing opportunity to give back to the community, gain invaluable leadership skills, and make friends that will last a lifetime! There are no costs for volunteers at PALS, and applicants can apply for travel costs to be covered as well. We are looking for male applicants at this point in our season. Females are welcome to apply but will likely be placed on a waitlist. The dates for each of our 15 camps is different based on their locations, but the dates for Baltimore are July 7-13 at UMBC, and Georgetown is July 28-August 3 at Georgetown University.

name: SEE Presents: Free Fall Movie Series - John Wick 3
description: SEE invites you to UMD’s own Hoff Theater to unwind and join us for our first Free Fall Movie Series of the 2019-20 school year! Enjoy and support several of this year’s hottest movies along with some classic cultural milestones in a large theatrical setting all semester long!Iron Man (2008)- August 29th @ 8:00pm(Action/Sci-Fi) "After being held captive in an Afghan cave, billionaire engineer Tony Stark creates a unique weaponized suit of armor to fight evil." (IMDb)Guardians of the Galaxy (2014) - August 30th @ 8:00pm(Action/Comedy) "A group of intergalactic criminals must pull together to stop a fanatical warrior with plans to purge the universe." (IMDb)Avengers: Endgame - August 31st @ 8:00pm(Action/Sci-Fi) "After the devastating events of Avengers: Infinity War (2018), the universe is in ruins. With the help of remaining allies, the Avengers assemble once more in order to reverse Thanos' actions and restore balance to the universe." (IMDb)Detective Pikachu - September 5th & 7th @ 8:00pm(Action/Comedy) "In a world where people collect Pokémon to do battle, a boy comes across an intelligent talking Pikachu who seeks to be a detective." (IMDb)Rocketman - September 11th & 12th @ 8:00pm(Biography/Drama) "A musical fantasy about the fantastical human story of Elton John's breakthrough years." (IMDb)Yesterday - September 13th & 14th @ 8:00pm(Comedy/Fantasy) "A struggling musician realizes he's the only person on Earth who can remember The Beatles after waking up in an alternate timeline where they never existed." (IMDb)John Wick: Chapter 3 - Parabellum - September 17th & 19th @ 8:00pm(Action/Crime/Thriller) "Super-assassin John Wick is on the run after killing a member of the international assassin's guild, and with a $14 million price tag on his head - he is the target of hit men and women everywhere." (IMDb)Bill and Ted’s Excellent Adventure (1989): A Special 30th Anniversary Screening - September 21st @ 10:00pm(Adventure/Comedy) "Two seemingly dumb teens set off on a quest to prepare the ultimate historical presentation with the help of a time machine." (IMDb)Midsommar - September 26th & 27th @ 8:00pm(Drama/Horror/Mystery) "A couple travels to Sweden to visit a rural hometown's fabled mid-summer festival. What begins as an idyllic retreat quickly devolves into an increasingly violent and bizarre competition at the hands of a pagan cult." (IMDb)The Rocky Horror Picture Show (1975) - September 28th @ 10:00pm(Comedy/Musical) "A newly engaged couple have a breakdown in an isolated area and must pay a call to the bizarre residence of Dr. Frank-N-Furter." (IMDb)Toy Story 4 - October 3rd & 4th @ 8:00pm(Animation/Comedy) "When a new toy called "Forky" joins Woody and the gang, a road trip alongside old and new friends reveals how big the world can be for a toy." (IMDb)Each screening will be in Hoff Theatre inside the Stamp Student Union. Each screening is open for anyone to attend and doors will open 30 minutues prior to showtime. Seating will be available on a first-come, first serve basis.All weekend movies hosted by Terps After Dark.

name: 2019 GBM #5 - Hardware Hacking with BusesCanFly
description: Hey everyone! We hope you had a wonderful Thanksgiving! Get ready for our last GBM of the semester - Hardware Hacking with BusesCanFly! CSEC Member BusesCanFly will be giving a beginner-level interactive hardware hacking demonstration, followed by a workshop where you all get to try the hack yourselves! We've purchased components and put together hardware kits for the workshop, so there will hardware for each and every one of you to work on! BusesCanFly will spend the first third of this GBM explaining the basics of hardware hacking and how you can get started. Following this, he'll do a demonstration of how you can bypass physical tamper-evident security seals. Finally, the remainder of the GBM will be given to you so that you can work on the hardware kits. Each hardware kit consists of a vulnerable Raspberry Pi that has been sealed in a sardine can with tamper evident tape. Come see if you can get into the hardware without leaving a trace, and pop a shell!

Racial Equity: Teams that are working to address racism, especially anti-Blackness, or that explicitly include racial equality/intersectionality work within the social issue they are working to address. New or Emerging Teams: Teams that have formed in the last two years, and/or teams that have not previously received a Mini-Grant or other funding from Do Good. Community-Centered Initiatives: Teams that have established community partnerships or extensive stakeholder engagement to show their initiative is welcome and needed. For the 2020-2021 Academic year, we will offer three rounds of Mini-Grants. For this round, please apply by Monday, September 21. Contact Cali Moore, Program Coordinator, at cacmoore@umd.edu for more information.

name: Historical Appropriation Among Far-Right Extremists
description: On Thursday, December 10 at 2:00 p.m. ET, START will host a virtual panel event on “Historical Appropriation Among Far-Right Extremists.” This event is free and open to the public, but RSVPs are required. If you have any questions, please email the START events team at start-events@umd.edu. In this discussion, Brandeis University Assistant Professor of English Dr. Dorothy Kim will discuss the use of Viking culture and symbols among white supremacists, Eidolon Editor-in-Chief Dr. Donna Zuckerberg will explore the use of ancient Greek and Latin texts among online male supremacists, and START Senior Researcher Dr. Elizabeth Yates will offer examples of famous violent extremists and how these historical claims are made clear in their writing. Dr. Dorothy Kim teaches Medieval Literature at Brandeis University. Her research focuses on race, gender, digital humanities, medieval women’s literary cultures, medievalism, Jewish/Christian difference, book history, digital media, and the alt-right. She was a 2013-2014 Fellow at the University of Michigan’s Frankel Institute of Advanced Judaic Studies where she drafted a monograph entitled Jewish/Christian Entanglements: Ancrene Wisse and its Material Worlds (under submission, University of Penn Press). She also has another book, The Alt-Medieval: Digital Whiteness and Medieval Studies forthcoming with the University of Minnesota Press. She has a forthcoming book with Lynn Ramey entitled Global Medieval Digital Humanities (Cambridge UP). She spent the 2018-2019 AAUW fellowship working on her next book, Race, the Crusades, and the Katherine Group. Dr. Donna Zuckerberg is the author of Not All Dead White Men: Classics and Misogyny in the Digital Age (Harvard University Press, 2018). She received her Ph.D. from Princeton University in 2014 and is the founder and Editor-in-Chief of Eidolon, a prize-winning online publication for informal Classics scholarship with more than 1.5 million views. Her writing has appeared in the Washington Post, the TLS, and Jezebel. She lives in California with her two sons and bulldog. Dr. Elizabeth Yates is a Senior Researcher on the domestic radicalization team at START. She works primarily on the suite of datasets associated with PIRUS (Profiles of Individual Radicalization in the United States) and BIAS (Bias Incidents and Actors Study), with a special focus on far-right violence, extremism, and hate crimes. She is also a co-Principal Investigator on a multi-year NIJ-funded project studying extremist offender reintegration. In addition, Dr. Yates has taught undergraduate classes in Terrorism Studies and Sociology at the University of Maryland and the University of Pittsburgh, respectively. She earned a doctorate in Sociology at the University of Pittsburgh, and a BA in International Relations at Tufts University.

name: Camp PALS Volunteer opportunity
description: Volunteer to be a Counselor for the PALS program Camp PALS this summer. PALS is a nonprofit organization that provides one week long summer camp opportunities for teens and young adults with Down syndrome and their peers at 14 college campuses across the country. This is a one-week experience from 9am-5pm. Listed below are some details about Camp PALS: Here are some details about Camp PALS: - They offer 14 week long sleep-away camps across the country, including Camp PALS Georgetown, Chicago, and North Carolina! - Volunteer counselors are paired one-to-one with a camper to provide an opportunity to build -meaningful friendships through trips and activities - Looking for volunteers ages 16-30 who are welcoming, genuine, passionate, supportive, and fun which are all the values of the program. - No experience with Down syndrome or the disability community is necessary! They encourage groups of applicants to apply together to share the camp experience. If you are interested please visit the website at palsprograms.org/volunteer or check out their social media pages on Facebook or YouTube channel to get a look at what the PALS experience is like. PALS is an amazing opportunity to give back to the community, gain invaluable leadership skills, and make friends that will last a lifetime! There are no costs for volunteers at PALS, and applicants can apply for travel costs to be covered as well. We are looking for male applicants at this point in our season. Females are welcome to apply but will likely be placed on a waitlist. The dates for each of our 15 camps is different based on their locations, but the dates for Baltimore are July 7-13 at UMBC, and Georgetown is July 28-August 3 at Georgetown University.

name: How Did 9/11 Affect Terrorism Research? A Look at Disciplines and Gender
description: On Wednesday, February 3 at 10:00 a.m. ET, University of Essex Senior Lecturer Dr. Brian J. Phillips will provide a virtual talk on “How Did 9/11 Affect Terrorism Research? A Look at Disciplines and Gender.” This event is free and open to the public, but RSVPs are required. If you have any questions, please email the START events team at start-events@umd.edu. Terrorism research increased markedly after the attacks of Sept. 11, 2001. Beyond increasing, how has research on this subject changed in the past 20 years? I examine data on more than 6,000 academic articles on terrorism between 1970 and 2019, and the more than 1,600 authors of multiple articles. Several interesting findings emerge. (1) The post-9/11 proliferation of terrorism research does not appear to be winding down. (2) The proportion of terrorism research in terrorism and conflict journals decreased after 9/11, with other types of journals starting to publish a great deal of terrorism research. (3) Psychologists became the dominant subgroup of terrorism researchers after 9/11, displacing Political Scientists, although this trend appears to have now reversed. (4) The proportion of female scholars increased substantially after 9/11, outpacing the rise in academia generally. The seems to be at least in part because scholars new to the field after 9/11 were often from relatively gender-balanced disciplines such as psychology. Dr. Brian J. Phillips is a senior lecturer (associate professor) in the Department of Government at the University of Essex, and an affiliated professor at the Center for Research and Teaching in Economics (CIDE) in Mexico City. He researches and teaches about terrorism, civil conflict, and organized crime.
