name: Intro to Virtual Reality Development
description: Want to learn how you can create your own VR app from scratch? Join us this Wednesday as we build a simple VR game together and test it using a VR simulator right from your own computer! That's right: no headset necessary! We'll be using Unity's brand new XR Interaction Toolkit, a cross-platform framework that allows you to quickly and easily add AR/VR interactions into to your Unity applications. Along the way, you'll also learn about and apply some of the principles of good VR app design, including using teleportation and snap rotations for movement, picking up and throwing objects with a controller, and adding spatial audio effects for a more immersive experience. No prior experience necessary; all majors welcome! Pre-requisites: This workshop requires you to have Unity 2019.4 (LTS) or later installed. The Unity Editor could take 30 mins or longer to download and install, so you will not have enough time during the workshop to install the software without falling behind. In order to run the project, you will need one of the following:• a 6-DOF VR headset, such as the Oculus Rift, Oculus Rift S, Oculus Quest, HTC Vive, or Windows Mixed Reality headsets.• the XR Interaction Toolkit VR Simulator, which can be bought on the Unity Asset Store for $5 (see here). Note that this is a third-party tool, not provided by Unity. We will guide you through the process of purchasing this during the workshop.

name: Race for Every Child
description: Every year, Children’s National Hospital hosts a 5k run called “Race For Every Child” in Washington DC, and it is one of Terp Thon’s favorite events to participate in. Due to the present circumstances, Children’s National has decided to host the Race For Every Child completely virtually, and we couldn’t be more excited! Instead of going to DC and doing the race there, Terp Thon has decided to convert this race into a completely virtual version that anyone in our community can take part in, whether they are on campus or at home! The race will take place on October 17-18 to allow all people who want to race to have the opportunity to race on trails without the risk of contact with other runners. We plan on having four different distances offered for the race, including a 1 mile “Fun Run”, a 5k, a 10k, and a half marathon! There won’t be any set trails, courses, or start and finish points in order to maximize social distancing. We will be offering marked trails if participants would like to use them, and for these we will have participants sign up for the time they would like to race to make sure no two people are on the same trail at the same time. All participants need to do is register for the event with some simple contact info through our provided Google Form for safety and track their race with any app or device that can track distance (example: Apple Watch Run or Nike Run App). Registration for this event is completely free, as Children’s National has decided to make their event completely free also, but there is an opportunity for participants to fundraise for the hospital if they have a DonorDrive page! In order to make this event completely contactless as well, we will not be providing any racing materials such as racing bibs, pins, or anything of the sort. Instead, we will be using social media as our platform for publicizing and making this race as special and fun as possible! We will be sending out multiple social media graphics with bib-like designs, different quotes, and places to share why you’re racing without being in-person! Terp Thon will be strongly advising against racing with groups, but if participants would like to race in small groups (2-3 people or with the people that they live with), they must wear a mask at all times when near others and choose the walking option. This same rule applies to other racers as well, and everyone must carry a mask with them at all times even if racing alone in case they come in contact with others on their path. Once participants finish their desired distance, they will take a picture of the tracking app they used to chart their path and send it to Terp Thon so we know they finished! There will be incentives for participants who complete each distance, but these are still being decided.

name: GRadulting Workshop Series - How do I prepare my taxes? - for domestic students
description: Filing Federal and State taxes are confusing for everyone, including graduate students! To help you through this process our offices are hosting a tax workshop for domestic students and another for international students. Get guidance on how to handle common tax issues and bring your questions to the Q&A session. For help with more complex questions, we will share free resources for one-on-one tax support. The Federal Filing deadline is April 15, 2021. Co-hosts: Graduate Student Legal Aid and International Student and Scholar Services Speakers: Professor Sam Handwerger, Lecturer and Advisor for TerpTax, UMD Smith's School of Business *** Gradute Student Legal Aid offers the GRadulting Virtual Workshop Series, often in collaboration with other offices on campus. GradTerps (and sometimes undergrads) are welcome to join us virtually on Tuesdays, usually at 12:30pm. Whether you are in the U.S. or in your home country, you can count on us for great information to help you navigate the issues and challenges of the adult world. If you are unable to attend, many of our speakers will give us permission to record the workshop so you can view it at your own convenience. We hope to see you there! What is GRadulting? Gradulting is defined as graduate students who are "adulting" -- (v): to carry out one or more of the duties and responsibilities expected of fully developed individuals, such as financial planning, buying a home, negotiating a salary, or estate planning. GradTerps, join our Google Group to receive a weekly reminder of the upcoming workshops!

name: Free Kenny Collins: Live from The Other Death Row
description: Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/events/215697458834729/ Kenny Collins has been in prison in Maryland for 30 years, including 17 years on death row. He was convicted of a robbery and murder that occurred in 1986. Kenny has always maintained his innocence and continues to do so to this day. The facts in his case make it hard to understand how he could have been convicted, let alone sentenced to death, and his case is emblematic of many of the problems with the criminal justice system in the U.S.overall and Maryland in particular. Join the Prison Resistance Project and the International Socialist Organization for a discussion of Kenny’s case, the general issues of life in prison in Maryland, including the aging prison population, and the fight for Kenny and for justice for all prisoners and how you can get involved. The racist system of mass incarceration, or “New Jim Crow” as Michele Alexander puts it, must be resisted! Location: University of Maryland Stamp Student Union. Room Pyon Su 2108 Speakers include: Kenny Collins, calling from prison. Laura Lising, activist and organizer of the Free Kenny Collins Campaign Tomiko Shine, Maryland chapter of RAPP (Release Aging People in Prison)

name: Complexifying Conversations
description: The African Diaspora Reading Group (ADRG) is excited to announce our two-part series titled "Complexifying Conversations: Performing Black Subjectivities throughout the African Diaspora" on April 6th @ 7-9:30 pm & 8th @ 6-9 pm - 2115 Tawes . Come speak, eat, and drink with allies and friends alike. The name “Real Talk” was chosen because sexual assault is often seen as a taboo topic, or something that we would rather tiptoe around but it is clear that this behavior towards the subject is dangerous. name: Work with At-Risk Kids: Change Your life!
description: We're gearing up for the best program year yet at the St. Francis Neighborhood Center and we're looking for dedicated volunteers to help in the Power Project, our free after school youth development program that serves the at-risk children of Reservoir Hill. The program starts Monday, Oct. 6 and we're looking for both tutors and program assistants to support staff and help make sure the program is fun for our kids, safe and successful. We know you're busy, but volunteering is important to you, which is why we're flexible and want to make sure your volunteer experience is the very best it can be. If you'd like to volunteer a few hours a week or a few hours a month, we'll make sure your time here is appreciated, valued and FUN! Our youth development program focuses on arts enrichment, academic support, mentoring and tutoring. Positions involve hands-on work with youth ages 5 to 13. Orientation and training are provided. Hours: Monday through Thursday from 3 to 6 pm. Skills: Experience working with children and the ability to volunteer on a regular basis. For more information, please email volunteer@stfranciscenter.org. About Us: St. Francis Neighborhood Center's mission is committed to breaking the cycles of poverty through education, inspiring self-esteem, self-improvement, and strengthening connections. We provide free academic and arts-based learning programs to community children in addition to mentoring, tutoring and meals.

name: Overnight Volunteer Position
description: Calvary Women's Services is a transitional housing program for homeless women in Southeast Washington, DC and we love working with UMD students! Our mission is to provide a safe, caring place for tonight; support, hope and change for tomorrow. Overnight Volunteers are needed to supervise our programs from 9:00 pm - 7:00 am, making our residents feel safe and secure. Calvary staff and the overnight volunteer will work as a team to ensure a smooth, quiet night. This volunteer position is ideal for a flexible individual looking to serve in an essential role. At night when they arrive, volunteers are responsible for setting out breakfast, welcoming residents arriving late from work or school, and doing a final walkthrough of the facility. In the morning, volunteers facilitate breakfast for residents and make sure clients are up and ready for the day. Volunteer shifts are available all nights of the week. Interested in more information? Contact us at 202.678.2341 or information@calvaryservices.org.

description: Seabury Resources for the Aging's mission is to provide personalized, affordable services and housing options to help older adults in Washington, DC to live with independence and dignity. Their Age-in-Place program allows for their clients to continue living in their lifelong homes and apartments by providing volunteers to help with basic upkeep and maintenance that they cannot do themselves. Students will work in groups at the residences of elderly and aging community members. The service itself can include house cleanup, yard work, small maintenance projects, and other upkeep tasks, not to mention engaging with the clients, who love speaking with college students! Volunteers should dress in clothes that they do not mind getting dirty, wear closed-toed shoes, and keep in mind that the sites may contain allergens (pets, dust, pollen, etc.). Volunteers should also dress in layers for the weather and bring a reusable water bottle. TerpService Days are one-time days of service targeted at the broad campus community. Students with significant or no experience in service-learning are welcome to participate. name: BSides DC - SOLD OUT
description: Security B-sides started out a few years ago to give a voice to talks that didn't make the cut at blackhat, but the community still felt were valuable to the information security industry. That first event was dubbed Security Bsides Las Vegas. Since then Security B-sides has turned into a grassroots template for putting together local, community driven information security conferences. More than 30 Bsides events took place both domestically and internationally in 2012. More information can be found at http://www.securitybsides.com BsidesDC 2013 is in its inaugural year and will take place on October 19th - 20th, 2013 at the Washington Marriott Metro Center. We are expecting ~300 attendees for the event. The general format will be 2 speaking tracks each day, with a keynote speaker on Saturday. More information can be found at http://www.bsidesdc.org The benefit to students: The spirit behind bsides events is one of participation, with the common goal of improving the information security community and helping the industry tackle some of today biggest infosec challenges. In that light, we welcome individuals of all ages and demographics to include high school and college students. The event will be a great networking opportunity for students who wish to pursue careers in cyber security, IT and information security and want to get face time with industry professionals/vendors. We currently have 13 confirmed sponors for the event, each of whom will have company representatives in attendance, and are working with several other companies to confirm their participation. We will also be allowing attendee to voluntarily submit resumes which will be forwarded to all sponsoring companies. Finally, the event should be rather convenient for students in the area as its scheduled on the weekend and tickets are only $10.60.

name: Guest Speaker: Rabbi Jonathan Bailey
description: At Kedma, we seek to provide the community at UMD with unique opportunities for Jewish education and spirituality. We are able to explore our deep connection to our culture and roots through the learning of Jewish texts. To help with this goal, we would like to host Rabbi Jonathan Bailey for a Torah lecture via Zoom to teach and inspire our organization to become better Torah scholars, as well as improve our character as people. Rabbi Jonathan Bailey is an internationally acclaimed bible scholar. He has taught at multiple institutions, including Yeshivat Eretz Hatzvi, Midreshet Lindenbaum, Midreshet Emunah V’Omanut and Midreshet Harova. Rav Bailey has worked full-time at Midreshet Harova since 2014, teaching a myriad of classes including Gemara, Chumash, Pirkei Avot, Contemporary Halakhah and a course in comparative literature. Inspired by his background in English Literature, Rav Bailey’s primary method of study is close textual analysis, encouraging his students to consider each word of a primary text so as to discover and understand its deepest meaning. This skill is not only applicable to the bible. It is extremely important to analyze texts in our lives in order to discover underlying meaning. Rabbi Bailey will be teaching on matters of Bible and Religion via Zoom to about 40 students. This lecture will benefit the campus community because it enhances the overall desire of the campus to generate a communal culture of learning. Rabbi Bailey’s teaching style focuses on challenging his students to think and self-discover, two ingredients he believes are vital to creating a true love of and dedication to Torah, its values, and its continued meaningfulness in their lives.

name: From Objects of Reproduction to Subjects of Immigrant Maternity
description: In this talk, Dr. Vera Rosas will discuss the political implications of claiming the undocumented mother as a “maternal figure” and as “an outlaw.” By analyzing cultural and political representations and drawing on interviews, this presentation centers the lives and stories of Latina immigrant mothers to think about the possibility of feminists futures that challenge normative notions of motherhood and legality. Dr. Vera-Rosas uses a feminist and decolonial framework to examine the political and cultural representations of mothers who exist outside the boundaries of legality in the Américas. Her research explores the limits and opportunities offered by visual culture to think critically about the social worlds destroyed and produced by the drug wars and restrictive immigration policies across the Hemisphere. name: The Barclay Brass (USA)
description: Trumpeter and UMD School of Music graduate Nathan Clark '13 , arranger and trombonist David Miller and UMD School of Music lecturer and tubist Willie Clark came together in 2015 to create a brass ensemble of the highest caliber—featuring some of Washington, D.C.'s finest military band musicians. From patriotic and ceremonial to classical and seasonal, the Barclay Brass performs for diverse audiences from K-12 students to the Pope. Recently, the ensemble was part of the Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum’s “The Force at 40,” a celebration of the 40th anniversary release of “Star Wars.” Committed to creating meaningful connections with the next generation of brass musicians, the ensemble has worked with various brass students across the country at institutions including Kent State University, University of Akron and George Mason University. At The Clarice, The Barclay Brass will collaborate on- and off-stage with the School of Music’s Fellowship Brass Quintet and teach masterclasses to brass students across the school. name: Terri Lyne Carrington & Social Science (USA)
description: For nearly four decades, Grammy award winner and National Endowment for the Arts Jazz Master Terri Lyne Carrington has been on the front lines of creating a new form of jazz—one without patriarchy. Her work as a drummer and bandleader has earned her a Doris Duke Artist Award and three Grammys, including Best Jazz Vocal Album for “The Mosaic Project,” which exclusively featured female musicians. In 2018, she founded the Berklee Institute of Jazz and Gender Justice to address a long history of inequality and sexual harassment. In late 2019, Carrington released “Waiting Game,” her seventh album as a bandleader and first with her new group, Social Science. The album leaps through an ebullient mix of improvised instrumental suites, electroacoustic textures and pointed social commentary. With pianist Aaron Parks and guitarist Matt Stevens, she guides a band built on kinetic energy and unbound curiosity. In the 2020-21 season, Carrington led a Jazz Clinic for students in the UMD School of Music’s Jazz Studies Division that focused on a lack of gender equity within the jazz community. She also participated in The Clarice’s popular Black Women in the Arts series alongside flutist/composer Nicole Mitchell and singer/songwriter Dianne Reeves. Behind the kit, Carrington is a commanding instrumentalist; as a bandleader, she is nothing less than the future of a more equitable jazz. Health + Safety There may be COVID safety policies such as mask requirements in place when you attend this event. Please see our health & safety page for the most up to date information about attendance!

name: Veterans Yoga
description: Sun Salutations (8/31) Get ready for a class to introduce health and vitality into the semester! This short class includes 20 minutes of cleansing movement fit for yogis of all shapes, sizes, and experience levels. Bonus: Do you not have time to relax and let go for even just a few minutes? Your instructor includes at least five minutes of required shavasana practice at the end of each class to give the mind a break from the rest of the world. Learn a New Pose (9/2) Today’s yoga session will include 18 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out, meaning that yogis of all experience and backgrounds will benefit! Get ready to build strength and resilience with this fun-to learn movement. Relaxation Meditation (9/7) Tuesday’s session will be focused on grounding yourself in this new semester. Just fifteen minutes of passive, yet focused yoga practice will bring you into the moment and out of the stresses of the new semester. Get a Workout in (9/9) After Tuesday’s session focused on relaxation and finding ground in the new semester, it’s time to ramp up the heat. You would never believe what just twenty minutes of poses can do to get that blood pumping and the sweat pouring! Don’t worry, though! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Open the Hips (9/14) We have been in class for a couple of weeks now and our bodies need us to keep moving to stay open and ready for all that life has to offer. Twenty three minutes of opening the hips will keep them from tightening from all the stress and constant sitting motion. Don’t forget! We also include at least five minutes of time to destress and prepare for the rest of the week. Learn a New Pose (9/16) Today’s yoga session will include 24 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out. Yogis of all experience and backgrounds will benefit from this fun practice! Get ready to build some awesome abdominal strength with this sequence. Relaxation Meditation (9/21) Today’s session will be focused on grounding yourself in this new semester. Twenty six minutes of passive, yet focused yoga practice will bring you into the moment and out of the stresses of the semester’s stressors. Getting in a Workout! (9/23) After Tuesday’s session focused on relaxation and finding ground in this awesome in-person semester, it’s time to get that body moving. Just thirty three minutes of poses will get that blood pumping and the sweat pouring! Don’t worry! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Plus, we won’t leave your muscles stiff from the hard work! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for the Booty (9/28) Looking to add cushion and tone to your derriere? Who isn’t?! Today’s session will be devoted to working to add strength to the glutes and hamstrings. Twenty minutes of work will show you some tips and tools to build your important muscle groups that keep your body healthy and moving! Learn a New Pose (9/30) Today’s yoga session will include 25 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out! Even the simplest of poses require detail-orientation! Get ready to build strength and resilience in simple poses. Relaxation Meditation (10/5) Tuesday’s session will be focused on staying sane as the semester continues to pose more difficulties. This is a time for you to take 26 minutes to treat yourself to reduce stress and a little self-care. Get a Workout In (10/7) After Tuesday’s session focused on relaxation and de-stressing, it’s time to move the mind, body, and spirit. Just 34 minutes of yoga flow will get that blood pumping! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in and focused throughout the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Plus, we won’t leave your muscles stiff from the hard work! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for Weak and Tight Shoulders (10/12) We get it. Being an athlete, veteran, human, parent, student, etc. comes with a price. Usually that price is paid in the body. Today we are going to focus on restoring weak and/or tight shoulders. Don’t shy away from class out of fear of injury! There are modifications for all flexibility levels in the shoulders. We are working to improve, not perfect! After all, we only have twenty six minutes! Learn a New Pose (10/14) Today’s yoga session will include 34 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out! Poses that seem difficult from the outside may be a bit simpler than you anticipate! We are focused on safety in strength. So first, we will build strength and confidence. Then we will build upon simple poses to create a beautiful movement to feel proud about. Relaxation Meditation (10/19) We are mid-semester. While it feels like this is the time to be working your butt off with as few breaks as possible, don’t forget about the importance of daily self-care. Today’s class will be nineteen minutes focused on nothing but bringing you back to yourself. This is a time to reclaim the best parts of yourself and create the person you want to be with focused intention. Get a Workout In (10/21) Tuesday got us mentally focused for the week, so now it is time to ramp up the energy to end the week strong! Thirty-one minutes of yoga flow will get that blood pumping! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in and focused. Don’t forget a towel! We will leave your muscles feeling worked, but not too stiff! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for Back Pain (10/26) Is your back constantly feeling stiff? Is the lower back achy and shoulder blades tight? Come to today’s yoga session for the opportunity to release some of that stiffness, and open yourself up to a world of relief! You might be surprised at what a short 33 minutes of stretching and strengthening can do for the body. Learn a New Pose (10/28) Ready to expand your yoga knowledge and experience? Today’s class will revolve around learning a yoga pose through-and-through. There is no reason to worry about the experience level needed for the pose, as all poses learned and performed here can be done at any level! Set aside 33 minutes and get mentally ready to learn reverse warrior so we can add it to your yoga repertoire! Relaxation Meditation (11/2) Meditating on a regular basis has positive effects on the body and mind, such as greater sense of focus, muscle relaxation, and increased creativity. Today’s meditation will be focused on gratitude and increasing happiness. Giving thanks can come in many forms, but have you tried it in the form of meditation?! Getting in a Workout! (11/4) After Tuesday’s session focused on gratitude in this challenging semester, it’s time to get that body moving. Just 34 minutes of sweat-inducing poses will get that blood pumping! This class is fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Plus, we won’t leave your muscles stiff from the hard work! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for a Better Mood (11/9) College is demanding, stressful, and can induce negative feelings! Combat those real-time stresses by moving the body and bonding with fellow veterans. Coming to this thirty minute vinyasa class will open the heart to the positivity you need to get you to the end of the semester. Learn a New Pose (11/11) Ready to expand your yoga knowledge and experience? Today’s class will revolve around learning a yoga pose through-and-through. There is no reason to worry about the experience level needed for the pose, as all poses learned and performed here can be done at any level! Set aside 35 minutes and get mentally ready to learn a new pose to add to your yoga repertoire! Relaxation Meditation (11/16) Today’s meditation practice will be short, sweet, and perfect to regain focus on your workflow. As we near the end of the semester, stress increases, the mind wanders, and we lose focus. We will be going through meditation techniques that can be utilized at home, work, or on the bus. Don’t underestimate the power of this 26 minute session. Come join your fellow veterans and enjoy the feeling of a clear mind. Get a Workout In (11/18) After Tuesday’s session focused on de-stressing and refocusing, it’s time to move that body. Just 34 minutes of yoga flow will get that blood pumping! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in and focused throughout the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Plus, we won’t leave your muscles stiff from the hard work! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for Neck Pain (11/23) After months of looking down at our computer screens, it’s no wonder so many of us have the amount of pain in our necks that we do! Today’s class will be all about de-stressing, communication, and releasing the tension in the neck through yoga practice. Set aside 31 minutes for this perfectly-paced practice.

name: Scholar in Residence: Rabbi Jesse Horn
description: Rabbi Jesse Horn is visiting as a Scholar in Residence for Kedma, hosted at Maryland Hillel on February 11-12, 2022. Rabbi Jesse Horn is a Senior Ram (head of education) at Yeshivat Hakotel. He is known for his methodological and Brisker approach to Gemara (Talmud), his creative shiurim in Tanach (Bible), and his warm personality. In his lectures, he motivates students to rigorously dissect texts, to ask major questions on the topic at hand, and to intuit the interpretations offered by the commentaries. Rabbi Horn also teaches at Michlelet Mevaseret Yerushalayim and has taught in other seminaries, such as Shaalvim for Women and Midreshet HaRova. He regularly lectures as a scholar-in-residence in communities all over the world. Rabbi Horn is the author of Double Take, a book about Biblical personalities, as well as numerous other articles for Beis Yitzhak, Arutz Sheva, World Mizrachi, and other scholarly publications. He also authors a weekly email in which he answers Jewish law questions to an audience of almost 1,500 readers.Rabbi Horn earned a B.A. in Judaic Studies and an M.A. in Jewish Education from Yeshiva University. He received his ordination from Yeshiva University/RIETS. As a Scholar in Residence, Rabbi Horn will be giving a lecture during dinner on Friday night, speaking at a ‘Lunch and Learn’ on the Shabbat day, and giving a lecture before the late afternoon prayer.

name: Naloxone Training
description: The University of Maryland Health Center is designated as an Overdose Response Program (ORP) through the Maryland Department of Health. As part of this designation, we offer overdose response resources to the UMD community, free of charge. One of the most popular resources we offer is Naloxone, an opioid overdose reversal medication. Similarly to how an EpiPen temporarily blocks the life-threatening symptoms of an allergic reaction (i.e. inability to breathe) while emergency medical assistance arrives, Naloxone offers this temporary support for those experiencing an opioid overdose. To get your free Naloxone through the Health Center, all you have to do is attend a brief training, which goes over how to recognize signs of an opioid overdose, instructions for using Naloxone, and what to do as emergency medical assistance makes its way to you and the person in crisis. Trainings are all offered in the Sahet Room of the Health Center, just past the main entrance to the building, and are free to any UMD community member interested in attending! Registration is required for attendance. --- RSVP URL: https://forms.gle/woguGFjSDnYfHs7VA

name: Walk with an Arborist & Your Baby
organization: University of Maryland Arboretum & Botanical Gardens
description: Walk with an Arborist & Your Baby encourages new parents to connect with each other and with the outdoors in a safe space, both physically and emotionally. Based in the Garden of Reflection & Remembrance at the Memorial Chapel, participants learn about trees and plants while having their newborns along. Parental leave and the welcoming of a new child can be lonely and stressful. By offering a tour specifically for new parents and caregivers, participants can interact as much (or as little) as they wish with other adults and have a focus in order to leave the house. According to the National Institutes of Health, one in seven women will develop postpartum depression and many others will still experience feelings of loneliness and isolation during parental leave. These symptoms can affect all genders, adoptive parents, and all caregivers, not just the birth parent. Things like cost, transportation, and child care can hinder access to alleviating symptoms. The Arboretum aims to make the outdoors and public gardens more accessible to everyone, regardless of where they are in life's journey. name: Walk with an Arborist & Your Baby
organization: University of Maryland Arboretum & Botanical Gardens
description: Walk with an Arborist & Your Baby encourages new parents to connect with each other and with the outdoors in a safe space, both physically and emotionally. Based in the Garden of Reflection & Remembrance at the Memorial Chapel, participants learn about trees and plants while having their newborns along. Parental leave and the welcoming of a new child can be lonely and stressful. By offering a tour specifically for new parents and caregivers, participants can interact as much (or as little) as they wish with other adults and have a focus in order to leave the house. According to the National Institutes of Health, one in seven women will develop postpartum depression and many others will still experience feelings of loneliness and isolation during parental leave. These symptoms can affect all genders, adoptive parents, and all caregivers, not just the birth parent. Things like cost, transportation, and child care can hinder access to alleviating symptoms. The Arboretum aims to make the outdoors and public gardens more accessible to everyone, regardless of where they are in life's journey. name: Beekeeping Club Weekly Meeting
description: During the late spring, summer, and early fall, we have meetings to check on our bees. We learn about sustainable beekeeping practices, what to look for and do while taking care of bees. People who show up to this meeting will have to wear bee-safe clothing such as close toed shoes, and preferably pants, though we have full suits and half suits along with gloves provided. Participants will also have to sign a safety waiver which accepts the possibility of bee stings. When it is too cold or rainy, we go to the UMD Greenhouses to complete workshops such as candles, chapstick, and soap using beeswax. Feel free to reach out through our TerpLink page, our email, or the Discord for more information! The Beekeeping Club does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, religion, age, or physical ability. The Mission of The Beekeeping Club is to educate students about bees and beekeeping through hands-on experience and lectures, about harvesting raw products from them in sustainable ways, and about turning those raw products a variety of goods. The Beekeeping Club seeks to offer anyone with a curiosity or passion for bees and beekeeping the ability to participate in beekeeping regardless of their skill level or prior experience and to guide them in learning more about bees and the role beekeeping plays a sustainable world.

name: Unity Gala 2024
description: This year’s Unity Gala is tied to the Asian Pacific Islander Desi American (APIDA) Heritage Month’s theme of Memories in Motion: Memories seemingly live in our past. Yet, they inform so much of our present and shape so much of our future. They aren’t just the makeup of our individual experiences, but a confluence of our collective identity—they are our ancestors, our stories, our traditions. Memories can evoke so many different feelings for each of us. At times, they bring us joy and laughter, and other recollections might bring pain and sadness. But what is constant is that they move us to think, reflect, and act. To honor our past and how it shapes us. To heal what has yet to be explored. To remember what has been forgotten in service to the broken promises of the American dream. To transform what weighs us down to what lifts us up. And to work in solidarity towards liberation, as all our histories are interconnected. Memories have power. Let them move us to action. Unity Gala is the culminating celebration of the University of Maryland’s recognition of APIDA Heritage Month in April. The mission of the annual Unity Gala is to eliminate cultural barriers between different APIDA student groups on campus to mark the end of Asian Pacific Islander Desi American Heritage Month at UMCP. On campus, Asian American student organizations host their own events within the wider AAPI circle, such as KSA’s KExpo, TASA’s Tour of Taiwan, and VSA’s Family Night. However, student organizations rarely interact with cultural organizations beyond the Asian American/Pacific Islander sphere. The Asian American Student Union strives to extend the sphere of APIDA Organizations through this gala. In the wake of troubling and hostile events, the gala is meant to create a space for a safe exchange of ideas, identities and cultures.

name: Beekeeping Club Weekly Meeting
description: During the late spring, summer, and early fall, we have meetings to check on our bees. We learn about sustainable beekeeping practices, what to look for and do while taking care of bees. People who show up to this meeting will have to wear bee-safe clothing such as close toed shoes, and preferably pants, though we have full suits and half suits along with gloves provided. Participants will also have to sign a safety waiver which accepts the possibility of bee stings. When it is too cold or rainy, we go to the UMD Greenhouses to complete workshops such as candles, chapstick, and soap using beeswax. Feel free to reach out through our TerpLink page, our email, or the Discord for more information! The Beekeeping Club does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, religion, age, or physical ability. The Mission of The Beekeeping Club is to educate students about bees and beekeeping through hands-on experience and lectures, about harvesting raw products from them in sustainable ways, and about turning those raw products a variety of goods. The Beekeeping Club seeks to offer anyone with a curiosity or passion for bees and beekeeping the ability to participate in beekeeping regardless of their skill level or prior experience and to guide them in learning more about bees and the role beekeeping plays a sustainable world.

name: Tianyi Spring Semester Friday Practices
description: Tianyi Dance Team, University of Maryland's only Chinese cultural dance team, is a group of students who express interest in Chinese culture through folk and traditional Chinese dance. Tianyi Dance Team strives to break down cross-cultural barriers through the graceful, yet powerful language of dance. name: GRadulting Workshop Series - Do you know how to cite sources and paraphrase to avoid getting charged with plagiarism?
description: Accidental plagiarism is usually the result of being rushed, unorganized, or uninformed about the citation and research process. Additionally, students often come to UMD from institutions and educational cultures where academic integrity and plagiarism standards are either taught in a different manner or not routinely enforced. Whether it’s an accident or an intentional act of plagiarism, the consequences are essentially the same. It can result in a reprimand, failed grade, failed course, or even worse. Attend this workshop to learn about the most common types of plagiarism and explore the best practices in citation and the ethical and appropriate use of sources. Speaker: Dr. Linda Macri (Director, Graduate School Writing Center) Co-Sponsor: The Graduate School Writing Center

name: I Resist This: Soft Sculpture Performance by Charlotte Richardson-Deppe
description: The Stamp Gallery is pleased to announce the artist residency of Charlotte Richardson-Deppe, who will utilize the Gallery as a studio, design lab, and performance venue to create wearable and installation-based soft sculptures from March 4 - April 6, 2024. Her residency will culminate in “I Resist This,” a new work of soft sculpture performance taking place at 7pm on Saturday, April 6. Richardson-Deppe’s work posits that soft sculpture is social practice. By stitching together bodily forms and offering them to the public as interactive performances, Richardson-Deppe facilitates community meditations on interdependence and care. Through the gallery’s glass walls, the residency will provide a literal window into Richardson-Deppe’s creative process and strengthen the fundamental role of community engagement in her practice. “I Resist This” addresses the inherent tension between independence and interdependence. Humans are fundamentally social creatures who often chafe against the social structures upon which we rely—we need other people in order to survive and thrive but we also crave freedom and independence. Through tension, weightsharing, and improvisation, performers and audience members will activate Richardson- Deppe’s wearables and soft sculptures to directly engage in the generative act of community. Artist Bio: Charlotte Richardson-Deppe is a queer feminist artist working between performance and soft sculpture. She received her MFA in Studio Art from the University of Maryland, College Park, where she teaches drawing, sculpture, and photography as a lecturer in the Department of Art. In Fall 2023 she was the Bresler Resident Artist at VisArts and the Montgomery College Collaborative Artist-in-Residence in Rockville, MD. Her solo exhibition “Unfurling” is on display at VisArts through March 17, 2024. This project was supported by the University of Maryland Department of Art Clarvit Endowed Faculty Fund in Art and Design. This exhibition and related programming is also supported in part by the Maryland State Arts Council (msac.org) and a Pepsi Grant. ABOUT THE GALLERY Located on the first floor of the Adele H. Stamp Student Union—Center for Campus Life at the University of Maryland, College Park, the Stamp Gallery is dedicated to exhibiting contemporary art, especially the work of emerging and mid-career artists. The Stamp Gallery supports contemporary art that is challenging, academically engaging, and attuned to broad community and social issues. Through meaningful exhibitions and programming, the Gallery offers outside-of-the-classroom experiential learning opportunities. It functions as a laboratory where emerging artists and curators experiment and work through their ideas. The Gallery’s programming aims to emphasize the importance of process to contemporary artistic practice and to provide a forum for dialogue. FREE and open to the public. Spring hours: Mondays–Thursdays: 10 am – 8 pm, Fridays: 10 am – 5 pm, Saturdays: 11 am – 5 pm, Sundays: Closed. More information: stamp.umd.edu/gallery.

name: En'Rage Models Practice
description: Our practice sessions are dynamic and empowering, designed to build confidence, enhance runway skills, and foster creativity in a supportive environment. Each session begins with a warm-up to prepare our models for the physical and mental demands of the runway. Models are then guided through a series of runway walks, where they practice posture, poise, and movement in a variety of styles that challenge traditional norms of fashion and modeling. Throughout the practice, we focus on perfecting choreography for upcoming shows, allowing models to develop their unique flair while staying in sync with the group’s overall performance. Our experienced runway coaches provide individual feedback to ensure that each model feels confident in expressing their own style, aligning with our mission of self-empowerment and diversity. In addition to runway practice, we also incorporate photoshoot preparation, helping models become comfortable in front of the camera, and working on their poses and expressions. Music is played to set the tone, and we regularly rotate different fashion themes to keep practices fresh and engaging. Each session concludes with a debrief, where we emphasize the importance of mutual support and encouragement, celebrating personal growth and teamwork. En'Rage Models practices are more than just rehearsals—they are an opportunity for our members to develop their self-esteem, push creative boundaries, and prepare for the high-energy experience of the runway.

description: Walk with an Arborist & Your Baby encourages new parents to connect with each other and with the outdoors in a safe space, both physically and emotionally. Registration Link: https://forms.gle/jAUt3ZJMAKfpn4T1A Parental leave and the welcoming of a new child can be lonely and stressful. By offering a tour specifically for new parents and caregivers, participants can interact as much (or as little) as they wish with other adults and have a focus in order to leave the house. According to the National Institutes of Health, one in seven women will develop postpartum depression and many others will still experience feelings of loneliness and isolation during parental leave. These symptoms can affect all genders, adoptive parents, and all caregivers, not just the birth parent. Things like cost, transportation, and child care can hinder access to alleviating symptoms. Based in the Garden of Reflection & Remembrance at the Memorial Chapel, participants learn about trees and plants while having their newborns along. Registration Link: https://forms.gle/EhzGqXnfaHEYPx1j6 Parental leave and the welcoming of a new child can be lonely and stressful. By offering a tour specifically for new parents and caregivers, participants can interact as much (or as little) as they wish with other adults and have a focus in order to leave the house. According to the National Institutes of Health, one in seven women will develop postpartum depression and many others will still experience feelings of loneliness and isolation during parental leave. These symptoms can affect all genders, adoptive parents, and all caregivers, not just the birth parent. Things like cost, transportation, and child care can hinder access to alleviating symptoms. The Arboretum aims to make the outdoors and public gardens more accessible to everyone, regardless of where they are in life's journey.

description: Join us for an album listening party to celebrate Multiracial Heritage Month through the music of Japanese Breakfast! Led by Michelle Zauner, a multiracial Korean-American artist and author of Crying in H-Mart, their music explores themes such as grief, identity, and heritage. Alongside their characteristic dreamy, ethereal indie-pop sound, we’ll come together to discuss our own relationship to multiracial identity. Come by to join our listening session and discuss the emotional experiences that define our identities through the music of Japanese Breakfast! Whether a longtime fan or new to her work, this event is a space for us to connect and celebrate how we creatively express our narratives. Enjoy an immersive listening session, followed by a discussion on how music can reflect and affirm cultural identity. Whether you’re a longtime fan or new to her work, this event is a space to connect, reflect, and celebrate diverse narratives.

name: En'Rage Models Practice
description: Our practice sessions are dynamic and empowering, designed to build confidence, enhance runway skills, and foster creativity in a supportive environment. Each session begins with a warm-up to prepare our models for the physical and mental demands of the runway. Models are then guided through a series of runway walks, where they practice posture, poise, and movement in a variety of styles that challenge traditional norms of fashion and modeling. Throughout the practice, we focus on perfecting choreography for upcoming shows, allowing models to develop their unique flair while staying in sync with the group’s overall performance. Our experienced runway coaches provide individual feedback to ensure that each model feels confident in expressing their own style, aligning with our mission of self-empowerment and diversity. In addition to runway practice, we also incorporate photoshoot preparation, helping models become comfortable in front of the camera, and working on their poses and expressions. Music is played to set the tone, and we regularly rotate different fashion themes to keep practices fresh and engaging. Each session concludes with a debrief, where we emphasize the importance of mutual support and encouragement, celebrating personal growth and teamwork. En'Rage Models practices are more than just rehearsals—they are an opportunity for our members to develop their self-esteem, push creative boundaries, and prepare for the high-energy experience of the runway.

name: NCC x FFN presents: "A European History of the Sauna Route"
description: To celebrate National Sauna Week this year, we will be joining a webinar held by Finlandia Foundation National that focuses on the history of sauna culture in Europe. Sauna culture is very important to some Nordic countries, especially Finland, so this webinar would be great for anyone interested in Nordic culture and how sauna culture spread and mutated throughout Europe. The speaker is Saija Silen, a native Finn that runs a sauna village in Jämsä, Finland. This village is part of the "Sauna Route" mentioned in the title, and Saija aims to explain this route more and trace it's history, telling us "it's not just a Finnish thing!" description: UPDATE: Over $400 in prizes announced for this competition! 1st place - $200* 2nd place - $100* 3rd place - $75* Random level 2 participant (Quadcopter)The New Hubsan X4 H107L Improved Version Random level 1 participant Hacking: The Art of Exploitation, 2nd Edition * Cash prizes will be either AMEX/Visa or Amazon Gift Cards Two prizes will be randomly given to players. Booz Allen is excited to announce: Kaizen, a Capture the Flag event designed to build the skills of information security professionals through hands-on, interactive hacking challenges. Kaizen was built to challenge participants of all skill levels; so, if you're experienced and want to sharpen your skills or if you're new to information security and want a healthy environment to learn then come check out Kaizen. Participants are immersed into an educational and competitive environment where continuous/on-the-fly learning is rewarded. Kaizen: Japanese word/philosophy for Continuous Learning/Improvement of skills and self, which we feels accurately describes our participants and our mindset. The Challenge: Kaizen is split into two separate levels with a variety of challenges ranging from network administration to web exploitation to binary reverse engineering. Participants work their way through solving real world information security challenges and submit challenge flags to a scoring server for points. The Kaizen scoring server also provides a leader board that tracks your score as you capture and submit challenge flags. With a laid back, educational atmosphere, you are sure to have a good time, learn something new, and possibly win prizes!

With modern technology and tools, it’s now possible for junior security analysts to gather detailed malware indicators to craft defense and alert signatures. More enticing, all of this can be done with free tools and applications, some written by this presenter. When not managing corporate intrusion responses, Brian is an intrusions analyst and malware reverse engineer for the Defense Computer Forensics Laboratory, part of the Defense Cyber Crime Center. For over 10 years Brian has worked to research, develop, and train forensic responses to growing network threats. Brian devotes much of his time to researching evolving Internet crimes, network protocol analysis, and Linux and UNIX intrusion responses. He has authored numerous books on computer security and developed software to allow for more efficient intrusion and malware analysis.

name: Work with At-Risk Kids: Change Your life!
description: We're gearing up for the best program year yet at the St. Francis Neighborhood Center and we're looking for dedicated volunteers to help in the Power Project, our free after school youth development program that serves the at-risk children of Reservoir Hill. The program starts Monday, Oct. 6 and we're looking for both tutors and program assistants to support staff and help make sure the program is fun for our kids, safe and successful. We know you're busy, but volunteering is important to you, which is why we're flexible and want to make sure your volunteer experience is the very best it can be. If you'd like to volunteer a few hours a week or a few hours a month, we'll make sure your time here is appreciated, valued and FUN! Our youth development program focuses on arts enrichment, academic support, mentoring and tutoring. Positions involve hands-on work with youth ages 5 to 13. Orientation and training are provided. Hours: Monday through Thursday from 3 to 6 pm. Skills: Experience working with children and the ability to volunteer on a regular basis. For more information, please email volunteer@stfranciscenter.org. About Us: St. Francis Neighborhood Center's mission is committed to breaking the cycles of poverty through education, inspiring self-esteem, self-improvement, and strengthening connections. We provide free academic and arts-based learning programs to community children in addition to mentoring, tutoring and meals.

name: Cyber Security Club GBM/Hackerspace
description: Every week we'll be having a general body meeting focused on a different topic in cybersecurity. These are a great chance to learn a new skill and get some hands-on experience. We'll have different challenges each week based around different skills. Members of all experience levels are welcome to join! Stop by, have some pizza (first come first serve), and learn a new skill or tool that you can add to your resume. We encourage everyone to participate and ask questions. description: What: Workshop on using low-cost, real-time air quality monitors for environmental justice When: Monday, April 8th (6:15PM - 8:00 PM) Where: School of Public Health Building, MIAEH Conference Room (2234CC) Many Maryland communities are threatened by high levels of air pollution and residents know they're breathing toxic air, but regulators and policymakers want proof. Join us for a workshop on using low-cost, real-time sensors to get communities the data they need. name: Camp PALS Volunteer opportunity
description: Volunteer to be a Counselor for the PALS program Camp PALS this summer. PALS is a nonprofit organization that provides one week long summer camp opportunities for teens and young adults with Down syndrome and their peers at 14 college campuses across the country. This is a one-week experience from 9am-5pm. Listed below are some details about Camp PALS: Here are some details about Camp PALS: - They offer 14 week long sleep-away camps across the country, including Camp PALS Georgetown, Chicago, and North Carolina! - Volunteer counselors are paired one-to-one with a camper to provide an opportunity to build -meaningful friendships through trips and activities - Looking for volunteers ages 16-30 who are welcoming, genuine, passionate, supportive, and fun which are all the values of the program. - No experience with Down syndrome or the disability community is necessary! They encourage groups of applicants to apply together to share the camp experience. If you are interested please visit the website at palsprograms.org/volunteer or check out their social media pages on Facebook or YouTube channel to get a look at what the PALS experience is like. PALS is an amazing opportunity to give back to the community, gain invaluable leadership skills, and make friends that will last a lifetime! There are no costs for volunteers at PALS, and applicants can apply for travel costs to be covered as well. We are looking for male applicants at this point in our season. Females are welcome to apply but will likely be placed on a waitlist. The dates for each of our 15 camps is different based on their locations, but the dates for Baltimore are July 7-13 at UMBC, and Georgetown is July 28-August 3 at Georgetown University.

name: Connected Diaspora: Opening Reception and Artist Talk
description: Connected Diaspora: Central American Visuality in the Age of Social Media casts light on a new generation of artists who visually reflect on U.S Central American lives and experiences in the era of social media. These new voices from the Central American diaspora have built a creative community that transcends state lines and borders. Their practices range from delicate ceramic sculptures to large scale paintings to digital art—exploring images of displacement, war, and trauma. Contemplations on everyday life, nature, and architecture, coupled with insights on invisibility and empowerment, are all manifested in this visual assembly. Central Americans make up the third largest U.S Latinx group—a statistic that is not equally reflected when referencing Latinx art. Beyond news articles, Central Americans in the diaspora are a creative force leading the way to a more expansive discourse on Latinx Art. Curated by Verónica Melendez Co-sponsored by the School of Languages, Literatures, and Cultures, the Department of Spanish and Portuguese at UMD, as well as La Casa de la Cultura de El Salvador in Washington, DC Event image: Xiomara Garay, Latina. Jigsaw Woodcut, 2017

name: Tortured Logic: Why Some Americans Support the Use of Torture in Counterterrorism
description: On Friday, September 18 at 12:00 p.m. ET, University of Alabama Assistant Professor Dr. Erin M. Kearns and American University Professor Dr. Joseph K. Young will provide a virtual talk on their new book “Tortured Logic: Why Some Americans Support the Use of Torture in Counterterrorism.” This event is free and open to the public, but RSVPs are required. If you have any questions, please email the START events team at start-events@umd.edu. Experts in the intelligence community say that torture is ineffec­tive. Yet much of the public appears unconvinced: surveys show that nearly half of Americans think that torture can be acceptable for counterterrorism purposes. Why do people persist in supporting torture—and can they be persuaded to change their minds? In Tortured Logic, Erin M. Kearns and Joseph K. Young draw upon a novel series of group experiments to understand how and why the average citizen might come to support the use of torture tech­niques. They find evidence that when torture is depicted as effective in the media, people are more likely to approve of it. Their analysis weighs variables such as the ethnicity of the interrogator and the suspect; the salience of one’s own mortality; and framing by experts. Kearns and Young also examine who changes their opinions about torture and how, demonstrating that only some individuals have fixed views while others have more malleable beliefs. They argue that efforts to reduce support for torture should focus on convinc­ing those with fluid views that torture is ineffective. The book fea­tures interviews with experienced interrogators and professionals working in the field to contextualize its findings. Bringing empirical rigor to a fraught topic, Tortured Logic has important implications for understanding public perceptions of counterterrorism strategy. Dr. Erin M. Kearns’ areas of expertise include how media depict terrorism and counterterrorism and the influence this how on public perceptions; community-police relations particularly in counterterrorism; strategic communication decisions among groups that use terrorism; and, factors that increase support for violent and non-violent political action. She has a number of publications on each of these issues. Dr. Kearns’ work has been funded through a number of sources, including the National Consortium for the Study of and Responses to Terrorism (START). Her work has been featured on numerous media outlets including CNN, The Economist, NPR, the Washington Post, and Vox. She serves on the editorial boards of Studies in Conflict and Terrorism and Dynamics of Asymmetric Conflict and on the advisory board for the Terrorism Prosecution Project. She has also served as a consultant for the Police Foundation and the Department of Justice’s Office of Community Oriented Policing. Professor Joseph K. Young's interests relate to the cross-national causes and consequences of political violence. He has published numerous peer-reviewed articles across academic disciplines, including political science, economics, criminology, and international studies. He has been invited to speak to organizations in the defense community and has consulted on a Department of Defense initiative focusing on countering violent extremism. The National Science Foundation and the National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) have funded his research. More information on Professor Young can be found on his professional website.

name: US-Venezuela Defense Relations
description: On Friday, October 8 at 2:00 p.m. ET, William J. Perry Center for Hemispheric Defense Studies Assistant Professor Dr. Fabiana Perera will provide a virtual talk on “US-Venezuela Defense Relations.” This event is free and open to the public, but RSVPs are required. If you have any questions, please email the START events team at start-events@umd.edu. Dr. Fabiana Perera is an Assistant Professor at the William J. Perry Center for Hemispheric Defense Studies. Prior to joining the Perry Center, Fabiana was a Rosenthal Fellow at the Office of the Secretary of Defense, Under Secretary for Policy, Western Hemisphere Affairs. Fabiana has experience working in the public and private sectors. She worked as a research associate at Mitsubishi International Corporation focusing on Latin America and the energy and infrastructure sectors. She also has experience serving at the Department of Veterans Affairs and the US Agency for International Development (USAID). Fabiana holds an MA in Latin American Studies from Georgetown University and earned a PhD in Political Science from The George Washington University. For her doctorate, Fabiana completed fieldwork in Venezuela and Ecuador. Fabiana has presented her research at the annual meetings of the American Political Science Association and the Latin American Studies Association. Her research and analysis have appeared in numerous publications including The Washington Post, CNN.com, and War on the Rocks. Her research and has been supported by numerous organizations including Columbia University's Women in Energy program and George Washington University's Center for International Business Education.

name: ASHRAE Seminar w Gordon Sharp on March 1st
description: Gordon Sharp Founder and Chairman of Aircuity, Inc. Founder, Former President and CEO of Phoenix Controls New Approaches to Slash Lab and Commercial Building Energy Use and Improve IEQ Wednesday, March 1st | 12:30PM DeWalt Seminar Room #2164 | Glenn L. Martin Hall #88 Bio: Gordon Sharp is the chairman of Aircuity, Inc. and has over 25 years of wide-ranging entrepreneurial experience and more than 25 U.S. patents in the fields of energy efficiency and laboratory controls. As founder, former president and CEO of Phoenix Controls, he led the development of this world leader in laboratory airflow controls that was acquired by Honeywell in 1998. The technologies invented by Mr. Sharp at Phoenix Controls are today saving over $1.5 billion annually in energy use. In 2000, Gordon founded Aircuity, which was spun out of Honeywell and is a smart airside energy efficiency company. Gordon is a graduate of MIT with bachelors and masters degrees in electrical engineering. He is also Executive Vice President and a member of the board of directors of I2SL (International Institute for Sustainable Laboratories), the nonprofit foundation that operates the former Labs21 conference and has numerous chapters around the US and globally. He has also testified before the US Congress on the topics of climate change and energy efficiency. Abstract: In the face of significant energy costs and concerns over global warming, buildings are receiving increasing scrutiny to reduce their carbon footprint and cut their energy expenses. For many buildings outside air is the largest single driver of both energy efficiency and indoor environmental quality. Demand control ventilation has attempted to reduce energy expenses by controlling outside air but the actual results over time have been mixed at best. This talk will discuss and provide case studies of both commercial and laboratory buildings for a more energy efficient and healthier variation on demand control ventilation that uses a new, cost effective, and more accurate sensing approach known as multiplexed sensing.
location: DeWalt Seminar Room #2164 | Glenn L. Martin Hall #88

name: Teach a child to dream.  Become a FLOC tutor.
description: More than 50% of DC students are not proficient in math, and nearly 50% lack proficiency in reading. YOU can change that! FLOC is currently recruiting volunteer tutors for the 2015-2016 school year. Our one-on-one tutoring program helps students achieve grade-level competency in reading and math. On average, students improve 1 year in reading or math competency after just 3 and a half months of consistent tutoring, while also gaining confidence in their abilities. We need your help! Each new volunteer allows us to impact the life of one more child. Training and ongoing professional support from staff are provided, so no experience is necessary! However, we are looking for a few particular qualities from our tutors: Patience Creativity and flexibility A sense of humor! Fluency in the English language. (Volunteers who are not native speakers of American English may be asked to tutor only in our math curriculum.) At least 16 years old Able and willing to commit 2.5 hours once a week for the full school year. We hope to make the best possible matches for each of our students and therefore seek a diverse pool of volunteer tutors. We especially encourage volunteers who are male, people of color, and/or first-generation college graduates to join us. Programs are offered on weekday afternoons, weekday evenings, and Saturdays, and at sites in Adams Morgan, Anacostia, Congress Heights, Eastern Market, and Dupont Circle. How to Apply: Complete a volunteer application at www.floc.org/get-involved/volunteer. If you have questions, please contact Elizabeth Metz, Recruitment and Outreach Manager, at emetz@floc.org or 202-349-3512. Or follow us on Twitter (@FLOC_DC) or Facebook (/forloveofchildren) to get updates on volunteer needs and deadlines.

name: Veteran Adventure Orientation
description: This adventure experience is designed exclusively for new veterans. Spend the first day on the ropes course on campus and the next two days navigating Wye Island on the Eastern Chesapeake Bay. While on your trip you will be exposed to basic outdoor skills such as kayaking, camping techniques, and outdoor cooking. In addition to outdoor skills, you will learn about group dynamics, leadership, and decision-making; all of which will help you in your future adventures as a Maryland student. During the trip, you will learn about campus resources available to veterans. Additionally time will be set aside to answer any questions you might have about the University of Maryland. This experience is unique and different from any other you may have as a college student, and it will be your first opportunity to meet other veterans while also experiencing personal growth through opportunities presented in an adventure setting.

description: Want to know more about START’s Global Terrorism Studies Minor Program? Sign up to attend one of our upcoming information sessions! START has developed an undergraduate minor in Global Terrorism Studies, a cross-disciplinary program housed in the College of Behavioral and Social Sciences at the University of Maryland. The minor is designed to train the next generation of terrorism analysts, including students who plan to pursue graduate study related to terrorism as well as employment in the federal, state, local, non-profit, and/or private sectors. The program is part of the University of Maryland’s Global Studies program, alongside the minors in International Development and Conflict Management, Global Poverty, and Global Engineering Leadership. START accepts applications to the program from University of Maryland undergraduates once per calendar year, during the spring semester. Students from all colleges and majors may apply. We will be offering two info sessions this fall, the first to take place in-person on Monday, October 11th, the second virtually on Wednesday, November 3rd, 2021. The info session will be led by START’s Director of Undergraduate Studies, Dr. Thomas Guarrieri, and START's Education Coordinator, who will discuss how the Global Terrorism Studies Minor Program currently works, what students have to gain from their experience in the program, application requirements, and any other questions attendees may have. This registration is for 6-7 p.m. ET on Wednesday, November 3rd, 2021. You will receive an email by the morning of the event with detailed information on how to access the webinar in UMD's Zoom platform via a computer or phone.

name: Unpacking Anti-Blackness In Thought and Practice
organization: Office of Diversity & Inclusion (including Bias Incident Support Services & Diversity Training & Education)
description: Venmo reparations, #BlackLivesMatter yard signs, solidarity statements and black squares. The past few months have been full of everyday people grappling with and fumbling through the long overdue conversation on racism in our country, much of this conversation revolving around “anti-Blackness.” But what does it mean to understand how anti-Blackness works systemically? What does anti-Blackness look like beyond slavery and police brutality and why does it continue to persist? What role does the university play in breaking the cycle of anti-Black ideologies and practices? In the first program of the Anti-Racism Toolkit programming series, we attempt to grapple with these questions and more with scholar-activists shaping the conversation. Hosted by ODI's Diversity Training & Education team.

name: NextLOOK ft. Rachel Grossman & Tosin Olufolabi: The Gift
description: The Gift is an immersive, interactive performance that invites the audience to transition from self-reflection to action and advocacy over the course of the event. Sometime in the U.S.'s future, when most illnesses have been cured, two doctors host the first clinical trial for the societally destructive infectious agent Preston-Weche-Rhys – the source of white supremacy culture – with the audience cast as the subjects. This event is part of NextLOOK. In partnership with Joe's Movement Emporium, NextLOOK supports the development of new music, plays, dance and other experiences by regionally-based performing artists. These artists are mentored by seasoned arts administrators from The Clarice and Joe’s Movement Emporium to construct innovative methods of deepening the audience’s involvement in their creative process. By removing logistical barriers of cost and space and providing a sounding board for artists creating new work, NextLOOK invests in the regional arts ecology and creates an accessible, exploratory environment that connects intriguing artists with adventurous audiences. Made possible, in part, by the Maryland State Arts Council and the Morris & Gwendolyn Cafritz Foundation.

name: BlackLight Summit 2022
description: Returning for a second year, The Clarice’s BlackLight Summit aims to activate the unimagined possibilities in dance– a convening that re-envisions dance as a conduit to galvanize resilience and inventiveness. The 2022 summit explores three fundamental inquiries: “What/Who are we Becoming,” “How do we return to one another?” and “Progress does not equal healing, but it can.” Throughout the 2021-22 season, the BlackLight Summit will also continue community connectivity by facilitating a series of mentoring and professional development opportunities, conversations and performances. Register + learn more: go.umd.edu/blacklightsummit2022 Health + Safety There may be COVID safety policies such as mask requirements in place when you attend this event. Please see our health & safety page for the most up to date information about attendance! BlackLight Summit 2022 Artists: Baye & Asa is a company creating movement art projects directed by Amadi ‘Baye’ Washington & Sam ‘Asa’ Pratt. They grew up together in New York City and that shared educational history is the mother of their work. Through the personal dynamics of their brotherhood, they address the larger political landscape of their upbringing, struggling to show a reality of violence while communicating a necessity for empathy. Charlie Maybee is a music and dance artist from Woodbridge, VA. He holds an M.F.A. in Dance from the University of Illinois with a certificate in Criticism and Interpretive Theory, a B.F.A. from Virginia Commonwealth University and is an alumnus of the Metropolitan Youth Tap Ensemble. As an educator, Charlie is currently on faculty at Shenandoah University where he primarily teaches tap dance technique, choreography, history and improvisation. Johnnie Cruise Mercer Recently acknowledged as a 2021 Princess Grace Award Recipent in Choreograpy, and nominated for two 2021 Bessie Awards in Dance and Performance, Johnnie Cruise Mercer is a queer-black think-maker, freelance-performer, educator and social entrepreneur based in New York City. A native of Richmond, VA, Mercer holds a BFA in Dance and Choreography from Virginia Commonwealth University. As the Company Director of Johnnie Cruise Mercer/TheREDprojectNYC, his processes/work has been shared and/or hosted by 92Y Harkness Dance Center, Gibney: Agnes Varis Performing Arts Center, Dixon Place, Danspace Project Inc, The Fusebox Festival, Mana Contemporary, The NADA Conference, Abrons Arts Center and most recently at The Clarice Performing Arts Center's BlackLight Summit. As an educator, Mercer facilitates within the New York Public School system through The Leadership Program-a mentorship-based organization that uses art to foster/engage restorative justice and motivate the true empowerment of self. Mercer has also been on teaching faculty/a guest artist at The American Dance Festival, Bates Dance Festival, PRATT Institute, NYU Tisch Dance Program, Gibney, University of Massachusetts Amherst, DeSales University, Muhlenberg College, the University of Texas at Austin, University of Maryland and The Dance Institute of Washington. Mercer was most recently a 2019-2021 Artist in Residence at Brooklyn Arts Exchange, a 2020-2021 Ping Chong and Company Creative Fellow and a 2020-2021 AIR through New Dance Alliance’s Black Artists Space to Create Residency curated by Angie Pittman. He is currently a 2022 Artist in Residence at Center for Performance Research. Greg David is a movement artist based in the DMV area. Exploring themes of grief, fear, care and solitude, the work and movement they enjoy making goes hand in hand with human emotion and experience and aims to capture that essence in motion. David joinedCulture Shock Washington DC® in 2012 and became the Artistic Director for their 2015 and 2016 seasons where, nationally and internationally, they presented stage works and taught workshops. Kayla Farrish/Decent Structures Arts is an emerging company combining filmmaking, storytelling, dance theater performance and sound score. The company has been commissioned by Gibney Dance Inc (2020-2021), Louis Armstrong House Museum (2020), Danspace Project Inc (2019), Pepatian and BAAD! (2018) and beyond. Kayla has been supported by creative residencies including Gallim Women + Residency (2021), Gibney Spotlight: New Voices, Barysnikov Arts Center and Arts On Site (2020).
location: The Clarice Smith Performing Arts Center
