name: Veterans Yoga
description: Sun Salutations (8/31) Get ready for a class to introduce health and vitality into the semester! This short class includes 20 minutes of cleansing movement fit for yogis of all shapes, sizes, and experience levels. Bonus: Do you not have time to relax and let go for even just a few minutes? Your instructor includes at least five minutes of required shavasana practice at the end of each class to give the mind a break from the rest of the world. Learn a New Pose (9/2) Today’s yoga session will include 18 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out, meaning that yogis of all experience and backgrounds will benefit! Get ready to build strength and resilience with this fun-to learn movement. Relaxation Meditation (9/7) Tuesday’s session will be focused on grounding yourself in this new semester. Just fifteen minutes of passive, yet focused yoga practice will bring you into the moment and out of the stresses of the new semester. Get a Workout in (9/9) After Tuesday’s session focused on relaxation and finding ground in the new semester, it’s time to ramp up the heat. You would never believe what just twenty minutes of poses can do to get that blood pumping and the sweat pouring! Don’t worry, though! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Open the Hips (9/14) We have been in class for a couple of weeks now and our bodies need us to keep moving to stay open and ready for all that life has to offer. Twenty three minutes of opening the hips will keep them from tightening from all the stress and constant sitting motion. Don’t forget! We also include at least five minutes of time to destress and prepare for the rest of the week. Learn a New Pose (9/16) Today’s yoga session will include 24 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out. Yogis of all experience and backgrounds will benefit from this fun practice! Get ready to build some awesome abdominal strength with this sequence. Relaxation Meditation (9/21) Today’s session will be focused on grounding yourself in this new semester. Twenty six minutes of passive, yet focused yoga practice will bring you into the moment and out of the stresses of the semester’s stressors. Getting in a Workout! (9/23) After Tuesday’s session focused on relaxation and finding ground in this awesome in-person semester, it’s time to get that body moving. Just thirty three minutes of poses will get that blood pumping and the sweat pouring! Don’t worry! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Plus, we won’t leave your muscles stiff from the hard work! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for the Booty (9/28) Looking to add cushion and tone to your derriere? Who isn’t?! Today’s session will be devoted to working to add strength to the glutes and hamstrings. Twenty minutes of work will show you some tips and tools to build your important muscle groups that keep your body healthy and moving! Learn a New Pose (9/30) Today’s yoga session will include 25 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out! Even the simplest of poses require detail-orientation! Get ready to build strength and resilience in simple poses. Relaxation Meditation (10/5) Tuesday’s session will be focused on staying sane as the semester continues to pose more difficulties. This is a time for you to take 26 minutes to treat yourself to reduce stress and a little self-care. Get a Workout In (10/7) After Tuesday’s session focused on relaxation and de-stressing, it’s time to move the mind, body, and spirit. Just 34 minutes of yoga flow will get that blood pumping! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in and focused throughout the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Plus, we won’t leave your muscles stiff from the hard work! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for Weak and Tight Shoulders (10/12) We get it. Being an athlete, veteran, human, parent, student, etc. comes with a price. Usually that price is paid in the body. Today we are going to focus on restoring weak and/or tight shoulders. Don’t shy away from class out of fear of injury! There are modifications for all flexibility levels in the shoulders. We are working to improve, not perfect! After all, we only have twenty six minutes! Learn a New Pose (10/14) Today’s yoga session will include 34 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out! Poses that seem difficult from the outside may be a bit simpler than you anticipate! We are focused on safety in strength. So first, we will build strength and confidence. Then we will build upon simple poses to create a beautiful movement to feel proud about. Relaxation Meditation (10/19) We are mid-semester. While it feels like this is the time to be working your butt off with as few breaks as possible, don’t forget about the importance of daily self-care. Today’s class will be nineteen minutes focused on nothing but bringing you back to yourself. This is a time to reclaim the best parts of yourself and create the person you want to be with focused intention. Get a Workout In (10/21) Tuesday got us mentally focused for the week, so now it is time to ramp up the energy to end the week strong! Thirty-one minutes of yoga flow will get that blood pumping! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in and focused. Don’t forget a towel! We will leave your muscles feeling worked, but not too stiff! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for Back Pain (10/26) Is your back constantly feeling stiff? Is the lower back achy and shoulder blades tight? Come to today’s yoga session for the opportunity to release some of that stiffness, and open yourself up to a world of relief! You might be surprised at what a short 33 minutes of stretching and strengthening can do for the body. Learn a New Pose (10/28) Ready to expand your yoga knowledge and experience? Today’s class will revolve around learning a yoga pose through-and-through. There is no reason to worry about the experience level needed for the pose, as all poses learned and performed here can be done at any level! Set aside 33 minutes and get mentally ready to learn reverse warrior so we can add it to your yoga repertoire! Relaxation Meditation (11/2) Meditating on a regular basis has positive effects on the body and mind, such as greater sense of focus, muscle relaxation, and increased creativity. Today’s meditation will be focused on gratitude and increasing happiness. Giving thanks can come in many forms, but have you tried it in the form of meditation?! Getting in a Workout! (11/4) After Tuesday’s session focused on gratitude in this challenging semester, it’s time to get that body moving. Just 34 minutes of sweat-inducing poses will get that blood pumping! This class is fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Plus, we won’t leave your muscles stiff from the hard work! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for a Better Mood (11/9) College is demanding, stressful, and can induce negative feelings! Combat those real-time stresses by moving the body and bonding with fellow veterans. Coming to this thirty minute vinyasa class will open the heart to the positivity you need to get you to the end of the semester. Learn a New Pose (11/11) Ready to expand your yoga knowledge and experience? Today’s class will revolve around learning a yoga pose through-and-through. There is no reason to worry about the experience level needed for the pose, as all poses learned and performed here can be done at any level! Set aside 35 minutes and get mentally ready to learn a new pose to add to your yoga repertoire! Relaxation Meditation (11/16) Today’s meditation practice will be short, sweet, and perfect to regain focus on your workflow. As we near the end of the semester, stress increases, the mind wanders, and we lose focus. We will be going through meditation techniques that can be utilized at home, work, or on the bus. Don’t underestimate the power of this 26 minute session. Come join your fellow veterans and enjoy the feeling of a clear mind. Get a Workout In (11/18) After Tuesday’s session focused on de-stressing and refocusing, it’s time to move that body. Just 34 minutes of yoga flow will get that blood pumping! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in and focused throughout the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Plus, we won’t leave your muscles stiff from the hard work! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for Neck Pain (11/23) After months of looking down at our computer screens, it’s no wonder so many of us have the amount of pain in our necks that we do! Today’s class will be all about de-stressing, communication, and releasing the tension in the neck through yoga practice. Set aside 31 minutes for this perfectly-paced practice.

name: NextLOOK ft. Sinclair Ogaga Emoghene, Pablo Regis & Kate Spanos: Performing Otherness (Ainihi e Alteridade)
description: This new dance and music project examines ainihi (“identity” in Hausa) and alteridade (“otherness” in Portuguese) based on the traditions of Nigeria and Brazil. Multidisciplinary artists Sinclair Ogaga Emoghene, Pablo Regis and Kate Spanos collaborate to look for both universality and cultural specificity in shared movements and rhythms. This work includes new and traditional songs and dances, a carnival-style parade, an audience feedback session and an artist discussion. This event is part of NextLOOK. In partnership with Joe's Movement Emporium, NextLOOK supports the development of new music, plays, dance and other experiences by regionally-based performing artists. These artists are mentored by seasoned arts administrators from The Clarice and Joe’s Movement Emporium to construct innovative methods of deepening the audience’s involvement in their creative process. By removing logistical barriers of cost and space and providing a sounding board for artists creating new work, NextLOOK invests in the regional arts ecology and creates an accessible, exploratory environment that connects intriguing artists with adventurous audiences. Made possible, in part, by the Maryland State Arts Council and the Morris & Gwendolyn Cafritz Foundation.

name: Sarah Hennies, Terry Berlier & The Living Earth Show: A Kind of Ache (USA)
description: A Kind of Ache is a multimedia installation and concert from composer Sarah Hennies, sculptor and conceptual artist Terry Berlier and electroacoustic duo The Living Earth Show (Andy Meyerson and Travis Andrews) that reimagines a world designed from and for a queer identity. The drums-and-guitar duo will play Hennies’ score on Berlier’s sculptures, using objects, music and their imaginations to wonder “What would it feel like to be the majority?” The Living Earth Show supports the next generation of artistic thinkers throughout their work. During the 2020-21 season and throughout the pandemic, they worked closely with UMD School of Music students in the creation of Music for Hard Times. The eight-week virtual project featured 70 UMD Wind Orchestra students in an open source composition that can never be replicated. During their 2021-22 residency at The Clarice, The Living Earth Show will continue to collaborate with UMD students in the making of a safe artistic space for queer-identifying individuals. They will host an Arts Citizenship Talk (ACTnow) and share their creative process with audiences. Health + Safety There may be COVID safety policies such as mask requirements in place when you attend this event. Please see our health & safety page for the most up to date information about attendance!

name: Intro to AR Development (Part I - Sensing the Environment)
description: Movies like Iron Man, Terminator, and Black Panther have long depicted the power of augmented reality. You may have even experienced it for yourself, with apps like Pokemon Go and Snapchat filters. But what if you wanted to make your own AR experience? Surely it must be way too complex for a beginner college student to handle! Wrong! Join the XR Club this Tuesday as we show you just how easy it is to build your own smartphone AR experience from scratch! We'll be using the new Unity XR Tech Stack, starting with Unity's AR Foundation, a multi-platform framework that connects you to the core underlying capabilities of both smartphone- and headset-based AR platforms. In the first part of this workshop series, you'll learn how to get the camera stream to show up in your applciation, how to track and visualize features of the environment, like planes and point clouds, and how to deploy an AR application to your phone. No prior experience necessary; all majors welcome!

name: Community Shabbat Dinner for Adar!
description: There is a mitzvah (Jewish commandment) to eat 3 meals with a blessing over grape juice and Challah (bread) over the course of Shabbat. As such, a huge part of our community observance of the Shabbat is coming together for meals on Friday night. Traditionally, students eat these meals in apartments with friends. A few times a semester, we gather together as an entire community to eat, share words of Torah, and sing Jewish songs together at the Maryland Hillel. There is a mandate from our Rabbis that when entering the month of Adar (the 6th month on the Jewish calendar), we should increase our happiness in preparation for the celebration of the holiday Purim, which happens on the 14th day of that month of Adar. To observe this increase in happiness, Jews have the tradition of dressing in costumes, playing pranks, singing, and acting in a more playful and silly manner starting from the new month through the Purim holiday. In observance of this obligation to increase in happiness, we will be hosting a fun, community wide Friday night dinner with Minute to Win It style competition games. This dinner will be on Friday night, February 18, 2022, which is during the month of Adar, at Maryland Hillel. During the dinner, we will be playing games such as cup stacking, throwing ping pong balls into buckets on people's heads, using straws to move jelly beans from bowl to bowl and more.

name: Van Gogh Exhibit: The Immersive Experience
description: https://youtu.be/ib34WI0H4qI Have you ever dreamt of stepping into a painting? Here is your chance, join the XR Club on Friday, November 11th as we visit the Van Gogh: The Immersive Experience, an exhibition in Washington DC that reinvents the concept of museums. Step into a 20,000 sq. ft. light and sound spectacular exhibit featuring two-story projections of the artist's most compelling works. Once you’re done, you’ll have the chance to try on a virtual reality experience, where you can walk alongside Van Gogh during a visually rich journey into the inspiration behind 8 of his most popular works, including Vincent’s Bedroom at Arles & Starry Night Over The Rhone. This exhibit was deemed the best immersive experience of 2021 by USA Today and ranked among the 12 best immersive experiences in the world by CNN. Eligibility Requirements:All attendees of this program must be undergraduate students who are members of the XR Club, as listed on our TerpLink roster. Overall, however, this workshop will focus on behavioral-based interviewing tips.2. What to know about an employer and the position before stepping foot into the interview or joining that Zoom call.3. How to think through and articulate your “power stories” - the stories you anticipate will come up in an interview and how to share that story in a way an outsider (i.e. the interviewer) will understand and appreciate.4. Additional ways to prepare for upcoming interviews.This workshop will be conducted virtually on a monthly basis through the University Career Center & The President's Promise. If this date doesn’t work for you, check out Handshake for future offerings. In addition to this workshop, students have access to Big Interview in Handshake to practice interview questions on your own time. You may also schedule a mock interview with a career advisor in Handshake through a career advising appointment. REGISTER HERE

The Beekeeping Club does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, religion, age, or physical ability. The Mission of The Beekeeping Club is to educate students about bees and beekeeping through hands-on experience and lectures, about harvesting raw products from them in sustainable ways, and about turning those raw products a variety of goods. name: National Hillel Basketball Tournament 2025
description: The National Hillel Basketball Tournament (NHBT) was founded in 2010 to bring Jewish students together around the inclusive and encompassing game of basketball. Solely organized by a board of 30 highly motivated students, what began as a small event has quickly developed into one of the largest collegiate gatherings of Jewish students in the country. Now in its 13th year, the non-profit initiative, annually housed in the University of Maryland’s state-of-the-art facilities, attracts over 1,500 participants from across the United States and Canada. This year, we expect over 50 teams from over 30 universities across North America to partake in the weekend-long tournament experience. Players and fans also participate in various off-the-court programs such as Shabbat meals, keynote speakers, and an exciting bar night to kick the weekend off. In addition to NHBT’s impressive scale and reach, its impact has reached new heights in recent years. By providing students a chance to meet, socialize, and compete in a positive Jewish environment, NHBT serves as an oasis for students experiencing antisemitism on their respective campuses. By platforming like-minded organizations and starting initiatives, NHBT has provided a beacon of hope and togetherness for Jewish and campus communities far and wide.

name: En'Rage Models Practice
description: Our practice sessions are dynamic and empowering, designed to build confidence, enhance runway skills, and foster creativity in a supportive environment. Each session begins with a warm-up to prepare our models for the physical and mental demands of the runway. Models are then guided through a series of runway walks, where they practice posture, poise, and movement in a variety of styles that challenge traditional norms of fashion and modeling. Throughout the practice, we focus on perfecting choreography for upcoming shows, allowing models to develop their unique flair while staying in sync with the group’s overall performance. Our experienced runway coaches provide individual feedback to ensure that each model feels confident in expressing their own style, aligning with our mission of self-empowerment and diversity. In addition to runway practice, we also incorporate photoshoot preparation, helping models become comfortable in front of the camera, and working on their poses and expressions. Music is played to set the tone, and we regularly rotate different fashion themes to keep practices fresh and engaging. Each session concludes with a debrief, where we emphasize the importance of mutual support and encouragement, celebrating personal growth and teamwork. En'Rage Models practices are more than just rehearsals—they are an opportunity for our members to develop their self-esteem, push creative boundaries, and prepare for the high-energy experience of the runway.

name: Yuri Kochiyama High School Leadership Program 2024

Each week, YK participants will come together to learn about Asian American history, identity, and leadership through intersectional community building. YKLP will end with an End-of-Program Celebration on April 13. The hybrid schedule is as follows: WEEK ONE (2/17): in-person WEEK TWO (2/24) : online WEEK THREE (3/02): in-person WEEK FOUR (3/09): online WEEK FIVE (3/16): in-person Graduation (4/13): in-person We hope to raise awareness about Asian Pacific Islander Desi American (APIDA) issues that matter to community members, highlighting APIDA experiences and engaging with each other to better integrate intersectional concepts within our daily lives. YKLP is open to all public high school students within the DMV who are of BIPOC-identifying background to facilitate inter-community building and learning.

name: Veteran Lifelong Leadership with Warrior Canine Connection (For Veterans and Civilians)
description: Veteran Lifelong Leadership with Warrior Canine Connection (For Veterans and Civilians) Did you know that learning how to train a service dog also provides a surprising opportunity to learn and practice a host of leadership skills. When you have a new teammate, subordinate, or supervisor how do you effectively work with them for a mutual goal. How do you communicate, create common ground, assess their personality, strengths, challenges, and learning styles? What inspires them? Dog training skills require just that. First and most importantly, we must create a bond between the trainee and the trainer. This promotes effective communication and focus, thus the ability to understand the dog’s body language, personality, and learn to work within the parameters of their individuality. Dogs, like humans, will challenge and question our leadership to reassure their confidence in our abilities and that they are seen and heard. Good leaders and teams need to be challenged to evolve and grow. We meet the dogs where they are, and they do the same with us. In training we set our dogs up for success, by starting small, learning in manageable increments “bit by bit”, and celebrating our wins. With consistency, the dog is able to anticipate, think, and draw conclusions. In the BASICS of dog training, you will learn about connection, timing, leading, coaching, and rewarding. Good leadership is intrinsic to these BASIC qualities. description: The Stamp Gallery invites you to join the reception for Lights Off at 8 pm, a group exhibition featuring artists that approach memory as inherently fluid and ever-shifting, capable of evoking different emotions—love, grief, joy, anxiety, fear—at once and across time. Stamp Student Union—Center for Campus Life at the University of Maryland, College Park, the Stamp Gallery is dedicated to exhibiting contemporary art, especially the work of emerging and mid-career artists. The Stamp Gallery supports contemporary art that is challenging, academically engaging, and attuned to broad community and social issues. Through meaningful exhibitions and programming, the Gallery offers outside-of-the-classroom experiential learning opportunities. It functions as a laboratory where emerging artists and curators experiment and work through their ideas. The Gallery’s programming aims to emphasize the importance of process to contemporary artistic practice and to provide a forum for dialogue. FREE and open to the public. name: Commuter Small Group
description: The Commuter Small Group is a welcoming community designed specifically for students who commute to campus. We recognize that commuter students often face unique challenges—such as limited time on campus, balancing home and school responsibilities, and difficulty finding consistent community. This small group creates space for commuters to connect, build friendships, and grow spiritually together in a supportive environment. Each week, the group gathers for a time of conversation, Bible study, and prayer, with a focus on exploring how faith intersects with daily life as a commuter student. Meetings are scheduled at accessible times to fit around commuting schedules and often include shared meals or snacks to foster fellowship. The goal of the Commuter Small Group is to provide a consistent community where students can be known, encouraged, and equipped to live out their faith both on campus and at home. Whether it’s offering a place to rest between classes or a group of friends to journey with through college, this small group helps commuters feel rooted and connected as part of the larger campus community.

name: STEM Queer Alumni Panel
organization: University Career Center & The Presidents Promise
description: Hear from LGBTQ+ alumni from UMD’s Clark School of Engineering and CMNS as they share their journeys in STEM, insights on building inclusive workplaces, and advice for current students. Open to all students, alumni, and allies. Alumni Speakers: Allison Li Class of 2025 · Information Science and Criminology-Criminal Justice Allison Li (any pronouns) is a bicultural Gen Z strategist and storyteller with a passion for the intersection of business, law, and technology. They hold dual degrees in Information Science and Criminology & Criminal Justice. With professional experience in data analysis, policy research, and venture strategy, Allison is committed to driving social impact through technology and equitable policy—especially for underrepresented communities. Allison formerly served as oSTEM’s Chapter President. Alex Ramos Medical Assistant · Anne Arundel Dermatology Class of 2022 · Bioengineering Alex Ramos (he/him/his) is a 2022 graduate of the University of Maryland, where he earned a B.S. in Bioengineering from the A. James Clark School of Engineering. Since graduation, he has held roles as an associate consultant at Veeva Systems Inc. and as a medical scribe at Montgomery Cardiology, LLC. He currently works as a Medical Assistant at Anne Arundel Dermatology in Rockville, Maryland. Marsh Hessler Post-Baccalaureate Researcher · National Eye Institute of the National Institutes of Health (NIH) Class of 2025 · Bioengineering Marsh Hessler (they/them) earned a B.S. in Bioengineering from the University of Maryland in Spring 2025. They are currently working as a wet lab post-baccalaureate researcher at the National Eye Institute of the National Institutes of Health (NIH), where they specialize in creating 3D in vitro retinal models. Tim White Engineer · Norfolk Naval Shipyard Class of 2025 · Electrical Engineering Tim White, a U.S. Army veteran, served ten years on active duty as a Health Care Specialist. His military service took him to Afghanistan, Germany, and Korea. His B.S. is in Electrical Engineering with a minor in Chinese. Deeply interested in the modernization of the electrical grid and climate change mitigation, he hopes to contribute to innovative energy infrastructure solutions. Tim actively advocates for expanding access to STEM education and fostering inclusive learning environments. Tytan Taliaferro Software Engineer · The Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory Class of 2021 · Computer Science Tytan Taliaferro manages complex software development projects at JHU-APL., including data visualization tools, mobile and web applications, and systems that translate operator needs into actionable technology. He's currently pursuing an MS in Engineering Management. He has served as co-president of the African American Culture Club and is a member of Allies in the Workplace, championing diversity and inclusion. He has received multiple awards in technical development and team collaboration. Marlon Cruz Class of 2024, Fire Protection Engineering Marlon Cruz currently serves as a Fire Engineer Consultant at Arup US. In addition to his engineering work, Cruz is a passionate community advocate, serving as the Community/Latino Liaison to Prince George’s County Council Member Jolene Ivey. A first-generation college graduate and the son of immigrants, he proudly identifies as Latino and has deep roots in both Guatemala—where he lived for seven years—and PG County, MD, where he attended public schools. His professional and volunteer work across political campaigns, non-profit outreach, the U.S. Census, and COVID-19 vaccine access has taught him the importance of meeting communities where they are. His strategy focuses on making politics and resources accessible and relevant, particularly within Latino neighborhoods.

name: SHAC Campus Health and Wellness Tabling Series
description: The SHAC Campus Health and Wellness Tabling Series is a weekly outreach initiative designed to strengthen student engagement with the University Health Center (UHC). Each week, a SHAC subcommittee—Preventive & Primary Care, Mental & Behavioral Health, Sexual & Reproductive Health, QMIT, or DEI—hosts a themed table in a central campus location. Tabling includes a feedback prompt, educational materials, interactive elements (e.g., surveys or QR codes), and wellness giveaways to encourage participation. The purpose of the series is to raise awareness of campus health resources, gather real-time student feedback, and offer approachable, consistent wellness engagement. It replaces larger, infrequent events with manageable, student-led outreach that better reflects student needs. This initiative supports SHAC’s mission to advise UHC, improve transparency, and promote student-centered health programming on campus.

name: Guest Speaker: Rabbi Yitzchak Breitowitz
description: At Kedma, we seek to provide the community at UMD with unique opportunities for Jewish education and spirituality. We are able to explore our deep connection to our culture and roots through the learning of Jewish texts. To help with this goal, we would like to host Rabbi Yitzcahk Breitowitz for a Torah lecture via Zoom to teach and inspire our organization to become better Torah scholars, as well as improve our character as people. Rabbi Dr. Yitzchak Breitowitz's scope of knowledge, brilliance, as well as a unique ability to grasp complicated material and communicate it clearly to others is legendary. Rabbi Breitowitz received his bachelor of arts from Johns Hopkins University and obtained semicha from Ner Israel Rabbinical College. He graduated magna cum laude from Harvard Law School and shortly thereafter became the Rav of the Silver Spring Woodside Shul in Silver Spring Maryland while maintaining status as a tenured professor at the University of Maryland School of Law. As Jews, we believe there is more to this world beyond ourselves. Our deep connection to our culture and roots through the learning of Jewish texts, as well as our profound connection to God through song and prayer, serve as multiple manifestations of these transformational and transcendent connections. Rabbi Breitowitz will be helpful in accomplishing in our goals. Rabbi Breitowitz will be teaching on matters of Bible and Religion via Zoom to about 40 students. This lecture will benefit the campus community because it enhances the overall desire of the campus to generate a communal culture of learning. Rabbi Breitowitz has written and lectured extensively both in the United States and Israel on the interface of halacha (Jewish Law) and contemporary society with a special interest and expertise in medical, family, business, and legal ethics. His articles cover topics such as stem cell research, cloning, organ donation, and Jewish perspectives on war and gun control.

name: A Dialog with Professors on Cutting-Edge XR Research and Courses
description: Want to drive the cutting edge of XR technology? This Tuesday, Dr. Dinesh Manocha and Dr. Ming Lin, professors who have been leading AR/VR research for over 30 years, will be meeting with members of the XR Club to discuss some exciting opportunities for undergrads.Dr. Manocha and Dr. Lin co-lead the GAMMA group. Their lab produces cutting edge research in the fields of computer graphics, robotics, virtual environments, XR, CAD/CAM, acoustics, pedestrian dynamics and medical simulation. Many technologies developed by former students of the group are now used in game engines and leading VR systems by Valve, Facebooks, etc. In fact, if you are playing any new game or using a VR system (HMD), you are probably using technology that originated in the GAMMA lab! Former students of the lab have also gone on to lead big groups in the areas of XR and game development, both in academia and in the industry, and some have even received technical oscars for their work that started in the GAMMA group.The GAMMA group just moved to UMD from UNC in 2018, but it has already published close to 20 papers on XR-related research projects at top conferences since then, including at IEEE VR, ISMAR, ACM SIGGRAPH and ACM SIGGRAPH Asia. About 25% of these papers had an undergraduate co-author, but Dr. Manocha and Dr. Lin are now looking to double those numbers, and potentially even have some undergrads be lead authors!Thus, the GAMMA group is looking for highly motivated undergraduate students with strong backgrounds to work on several hands-on XR research projects utilizing cutting-edge XR technologies, such as these new neural wristbands for AR glasses that were recently revealed by Facebook Reality Labs. Interested students should be looking to pursue serious, quality research that can produce top papers. Writing a paper for a top conference is a major commitment, so interested students must ensure they can dedicate the necessary time. At this event, Dr. Manocha and Dr. Lin will go into more detail on some specific opportunities in their lab.Dr. Manocha and Dr. Lin are also looking to introduce a new 400-level CS elective course in AR/VR, one that would complement UMD's existing undergraduate courses in game development and graphics while also bringing in industry connections. As part of this event, students will also have the opportunity to offer Dr. Manocha and Dr. Lin their thoughts, ideas, and feedback on such a course.For more details on the GAMMA lab, you can visit their website at gamma.umd.edu. You can also learn more about some of their alumni at https://gamma.umd.edu/people/

name: Akea Brionne Brown Artist Talk
description: Akea Brionne Brown (b. 1996, New Orleans, LA) is a photographer, writer, curator, and researcher whose personal work investigates the implications of historical racial and social structures in relation to the development of contemporary black life and identity within America. With a particular focus on the ways in which history influences the contemporary cultural milieu of the American black middle class and the history of urban and suburban planning; she explores current political and social themes, as they relate to historical forms of oppression, discrimination, segregation and black identity in the American cultural landscape. Her work also explores the connection between black familial relationships, space, and the role of black female identity through the lens of generational trauma. Akea Brionne has received the Visual Task Force Award from the National Association of Black Journalists. Her work is also featured in the Smithsonian's Ralph Rinzler Collection and Archives. She was announced the 2018 Documentarian of Color by Duke University. Her series, Black Picket Fences, was acquired for their permanent collection, and is on preserve at the David M. Rubenstein Rare Book & Manuscript Library. She was nominated for PDN's 30 (Photo District News) 2018: New and Emerging Photographers to Watch. Brown was also named the 2019 Janet & Walter Sondheim Winner. In 2019, Akea Brionne co-founded Shades Collective. Akea received her BFA (2018) from the Maryland Institute College of Art, in the dual degree program of Photography and Humanities. Akea Brionne lives and works in Detroit, Michigan. Participants can join the talk virtually at https://go.umd.edu/akeabrowntalk or in person at the Michelle Smith Collaboratory for Visual Culture. This talk is presented in conjunction with New Arrivals 2021 in the Stamp Gallery and is supported in part by the Maryland State Arts Council (msac.org). This fall the Stamp Gallery at the University of Maryland, College Park, presents New Arrivals 2021, an exhibition of artwork acquired this year by the University’s Contemporary Art Purchasing Program (CAPP). On view August 30 through October 16, 2021, the exhibition features seven artworks by five emerging and mid-career artists. All completed within the two years, the works come from artists connected to the Baltimore-Washington area. The 2020-2021 CAPP Committee (Thomas Boland-Reeves, Emily Gilman, Katherine Jackson, Daniela Ruiz Perez) spent a year researching, writing, discussing and conducting virtual studio and gallery visits. The result of this work is a collection of artworks around their interests and concerns as University of Maryland students and global citizens in 2021. Of their selections, the Committee wrote “Art is fundamental to everyday life, and is essential in providing a medium of catharsis for both suffering and celebration. We strive to showcase works that prioritize inclusivity and diversity by uplifting marginalized voices, such as BIPOC, LGBTQ+, and female communities. The 2020-2021 selections will offer opportunities for both conversation and education that cultivate threads of connection within the UMD community.” For more information visit stamp.umd.edu/gallery

name: Ak Dan Gwang Chil (ADG7) (South Korea)
description: From an ornate wind instrument called a saenghwang to a zither-like behemoth called a gayageum, nine-member Korean band Ak Dan Gwang Chil, or ADG7, pairs the traditional tools of their country’s folk music and sacred tunes with three singers and a panoply of percussion. ADG7 taps multiple traditions of Korean music, drawing on the songbooks of what is now the Hwanghae province. But the music they make is unapologetically and enthusiastically modern, with magnetic hooks delivered by colorfully clad singers who bound around the stage. Theatrically minded, ADG7 mirrors that anachronistic fusion of sounds visually, creating frisson by allowing the sight of old traditions to brush against the sound of contemporary exuberance. In 2021-22, ADG7 will share their magic with K-12 students in Prince George's County Public Schools via livestreamed demos and performances. They will also visit ethnomusicology students in the UMD School of Music and host a dinner with community members who perform in Korean ensembles. Time spent with this group is a musical celebration unlike any you’ve ever experienced! Health + Safety There may be COVID safety policies such as mask requirements in place when you attend this event. Please see our health & safety page for the most up to date information about attendance!

name: Camp PALS Volunteer opportunity
description: Volunteer to be a Counselor for the PALS program Camp PALS this summer. PALS is a nonprofit organization that provides one week long summer camp opportunities for teens and young adults with Down syndrome and their peers at 14 college campuses across the country. This is a one-week experience from 9am-5pm. Listed below are some details about Camp PALS: Here are some details about Camp PALS: - They offer 14 week long sleep-away camps across the country, including Camp PALS Georgetown, Chicago, and North Carolina! - Volunteer counselors are paired one-to-one with a camper to provide an opportunity to build -meaningful friendships through trips and activities - Looking for volunteers ages 16-30 who are welcoming, genuine, passionate, supportive, and fun which are all the values of the program. - No experience with Down syndrome or the disability community is necessary! They encourage groups of applicants to apply together to share the camp experience. If you are interested please visit the website at palsprograms.org/volunteer or check out their social media pages on Facebook or YouTube channel to get a look at what the PALS experience is like. PALS is an amazing opportunity to give back to the community, gain invaluable leadership skills, and make friends that will last a lifetime! There are no costs for volunteers at PALS, and applicants can apply for travel costs to be covered as well. We are looking for male applicants at this point in our season. Females are welcome to apply but will likely be placed on a waitlist. The dates for each of our 15 camps is different based on their locations, but the dates for Baltimore are July 7-13 at UMBC, and Georgetown is July 28-August 3 at Georgetown University.

description: The Ethiopian Community Development Council is a refugee resettlement agency looking for summer and fall volunteers in a variety of sectors at our Silver Spring, MD Office. These tasks include: domestic violence, employment, health, language, development, and communications services for the immigrant and refugee populations of Silver Spring. The service opportunities are available through program internships or through our First Friends Mentorship Program, where we match a volunteer with a family in need. The hours of operation are from 9:00 AM - 5:00 PM. As an intern you must be able to commit to at least 2 days a week, about 14-16 hours a week. The location is 8121 Georgia Avenue Suite 800, Silver Spring, MD 20910 and for more information contact Yariana Rodriguez at yrodriguez@ecdcus.org or 703-685-0510.Volunteer and internship opportunities are posted on the ecdcus.org website. The summer internships begin in May 2019 and the fall internships begin in August 2019, to apply please send your Resume and Cover Letter. Applications are accepted on an ongoing basis.

name: Online SKY Campus Happiness
description: We are excited to announce that we are doing our famous SKY Campus Happiness Retreat again, this time online! This is a paid retreat. However, we are giving out 50-70% scholarships to students to attend the Online SKY Happiness Retreat. Fill out the scholarship link to get a scholarship Scholarship Link: tiny.cc/SKYstudent You will learn the SKY breathing technique, yoga, and meditation. Meditation? Yeah... it’s pretty lit! Over 70 independent studies have been conducted on its effects. Studies have shown that it reduces depression, stress, anxiety and it increases immunity & sense of well being. After the course, 95% of participants report higher energy and being better able to connect with themselves. We invite you to come to this retreat so that you can also come home to yourself ! The SKY Happiness retreat is one of the coolest places to connect with yourself, make awesome friends and have fun! Retreat Timings EDT time zone (all sessions are mandatory) June 26-28 , 2020 Friday-Sunday 06/26 Fri 7.30 PM - 9 PM EDT 06/27 Sat 12 PM - 3 PM EDT 06/28 Sun 12 PM - 3 PM EDT For Questions Email: meghavi.prashnani@artofliving.org‬ The Sudarshan Kriya The cornerstone of SKY retreat is the healing breath known as the Sudarshan Kriya(SKY). This unique breathing practice is a potent energizer, with the following benefits: every cell becomes fully oxygenated and flooded with new lifeflushes out negative emotions from the bodyreleases tensions, frustrations and angerclears anxiety, depression, and lethargygives relief to both the mind and bodytakes you to the door of meditationWith regular practice, one becomes calm and centered with a clearer mind. A sense of joy in the moment prevails, and one is able to smile from the heart. The benefits of meditation are innumerable, and each and every human must tap into their inner being for a more enriched living. About SKY Campus Happiness SKY Campus Happiness supports happiness, social connection, and resilience so that students can achieve personal and professional success as compassionate and service-minded leaders of tomorrow. Neither at home nor at school are students taught how to deal with stress in healthy ways. Our innovative life-skills training programs combine breath work and meditation with interactive discussions and experiential processes so students gain valuable skills to better navigate the personal, social, and academic landscape and pressures of college. name: Virtual Symposium on Changing Threats (SIA / START Webinar)
description: The Security Industry Association (SIA), START and the University of Maryland will host a virtual event Thursday, Sept. 10 at 1 p.m. that teaches how new tools and partnerships can mitigate changing threats. Topics will include the capability development framework tool for risk assessment, horizon scanning for future threats and the new generation of threats and countermeasures. The day will conclude with Q&A. The webinar is free and open to the public. Register on the SIA website here. AGENDA (All times in EDT) 1:00 p.m. - Introduction (Don Erickson and Rob Reiter, SIA) 1:10 p.m. - Introduction of START 1:15 p.m. - The Global Terrorism Database (and the T2V Database) | Discussion Leader: Erin Miller, START 1:25 p.m. - The Capability Development Framework Tool for Risk Assessment | Discussion Leader: Marc Boyd, START 1:35 p.m. - Profiles of Individual-Level Radicalization in the United States Database | Discussion Leader: Mike Jensen, START 1:45 p.m. - START Training Programs | Discussion Leader: Liberty Day, START 1:55 p.m. - Horizon Scanning for Future Threats | Discussion Leader: Steve Sin, START 2:05 p.m. - ICONS: Online Simulations for Contingency Planning | Discussion Leader: Devin Ellis, START 2:15 p.m. - How a relationship with educational centers like the University of Maryland and START can help SIA members recruit talent in the next decade | Discussion Leader: Kathryn Bartunek, security engineer, AECOM 2:35 p.m. - Unmanned Aviation Systems – Rethinking a Secure Perimeter | Discussion Leaders: Tommy Luginbill, the University of Maryland TechPort; Amit Samani, Dedrone 3:05 p.m. - Modeling Risk, Threat and Vulnerability for Analysis and Assessments | Discussion Leaders: Barnett Koven, START; Bill Braniff, START; Rob Reiter, SIA 3:35 p.m. - The New Generation of Threats and Countermeasures | Discussion Leader: Laura Pearson, acting deputy director, division of facilities and security, Nuclear Regulatory Commission 4:05 p.m. - New Dimensions in Security 4:35 p.m. - Closing Remarks

name: UKC2017
organization: Korean Engineering and Science Student Association
description: We are pleased to announce this call for papers for the annual US-Korea Conference on Science, Technology, and Entrepreneurship (UKC) to be held August 9 – 12, 2017 in the Hyatt Regency Crystal City near Washington DC, Capitol of the United States. Please note that the early paper submission deadline for registration discount is March 31, 2017. UKC is an annual conference jointly organized by the Korean-American Scientists and Engineers Association (KSEA) and the Korean Federation of Science and Technology Societies (KOFST). It draws over 1,000 scientists, engineers, government officials, industry executives, and policy-makers. The UKC 2017 theme “Engagement Opportunities for Global Challenges: Convergence and Innovation through Cooperation” focuses on UKC’s special multi-disciplinary nature. Building on the strength of having numerous National Laboratories, Government Agencies, Universities and industries in the region, UKC2017 provides valuable opportunities for cooperation between the US and Korea. On behalf of the UKC 2017 Program Committee and sponsoring organizations, we invite you to submit a paper presenting significant research findings, R&D trends, and future prospects of sciences and technologies in areas including but not limited to the following: Basic Science Symposiums Physics (PHY) Chemistry (CHM) Math/Applied Math/Statistics (MAS) Engineering Symposiums Chemical Engineering (CHE) Computer Sciences and Information Technologies (CIT) Materials Science and Engineering (MSE) Mechanical, Aerospace and Naval Engineering (MAN) Civil, Environmental, Architecture (CEA) Electrical, Electronics and Communications (EEC) Health and Medical Symposiums Food, Agriculture and Nutrition (FAN) Bio, Medical and Pharmaceutical (BMP) Biomedical Engineering (BME) Interdisciplinary Symposiums Connected and Automated Vehicle (CIT, CEA & EEC) Nano Technology and Materials for Energy Applications (CHM & CHE) Math and Statistical Modeling for Biomedical Engineering (MAS, BME & BMP) Advanced Simulations for Biology (MAS, BME & BMP) Energy and Material (CHM & MSE) Energy Production and Storage (MSE & ECE) Additive Manufacturing (MSE & ECE) Nano-Micro Fabrication for Bio/Energy/Material (MAN with BMP, CHE & MSE) Cyber Physical System for Transportation/Health (EEC with CEA & BMP/BME) Smart City and Smart Grid (EEC & CEA) Carbon Capture Storage and Utilization (CEA with CHM/MAN/MSE) Precision Medicine and New Drug Discovery (BMP & BME) Forums Sponsor named forums such as KEIT, CJ etc. Young Generation and Professional Forum (YGPF) Korean-American Women in Science and Engineering (KWiSE) Forum KSEA History Forum Intellectual Property Forum Science Policy Forum Workshop Small and Medium Business Workshop (SMB) All papers are required to be written and presented in English. The papers will be reviewed and selected by each Symposium Program Committee in consultation with the Conference Program Committee. All papers presented at the Conference will be collected and published in a Proceedings. Important Dates Early paper submission deadline: March 31, 2017 (for registration discount) Travel grant application deadline: March 31, 2017 (for student, early career people) Notification of acceptance: April 15, 2017 Final paper submission deadline: April 30, 2017 (no extension will be granted) Online payment for registration: May 1, 2017 Final notification of acceptance: May 15, 2017 Early registration deadline: May 31, 2017 Online registration closure: June 30, 2017 Submission of papers All submissions should use online system at the submission page at http://ukc.ksea.org/ukc2017/call-for-paper/paper-submission/ using the attached template. Additional information can be found at http://ukc.ksea.org/ukc2017/. Should you have any questions, please feel free to contact the Program Committee at ukc2017@gmail.com. Sincerely, Byungkyu Brian Park, Program Chair Young-Kee Kim, Program Co-Chair Eun-Suk Seo, Conference Chair / KSEA President-Elect Myung-Ja Kim, Conference Co-Chair / KOFST President-Elect

name: SEE Presents: An Evening with Mary Lambert
description: Singer-songwriter and spoken word artist Mary Lambert will give a lecture/performance in Hoff Theatre on April 26th! This is a FREE ticketed event with tickets available for pick-up at the Stamp ticket office. Known for her work with Macklemore and Ryan Lewis on their Grammy-nominated song “Same Love”, Lambert writes from her vantage point of being both a Christian and a lesbian. Writing and singing the hook also led to the iconic performance alongside pop legend Madonna at the 2014 Grammys. Mary soon after released her debut album Heart on My Sleeve. Her single, “Secrets” launched to No. 1 on the Billboard Dance charts, and went RIAA Gold in 2015. Inspired by confessional folk singers as well as spoken-word performers, Lambert is a candid writer who deals directly in her art with her past as Lambert has been diagnosed with bipolar disorder, and is a sexual assault survivor. Overall, Mary is disarmingly hilarious, charms effortlessly, and the effect on her audience is bewitching.

name: BlackLight Summit 2022
description: Returning for a second year, The Clarice’s BlackLight Summit aims to activate the unimagined possibilities in dance– a convening that re-envisions dance as a conduit to galvanize resilience and inventiveness. The 2022 summit explores three fundamental inquiries: “What/Who are we Becoming,” “How do we return to one another?” and “Progress does not equal healing, but it can.” Throughout the 2021-22 season, the BlackLight Summit will also continue community connectivity by facilitating a series of mentoring and professional development opportunities, conversations and performances. Register + learn more: go.umd.edu/blacklightsummit2022 Health + Safety There may be COVID safety policies such as mask requirements in place when you attend this event. Please see our health & safety page for the most up to date information about attendance! BlackLight Summit 2022 Artists: Baye & Asa is a company creating movement art projects directed by Amadi ‘Baye’ Washington & Sam ‘Asa’ Pratt. They grew up together in New York City and that shared educational history is the mother of their work. Through the personal dynamics of their brotherhood, they address the larger political landscape of their upbringing, struggling to show a reality of violence while communicating a necessity for empathy. Charlie Maybee is a music and dance artist from Woodbridge, VA. He holds an M.F.A. in Dance from the University of Illinois with a certificate in Criticism and Interpretive Theory, a B.F.A. from Virginia Commonwealth University and is an alumnus of the Metropolitan Youth Tap Ensemble. As an educator, Charlie is currently on faculty at Shenandoah University where he primarily teaches tap dance technique, choreography, history and improvisation. Johnnie Cruise Mercer Recently acknowledged as a 2021 Princess Grace Award Recipent in Choreograpy, and nominated for two 2021 Bessie Awards in Dance and Performance, Johnnie Cruise Mercer is a queer-black think-maker, freelance-performer, educator and social entrepreneur based in New York City. A native of Richmond, VA, Mercer holds a BFA in Dance and Choreography from Virginia Commonwealth University. As the Company Director of Johnnie Cruise Mercer/TheREDprojectNYC, his processes/work has been shared and/or hosted by 92Y Harkness Dance Center, Gibney: Agnes Varis Performing Arts Center, Dixon Place, Danspace Project Inc, The Fusebox Festival, Mana Contemporary, The NADA Conference, Abrons Arts Center and most recently at The Clarice Performing Arts Center's BlackLight Summit. As an educator, Mercer facilitates within the New York Public School system through The Leadership Program-a mentorship-based organization that uses art to foster/engage restorative justice and motivate the true empowerment of self. Mercer has also been on teaching faculty/a guest artist at The American Dance Festival, Bates Dance Festival, PRATT Institute, NYU Tisch Dance Program, Gibney, University of Massachusetts Amherst, DeSales University, Muhlenberg College, the University of Texas at Austin, University of Maryland and The Dance Institute of Washington. Mercer was most recently a 2019-2021 Artist in Residence at Brooklyn Arts Exchange, a 2020-2021 Ping Chong and Company Creative Fellow and a 2020-2021 AIR through New Dance Alliance’s Black Artists Space to Create Residency curated by Angie Pittman. He is currently a 2022 Artist in Residence at Center for Performance Research. Greg David is a movement artist based in the DMV area. Exploring themes of grief, fear, care and solitude, the work and movement they enjoy making goes hand in hand with human emotion and experience and aims to capture that essence in motion. David joinedCulture Shock Washington DC® in 2012 and became the Artistic Director for their 2015 and 2016 seasons where, nationally and internationally, they presented stage works and taught workshops. Kayla Farrish/Decent Structures Arts is an emerging company combining filmmaking, storytelling, dance theater performance and sound score. The company has been commissioned by Gibney Dance Inc (2020-2021), Louis Armstrong House Museum (2020), Danspace Project Inc (2019), Pepatian and BAAD! (2018) and beyond. Kayla has been supported by creative residencies including Gallim Women + Residency (2021), Gibney Spotlight: New Voices, Barysnikov Arts Center and Arts On Site (2020).

name: Veterans Yoga
description: Sun Salutations (8/31) Get ready for a class to introduce health and vitality into the semester! This short class includes 20 minutes of cleansing movement fit for yogis of all shapes, sizes, and experience levels. Bonus: Do you not have time to relax and let go for even just a few minutes? Your instructor includes at least five minutes of required shavasana practice at the end of each class to give the mind a break from the rest of the world. Learn a New Pose (9/2) Today’s yoga session will include 18 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out, meaning that yogis of all experience and backgrounds will benefit! Get ready to build strength and resilience with this fun-to learn movement. Relaxation Meditation (9/7) Tuesday’s session will be focused on grounding yourself in this new semester. Just fifteen minutes of passive, yet focused yoga practice will bring you into the moment and out of the stresses of the new semester. Get a Workout in (9/9) After Tuesday’s session focused on relaxation and finding ground in the new semester, it’s time to ramp up the heat. You would never believe what just twenty minutes of poses can do to get that blood pumping and the sweat pouring! Don’t worry, though! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Open the Hips (9/14) We have been in class for a couple of weeks now and our bodies need us to keep moving to stay open and ready for all that life has to offer. Twenty three minutes of opening the hips will keep them from tightening from all the stress and constant sitting motion. Don’t forget! We also include at least five minutes of time to destress and prepare for the rest of the week. Learn a New Pose (9/16) Today’s yoga session will include 24 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out. Yogis of all experience and backgrounds will benefit from this fun practice! Get ready to build some awesome abdominal strength with this sequence. Relaxation Meditation (9/21) Today’s session will be focused on grounding yourself in this new semester. Twenty six minutes of passive, yet focused yoga practice will bring you into the moment and out of the stresses of the semester’s stressors. Getting in a Workout! (9/23) After Tuesday’s session focused on relaxation and finding ground in this awesome in-person semester, it’s time to get that body moving. Just thirty three minutes of poses will get that blood pumping and the sweat pouring! Don’t worry! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Plus, we won’t leave your muscles stiff from the hard work! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for the Booty (9/28) Looking to add cushion and tone to your derriere? Who isn’t?! Today’s session will be devoted to working to add strength to the glutes and hamstrings. Twenty minutes of work will show you some tips and tools to build your important muscle groups that keep your body healthy and moving! Learn a New Pose (9/30) Today’s yoga session will include 25 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out! Even the simplest of poses require detail-orientation! Get ready to build strength and resilience in simple poses. Relaxation Meditation (10/5) Tuesday’s session will be focused on staying sane as the semester continues to pose more difficulties. This is a time for you to take 26 minutes to treat yourself to reduce stress and a little self-care. Get a Workout In (10/7) After Tuesday’s session focused on relaxation and de-stressing, it’s time to move the mind, body, and spirit. Just 34 minutes of yoga flow will get that blood pumping! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in and focused throughout the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Plus, we won’t leave your muscles stiff from the hard work! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for Weak and Tight Shoulders (10/12) We get it. Being an athlete, veteran, human, parent, student, etc. comes with a price. Usually that price is paid in the body. Today we are going to focus on restoring weak and/or tight shoulders. Don’t shy away from class out of fear of injury! There are modifications for all flexibility levels in the shoulders. We are working to improve, not perfect! After all, we only have twenty six minutes! Learn a New Pose (10/14) Today’s yoga session will include 34 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out! Poses that seem difficult from the outside may be a bit simpler than you anticipate! We are focused on safety in strength. So first, we will build strength and confidence. Then we will build upon simple poses to create a beautiful movement to feel proud about. Relaxation Meditation (10/19) We are mid-semester. While it feels like this is the time to be working your butt off with as few breaks as possible, don’t forget about the importance of daily self-care. Today’s class will be nineteen minutes focused on nothing but bringing you back to yourself. This is a time to reclaim the best parts of yourself and create the person you want to be with focused intention. Get a Workout In (10/21) Tuesday got us mentally focused for the week, so now it is time to ramp up the energy to end the week strong! Thirty-one minutes of yoga flow will get that blood pumping! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in and focused. Don’t forget a towel! We will leave your muscles feeling worked, but not too stiff! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for Back Pain (10/26) Is your back constantly feeling stiff? Is the lower back achy and shoulder blades tight? Come to today’s yoga session for the opportunity to release some of that stiffness, and open yourself up to a world of relief! You might be surprised at what a short 33 minutes of stretching and strengthening can do for the body. Learn a New Pose (10/28) Ready to expand your yoga knowledge and experience? Today’s class will revolve around learning a yoga pose through-and-through. There is no reason to worry about the experience level needed for the pose, as all poses learned and performed here can be done at any level! Set aside 33 minutes and get mentally ready to learn reverse warrior so we can add it to your yoga repertoire! Relaxation Meditation (11/2) Meditating on a regular basis has positive effects on the body and mind, such as greater sense of focus, muscle relaxation, and increased creativity. Today’s meditation will be focused on gratitude and increasing happiness. Giving thanks can come in many forms, but have you tried it in the form of meditation?! Getting in a Workout! (11/4) After Tuesday’s session focused on gratitude in this challenging semester, it’s time to get that body moving. Just 34 minutes of sweat-inducing poses will get that blood pumping! This class is fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Plus, we won’t leave your muscles stiff from the hard work! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for a Better Mood (11/9) College is demanding, stressful, and can induce negative feelings! Combat those real-time stresses by moving the body and bonding with fellow veterans. Coming to this thirty minute vinyasa class will open the heart to the positivity you need to get you to the end of the semester. Learn a New Pose (11/11) Ready to expand your yoga knowledge and experience? Today’s class will revolve around learning a yoga pose through-and-through. There is no reason to worry about the experience level needed for the pose, as all poses learned and performed here can be done at any level! Set aside 35 minutes and get mentally ready to learn a new pose to add to your yoga repertoire! Relaxation Meditation (11/16) Today’s meditation practice will be short, sweet, and perfect to regain focus on your workflow. As we near the end of the semester, stress increases, the mind wanders, and we lose focus. We will be going through meditation techniques that can be utilized at home, work, or on the bus. Don’t underestimate the power of this 26 minute session. Come join your fellow veterans and enjoy the feeling of a clear mind. Get a Workout In (11/18) After Tuesday’s session focused on de-stressing and refocusing, it’s time to move that body. Just 34 minutes of yoga flow will get that blood pumping! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in and focused throughout the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Plus, we won’t leave your muscles stiff from the hard work! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for Neck Pain (11/23) After months of looking down at our computer screens, it’s no wonder so many of us have the amount of pain in our necks that we do! Today’s class will be all about de-stressing, communication, and releasing the tension in the neck through yoga practice. Set aside 31 minutes for this perfectly-paced practice.

Unfortunately, the local organization that owns LEAFhouse has plans to sell it and move it off campus. This would be a big loss to sustainability on campus and to all the student groups who use it. So what are we doing about it? We are planning on buying it. Come help us as we coordinate with other groups, apply to grants, petition the university, and plan funding and maintenance plans to procure the building! Any assistance is welcome! description: Event Details: Want an effective resume? Think you would benefit from employer feedback before you apply for a job? You will see the resume clinic information. SELECT YOUR UPLOADED RESUME IN THE BOX AND SELECT A TIME TO SIGN UP! (Please check your schedule before selecting a time slot) Employers: TO VOLUNTEER PLEASE VISIT: www.Careers.umd.edu/ClinicSignup For additional information about this event: contact Robert Piper at rpiper@umd.edu

name: Arts Citizenship Talks (ACTnow): Revelations by Black Women in the Arts–Dance
description: From themes of racial violence and cultural appropriation to multiculturalism and gender equality, the work of The Clarice's 2020-21 artists is complex, provocative and deeply sensitive. Arts Citizenship Talks (ACTnow) are opportunities to hear from these artists about the issues reflected in their works. These conversations are an invitation to act now! Revelations by Black Women in the Arts is a series of powerful conversations by Black woman scholars, performers, educators and leaders delves into the essence of being a Black female artist in a society ill-equipped to receive and make room for them. Whether they move along the margins or at the center of their fields, these extraordinary women will share their artistry, scholarship, vision and creativity throughout Spring 2021. These conversations will be centered around their highs and lows, victories and losses, and will be moderated by dancer, choreographer and scholar Ronya-Lee Anderson M.F.A. dance ‘20 and current Ph.D. candidate in the UMD School of Theatre, Dance, and Performance Studies.

name: The Revolutionists
description: Juxtaposed against the background of the French Revolution’s Reign of Terror, this raucous comedy portrays a sisterhood of four women: a playwright, an assassin, a former queen and a rebel. The play touches on themes of legacy, activism, terrorism and feminism to suggest how women can change the world. Though set in 1793, this production uses language, culture and references to contemporary culture to highlight the relevance of such themes today. “…a sassy, hold-on-to-your-seats theatrical adventure…[Gunderson] has created a play that is wonderfully wild and raucous…It’s a wild ride, filled with verbal gymnastics that come racing at you so quickly it’s occasionally hard to keep up. Listen closely, though, and hang on tight. If you do, you’ll be treated to an invigorating and enlightening journey.”—Cincinnati Enquirer Note: All COVID-19 safety protocols are followed in this production. Rehearsals and performances take place completely virtually.

name: IGSF's Yalda Night!
description: In ancient Iranian traditions, the winter solstice – with the longest and darkest night of the year – was a fortunate day, and included customs intended to protect people from misfortune. Based on Gregorian calendar, it is the night between the last day of autumn and the first day of winter. People celebrate this night with parties and gatherings, and ate the last remaining fresh fruits from left over from the summer season. Today, in Iran and some other Persian-speaking countries like Afghanistan and Tajikistan, this tradition has passed through many generations and is still celebrated. Nowadays the winter solstice is called “Shab-e Yalda.” In this special night family and friends get together, recite Persian poetry, enjoy a spread of nuts, and fruits, and eat a specific food. In addition to this, telling tales and anecdotes by the elders is a tradition observed on this night. The color for this night is red as it represents the crimson hues of dawn and the glow of life. So we can find a lot of red fruits like watermelon, pomegranates in Yalda table. The IGSF, as a small Iranian community at the University of Maryland, would like to celebrate Yalda as the first night of the winter. We are trying to keep the memory of this important night alive in Persian culture; and give its message to the students at UMD who come from different countries and backgrounds. We will also invite them to join us for celebrating the ancient Persian culture of which they may have heard a lot. It provides us with an opportunity to renew our cultural bounds with those friends from various nations. Unfortunately, due to funding difficulties in the past years, we had to keep our parties very small by organizing a small Yalda event. We hope to be able to organize a bigger event this year around! Financial support from GSG is indeed critical for doing such a thing. We hope this event will: - Introduce Iranian traditions and Persian culture to non-Iranian members of the campus community. - Provide a warm and friendly atmosphere in which students can discuss things with their peers. - Allow the students to have entertainment and a relaxing time during their Winter break. We would like to organize Yalda as a free event if we can get enough funding for it.

description: Nearly 75% of DC students perform at or below basic levels in reading and math, and without intervention, low-income students are at risk to lose 2 months of proficiency in reading and math this summer. In just 22 hours of tutoring, students improve an average of 1 year in reading and math skills while gaining confidence in their abilities. We need your help! Each new volunteer allows us to impact the life of one more child. Training and ongoing professional support from staff are provided, so no experience is necessary! However, we are looking for a few particular qualities from our tutors: Patience Creativity and flexibility Fluency in the English language (Volunteers who are not native speakers of American English may be asked to tutor only in our math curriculum.) A sense of humor! Able and willing to commit for the full summer Will you join us as a volunteer tutor this summer? The commitment is 2.5 hours twice a week, in one of two programs: Reading tutoring, Mondays & Wednesdays from 5:45-8:15pm Math tutoring, Tuesdays & Thursdays from 5:45 to 8:15pm Both programs will be held at our Adams Morgan office at 1763 Columbia Road NW. The program will run from June 22nd – July 30th. How to Apply: Complete a volunteer application at www.floc.org/get-involved/volunteer or contact Elizabeth Metz, Recruitment and Outreach Manager at emetz@floc.org or (202)349-3512. name: Intro to Kyaking and White Water Trip
description: This series of pool sessions and trips is designed to introduce you to the thrilling sport of whitewater kayaking and rafting. Learn the basics of paddling and kayak rolling in the pool before heading out to the Potomac River to learn about river features and practice your skills. Then we’ll head to the Youghiogheny River, affectionately known as the Yough, for an adventure-filled weekend of whitewater kayaking and whitewater rafting. We’ll spend the first day whitewater kayaking on the class II Middle Yough, enjoy a night of camping, and spend the second day whitewater rafting on the class III Lower Yough. No previous kayaking experience is necessary but you must attend all sessions in order to be able to participate in the final trip. This program is free for veteran students thanks to generous support from the U.S. Department of Veteran Affairs.

name: Share your knowledge and skills with women at Calvary! (Interview day for eight week commitment)
description: Calvary Women’s Services offers housing, health, employment and education programs that empower homeless women in Washington, DC to change their lives. Our programs carry out our mission to offer “a safe, caring place for tonight; support, hope and change for tomorrow.” We'd love to include you in carrying out this important mission. Currently, we're looking for volunteers to teach classes through our educational services, known at Calvary as LEAP (Life skills, Education and Arts Programming). LEAP empowers women with the skills and basic knowledge needed in their transition out of homelessness. All of the classes are facilitated by our wonderful volunteers. On April 30th, we will be holding interviews for volunteers looking to facilitate an eight week class. Right now, we're looking for volunteers to facilitate classes on the following topics: Geography Yarn Works Spanish for the workplace Writing Workshop Basic Computer Skills Voice and Song Healthy Cooking Options Vocabulary Building A topic you are passionate about and would like to share! The time commitment is once a week for an hour on a weekday afternoon (either 1:30 pm or 3:30 pm) for eight weeks (for example, Monday afternoons at 1:30pm for 8 weeks). All curriculum will be provided! We'd love to include you in our LEAP team. In order to apply or ask further questions, you can reach out to our Community Engagement Coordinator, Arielle Baker, at abaker@calvaryservices.org.

name: Intro to AR Development (Part II - Interactions and Realism)
description: Join the XR Club this Tuesday for the second part of our AR Development workshop series, where you'll build upon your application from last week in order to place your very own virtual pet into your physical space, interact with it using some common AR touch gestures, and utilize information about the real-world environment in order to make the digital objects fit in realistically. We'll be using the new Unity XR Tech Stack, including AR Foundation, a multi-platform framework that connects you to the core underlying capabilities of both smartphone and headset based AR platforms, and the XR Interaction Toolkit, which allows you to quickly and easily add common AR/VR interactions into your Unity app. No prior experience is necessary; all majors welcome! Notes:This workshop requires you to bring a computer with a variety of special software tools installed prior to attending the workshop. These tools could take 30 mins or longer to download and install, so you will not have enough time during the workshop to install the software without falling behind. Additionally, it is strongly recommended that you bring a physical mouse. For Android:You will need to have Unity 2021.2 or later installed along with the Android Build Support module and the options for the Android SDK & NDK Tools and OpenJDK. All of these should be installed with the Unity Hub. You will also need to enable developer options and USB debugging on your phone, as described at https://developer.android.com/studio/debug/dev-options#enable For iOS:You will need to have Unity 2021.2 or later installed along with the iOS Build Support module. You will also need to install the latest version of Apple's Xcode IDE, which can be found on the Mac App Store. Once you've done that, add your Apple ID account to your Xcode preferences, as described at https://help.apple.com/xcode/mac/current/#/devaf282080a Note that the Xcode IDE is only available on Macs. If you have a Windows computer, you will still be able to develop an AR applications in Unity and export it to an Xcode project, but you will not be able to open that Xcode project and deploy the build to an iOS device for testing As per University guidelines, all attendees of this event will be required to wear KN95 masks. Violators will be denied entry into the event.

name: Build Your Own XR Tracking System from Scratch
description: Have you ever wondered how VR headsets are able to seamlessly track your head and controllers while you play? Are you interested in full-body tracking solutions for VR games, where your virtual avatar’s arm and leg movements match almost perfectly with your own? Then look no further, this is the workshop for you! Join us on Tuesday, April 12th at 6:30 PM. In this workshop, we will give you a comprehensible crash course on the basic fundamentals of today’s common strategies for tracking VR devices, such as “outside-in” and “inside-out” tracking. We will also discuss full-body tracking by defining its key components: what it is, what its benefits are, and its design challenges. Then, using these principles, you will build your very own “tracker” that can be seen and tracked by your webcam. No prior experience is necessary; any and all majors are welcome and encouraged to come! As per University guidelines, all attendees of this event will be required to wear KN95 masks. Violators will be denied entry into the event.
