name: Safeguarding Critical System Supply Chains Against Compromise
description: On Thursday, July 14, START will co-host a workshop on critical system supply chains with the Center for Advanced Life Cycle Engineering (CALCE), the Applied Research Laboratory for Intelligence and Security (ARLIS), and the Center for Governance of Technology and Systems at START Headquarters. This event is free and open to the public, but RSVPs are required. “Critical systems” are systems associated with human safety (transportation, medical), the delivery of critical services (infrastructure, energy generation), important humanitarian and military missions, and global economic stability. The risk of supply chains being compromised is a significant problem for critical systems due to the system’s long manufacturing and support life. Compromise of a system component means that its content, function, quality and/or reliability has been modified in some way (either with, or without malicious intent) to be something other than what the system expected (i.e., was qualified for). The supply chains for system components can be compromised by natural events or the active introduction of manipulated parts, materials, software, or information, as well as interferences with networks and processes. Compromise impacts the quality, reliability, and/or security of a final system. Compromise can occur, for example, when the customer receives components that are compromised and those compromised items lead to a compromised system. In this case, a component could refer to hardware, material, software, data, algorithms, human, etc. Sourcing components for critical systems is a challenge because the supply chains for the components diverge from mainstream commercial supply chains over time. As a result, the operators of critical systems impose a myriad of restrictions on how components can be sourced in order to minimize the risk of compromised components finding their way into critical systems. Similarly, the information that these systems depend on to operate can be compromised impacting the system’s support and/or manufacturing. These requirements limit the available sources and can make the process time consuming and expensive and on the other hand open opportunities for impostors to enter the supply chain. This workshop will focus on the unique issues posed by compromised components (hardware, material, software, data, algorithms, humans), and how they can be predicted and mitigated. This is a convergent workshop whose participants will include academics, industry practitioners, and stakeholders from the critical systems community whose concern is disruption and compromise of the technology and supply chain for critical systems. For more information about the workshop, please contact Dr. Diganta Das and Prof. Peter Sandborn.

description: Do YOU have a badge? If not, come on down and get one! An important aspect of furry culture are badges. Badges are a way to show off one’s own art or commissioned art and more importantly an individual's “fursona”. Badges typically show off artwork of your fursona and your fursona’s name. This is important because these things can help distinguish you from others at either furry meetups or conventions. This event will allow members to show off their artwork and have an easier experience at furry conventions and meet ups within the club by creating their own custom printed badges. No fees will be required to attend. The event will be open to all Unifursity Furries club members as well as any other interested UMD students.

description: The Yuri Kochiyama High School Leadership Program (YKLP) is an annual opportunity for DMV high school students to learn about the history of Asian American activism, strengthen their sense of identity through learning about cross-racial and intersectional community building, and develop peer solidarity and mentorship with other BIPOC-identifying individuals at UMD and other high school students.Hosted by the Asian American Student Union (AASU) at the University of Maryland, College Park (UMCP), YKLP seeks to celebrate the legacy of Japanese American activist, Yuri Kochiyama, by providing community education and mentorship to students interested in Asian American issues--completely free of charge.This year, we are taking applications for a cohort that will meet once a week through a hybrid format over a 5-week session during the spring. Each week, YK participants will come together to learn about Asian American history, identity, and leadership through intersectional community building. YKLP will end with an End-of-Program Celebration on April 13. The hybrid schedule is as follows: WEEK ONE (2/17): in-person WEEK TWO (2/24) : online WEEK THREE (3/02): in-person WEEK FOUR (3/09): online WEEK FIVE (3/16): in-person Graduation (4/13): in-person We hope to raise awareness about Asian Pacific Islander Desi American (APIDA) issues that matter to community members, highlighting APIDA experiences and engaging with each other to better integrate intersectional concepts within our daily lives. YKLP is open to all public high school students within the DMV who are of BIPOC-identifying background to facilitate inter-community building and learning.

description: During the late spring, summer, and early fall, we have meetings to check on our bees. We learn about sustainable beekeeping practices, what to look for and do while taking care of bees. People who show up to this meeting will have to wear bee-safe clothing such as close toed shoes, and preferably pants, though we have full suits and half suits along with gloves provided. Participants will also have to sign a safety waiver which accepts the possibility of bee stings. When it is too cold or rainy, we go to the UMD Greenhouses to complete workshops such as candles, chapstick, and soap using beeswax. Feel free to reach out through our TerpLink page, our email, or the Discord for more information! The Beekeeping Club does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, religion, age, or physical ability. The Mission of The Beekeeping Club is to educate students about bees and beekeeping through hands-on experience and lectures, about harvesting raw products from them in sustainable ways, and about turning those raw products a variety of goods. The Beekeeping Club seeks to offer anyone with a curiosity or passion for bees and beekeeping the ability to participate in beekeeping regardless of their skill level or prior experience and to guide them in learning more about bees and the role beekeeping plays a sustainable world.

name: Walk with an Arborist & Your Baby
organization: University of Maryland Arboretum & Botanical Gardens
description: Walk with an Arborist & Your Baby encourages new parents to connect with each other and with the outdoors in a safe space, both physically and emotionally. Based in the Garden of Reflection & Remembrance at the Memorial Chapel, participants learn about trees and plants while having their newborns along. Parental leave and the welcoming of a new child can be lonely and stressful. By offering a tour specifically for new parents and caregivers, participants can interact as much (or as little) as they wish with other adults and have a focus in order to leave the house. According to the National Institutes of Health, one in seven women will develop postpartum depression and many others will still experience feelings of loneliness and isolation during parental leave. These symptoms can affect all genders, adoptive parents, and all caregivers, not just the birth parent. Things like cost, transportation, and child care can hinder access to alleviating symptoms. The Arboretum aims to make the outdoors and public gardens more accessible to everyone, regardless of where they are in life's journey. Registration is required on the Arboretum website: https://arboretum.umd.edu/maps-tours/walk-arborist-your-baby

name: Gift of Life Marrow Registry Tabling Event
organization: Health and Education for All: UMD Student Chapter
description: HAEFA-UMD and Youth in Public Health are partnering with The Gift of Life Marrow Registry, a nonprofit organization founded in 1991 and headquartered in Boca Raton, Florida. The Gift of Life operates a public blood stem cell and bone marrow registry, facilitating transplants for children and adults battling life-threatening illnesses such as leukemia, lymphoma, other cancers, and genetic diseases. This drive encourages the University of Maryland community to participate in a cheek swab to help find compatible, lifesaving donors urgently needed by those battling blood cancer, sickle cell, inherited immune disorders, and over 70 other diseases. College students play a crucial role in this effort, as more than 65 percent of donors identified as matches are between 18 and 29. Transplant physicians have determined that patients who receive bone marrow or blood stem cells from younger donors tend to have better outcomes. Adding new donors to the registry is incredibly rewarding, especially when your swab could match and save a patient’s life.

Bonus Event (Hosted by Graduate Student Government): Pizza and Connections Time: 6:00 - 8:00 p.m. Location: TerpZone Can't make it earlier in the evening? No problem! name: ANTHRO+ Anthropology of Community: Reconnecting with the Field
description: ANTHRO+ is a conference put on by the Practicing Anthropology Student Association (PASA) at the University of Maryland, College Park. UMD's Department of Anthropology has a focus on medical anthropology, environmental anthropology, historical archaeology, and the study of cultural heritage, but all subfields and theoretical focuses are welcome at our conference! The goal of the conference is to enable graduate and undergraduate students of anthropology and related disciplines to present and engage with research in a student-centric space. This year will mark the 14th annual ANTHRO+ Conference, and we are interested in highlighting research both inside and outside the discipline of anthropology. While normally an in-person only event, this year ANTRHO+ will be held online over the course of Saturday, March 11, 2023, from 9 AM to 3:15 PM. This year’s theme, Anthropology of Community: Reconnecting with the Field, focuses on emerging methods that have assisted the anthropologist/researcher in connecting with a new field given the COVID-19 pandemic. Additionally, our focus on community opens up a discussion of community-engaged methodologies, work on heritage, and the understanding of the socio-cultural implications of change or continuity and people’s response to it in both the past and present.

name: Weekly Workshop- Preparing Hive Frames
description: The populations of hives start to boom during the start of spring, so this week we will be preparing for hive expansion by prepping frames to give them. Come join this workshop to learn about the yearly cycle of beekeeping and to help prepare our hives for pollinator season! This is an event that anyone can attend, no previous membership or experience necessary. Join our Discord for the most up-to-date information and announcements on event details. Also feel free to reach out through our TerpLink page or email for any questions you might have. description: The National Hillel Basketball Tournament (NHBT) was founded in 2010 to bring Jewish students together around the inclusive and encompassing game of basketball. Players and fans also participate in various off-the-court programs such as Shabbat meals, keynote speakers, and an exciting bar night to kick the weekend off. In addition to NHBT’s impressive scale and reach, its impact has reached new heights in recent years. By providing students a chance to meet, socialize, and compete in a positive Jewish environment, NHBT serves as an oasis for students experiencing antisemitism on their respective campuses. By platforming like-minded organizations and starting initiatives, NHBT has provided a beacon of hope and togetherness for Jewish and campus communities far and wide.

description: Walk with an Arborist & Your Baby encourages new parents to connect with each other and with the outdoors in a safe space, both physically and emotionally. Based in the Garden of Reflection & Remembrance at the Memorial Chapel, participants learn about trees and plants while having their newborns along. Registration Link: https://forms.gle/DHhgXipMirJXoH8v8 Parental leave and the welcoming of a new child can be lonely and stressful. By offering a tour specifically for new parents and caregivers, participants can interact as much (or as little) as they wish with other adults and have a focus in order to leave the house. According to the National Institutes of Health, one in seven women will develop postpartum depression and many others will still experience feelings of loneliness and isolation during parental leave. These symptoms can affect all genders, adoptive parents, and all caregivers, not just the birth parent. Things like cost, transportation, and child care can hinder access to alleviating symptoms. name: CARing
description: The Thursday CARing Kids program is a weekly service opportunity for University of Maryland students. The program seeks to provide role models to the elementary school children of Langley Park. This program pairs each child one-on-one with a university student, who is their buddy for the semester. name: En Camino
description: En Camino con la Comunidad is a weekly service opportunity for University of Maryland students. Students are transported by van from campus to an elementary school in Langley Park. University students tutor and mentor elementary school children (pre-k to 6th grade) for several hours. Volunteers help the children with homework, reading, workbooks, crafts and games. As Lutherans, we do En Camino because of a deep sense of God’s call to love and serve our neighbor. However, there is no religious instruction involved in En Camino, and volunteers do not need to have a certain religious orientation to participate or contribute to the program.

name: Overdose Response Training
description: These trainings are designed to prepare UMD community members to respond to alcohol and opioid overdose situations. The trainings run for about an hour, but may run slightly over time, depending on the audience's engagement levels. All training sessions will take place in Room 1150 at the University Health Center, which is located on the First Floor of the building, around the corner from the Pharmacy. At the end of each training, participants will receive a UHC Overdose Response Kit, which includes: two doses of Naloxone (1 box of Narcan), a CPR Face Shield, Fentanyl and Xylazine Test Strips (quantity based on availability), informational flyers, and our signature "Proud to Carry Naloxone" button and sticker. Reminder emails for the training you have registered for will go out approximately 24 hours in advance with reminders about the time and location of the training to the email address provided on the Google Form. Please register for the Overdose Response Training using the following link: Overdose Response Training Registration

description: The John and Stella Graves Makerspace and the Libraries' GIS Team are hosting a student competition highlighting our Augmented Reality Sandbox and its applications across many academic disciplines. There will be a total of 5 topography competitions that will take place in the Fall '23 and Spring '24 semesters. The winner of each monthly competition will receive a $50 Amazon gift card! From November 5th-17th, undergraduate and graduate students are invited to use the AR Sandbox to create and submit a 3D rendering of the provided 2D topographical map. November's map is of the Western Side of Crater Lake, Oregon. Participants' submissions will be judged based on aesthetics and overall accuracy to the reference map. The GIS team will be hosting open hours on Mondays from 2-3pm and Wednesdays from 1-3pm to provide additional support for students creating their map submissions. Submissions can be created outside of these hours, but they are recommended for students who are unfamiliar with reading topography. For full competition rules and submission instructions, see details below. Competition Rules 1. Participants must be currently enrolled undergraduate or graduate students at the University of Maryland, College Park. 2. Each submission should be completed and submitted by one individual student. 3. Each student is allowed only one submission per competition (5 total submissions if a student participates in every iteration of the competition). 4. Each participant will have a maximum of 30 minutes to complete their submission. 5. The winner of the competition will be announced November 20th, 2023 6. The winning submission will be posted to the @umdlibstem Instagram. 7. Before collecting the $50 Amazon gift card prize, the winner will need to provide contact information and a signature for Library documentation. Submission Instructions 1. Book time to use the AR Sandbox here. You will receive an email to confirm your requested time. We may not approve your request if there are conflicting appointments, trainings, or makerspace events. 2. Come to the JSG Makerspace in the STEM Library at your confirmed time. Makerspace staff will help you set up the AR Sandbox to complete your submission. 3. Recreate the 2D topographical map using the AR Sandbox within the 30 minute time limit. 4. Take a picture of both the sandbox itself and the screen projecting your creation's topography. 5. Name your image files in the following format: FirstNameLastName_sandboxsubmission 6. Complete the submission google form, including both photos. 7. Wait to hear if you are our winner! description: During the late spring, summer, and early fall, we have meetings to check on our bees. We learn about sustainable beekeeping practices, what to look for and do while taking care of bees. People who show up to this meeting will have to wear bee-safe clothing such as close toed shoes, and preferably pants, though we have full suits and half suits along with gloves provided. Participants will also have to sign a safety waiver which accepts the possibility of bee stings. When it is too cold or rainy, we go to the UMD Greenhouses to complete workshops such as candles, chapstick, and soap using beeswax. Feel free to reach out through our TerpLink page, our email, or the Discord for more information! The Beekeeping Club does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, religion, age, or physical ability. The Mission of The Beekeeping Club is to educate students about bees and beekeeping through hands-on experience and lectures, about harvesting raw products from them in sustainable ways, and about turning those raw products a variety of goods. The Beekeeping Club seeks to offer anyone with a curiosity or passion for bees and beekeeping the ability to participate in beekeeping regardless of their skill level or prior experience and to guide them in learning more about bees and the role beekeeping plays a sustainable world.

name: International Mother Language Day Celebration
description: This event will be a powerful way to celebrate the Mother Languages of all the students, faculty and staff from different cultures and inspire them to build a community in the spirit of preserving linguistic values and cultural diversity. Besides being the means of communication, language serves to manifest the identity of culture. Through this event, we will invite participants from different cultures to engage in showcasing their languages through performances, music, poetry, art and cuisine. It will allow everyone on campus to discover and embrace new cultures, fostering a deeper understanding of the world around them. We heartily invite individuals from all ethnic backgrounds – students, faculty, and staff – who are eager to connect, celebrate, and honor the diverse linguistic tapestry of our campus. This event will not only spotlight the major languages but also pay homage to the languages of underrepresented groups who endeavor to maintain their linguistic integrity in a majority culture. From the curious students to the researchers at the Language Science Center, our event offers a chance for everyone to dive deep into the richness of linguistic diversity, understand cultural nuances, and foster a leadership mindset ready for a globalized world.

It is strongly recommended that you bring a physical mouse since it can be difficult to work in Unity with a laptop trackpad.

J'ouvert involves calypso/soca bands and their followersdancing in the capital cities of the various islands, with a history going back to the 1800swhen carnival and music were banned by the colonizers in the Caribbean. The festivalstarts well before dawn and peaks a few hours a!er sunrise. Part of the tradition involvessmearing paint, mud, or oil on the participants. name: En'Rage Models Practice
description: Our practice sessions are dynamic and empowering, designed to build confidence, enhance runway skills, and foster creativity in a supportive environment. Each session begins with a warm-up to prepare our models for the physical and mental demands of the runway. Models are then guided through a series of runway walks, where they practice posture, poise, and movement in a variety of styles that challenge traditional norms of fashion and modeling. Throughout the practice, we focus on perfecting choreography for upcoming shows, allowing models to develop their unique flair while staying in sync with the group’s overall performance. Our experienced runway coaches provide individual feedback to ensure that each model feels confident in expressing their own style, aligning with our mission of self-empowerment and diversity. In addition to runway practice, we also incorporate photoshoot preparation, helping models become comfortable in front of the camera, and working on their poses and expressions. Music is played to set the tone, and we regularly rotate different fashion themes to keep practices fresh and engaging. Each session concludes with a debrief, where we emphasize the importance of mutual support and encouragement, celebrating personal growth and teamwork. En'Rage Models practices are more than just rehearsals—they are an opportunity for our members to develop their self-esteem, push creative boundaries, and prepare for the high-energy experience of the runway.

description: The Commuter Small Group is a welcoming community designed specifically for students who commute to campus. This small group creates space for commuters to connect, build friendships, and grow spiritually together in a supportive environment. Each week, the group gathers for a time of conversation, Bible study, and prayer, with a focus on exploring how faith intersects with daily life as a commuter student. Meetings are scheduled at accessible times to fit around commuting schedules and often include shared meals or snacks to foster fellowship. name: Weaving New Worlds: Banner Making Workshop
description: Facilitated by Jadelynn St Dre and Hannah Brancato Co-hosted by the Stamp Gallery and the LGBTQ Equity Center September 29, 4-7 p.m. Exhibition and All Programs are Free and Open to the Public. In this workshop, students will be invited to discuss dreams and visions for a world without sexual violence, rooted in queer histories, wisdom, and brilliance. We will make collaborative banners to be included in the upcoming exhibition at Stamp Gallery: We Will Not Be Silent: Art Transforming Rape Culture, October 30-December 15, 2025. About the facilitators: Jadelynn St Dre is a featured artist in “We Will Not Be Silent.” Her work bridges the intersections of interdisciplinary performance and community support work, creating rituals that highlight interdependence, radical care and resistance. Jadelynn is a Queer, disabled, Latine, cis-femme interdisciplinary performance artist of European and Indigenous descent. With over fifteen years of experience as an organizer and artist in anti-violence spaces, she works to amplify the voices of those often marginalized within mainstream movements. Hannah Brancato is the curator of the exhibition, a current PhD student in American Studies at the University of Maryland, and an artist. Her research focuses on memory work and the role of art in anti-sexual violence movements, and is informed by her role as co-founder FORCE: Upsetting Rape Culture, an art/organizing collective active from 2010-2020, that produced a range of creative interventions to create a culture of consent. FORCE is best known for the Monument Quilt, a collection of 3,000 stories from survivors of sexual violence, written, painted and stitched onto red fabric. Her current collaborative artwork, Dreamseeds, is currently on view at the Baltimore Museum of Art. This workshop is in conjunction with the current exhibition at the Stamp Gallery, "We Will Not Be Silent: Art Transforming Rape Culture," on view from October 30 to December 15, 2025. This exhibition is supported by a Do Good Institute Campus Fund Grant, Arts For All, and the Maryland State Arts Council. Programming is supported by the LGBTQ+ Equity Center and CARE to Stop Violence. Accessibility for this exhibition includes content warnings, sensory objects, tactile artworks, seating, braille labels, and visual descriptions of artworks. Visitors are encouraged to wear a mask while visiting the opening. A full statement of accessibility is available here. Wheelchair accessibility: This workshop is located at the LGBTQ+ Equity Center. The building has automatic door openers but the Equity Center itself does not. Visitors can knock or ring the doorbell and a staff member can help open the door. Marie Mount Hall has elevators to the second floor, where the LGBTQ+ Equity Center is located. Building Navigation: Marie Mount Hall can be difficult to navigate. The Queers with Disabilities student group has made this slideshow to describe how to get to the Equity Center from the front of the building without needing stairs. It's much easier from the back of the building, by the Memorial Chapel (just go in, take the elevator on the left to the 2nd floor, and you're right there). Restrooms: there are men's and women's bathrooms close to the Equity Center at the end of the hall. There is a gender neutral bathroom in the other direction down the hall where it bends to the right. Scents: Please avoid wearing strong scents to the workshop for folks with sensitivity. Community Care: To protect and be in solidarity with those most vulnerable to COVID and other infection, including disabled and immunocompromised folks, participants are encouraged to wear a tight fitting mask while in the gallery, unless you are eating. The Equity center has masks available for any attendees. Trauma informed space: Centering the needs of victims and survivors of trauma, including sexual and intimate partner violence, is essential to this exhibition. name: TNC GBM: Rethinking the Right's Economic Framework with Wells King
description: For many years, the American Right has fully embraced a libertarian economic view. So long as an economic outcome is decided by autonomous individuals, the Right has generally accepted that outcome. In recent years, many on the Right have tried to explore what a more nuanced, conservative economic framework looks like. Wells King, Research Director at American Compass, will talk about the failures of conventional right-of-center economic policy and outline what a truly conservative economic framework looks like.

name: Veterans Yoga
description: Sun Salutations (8/31) Get ready for a class to introduce health and vitality into the semester! This short class includes 20 minutes of cleansing movement fit for yogis of all shapes, sizes, and experience levels. Bonus: Do you not have time to relax and let go for even just a few minutes? Your instructor includes at least five minutes of required shavasana practice at the end of each class to give the mind a break from the rest of the world. Learn a New Pose (9/2) Today’s yoga session will include 18 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out, meaning that yogis of all experience and backgrounds will benefit! Get ready to build strength and resilience with this fun-to learn movement. Relaxation Meditation (9/7) Tuesday’s session will be focused on grounding yourself in this new semester. Just fifteen minutes of passive, yet focused yoga practice will bring you into the moment and out of the stresses of the new semester. Get a Workout in (9/9) After Tuesday’s session focused on relaxation and finding ground in the new semester, it’s time to ramp up the heat. You would never believe what just twenty minutes of poses can do to get that blood pumping and the sweat pouring! Don’t worry, though! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Open the Hips (9/14) We have been in class for a couple of weeks now and our bodies need us to keep moving to stay open and ready for all that life has to offer. Twenty three minutes of opening the hips will keep them from tightening from all the stress and constant sitting motion. Don’t forget! We also include at least five minutes of time to destress and prepare for the rest of the week. Learn a New Pose (9/16) Today’s yoga session will include 24 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out. Yogis of all experience and backgrounds will benefit from this fun practice! Get ready to build some awesome abdominal strength with this sequence. Relaxation Meditation (9/21) Today’s session will be focused on grounding yourself in this new semester. Twenty six minutes of passive, yet focused yoga practice will bring you into the moment and out of the stresses of the semester’s stressors. Getting in a Workout! (9/23) After Tuesday’s session focused on relaxation and finding ground in this awesome in-person semester, it’s time to get that body moving. Just thirty three minutes of poses will get that blood pumping and the sweat pouring! Don’t worry! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Plus, we won’t leave your muscles stiff from the hard work! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for the Booty (9/28) Looking to add cushion and tone to your derriere? Who isn’t?! Today’s session will be devoted to working to add strength to the glutes and hamstrings. Twenty minutes of work will show you some tips and tools to build your important muscle groups that keep your body healthy and moving! Learn a New Pose (9/30) Today’s yoga session will include 25 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out! Even the simplest of poses require detail-orientation! Get ready to build strength and resilience in simple poses. Relaxation Meditation (10/5) Tuesday’s session will be focused on staying sane as the semester continues to pose more difficulties. This is a time for you to take 26 minutes to treat yourself to reduce stress and a little self-care. Get a Workout In (10/7) After Tuesday’s session focused on relaxation and de-stressing, it’s time to move the mind, body, and spirit. Just 34 minutes of yoga flow will get that blood pumping! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in and focused throughout the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Plus, we won’t leave your muscles stiff from the hard work! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for Weak and Tight Shoulders (10/12) We get it. Being an athlete, veteran, human, parent, student, etc. comes with a price. Usually that price is paid in the body. Today we are going to focus on restoring weak and/or tight shoulders. Don’t shy away from class out of fear of injury! There are modifications for all flexibility levels in the shoulders. We are working to improve, not perfect! After all, we only have twenty six minutes! Learn a New Pose (10/14) Today’s yoga session will include 34 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out! Poses that seem difficult from the outside may be a bit simpler than you anticipate! We are focused on safety in strength. So first, we will build strength and confidence. Then we will build upon simple poses to create a beautiful movement to feel proud about. Relaxation Meditation (10/19) We are mid-semester. While it feels like this is the time to be working your butt off with as few breaks as possible, don’t forget about the importance of daily self-care. Today’s class will be nineteen minutes focused on nothing but bringing you back to yourself. This is a time to reclaim the best parts of yourself and create the person you want to be with focused intention. Get a Workout In (10/21) Tuesday got us mentally focused for the week, so now it is time to ramp up the energy to end the week strong! Thirty-one minutes of yoga flow will get that blood pumping! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in and focused. Don’t forget a towel! We will leave your muscles feeling worked, but not too stiff! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for Back Pain (10/26) Is your back constantly feeling stiff? Is the lower back achy and shoulder blades tight? Come to today’s yoga session for the opportunity to release some of that stiffness, and open yourself up to a world of relief! You might be surprised at what a short 33 minutes of stretching and strengthening can do for the body. Learn a New Pose (10/28) Ready to expand your yoga knowledge and experience? Combat those real-time stresses by moving the body and bonding with fellow veterans. Coming to this thirty minute vinyasa class will open the heart to the positivity you need to get you to the end of the semester. As we near the end of the semester, stress increases, the mind wanders, and we lose focus. We will be going through meditation techniques that can be utilized at home, work, or on the bus. Don’t underestimate the power of this 26 minute session. Come join your fellow veterans and enjoy the feeling of a clear mind. Get a Workout In (11/18) After Tuesday’s session focused on de-stressing and refocusing, it’s time to move that body. Just 34 minutes of yoga flow will get that blood pumping! Yoga for Neck Pain (11/23) After months of looking down at our computer screens, it’s no wonder so many of us have the amount of pain in our necks that we do! name: Veterans Yoga
description: Sun Salutations (8/31) Get ready for a class to introduce health and vitality into the semester! This short class includes 20 minutes of cleansing movement fit for yogis of all shapes, sizes, and experience levels. Bonus: Do you not have time to relax and let go for even just a few minutes? Your instructor includes at least five minutes of required shavasana practice at the end of each class to give the mind a break from the rest of the world. Learn a New Pose (9/2) Today’s yoga session will include 18 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out, meaning that yogis of all experience and backgrounds will benefit! Get ready to build strength and resilience with this fun-to learn movement. Relaxation Meditation (9/7) Tuesday’s session will be focused on grounding yourself in this new semester. Just fifteen minutes of passive, yet focused yoga practice will bring you into the moment and out of the stresses of the new semester. Get a Workout in (9/9) After Tuesday’s session focused on relaxation and finding ground in the new semester, it’s time to ramp up the heat. You would never believe what just twenty minutes of poses can do to get that blood pumping and the sweat pouring! Don’t worry, though! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Open the Hips (9/14) We have been in class for a couple of weeks now and our bodies need us to keep moving to stay open and ready for all that life has to offer. Twenty three minutes of opening the hips will keep them from tightening from all the stress and constant sitting motion. Don’t forget! We also include at least five minutes of time to destress and prepare for the rest of the week. Learn a New Pose (9/16) Today’s yoga session will include 24 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out. Yogis of all experience and backgrounds will benefit from this fun practice! Get ready to build some awesome abdominal strength with this sequence. Relaxation Meditation (9/21) Today’s session will be focused on grounding yourself in this new semester. Twenty six minutes of passive, yet focused yoga practice will bring you into the moment and out of the stresses of the semester’s stressors. Getting in a Workout! (9/23) After Tuesday’s session focused on relaxation and finding ground in this awesome in-person semester, it’s time to get that body moving. Just thirty three minutes of poses will get that blood pumping and the sweat pouring! Don’t worry! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Plus, we won’t leave your muscles stiff from the hard work! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for the Booty (9/28) Looking to add cushion and tone to your derriere? Who isn’t?! Today’s session will be devoted to working to add strength to the glutes and hamstrings. Twenty minutes of work will show you some tips and tools to build your important muscle groups that keep your body healthy and moving! Learn a New Pose (9/30) Today’s yoga session will include 25 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out! Even the simplest of poses require detail-orientation! Get ready to build strength and resilience in simple poses. Relaxation Meditation (10/5) Tuesday’s session will be focused on staying sane as the semester continues to pose more difficulties. This is a time for you to take 26 minutes to treat yourself to reduce stress and a little self-care. Get a Workout In (10/7) After Tuesday’s session focused on relaxation and de-stressing, it’s time to move the mind, body, and spirit. Just 34 minutes of yoga flow will get that blood pumping! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in and focused throughout the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Plus, we won’t leave your muscles stiff from the hard work! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for Weak and Tight Shoulders (10/12) We get it. Being an athlete, veteran, human, parent, student, etc. comes with a price. Usually that price is paid in the body. Today we are going to focus on restoring weak and/or tight shoulders. Don’t shy away from class out of fear of injury! There are modifications for all flexibility levels in the shoulders. We are working to improve, not perfect! After all, we only have twenty six minutes! Learn a New Pose (10/14) Today’s yoga session will include 34 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out! Poses that seem difficult from the outside may be a bit simpler than you anticipate! We are focused on safety in strength. So first, we will build strength and confidence. Then we will build upon simple poses to create a beautiful movement to feel proud about. Relaxation Meditation (10/19) We are mid-semester. While it feels like this is the time to be working your butt off with as few breaks as possible, don’t forget about the importance of daily self-care. Today’s class will be nineteen minutes focused on nothing but bringing you back to yourself. This is a time to reclaim the best parts of yourself and create the person you want to be with focused intention. Get a Workout In (10/21) Tuesday got us mentally focused for the week, so now it is time to ramp up the energy to end the week strong! Thirty-one minutes of yoga flow will get that blood pumping! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in and focused. Don’t forget a towel! We will leave your muscles feeling worked, but not too stiff! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for Back Pain (10/26) Is your back constantly feeling stiff? Is the lower back achy and shoulder blades tight? Come to today’s yoga session for the opportunity to release some of that stiffness, and open yourself up to a world of relief! You might be surprised at what a short 33 minutes of stretching and strengthening can do for the body. Learn a New Pose (10/28) Ready to expand your yoga knowledge and experience? Today’s class will revolve around learning a yoga pose through-and-through. There is no reason to worry about the experience level needed for the pose, as all poses learned and performed here can be done at any level! Set aside 33 minutes and get mentally ready to learn reverse warrior so we can add it to your yoga repertoire! Relaxation Meditation (11/2) Meditating on a regular basis has positive effects on the body and mind, such as greater sense of focus, muscle relaxation, and increased creativity. Today’s meditation will be focused on gratitude and increasing happiness. Giving thanks can come in many forms, but have you tried it in the form of meditation?! Getting in a Workout! (11/4) After Tuesday’s session focused on gratitude in this challenging semester, it’s time to get that body moving. Just 34 minutes of sweat-inducing poses will get that blood pumping! This class is fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Plus, we won’t leave your muscles stiff from the hard work! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for a Better Mood (11/9) College is demanding, stressful, and can induce negative feelings! Combat those real-time stresses by moving the body and bonding with fellow veterans. Coming to this thirty minute vinyasa class will open the heart to the positivity you need to get you to the end of the semester. Learn a New Pose (11/11) Ready to expand your yoga knowledge and experience? Today’s class will revolve around learning a yoga pose through-and-through. There is no reason to worry about the experience level needed for the pose, as all poses learned and performed here can be done at any level! Set aside 35 minutes and get mentally ready to learn a new pose to add to your yoga repertoire! Relaxation Meditation (11/16) Today’s meditation practice will be short, sweet, and perfect to regain focus on your workflow. As we near the end of the semester, stress increases, the mind wanders, and we lose focus. We will be going through meditation techniques that can be utilized at home, work, or on the bus. Don’t underestimate the power of this 26 minute session. Come join your fellow veterans and enjoy the feeling of a clear mind. Get a Workout In (11/18) After Tuesday’s session focused on de-stressing and refocusing, it’s time to move that body. Just 34 minutes of yoga flow will get that blood pumping! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in and focused throughout the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Plus, we won’t leave your muscles stiff from the hard work! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for Neck Pain (11/23) After months of looking down at our computer screens, it’s no wonder so many of us have the amount of pain in our necks that we do! Today’s class will be all about de-stressing, communication, and releasing the tension in the neck through yoga practice. Set aside 31 minutes for this perfectly-paced practice.

name: Second Look Fair 2022 - Day 1
description: Whatever your thing is—sports, theater, community service, beekeeping, or just about anything else you can imagine—you have a second chance to find your thing at the Second Look Fair! Due to the global health crisis, this year will be unlike any other as we welcome our students this fall. To ensure the safety of our community, this year’s Second Look Fair will take place online through a passive portion hosted on the Second Look Fair website and live components. If you attend 3 of the Second Look Fair days AND check-in to the Student Involvement Suite at the All Niter (Feb 4), you will be entered to win a prize!

name: KTP Terpzone Social!
description: Kappa Theta Pi is the world's first co-educational professional technology fraternity, and we want to welcome you back to school the right way. We are renting out all of Terpzone from 6-8 pm on February 2, 2022. Come bowl, play pool, or play some video games for free! All are welcome! The only thing we ask is that you take some time to get to know us while you’re here! We’ll be taking full advantage of Terpzone and having some of our own fun the whole time, so feel free to jump in a game! If you have any questions, any of us would be happy to answer them. This would be a great time to get to know our members and the organization ahead of the rush season. We do have about a max capacity of 200 people within Terpzone at one time so we will be letting people in on a first come first serve basis.

name: BlackLight Summit 2022
description: Returning for a second year, The Clarice’s BlackLight Summit aims to activate the unimagined possibilities in dance– a convening that re-envisions dance as a conduit to galvanize resilience and inventiveness. The 2022 summit explores three fundamental inquiries: “What/Who are we Becoming,” “How do we return to one another?” and “Progress does not equal healing, but it can.” Throughout the 2021-22 season, the BlackLight Summit will also continue community connectivity by facilitating a series of mentoring and professional development opportunities, conversations and performances. Register + learn more: go.umd.edu/blacklightsummit2022 Health + Safety There may be COVID safety policies such as mask requirements in place when you attend this event. Please see our health & safety page for the most up to date information about attendance! BlackLight Summit 2022 Artists: Baye & Asa is a company creating movement art projects directed by Amadi ‘Baye’ Washington & Sam ‘Asa’ Pratt. They grew up together in New York City and that shared educational history is the mother of their work. Through the personal dynamics of their brotherhood, they address the larger political landscape of their upbringing, struggling to show a reality of violence while communicating a necessity for empathy. Charlie Maybee is a music and dance artist from Woodbridge, VA. He holds an M.F.A. in Dance from the University of Illinois with a certificate in Criticism and Interpretive Theory, a B.F.A. from Virginia Commonwealth University and is an alumnus of the Metropolitan Youth Tap Ensemble. As an educator, Charlie is currently on faculty at Shenandoah University where he primarily teaches tap dance technique, choreography, history and improvisation. Johnnie Cruise Mercer Recently acknowledged as a 2021 Princess Grace Award Recipent in Choreograpy, and nominated for two 2021 Bessie Awards in Dance and Performance, Johnnie Cruise Mercer is a queer-black think-maker, freelance-performer, educator and social entrepreneur based in New York City. A native of Richmond, VA, Mercer holds a BFA in Dance and Choreography from Virginia Commonwealth University. As the Company Director of Johnnie Cruise Mercer/TheREDprojectNYC, his processes/work has been shared and/or hosted by 92Y Harkness Dance Center, Gibney: Agnes Varis Performing Arts Center, Dixon Place, Danspace Project Inc, The Fusebox Festival, Mana Contemporary, The NADA Conference, Abrons Arts Center and most recently at The Clarice Performing Arts Center's BlackLight Summit. As an educator, Mercer facilitates within the New York Public School system through The Leadership Program-a mentorship-based organization that uses art to foster/engage restorative justice and motivate the true empowerment of self. Mercer has also been on teaching faculty/a guest artist at The American Dance Festival, Bates Dance Festival, PRATT Institute, NYU Tisch Dance Program, Gibney, University of Massachusetts Amherst, DeSales University, Muhlenberg College, the University of Texas at Austin, University of Maryland and The Dance Institute of Washington. Mercer was most recently a 2019-2021 Artist in Residence at Brooklyn Arts Exchange, a 2020-2021 Ping Chong and Company Creative Fellow and a 2020-2021 AIR through New Dance Alliance’s Black Artists Space to Create Residency curated by Angie Pittman. He is currently a 2022 Artist in Residence at Center for Performance Research. Greg David is a movement artist based in the DMV area. Exploring themes of grief, fear, care and solitude, the work and movement they enjoy making goes hand in hand with human emotion and experience and aims to capture that essence in motion. David joinedCulture Shock Washington DC® in 2012 and became the Artistic Director for their 2015 and 2016 seasons where, nationally and internationally, they presented stage works and taught workshops. Kayla Farrish/Decent Structures Arts is an emerging company combining filmmaking, storytelling, dance theater performance and sound score. The company has been commissioned by Gibney Dance Inc (2020-2021), Louis Armstrong House Museum (2020), Danspace Project Inc (2019), Pepatian and BAAD! (2018) and beyond. Kayla has been supported by creative residencies including Gallim Women + Residency (2021), Gibney Spotlight: New Voices, Barysnikov Arts Center and Arts On Site (2020).

name: Lara Downes, Britton-René Collins & Clarice Assad: World Of Change
description: Pianist Lara Downes and composer and multi-instrumentalist Clarice Assad present World of Change, a concert considering the changing climate and the acceleration of our device-intensive existence. In this musical exploration, Clarice and Lara take a step back from the political and international turmoil to consider the wider landscape of our world and to pose self-reflective questions about how we interact with it. Classically trained and having taught in some of Europe’s most prestigious conservatories, Lara Downes now finds herself fully rooted in musical activism and advocacy. Across her 20-year career, she has recorded tributes to Duke Ellington and Billie Holiday, recorded world premieres of works by Florence Price, explored the songbook of Leonard Bernstein and more recently recorded a fascinating alternate history of modern music featuring the voices and works of underrepresented women. A foremost figure in their recent collaborations is Grammy-nominated composer, pianist, vocalist and educator Clarice Assad. A member of a Brazilian musical dynasty who has become one of the Western Hemisphere’s most versatile talents, Clarice has garnered a reputation as a bold singer, captivating pianist, radiant classical guitarist and exploratory composer throughout her career as a prominent voice in the classical, world music, pop and jazz genres. Percussionist Britton-René Collins has dedicated her artistry to shaping an equitable community for all musicians to thrive equally. The Clarice's Visiting Artist Series is committed to providing extensive campus and community engagement opportunities that extend academic learning and cultural opportunities. As part of their residency, Clarice Assad will hold a Composer Colloquium with University of Maryland School of Music student composers and Lara Downes will lead a masterclass with the Collaborative Piano Studio. The duo will also present a Concert in the Quad in partnership with the Arts Scholars program, take part in the School of Music’s Renegade series, lead a percussion masterclass and host both a pre-concert talk and a meet & greet. Health + Safety There may be COVID safety policies such as mask requirements in place when you attend this event. Please see our health & safety page for the most up to date information about attendance!

name: GSO Large Ensemble Concert
description: (Photo by Ken Rubin) Join the Gamer Symphony Orchestra for its triumphant return to stage at its delayed Fall 2021 concerts! This semester, the performance includes pieces from Pokémon, Zelda, League of Legends, Frogger, and much more. Don't miss out - tickets go fast: https://theclarice.umd.edu/events/2022/gamer-symphony-orchestra-large-ensemble-concert. If you can't attend in person, this concert will be streamed on our Twitch channel: https://www.twitch.tv/gamersymphonyumd/. Tickets for the orginal concert dates in December 2021 are no longer valid - please reserve a new ticket to join us in February! The Gamer Symphony Orchestra is a student-run symphonic orchestra at the University of Maryland and the first collegiate ensemble exclusively devoted to performing orchestral arrangements of video game music. Since its establishment in 2005, it has striven to promote video game music as an art form and to continue bringing video game worlds to life through orchestral arrangements - almost all of which are created by its own members. For more information, visit umd.gamersymphony.org. Parking Information For in-person attendance on February 27, guests and performers should park in Lot 1 or in the Union Drive Garage. On Sunday, February 27, 2022 Stadium Drive Garage will be restricted beginning at 12 p.m. and only faculty, staff and basketball permits will be permitted. At 1 p.m., they will begin ticketing and towing vehicles that are in violation. Health + Safety All patrons 12 years of age and older are required to provide proof of vaccination or a negative COVID-19 test result from a test taken within 48 hours of the performance for entry into the venue (home tests will NOT be accepted). Masks must be worn at all times. Please see our Health + Safety page for more information.

name: Virtual Information Session: Global Terrorism Studies Minor Program (04/21/22)
description: Want to know more about START’s Global Terrorism Studies Minor Program? Sign up to attend one of our upcoming information sessions! START has developed an undergraduate minor in Global Terrorism Studies, a cross-disciplinary program housed in the College of Behavioral and Social Sciences at the University of Maryland. The minor is designed to train the next generation of terrorism analysts, including students who plan to pursue graduate study related to terrorism as well as employment in the federal, state, local, non-profit, and/or private sectors. The program is part of the University of Maryland’s Global Studies program, alongside the minors in International Development and Conflict Management, Global Poverty, and Global Engineering Leadership. START accepts applications to the program from University of Maryland undergraduates once per calendar year, during the spring semester. Students from all colleges and majors may apply. We will be offering two info sessions this spring, the first to take place in-person on Tuesday, April 12th, the second virtually on Thursday, April 21st, 2022. The info session will be led by START’s Director of Undergraduate Studies, Dr. Thomas Guarrieri, and START's Education Coordinator, who will discuss how the Global Terrorism Studies Minor Program currently works, what students have to gain from their experience in the program, application requirements, and any other questions attendees may have. This registration is for 6-7 p.m. ET on Thursday, April 21st, 2022. You will receive an email by the morning of the event with detailed information on how to access the webinar in UMD's Zoom platform via a computer or phone.

name: SEE Presents: Free Fall Movie Series - Yesterday
description: SEE invites you to UMD’s own Hoff Theater to unwind and join us for our first Free Fall Movie Series of the 2019-20 school year! Enjoy and support several of this year’s hottest movies along with some classic cultural milestones in a large theatrical setting all semester long!Iron Man (2008)- August 29th @ 8:00pm(Action/Sci-Fi) "After being held captive in an Afghan cave, billionaire engineer Tony Stark creates a unique weaponized suit of armor to fight evil." (IMDb)Guardians of the Galaxy (2014) - August 30th @ 8:00pm(Action/Comedy) "A group of intergalactic criminals must pull together to stop a fanatical warrior with plans to purge the universe." (IMDb)Avengers: Endgame - August 31st @ 8:00pm(Action/Sci-Fi) "After the devastating events of Avengers: Infinity War (2018), the universe is in ruins. With the help of remaining allies, the Avengers assemble once more in order to reverse Thanos' actions and restore balance to the universe." (IMDb)Detective Pikachu - September 5th & 7th @ 8:00pm(Action/Comedy) "In a world where people collect Pokémon to do battle, a boy comes across an intelligent talking Pikachu who seeks to be a detective." (IMDb)Rocketman - September 11th & 12th @ 8:00pm(Biography/Drama) "A musical fantasy about the fantastical human story of Elton John's breakthrough years." (IMDb)Yesterday - September 13th & 14th @ 8:00pm(Comedy/Fantasy) "A struggling musician realizes he's the only person on Earth who can remember The Beatles after waking up in an alternate timeline where they never existed." (IMDb)John Wick: Chapter 3 - Parabellum - September 17th & 19th @ 8:00pm(Action/Crime/Thriller) "Super-assassin John Wick is on the run after killing a member of the international assassin's guild, and with a $14 million price tag on his head - he is the target of hit men and women everywhere." (IMDb)Bill and Ted’s Excellent Adventure (1989): A Special 30th Anniversary Screening - September 21st @ 10:00pm(Adventure/Comedy) "Two seemingly dumb teens set off on a quest to prepare the ultimate historical presentation with the help of a time machine." (IMDb)Midsommar - September 26th & 27th @ 8:00pm(Drama/Horror/Mystery) "A couple travels to Sweden to visit a rural hometown's fabled mid-summer festival. What begins as an idyllic retreat quickly devolves into an increasingly violent and bizarre competition at the hands of a pagan cult." (IMDb)The Rocky Horror Picture Show (1975) - September 28th @ 10:00pm(Comedy/Musical) "A newly engaged couple have a breakdown in an isolated area and must pay a call to the bizarre residence of Dr. Frank-N-Furter." (IMDb)Toy Story 4 - October 3rd & 4th @ 8:00pm(Animation/Comedy) "When a new toy called "Forky" joins Woody and the gang, a road trip alongside old and new friends reveals how big the world can be for a toy." (IMDb)Each screening will be in Hoff Theatre inside the Stamp Student Union. Each screening is open for anyone to attend and doors will open 30 minutues prior to showtime. Seating will be available on a first-come, first serve basis.All weekend movies hosted by Terps After Dark.

name: Hybrid Information Session: Global Terrorism Studies Minor Program (10/27/22)
description: Want to know more about START’s Global Terrorism Studies Minor Program? Sign up to attend one of our upcoming information sessions! This event is free and open to the public, but registration is required. Once you are registered, you will receive the login information before the event. START has developed an undergraduate minor in Global Terrorism Studies, a cross-disciplinary program housed in the College of Behavioral and Social Sciences at the University of Maryland. The minor is designed to train the next generation of terrorism analysts, including students who plan to pursue graduate study related to terrorism as well as employment in the federal, state, local, non-profit, and/or private sectors. The program is part of the University of Maryland’s Global Studies program, alongside the minors in International Development and Conflict Management, Global Poverty, and Global Engineering Leadership. START accepts applications to the program from University of Maryland undergraduates once per calendar year, during the spring semester. Students from all colleges and majors may apply. We will be offering a hybrid info session this Fall on Thursday, October 27th, 2022 at 6:00 PM ET at Tydings Hall 0101 and Online at the same time. The info session will be led by START’s Director of Undergraduate Studies, Dr. Thomas Guarrieri, and START's Education Coordinator, who will discuss how the Global Terrorism Studies Minor Program currently works, what students have to gain from their experience in the program, application requirements, and any other questions attendees may have. You will receive an email by the morning of the event with detailed information on how to access the session in UMD's Zoom platform via a computer or phone.

name: Work with At-Risk Kids: Change Your life!
description: We're gearing up for the best program year yet at the St. Francis Neighborhood Center and we're looking for dedicated volunteers to help in the Power Project, our free after school youth development program that serves the at-risk children of Reservoir Hill. The program starts Monday, Oct. 6 and we're looking for both tutors and program assistants to support staff and help make sure the program is fun for our kids, safe and successful. We know you're busy, but volunteering is important to you, which is why we're flexible and want to make sure your volunteer experience is the very best it can be. If you'd like to volunteer a few hours a week or a few hours a month, we'll make sure your time here is appreciated, valued and FUN! Our youth development program focuses on arts enrichment, academic support, mentoring and tutoring. Positions involve hands-on work with youth ages 5 to 13. Orientation and training are provided. Hours: Monday through Thursday from 3 to 6 pm. Skills: Experience working with children and the ability to volunteer on a regular basis. For more information, please email volunteer@stfranciscenter.org. Our youth development program focuses on arts enrichment, academic support, mentoring and tutoring. Positions involve hands-on work with youth ages 5 to 13. Orientation and training are provided. Hours: Monday through Thursday from 3 to 6 pm. Skills: Experience working with children and the ability to volunteer on a regular basis. For more information, please email volunteer@stfranciscenter.org. About Us: St. Francis Neighborhood Center's mission is committed to breaking the cycles of poverty through education, inspiring self-esteem, self-improvement, and strengthening connections. We provide free academic and arts-based learning programs to community children in addition to mentoring, tutoring and meals.

name: Intro to Augmented Reality Development
description: Movies like Iron Man, Terminator, and Black Panther have long depicted the power of augmented reality. You may have even experienced it for yourself, with apps like Pokémon Go and Snapchat filters. But what if you wanted to make your own AR experience? Surely it must be way too complex for a beginner college student to handle! Wrong! Join the XR Club this Monday as we show you just how easy it is to build your own smartphone AR experience from scratch! We'll be using the new Unity XR Tech Stack, including AR Foundation, a multi-platform framework that connects you to the core underlying capabilities of both smartphone- and headset-based AR platforms, and the XR Interaction Toolkit, which allows you to quickly and easily add common AR/VR interactions into your Unity app. Along the way, you'll also learn about fundamental AR concepts that explain how your devices are able to understand the real-world environment and utilize this information to make your experience feel more realistic and immersive. No prior experience necessary; all majors welcome! Pre-requisites: This workshop requires you to have a variety of special software tools installed prior to attending the workshop. These tools could take 30 mins or longer to download and install, so you will not have enough time during the workshop to install the software without falling behind. For Android: You will need to have Unity 2019.4 (LTS) or later installed along with the Android Build Support module and the options for the Android SDK & NDK Tools and OpenJDK. All of these should be installed with the Unity Hub. You will also need to enable developer options and USB debugging on your phone, as described here. For iOS: You will need to have Unity 2019.4 (LTS) along with the iOS Build Support module. You will also need to install the latest version of Apple's Xcode IDE, which can be found on the Mac App Store. Once you've done that, add your Apple ID account to your Xcode preferences, as described here. Note that the Xcode IDE is only available on Macs. If you have a Windows computer, you will still be able to develop an AR applications in Unity and export it to an Xcode project, but you will not be able to open that Xcode project and deploy the build to an iOS device for testing.

name: Camp PALS Volunteer opportunity
description: Volunteer to be a Counselor for the PALS program Camp PALS this summer. PALS is a nonprofit organization that provides one week long summer camp opportunities for teens and young adults with Down syndrome and their peers at 14 college campuses across the country. This is a one-week experience from 9am-5pm. Listed below are some details about Camp PALS: Here are some details about Camp PALS: - They offer 14 week long sleep-away camps across the country, including Camp PALS Georgetown, Chicago, and North Carolina! - Volunteer counselors are paired one-to-one with a camper to provide an opportunity to build -meaningful friendships through trips and activities - Looking for volunteers ages 16-30 who are welcoming, genuine, passionate, supportive, and fun which are all the values of the program. - No experience with Down syndrome or the disability community is necessary! They encourage groups of applicants to apply together to share the camp experience. If you are interested please visit the website at palsprograms.org/volunteer or check out their social media pages on Facebook or YouTube channel to get a look at what the PALS experience is like. PALS is an amazing opportunity to give back to the community, gain invaluable leadership skills, and make friends that will last a lifetime! There are no costs for volunteers at PALS, and applicants can apply for travel costs to be covered as well. We are looking for male applicants at this point in our season. Females are welcome to apply but will likely be placed on a waitlist. The dates for each of our 15 camps is different based on their locations, but the dates for Baltimore are July 7-13 at UMBC, and Georgetown is July 28-August 3 at Georgetown University.

name: "Nor Any Drop To Drink" Flint Water Crisis Documentary & Discussion Panel
description: What: "Nor Any Drop to Drink" Screening, Discussion Panel & Reception When: Friday, April 5th (4-5pm Reception, 5:00-6:30pm Screening, 6:30 - 7:30pm Discussion Panel) Where: School of Public Health Building, Friedgen Seminar Room 2236 Join us on Friday April, 5, 2019 from 5:00PM to 7:30PM for a screening of "Nor Any Drop to Drink: Flint's Water Crisis." Toxic lead exposure gained national attention in 2014 when it was revealed that residents of Flint, Michigan were being poisoned by the city's drinking water system. Years later, and in the absence of mainstream news media coverage, "Nor Any Drop to Drink" chronicles the ongoing and lasting effects of this crisis. Our panelists will discuss the film, the prevalence of lead exposures throughout the United States--including Maryland--and its disproportionate impacts on communities of color. Panelists: Cedric Taylor, Co-director "Nor Any Drop To Drink"; Krystina White, Chief Operating Officer of Black Millennials 4 Flint; Dr. Janet Phoenix, Assistant Research Professor of the Milken Institute School of Public Health at George Washington University; Dr. Alexander Wooten, Assistant Professor at Morgan State University School of Community Health and Policy Light refreshments will be provided. ----- The documentary, Nor Any Drop to Drink: The Flint Water Crisis, focuses on the water crisis in Flint, Michigan. In 2014, in order to save money, the state switched Flint’s water supply to the heavily polluted Flint River as a cost saving measure. Almost immediately, residents complained of rashes and hair loss. Reports of Legionnaires disease, and elevated lead among children followed. As a result of the heroism and activism of Flint residents and others, belatedly, officials admitted that the water was contaminated. Both Michigan and the federal government declared a state of emergency. In 2016, we were inundated with images contaminated water, bags of hair, protests, and crowded water distribution sites. Today, Flint has largely dropped out of national headlines. However, the horrors faced by many residents still remain. Punctuated by the experiences of ordinary residents, Nor Any Drop to Drink sheds light on how failure of government and economic policy created the Flint water crisis. Nor Any Drop to Drink illuminates the full context of the Flint Water Crisis. Not only is the documentary comprehensive, it gives some insight regarding relatively recent developments in Flint. The film shows why today in Flint, a city in the Great Lakes State, there is neither trust in governmental institutions…nor any drop to drink. Website: https://www.noranydropfilm.com/ Facebook page: https://www.facebook.com/NorAnyDroptoDrink/
location: 4200 Valley Drive, Friedgen Room (Suite 2236), College Park, Maryland, 20742

name: Camp PALS Volunteer opportunity
description: Volunteer to be a Counselor for the PALS program Camp PALS this summer. PALS is a nonprofit organization that provides one week long summer camp opportunities for teens and young adults with Down syndrome and their peers at 14 college campuses across the country. This is a one-week experience from 9am-5pm. Listed below are some details about Camp PALS: Here are some details about Camp PALS: - They offer 14 week long sleep-away camps across the country, including Camp PALS Georgetown, Chicago, and North Carolina! - Volunteer counselors are paired one-to-one with a camper to provide an opportunity to build -meaningful friendships through trips and activities - Looking for volunteers ages 16-30 who are welcoming, genuine, passionate, supportive, and fun which are all the values of the program. - No experience with Down syndrome or the disability community is necessary! They encourage groups of applicants to apply together to share the camp experience. If you are interested please visit the website at palsprograms.org/volunteer or check out their social media pages on Facebook or YouTube channel to get a look at what the PALS experience is like. PALS is an amazing opportunity to give back to the community, gain invaluable leadership skills, and make friends that will last a lifetime! There are no costs for volunteers at PALS, and applicants can apply for travel costs to be covered as well. We are looking for male applicants at this point in our season. Females are welcome to apply but will likely be placed on a waitlist. The dates for each of our 15 camps is different based on their locations, but the dates for Baltimore are July 7-13 at UMBC, and Georgetown is July 28-August 3 at Georgetown University.

name: Overnight Volunteer Position
description: Calvary Women's Services is a transitional housing program for homeless women in Southeast Washington, DC and we love working with UMD students! Our mission is to provide a safe, caring place for tonight; support, hope and change for tomorrow. Overnight Volunteers are needed to supervise our programs from 9:00 pm - 7:00 am, making our residents feel safe and secure. Overnight volunteers are paired with a staff member and are an essential piece to the team that ensures a smooth, quiet night. This volunteer position is ideal for a flexible individual looking to serve in an important role. At night when they arrive, volunteers are responsible for setting out breakfast, welcoming residents arriving late from work or school, and doing a final walkthrough of the facility. In the morning, volunteers facilitate breakfast for residents and make sure clients are up and ready for the day. Volunteer shifts are available all nights of the week. Interested in more information? Contact Arielle Baker, our Community Engagement Coordinator, at 202.678.2341 ext. 233 or abaker@calvaryservices.org.
location: Calvary Women's Services - 1217 Good Hope Road, SE, Washington, DC 20010

name: Debut 2016
description: You are cordially invited to FCA's annual debut! A Filipino Debut is a coming-of-age party, similar to a Quinceanera or Sweet 16, to celebrate a young woman's 18th birthday. This event is meant to give general body members, who have not yet had a debut, an opportunity to experience one. But wait, there's more! Traditionally, aunts and uncles present a meaningful "treasure", or gift, to the debutant that is meant to guide them in life. This year, FCA is donating goods to St. Ann's Center for Children, Youth and Families. We ask guests bring an item, preferably hygienic item, from this list (http://www.stanns.org/donate/wishlist) to the Debut, where we will have a donation box. The class and their respective debutant with the most items will receive a surprise during the event! Please come dressed in your classiest red apparel. Dinner will be provided. We can't wait to see you there. https://www.facebook.com/events/196793474014795/

The night showcases a student produced play featuring both modern and cultural dances, our renowned a cappella ensemble - The Mezzopinoys - and a traditional Filipino dinner. name: Intro to Augmented Reality Development
description: Movies like Iron Man, Terminator, and Black Panther have long depicted the power of augmented reality. You may have even experienced it for yourself, with apps like Pokémon Go and Snapchat filters. But what if you wanted to make your own AR experience? Surely it must be way too complex for a beginner college student to handle! Wrong! Join the XR Club this Monday as we show you just how easy it is to build your own smartphone AR experience from scratch! We'll be using the new Unity XR Tech Stack, including AR Foundation, a multi-platform framework that connects you to the core underlying capabilities of both smartphone- and headset-based AR platforms, and the XR Interaction Toolkit, which allows you to quickly and easily add common AR/VR interactions into your Unity app. Along the way, you'll also learn about fundamental AR concepts that explain how your devices are able to understand the real-world environment and utilize this information to make your experience feel more realistic and immersive. No prior experience necessary; all majors welcome! Pre-requisites: This workshop requires you to have a variety of special software tools installed prior to attending the workshop. These tools could take 30 mins or longer to download and install, so you will not have enough time during the workshop to install the software without falling behind. For Android: You will need to have Unity 2019.4 (LTS) or later installed along with the Android Build Support module and the options for the Android SDK & NDK Tools and OpenJDK. All of these should be installed with the Unity Hub. You will also need to enable developer options and USB debugging on your phone, as described here. For iOS: You will need to have Unity 2019.4 (LTS) along with the iOS Build Support module. You will also need to install the latest version of Apple's Xcode IDE, which can be found on the Mac App Store. Once you've done that, add your Apple ID account to your Xcode preferences, as described here. Note that the Xcode IDE is only available on Macs. If you have a Windows computer, you will still be able to develop an AR applications in Unity and export it to an Xcode project, but you will not be able to open that Xcode project and deploy the build to an iOS device for testing.

name: BlackLight Summit
description: Presented by the Artist Partner Programs at The Clarice, the BlackLight Summit is a year-long dance initiative that investigates how time, people, possibility and hope come together to examine legacy, citizenship and scholarship. The summit asks, through the practice of being socially responsible within the arts: How do we create traditions? How do we transform them into enduring legacies? The peak of the BlackLight Summit is a three-day convening that features roundtable conversations, artistic presentations and student engagement. This initiative re-envisions dance performance as a conduit to galvanize imagination, resilience and inventiveness. Pre-Registration is now open! By signing up, you’ll receive the latest summit news and be the first to know when Summit registration opens in Winter 2021. All events will be able to be experienced virtually. For questions or assistance, contact blacklight-summit@umd.edu.

name: Tracking Emerging Threats and Risk Networks in Eurasia
description: On Wednesday, March 24 at 11:00 a.m. ET, Refinitiv World-Check Senior Research Analyst Liza Layer will provide a virtual talk on “Tracking Emerging Threats and Risk Networks in Eurasia.” This event is free and open to the public, but RSVPs are required. If you have any questions, please email the START events team at start-events@umd.edu. This discussion will explore understanding sanctions networks and emerging threats posed by extremists active in Eurasia. The conversation will provide insights into her investigative work on sanctioned actors and their associates, and the process of tracking terrorists cells operating in Europe. Liza Layer is a Senior Research Analyst for Refinitiv. Her focus areas include terrorism in Russia and Tajikistan, and sanctions related content. In the past, she has worked with Transparency International-Russia and the Woodrow Wilson International Center for Scholars. She holds a BA in International Studies from American University.

name: Walk with an Arborist & Your Baby
organization: University of Maryland Arboretum & Botanical Gardens
description: Walk with an Arborist & Your Baby encourages new parents and caregivers to connect with each other and with the outdoors in a safe space, both physically and emotionally. Based in the Garden of Reflection & Remembrance at the Memorial Chapel, participants learn about trees and plants while having their newborns along. Parental leave and the welcoming of a new child can be lonely and stressful. By offering a tour specifically for new parents and caregivers, participants can interact as much (or as little) as they wish with other adults and have a focus in order to leave the house. According to the National Institutes of Health, one in seven women will develop postpartum depression and many others will still experience feelings of loneliness and isolation during parental leave. These symptoms can affect all genders, adoptive parents, and all caregivers, not just the birth parent. Things like cost, transportation, and child care can hinder access to alleviating symptoms. The Arboretum aims to make the outdoors and public gardens more accessible to everyone, regardless of where they are in life's journey. Registration on the Arboretum website is required: https://arboretum.umd.edu/maps-tours/walk-arborist-your-baby
