name: Global Terps Spring Festival
description: Global Terps Spring Festival will be an opportunity for all UMD students, faculty and staff to learn about and enjoy the immense benefits of living, studying and working in an international/global community such as ours. According to UMD International Student and Scholar Services’ (ISSS) last report (Fall 2018), there were 6,806 international students at UMD --representing a total of 134 countries--, and 1,089 scholars --representing a total of 82 countries. Along with this, many of our additional community members have an international background and/or are interested in learning about and sharing cultures of the world. Regardless of anyone’s background and interests, in a world that is more interconnected than ever before, it is crucial that we all learn from each other's global cultures and experiences and that is the main purpose of the Global Terps Spring Festival. UMD community members will be able to learn and interact while enjoying the following activities: Learning about languages, games, sports, and traditions from around the world. Dance lessons from different communities. Snacks from different cuisines. Arts and crafts from different communities. Global Terps Spring Festival will allow all of us to learn about our rich, global community and prepare us to live, work, travel, and enjoy the many beauties of our interconnected and diverse world.

name: Beekeeping Club Weekly Meeting
description: During the late spring, summer, and early fall, we have meetings to check on our bees. We learn about sustainable beekeeping practices, what to look for and do while taking care of bees. People who show up to this meeting will have to wear bee-safe clothing such as close toed shoes, and preferably pants, though we have full suits and half suits along with gloves provided. Participants will also have to sign a safety waiver which accepts the possibility of bee stings. When it is too cold or rainy, we go to the UMD Greenhouses to complete workshops such as candles, chapstick, and soap using beeswax. Feel free to reach out through our TerpLink page, our email, or the Discord for more information! The Beekeeping Club does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, religion, age, or physical ability. The Mission of The Beekeeping Club is to educate students about bees and beekeeping through hands-on experience and lectures, about harvesting raw products from them in sustainable ways, and about turning those raw products a variety of goods. The Beekeeping Club seeks to offer anyone with a curiosity or passion for bees and beekeeping the ability to participate in beekeeping regardless of their skill level or prior experience and to guide them in learning more about bees and the role beekeeping plays a sustainable world.

description: Registration for Fall Weekend, Winter & Spring Break experiences is open! Alternative Breaks (AB) are week-long service-learning immersion experiences during the university's Winter, Spring, and Summer breaks that address social issues in local, national, and international communities. Students can lead or participate in the experiences, and there are mentoring opportunities for faculty & staff! Alternative Break Experiences focus on exploring a range of issues including - but not limited to - environmental conservation, education, socioeconomic inequality, healthcare, and more! Alternative Break participants travel to communities all over the country and internationally. Interested students must be willing & able to commit to the full duration of the experience and any pre-trip meetings organized by the trip’s Experience Leaders: Alternative Weekend Experience: Friday, October 4th - Sunday, October 6th, 2024Alternative Winter Break Experiences: Wednesday, January 8th - Saturday, January 18th, 2025Alternative Spring Break Experiences: Saturday, March 15th - Saturday, March 22nd, 2025. Students will participate in deliberative and reflective dialogues, direct service, and meaningful education, where they will exchange, evaluate, and take action towards different ideas and approaches that challenge specific social, political and economic structures of our domestic & global communities. Direct service with community partners will demonstrate how students can turn their knowledge into action in safe, responsible, and sustainable ways. description: Weed Warriors on Campus is a volunteer event for UMD students, faculty, staff, and community members that hosts educational invasive species removal events. Removing these species will improve the health of our native trees and plants, as well as the insects, birds, and animals that our native plants support. Weed Warriors on Campus is a great way to get outdoors on campus and meet other people that care about the environment!

name: Badge Making
description: Do YOU have a badge? If not, come on down and get one! An important aspect of furry culture are badges. Badges are a way to show off one’s own art or commissioned art and more importantly an individual's “fursona”. A fursona (furry + persona) is a personalized character created by someone in the furry community. They represent the combination of a furry’s individual identity and an anthropomorphic character. Badges typically show off artwork of your fursona and your fursona’s name. This is important because these things can help distinguish you from others at either furry meetups or conventions. This event will allow members to show off their artwork and have an easier experience at furry conventions and meet ups within the club by creating their own custom printed badges. No fees will be required to attend. The event will be open to all Unifursity Furries club members as well as any other interested UMD students.

name: En Camino
description: En Camino con la Comunidad is a weekly service opportunity for University of Maryland students. Students are transported by van from campus to an elementary school in Langley Park. University students tutor and mentor elementary school children (pre-k to 6th grade) for several hours. Volunteers help the children with homework, reading, workbooks, crafts and games. name: How to Prepare For an Interview
organization: University Career Center & The Presidents Promise
description: Interviewing takes practice and interviews do not need to be perfect. You will say "um” at certain points. You will get caught off-guard by an unexpected interview question and will need some time to think through how to best answer it. You may need to ask the interviewer to repeat a question because you want to make sure you understood it correctly. These scenarios are okay! We are human. The key is to be prepared and be yourself throughout the interview process.In this session, we will discuss: The different types of interviews (live phone/virtual, asynchronous, case, technical, etc) and quick tips to prepare for each. Overall, however, this workshop will focus on behavioral-based interviewing tips. What to know about an employer and the position before stepping foot into the interview or joining that Zoom call. How to think through and articulate your “power stories” - the stories you anticipate will come up in an interview and how to share that story in a way an outsider (i.e. the interviewer) will understand and appreciate. Additional ways to prepare for upcoming interviews. This workshop will be conducted virtually on a monthly basis through the University Career Center & The President's Promise. If this date doesn’t work for you, check out Handshake for future offerings.In addition to this workshop, students have access to Big Interview in Handshake to practice interview questions on your own time. name: How to Prepare For an Interview
organization: University Career Center & The Presidents Promise
description: Interviewing takes practice and interviews do not need to be perfect. You will say "um” at certain points. You will get caught off-guard by an unexpected interview question and will need some time to think through how to best answer it. You may need to ask the interviewer to repeat a question because you want to make sure you understood it correctly. These scenarios are okay! We are human. The key is to be prepared and be yourself throughout the interview process.In this session, we will discuss: The different types of interviews (live phone/virtual, asynchronous, case, technical, etc) and quick tips to prepare for each. Overall, however, this workshop will focus on behavioral-based interviewing tips. What to know about an employer and the position before stepping foot into the interview or joining that Zoom call. How to think through and articulate your “power stories” - the stories you anticipate will come up in an interview and how to share that story in a way an outsider (i.e. the interviewer) will understand and appreciate. Additional ways to prepare for upcoming interviews. This workshop will be conducted virtually on a monthly basis through the University Career Center & The President's Promise. If this date doesn’t work for you, check out Handshake for future offerings.In addition to this workshop, students have access to Big Interview in Handshake to practice interview questions on your own time. name: National Hillel Basketball Tournament 2025
description: The National Hillel Basketball Tournament (NHBT) was founded in 2010 to bring Jewish students together around the inclusive and encompassing game of basketball. Solely organized by a board of 30 highly motivated students, what began as a small event has quickly developed into one of the largest collegiate gatherings of Jewish students in the country. Now in its 13th year, the non-profit initiative, annually housed in the University of Maryland’s state-of-the-art facilities, attracts over 1,500 participants from across the United States and Canada. This year, we expect over 50 teams from over 30 universities across North America to partake in the weekend-long tournament experience. Players and fans also participate in various off-the-court programs such as Shabbat meals, keynote speakers, and an exciting bar night to kick the weekend off. In addition to NHBT’s impressive scale and reach, its impact has reached new heights in recent years. By providing students a chance to meet, socialize, and compete in a positive Jewish environment, NHBT serves as an oasis for students experiencing antisemitism on their respective campuses. By platforming like-minded organizations and starting initiatives, NHBT has provided a beacon of hope and togetherness for Jewish and campus communities far and wide.

name: En'Rage Models Practice
description: Our practice sessions are dynamic and empowering, designed to build confidence, enhance runway skills, and foster creativity in a supportive environment. Each session begins with a warm-up to prepare our models for the physical and mental demands of the runway. Models are then guided through a series of runway walks, where they practice posture, poise, and movement in a variety of styles that challenge traditional norms of fashion and modeling. Throughout the practice, we focus on perfecting choreography for upcoming shows, allowing models to develop their unique flair while staying in sync with the group’s overall performance. Our experienced runway coaches provide individual feedback to ensure that each model feels confident in expressing their own style, aligning with our mission of self-empowerment and diversity. In addition to runway practice, we also incorporate photoshoot preparation, helping models become comfortable in front of the camera, and working on their poses and expressions. Music is played to set the tone, and we regularly rotate different fashion themes to keep practices fresh and engaging. Each session concludes with a debrief, where we emphasize the importance of mutual support and encouragement, celebrating personal growth and teamwork. En'Rage Models practices are more than just rehearsals—they are an opportunity for our members to develop their self-esteem, push creative boundaries, and prepare for the high-energy experience of the runway.

name: Commuter Small Group
description: The Commuter Small Group is a welcoming community designed specifically for students who commute to campus. We recognize that commuter students often face unique challenges—such as limited time on campus, balancing home and school responsibilities, and difficulty finding consistent community. This small group creates space for commuters to connect, build friendships, and grow spiritually together in a supportive environment. Each week, the group gathers for a time of conversation, Bible study, and prayer, with a focus on exploring how faith intersects with daily life as a commuter student. Meetings are scheduled at accessible times to fit around commuting schedules and often include shared meals or snacks to foster fellowship. name: Life of a Neuron Immersive Exhibition
description: Walk through a neuron—the “thinking cells” of the brain—and witness first-hand the beauty of one of science’s greatest mysteries: the human brain. - ARTECHOUSE Join the XR Club on Friday, November 19 as we visit ARTECHOUSE for their latest and greatest exhibition: The Life of a Neuron. ARTECHOUSE is an innovative art destination dedicated to the intersection of art, science and technology. Their exhibits are immersive in nature, allowing for 360-degree immersion, and are enhanced by an XR mobile app, which allows visitors to scan augmented reality (AR) markers throughout the exhibit and unlock hidden AR features. The current exhibition on display at ARTECHOUSE's DC location is Life of a Neuron, which brings artists and scientists together for a groundbreaking collaboration to explore how the brain shapes the shared human experience. Through their collaboration with the Society for Neuroscience and the world’s leading scientists and creatives, this immersive exhibit will allow us to experience a neuron—from pre-birth to death—providing an experiential view of life at a cellular level. This exhibition is a perfect demonstration of how XR technology can be used as a tool to visualize difficult concepts. Eligibility Requirements: All attendees of this program must be undergraduate students who are members of the XR Club, as listed on our TerpLink roster. Attendance will be limited to the first 30 members who RSVP to this event. Once registration has filled up, students may be added to a waitlist. Student on the waitlist will be contacted in the event of any cancellations and are encouraged to stop by check-in in the event of any no-shows. Any student who cancels their registration within 24 hours of the event or does not show up to the event may be ineligible to attend any future funded off-campus events for this school year. Event Details: 5:00 PM - Gather at XR Club Lab (AVW 4176) to check-in members 5:15 PM - Board bus in parking lot GG1 (behind AVW) 6:15 PM - Arrive at ARTECHOUSE DC 6:30 PM - Exhibition Starts 7:30 PM - Exhibition Ends, visit gift shop 7:45 PM - Board bus 8:30 PM - Arrive back at UMD Cost Tickets and transportation are being provided FREE of charge, thanks to the generosity of the UMD SGA!

name: Rich Kids: A History of Shopping Malls in Tehran (UK)
description: Around the world, the gap between rich and poor continues to widen. Images of the children of the elite and of post-colonial dictatorships often feature cash and seaside holidays while the working population suffers under sanctions and dictatorships. In this virtual presentation, The Javaad Alipoor Company’s Rich Kids: A History of Shopping Malls in Tehran explores entitlement and greedy consumption, as well as the role of digital technology, in creating this new apartheid and gentrification. As the performance is completely live streamed, audiences can access the performance from the comfort of their own homes with a supplemental experience on Instagram that is not required, but highly recommended! Always taking stories beyond the stage through powerful multi-platform creations, The Javaad Alipoor Company explores the intersection of politics and technology in our ever-changing world. The company is devoted to creating works for diverse audiences and communities, and their 2021-22 virtual visit with The Clarice will include an Arts Citizenship Talk (ACTnow), visits to the UMD School of Theatre, Dance, and Performance Studies and a dynamic partnership with UMD’s Roshan Institute for Persian Studies. In 2017, the company began writing a trilogy that highlights society’s fracturing identities and technology’s impact on the world; Rich Kids is the second installment.

This short class includes 20 minutes of cleansing movement fit for yogis of all shapes, sizes, and experience levels. Bonus: Do you not have time to relax and let go for even just a few minutes? Your instructor includes at least five minutes of required shavasana practice at the end of each class to give the mind a break from the rest of the world. Get ready to build strength and resilience with this fun-to learn movement. Relaxation Meditation (9/7) Tuesday’s session will be focused on grounding yourself in this new semester. Just fifteen minutes of passive, yet focused yoga practice will bring you into the moment and out of the stresses of the new semester. Get a Workout in (9/9) After Tuesday’s session focused on relaxation and finding ground in the new semester, it’s time to ramp up the heat. You would never believe what just twenty minutes of poses can do to get that blood pumping and the sweat pouring! Don’t worry, though! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Twenty three minutes of opening the hips will keep them from tightening from all the stress and constant sitting motion. Don’t forget! We also include at least five minutes of time to destress and prepare for the rest of the week. Learn a New Pose (9/16) Today’s yoga session will include 24 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out. Yogis of all experience and backgrounds will benefit from this fun practice! Get ready to build some awesome abdominal strength with this sequence. Relaxation Meditation (9/21) Today’s session will be focused on grounding yourself in this new semester. Twenty six minutes of passive, yet focused yoga practice will bring you into the moment and out of the stresses of the semester’s stressors. Getting in a Workout! This is a time to reclaim the best parts of yourself and create the person you want to be with focused intention. This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in and focused. Don’t forget a towel! Yoga for Back Pain (10/26) Is your back constantly feeling stiff? Is the lower back achy and shoulder blades tight? Today’s class will revolve around learning a yoga pose through-and-through. There is no reason to worry about the experience level needed for the pose, as all poses learned and performed here can be done at any level! Set aside 33 minutes and get mentally ready to learn reverse warrior so we can add it to your yoga repertoire! Today’s meditation will be focused on gratitude and increasing happiness. Giving thanks can come in many forms, but have you tried it in the form of meditation?! Getting in a Workout! This class is fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Plus, we won’t leave your muscles stiff from the hard work! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for a Better Mood (11/9) College is demanding, stressful, and can induce negative feelings! Combat those real-time stresses by moving the body and bonding with fellow veterans. Coming to this thirty minute vinyasa class will open the heart to the positivity you need to get you to the end of the semester. There is no reason to worry about the experience level needed for the pose, as all poses learned and performed here can be done at any level! Set aside 35 minutes and get mentally ready to learn a new pose to add to your yoga repertoire! Relaxation Meditation (11/16) Today’s meditation practice will be short, sweet, and perfect to regain focus on your workflow. As we near the end of the semester, stress increases, the mind wanders, and we lose focus. We will be going through meditation techniques that can be utilized at home, work, or on the bus. Don’t underestimate the power of this 26 minute session. Come join your fellow veterans and enjoy the feeling of a clear mind. Get a Workout In (11/18) After Tuesday’s session focused on de-stressing and refocusing, it’s time to move that body. Just 34 minutes of yoga flow will get that blood pumping! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in and focused throughout the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Plus, we won’t leave your muscles stiff from the hard work! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for Neck Pain (11/23) After months of looking down at our computer screens, it’s no wonder so many of us have the amount of pain in our necks that we do! Today’s class will be all about de-stressing, communication, and releasing the tension in the neck through yoga practice. Set aside 31 minutes for this perfectly-paced practice.

name: Soldiers of End-Times: Assessing the Military Effectiveness of the Islamic State
description: On Thursday, March 3 at 12:00 p.m. ET, Washington Institute for Near East Policy Associate Fellow Ido Levy will provide a virtual talk on his book, Soldiers of End-Times: Assessing the Military Effectiveness of the Islamic State. This event is free and open to the public, but RSVPs are required. If you have any questions, please email the START events team at start-events@umd.edu. In 2014, the Islamic State shocked the world when it defeated national armies on the battlefield and seized large swaths of territory in Iraq and Syria. The group’s military success can be traced to four key variables: organizational innovation, shaping operations, will to fight, and a knack for retaining the initiative. The IS military project led not only to the declaration of a “caliphate,” but to the proliferation of jihadist franchises that devastated countries, displaced millions, and killed tens of thousands. Yet the group’s weaknesses ultimately led to the collapse of its territorial achievement. Expert Ido Levy begins this pioneering study by surveying jihadist warfare from the 1970s to the present. He then incorporates primary sources and interviews with military officers, experts, and journalists to explain how IS used conventional military capabilities to defeat larger, better-equipped state armies and conquer land in Syria, Iraq, Libya, the Philippines, and Nigeria. Anchored by four case studies—Ramadi, Kobane, Mosul, and Baghuz—the volume illuminates potential strategies to prevent a resurgence by IS or similar groups. Ido Levy is an associate fellow working with the Washington Institute for Near East Policy’s Military and Security Studies Program. He holds a Master of Public Policy from Georgetown University’s McCourt School of Public Policy. He is the author of the book Soldiers of End-Times: Assessing the Military Effectiveness of the Islamic State, now available as a free ebook. For universities, research centers, libraries, and other institutions, free hard copies of the book are available upon request. In 2015, Levy studied Arabic at Givat Haviva, Israel and, in 2018, received his B.A. summa cum laude in government, counter-terrorism, and global affairs from IDC Herzliya. In Israel, he researched radicalization and deradicalization programs at the International Institute for Counter-Terrorism (ICT) and Iraqi political affairs at the Institute for National Security Studies (INSS). During his graduate studies, Levy conducted further research on Iraq and other countries in the Middle East at the Council on Foreign Relations (CFR) and ideologies and lethality rates of terrorist groups at the START Consortium. He was also a research and teaching assistant at the McCourt School of Public Policy and the editor-in-chief of the Georgetown Public Policy Review. His work has appeared in ICT, Studies in Conflict & Terrorism, Middle East Policy, Terrorism and Political Violence, Small Wars Journal, NBC, Jerusalem Post, The Forward, and other publications. He is fluent in Hebrew and speaks Arabic at an advanced level.

name: St. Lawrence String Quartet with Osvaldo Golijov
description: In the more than three decades since their inception, the St. Lawrence String Quartet (SLSQ) has risen to prominence in international competitions and concert halls for their electrifying performances, ever-expanding repertoire and dedication to engagement with audiences, composers and emerging artists. With performances hailed as, “wickedly attentive” (The Gazette, Montreal) and “with a hint of rock ‘n roll energy” (LA Times), the Grammy-nominated quartet has thrilled listeners with their rousing interpretations of music by Schumann, Tchaikovsky, Haydn, Adams and Golijov. Residencies at renowned institutions such as Stanford University and Spoleto Festival USA along with collaborations with Michael Tilson Thomas and the San Francisco Symphony, Gustavo Dudamel and the LA Philharmonic and Marin Alsop and the Baltimore Symphony have reimagined the role of chamber music in the lives of concertgoers, students and young artists. The 2021-22 season unveils their latest creation and collaborative endeavor with composer Osvaldo Golijov. The new octet for strings is a generously-crafted work for the St. Lawrence String Quartet and four locally based string players, highlighting a once-in-a-career opportunity for exceptional student artists or orchestral leaders in communities across North America. The performance at The Clarice will feature members of the Thalea Quartet, the School of Music’s Fellowship String Quartet. As conceived by Golijov, this chamber music experiment will, "explore the dimensions opened by combining an organism with its own breathing and metabolism, like a string quartet, (especially one that is "mature" as SLSQ) together with four individual players that come to orbit, interact and disrupt this organism.” While visiting The Clarice, members of the St. Lawrence String Quartet and Osvaldo Golijov will visit the UMD School of Music’s Chamber Music Class, rehearse and perform works by student composers and will lead a pre-concert talk.

name: Veterans Yoga
description: Sun Salutations (8/31) Get ready for a class to introduce health and vitality into the semester! This short class includes 20 minutes of cleansing movement fit for yogis of all shapes, sizes, and experience levels. Bonus: Do you not have time to relax and let go for even just a few minutes? Your instructor includes at least five minutes of required shavasana practice at the end of each class to give the mind a break from the rest of the world. Learn a New Pose (9/2) Today’s yoga session will include 18 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out, meaning that yogis of all experience and backgrounds will benefit! Get ready to build strength and resilience with this fun-to learn movement. Relaxation Meditation (9/7) Tuesday’s session will be focused on grounding yourself in this new semester. Just fifteen minutes of passive, yet focused yoga practice will bring you into the moment and out of the stresses of the new semester. Get a Workout in (9/9) After Tuesday’s session focused on relaxation and finding ground in the new semester, it’s time to ramp up the heat. You would never believe what just twenty minutes of poses can do to get that blood pumping and the sweat pouring! Don’t worry, though! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Open the Hips (9/14) We have been in class for a couple of weeks now and our bodies need us to keep moving to stay open and ready for all that life has to offer. Twenty three minutes of opening the hips will keep them from tightening from all the stress and constant sitting motion. Don’t forget! We also include at least five minutes of time to destress and prepare for the rest of the week. Learn a New Pose (9/16) Today’s yoga session will include 24 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out. Yogis of all experience and backgrounds will benefit from this fun practice! Get ready to build some awesome abdominal strength with this sequence. Relaxation Meditation (9/21) Today’s session will be focused on grounding yourself in this new semester. Twenty six minutes of passive, yet focused yoga practice will bring you into the moment and out of the stresses of the semester’s stressors. Getting in a Workout! (9/23) After Tuesday’s session focused on relaxation and finding ground in this awesome in-person semester, it’s time to get that body moving. Just thirty three minutes of poses will get that blood pumping and the sweat pouring! Don’t worry! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Plus, we won’t leave your muscles stiff from the hard work! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for the Booty (9/28) Looking to add cushion and tone to your derriere? Who isn’t?! Today’s session will be devoted to working to add strength to the glutes and hamstrings. Twenty minutes of work will show you some tips and tools to build your important muscle groups that keep your body healthy and moving! Learn a New Pose (9/30) Today’s yoga session will include 25 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out! Even the simplest of poses require detail-orientation! Get ready to build strength and resilience in simple poses. Relaxation Meditation (10/5) Tuesday’s session will be focused on staying sane as the semester continues to pose more difficulties. This is a time for you to take 26 minutes to treat yourself to reduce stress and a little self-care. Get a Workout In (10/7) After Tuesday’s session focused on relaxation and de-stressing, it’s time to move the mind, body, and spirit. Just 34 minutes of yoga flow will get that blood pumping! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in and focused throughout the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Plus, we won’t leave your muscles stiff from the hard work! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for Weak and Tight Shoulders (10/12) We get it. Being an athlete, veteran, human, parent, student, etc. comes with a price. Usually that price is paid in the body. Today we are going to focus on restoring weak and/or tight shoulders. Don’t shy away from class out of fear of injury! There are modifications for all flexibility levels in the shoulders. We are working to improve, not perfect! After all, we only have twenty six minutes! Learn a New Pose (10/14) Today’s yoga session will include 34 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out! Poses that seem difficult from the outside may be a bit simpler than you anticipate! We are focused on safety in strength. So first, we will build strength and confidence. Then we will build upon simple poses to create a beautiful movement to feel proud about. Relaxation Meditation (10/19) We are mid-semester. While it feels like this is the time to be working your butt off with as few breaks as possible, don’t forget about the importance of daily self-care. Today’s class will be nineteen minutes focused on nothing but bringing you back to yourself. This is a time to reclaim the best parts of yourself and create the person you want to be with focused intention. Get a Workout In (10/21) Tuesday got us mentally focused for the week, so now it is time to ramp up the energy to end the week strong! Thirty-one minutes of yoga flow will get that blood pumping! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in and focused. Don’t forget a towel! We will leave your muscles feeling worked, but not too stiff! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for Back Pain (10/26) Is your back constantly feeling stiff? Is the lower back achy and shoulder blades tight? Come to today’s yoga session for the opportunity to release some of that stiffness, and open yourself up to a world of relief! You might be surprised at what a short 33 minutes of stretching and strengthening can do for the body. Learn a New Pose (10/28) Ready to expand your yoga knowledge and experience? Today’s class will revolve around learning a yoga pose through-and-through. There is no reason to worry about the experience level needed for the pose, as all poses learned and performed here can be done at any level! Set aside 33 minutes and get mentally ready to learn reverse warrior so we can add it to your yoga repertoire! Relaxation Meditation (11/2) Meditating on a regular basis has positive effects on the body and mind, such as greater sense of focus, muscle relaxation, and increased creativity. Today’s meditation will be focused on gratitude and increasing happiness. Giving thanks can come in many forms, but have you tried it in the form of meditation?! Getting in a Workout! (11/4) After Tuesday’s session focused on gratitude in this challenging semester, it’s time to get that body moving. Just 34 minutes of sweat-inducing poses will get that blood pumping! This class is fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Plus, we won’t leave your muscles stiff from the hard work! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for a Better Mood (11/9) College is demanding, stressful, and can induce negative feelings! Combat those real-time stresses by moving the body and bonding with fellow veterans. Coming to this thirty minute vinyasa class will open the heart to the positivity you need to get you to the end of the semester. Learn a New Pose (11/11) Ready to expand your yoga knowledge and experience? Today’s class will revolve around learning a yoga pose through-and-through. There is no reason to worry about the experience level needed for the pose, as all poses learned and performed here can be done at any level! Set aside 35 minutes and get mentally ready to learn a new pose to add to your yoga repertoire! Relaxation Meditation (11/16) Today’s meditation practice will be short, sweet, and perfect to regain focus on your workflow. As we near the end of the semester, stress increases, the mind wanders, and we lose focus. We will be going through meditation techniques that can be utilized at home, work, or on the bus. Don’t underestimate the power of this 26 minute session. Come join your fellow veterans and enjoy the feeling of a clear mind. Get a Workout In (11/18) After Tuesday’s session focused on de-stressing and refocusing, it’s time to move that body. Just 34 minutes of yoga flow will get that blood pumping! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in and focused throughout the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Plus, we won’t leave your muscles stiff from the hard work! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for Neck Pain (11/23) After months of looking down at our computer screens, it’s no wonder so many of us have the amount of pain in our necks that we do! Today’s class will be all about de-stressing, communication, and releasing the tension in the neck through yoga practice. Set aside 31 minutes for this perfectly-paced practice.

description: Whatever your thing is—sports, theater, community service, beekeeping, or just about anything else you can imagine—you have a second chance to find your thing at the Second Look Fair! Due to the global health crisis, this year will be unlike any other as we welcome our students this fall. Americana is the Student Archivists at Maryland (SAM) annual symposium that brings archives professionals back to campus to speak to UMD iSchool students, alumni, faculty, area professionals, and the general public about their experiences in the field. This event is always a meaningful, substantive celebration of the University of Maryland archival community and the richness of the archival field. This year’s Americana explores the delicate but constant relationship between the archivist, the public, and the record. Please join us for Americana 2017: Archives and Public Memory in a Post-Truth World! #americana17 The event will begin with a reception from 5:00-5:30, during which light refreshments will be served. The presentation will begin at 5:30, followed by a question-and-answer session. Alumni Award In addition, we will be presenting our Distinguished Archives Alumni Award to Laura Starr '09, MLS and MA, History, Senior Archivist at History Associates Incorporated. This event is free and open to all students and to the general public. This event is funded in part by your Graduate Student Activities Fee. We would like to thank our co-sponsor, the iSchool Alumni Chapter.

They need your help to get the job done. Requirements Waiver: We require that you pre-register for our events, so that you can fill out our waiver before arriving at the event. Youth Volunteers: Volunteers under 18 years of age must have their parent or legal guardian sign their consent form and be supervised by an adult at all times. Please note you must be over 18 years of age to become a team leader. Closed-toe shoes: Boots are preferred over sneakers. No specific skills or tools required. Each event starts with a tool safety and planting demonstration. Volunteers plant alongside experienced Citizen Foresters and staff. Arrive on time and stay for the duration of the event. Dress comfortably and appropriately for the weather. We recommend long pants and other protections for sun, bugs and poison ivy. No animals are allowed into the event, except for service animals. Water: Bring a water bottle or reusable cup to refill. Water will be available on site. What to expect on site: Sign-In opens at 8:30am Tool safety demo is at 8:45am - If you miss the demo you cannot participate in the tree planting Team leaders are announced and you begin working with your team Plant 2-6 trees with your team End with a celebratory lunch with your team and all that planted that day! Meet in the Ground Floor Lounge NO LATER than 8:00am so that you can arrive by 8:30am for check-in. Driver Needed - please indicate in your RSVP if you can drive. Reflection Leader Needed - please indicate in your RSVP if you can serve as Reflection Leader. If you must cancel your participation within 5 days of the project date, you are responsible for finding a substitute and notifying us (you may leave a comment below). name: Alternative Breaks | Fall 2020 Participant Application Open!
description: What does student social justice work look like in a world where our campus is predominantly operating online? How do we connect meaningfully and sustainably with one another in a virtual environment? If you’ve been asking yourself these questions, Alternative Breaks’ adapted programming might be the perfect fit for you. This fall, in the interest of ensuring the health and safety of all our participants and Experience Leaders, Alternative Breaks has created a FREE semester-long fully virtual experience focused on empowering students to learn in community with one another and take action toward just causes. The Alternative Breaks Dialogue Program will consist of intentional and reflective dialogues addressing global social issues. Each team will be diving deeply into a particular social issue area by evaluating resources together, engaging with the topic in individual and global contexts, and seeking an active role in social justice. Issue areas will include Environmental Conservation, Education, Ability, Socioeconomic Equity, Health and Wellness, and Food Insecurity. Facilitators will be diving deep into a specific aspect of their issue area as they move through the dialogue sessions. These dialogues will take place once a week for five weeks between October 19th, 2020 and November 16th, 2020. Each weekly session will be 1.5 hours long, and students must be able to commit to all of the dialogue sessions in their series to participate. Participant applications open Sunday, September 20th, 2020! If you have any questions or need more information, email alternativebreaks@umd.edu or check out our website at Alternativebreaks.umd.edu.

We’ll spend the first day whitewater kayaking on the class II Middle Yough and spend the second day whitewater rafting on the class III Lower Yough. name: Camp PALS Volunteer opportunity
description: Volunteer to be a Counselor for the PALS program Camp PALS this summer. PALS is a nonprofit organization that provides one week long summer camp opportunities for teens and young adults with Down syndrome and their peers at 14 college campuses across the country. This is a one-week experience from 9am-5pm. Listed below are some details about Camp PALS: Here are some details about Camp PALS: - They offer 14 week long sleep-away camps across the country, including Camp PALS Georgetown, Chicago, and North Carolina! - Volunteer counselors are paired one-to-one with a camper to provide an opportunity to build -meaningful friendships through trips and activities - Looking for volunteers ages 16-30 who are welcoming, genuine, passionate, supportive, and fun which are all the values of the program. - No experience with Down syndrome or the disability community is necessary! They encourage groups of applicants to apply together to share the camp experience. If you are interested please visit the website at palsprograms.org/volunteer or check out their social media pages on Facebook or YouTube channel to get a look at what the PALS experience is like. PALS is an amazing opportunity to give back to the community, gain invaluable leadership skills, and make friends that will last a lifetime! There are no costs for volunteers at PALS, and applicants can apply for travel costs to be covered as well. We are looking for male applicants at this point in our season. Females are welcome to apply but will likely be placed on a waitlist. The dates for each of our 15 camps is different based on their locations, but the dates for Baltimore are July 7-13 at UMBC, and Georgetown is July 28-August 3 at Georgetown University.

name: Intro to VR Development (Part II)
description: In this beginner-friendly workshop series, you will learn the basics of developing virtual reality (VR) experiences using Unity's cross-platform XR Interaction Toolkit as you create a simple Beat Saber VR clone from start to finish. In this second episode of the workshop series, you will integrate spatial audio and haptic feedback to enable more immersive interactions and learn how to transform user interfaces (UIs) to work well in a 3D environment as you create menus and score displays for your game. NOTES: This workshop requires you to bring a computer with Unity 2021.2 installed along with the Android Build Support module and the options for the Android SDK & NDK Tools and OpenJDK. All of these must be installed with the Unity Hub, even if you have other versions on your computer. The Unity Editor could take 30 mins or longer to download and install, so you will not have enough time during the workshop to install the software without falling behind. It is recommended you install the software well in advance of the workshop. It is strongly recommended that you bring a physical mouse since it can be difficult to work in Unity with a laptop trackpad. As per University guidelines, all attendees of this event will be required to wear KN95 masks. Violators will be denied entry into the event.

AEES along with alumni, students, campus groups, and faculty are joining together to purchase LEAFhouse and keep it on campus to be used as a resource for student clubs now and in the future. For more information, please email volunteer@stfranciscenter.org. About Us: St. Francis Neighborhood Center's mission is committed to breaking the cycles of poverty through education, inspiring self-esteem, self-improvement, and strengthening connections. We provide free academic and arts-based learning programs to community children in addition to mentoring, tutoring and meals.

name: Day of Remembrance
description: Hey everyone, it would be great if you guys could come out to this event in respect to the historical tragedy that occurred 73 years ago. It will feature very prominent experts. Also if you are taking a class in the AAST department you could probably barter for extra credit with this assignment. Maybe even a class in the JAPN department. Please come and support the Japanese American Student Association, the Asian American Student Union, the JAPN and AAST departments, and Japanese Americans everywhere. ---- On February 19, 1942, President Franklin Delano Roosevelt signed Executive Order 9066, resulting in the internment of over 110,000 Japanese Americans. Join the UMCP Japanese American Student Association and the Asian American Student Union at UMCP in remembrance of the internment exactly 73 years later, on Thursday, February 19, 2015. We will view a documentary called "Rabbit in the Moon" about the experiences of Japanese Americans in the internment camps. We will then hear reflections about the documentary and the internment from panelists Dr. Michele Mason of the University of Maryland Japanese Department and Dr. Douglas Ishii of the University of Maryland Asian American Studies Department, and Mr. Floyd Mori of the Asian Pacific American Institute for Congressional Studies. The event will take place from 3:00 pm to 5:30 pm in the Charles Carroll A Room on the second floor of the Adele H. Stamp Student Union at the University of Maryland College Park. Dr. Mason and Dr. Ishii will be offering extra credit to students in their courses for attending the event. Please RSVP by filling out this form: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/1BV2mTqIzATatm3-WC077fFjpX6YZCzc20YpdCZFPrZ8/viewform You can also find the event on Facebook here: https://www.facebook.com/events/583900568412446/?fref=ts

name: AnthroPlus Student Conference: Building Community Engagement and Social Equity in a Changing World
description: The Practicing Anthropologist Student Association (PASA) is proud to present its 7th annual AnthroPlus Student Conference on Saturday, March 5, 2016. This year, join our conversation about "Building Community Engagement and Social Equity in a Changing World.” How do communities and professionals engage each other in issues of global social equity? What are the benefits and challenges of conducting applied research inside and outside the boundaries of academia? We are pleased to present Dr. Rachel Watkins, as our keynote speaker. She will discuss her work examining the health consequences of poverty and inequality through skeletal and documentary analysis. Dr. Watkins’ engages in socially relevant research that is useful for understanding health and disease patterns in marginal populations over time. AnthroPlus is a free event and all are welcome to attend! Anthro+ is a conference by graduate students for students of Anthropology and other disciplines. It is sponsored by the Department of Anthropology, the College of Behavioral and Social Sciences, and Graduate Student Government. This event is funded in part by your Graduate Student Activities Fee.

name: GRadulting Workshop Series: How do I avoid accidental plagiarism?
description: Accidental plagiarism is usually the result of being rushed, unorganized, or uninformed about the citation and research process. Additionally, students often come to UMD from institutions and educational cultures where academic integrity and plagiarism standards are either taught in a different manner or not routinely enforced. Whether it’s an accident or an intentional act of plagiarism, the consequences are essentially the same. It can result in a reprimand, failed grade, failed course, or even worse. We will be offering two hybrid info sessions this Fall: Tuesday, September 20th, 2022 at 6:00 PM ET at Tydings Hall 0101 and Online Thursday, October 27th, 2022 at 6:00 PM ET at Tydings Hall 0101 and Online The info session will be led by START’s Director of Undergraduate Studies, Dr. Thomas Guarrieri, and START's Education Coordinator, who will discuss how the Global Terrorism Studies Minor Program currently works, what students have to gain from their experience in the program, application requirements, and any other questions attendees may have. name: GRadulting Workshop Series: What is the best health insurance plan for me?

name: Introduction to AR Development
description: Movies like Iron Man, Terminator, and Black Panther have long depicted the power of augmented reality. You may have even experienced it for yourself, with apps like Pokemon Go and Snapchat filters. But what if you wanted to make your own AR experience? Surely it must be way too complex for a beginner college student to handle! Wrong! Join the XR Club this Monday as we show you just how easy it is to build your own smartphone AR experience from scratch! We'll be using Unity's AR Foundation, a multi-platform framework that connects you to the core underlying capabilities of both smartphones- and headset-based AR platforms. In the first part of this workshop series, you'll learn how to get the camera stream to show up in your application, how to track and visualize features of the environment, like planes and point clouds, and how to deploy an AR application to your phone. No prior experience is necessary; all majors welcome! Notes:This workshop requires you to bring a computer with a variety of special software tools installed prior to attending the workshop. These tools could take 30 mins or longer to download and install, so you will not have enough time during the workshop to install the software without falling behind. Additionally, it is strongly recommended that you bring a physical mouse. For Android:You will need to have Unity 2021 LTS or later installed along with the Android Build Support module and the options for the Android SDK & NDK Tools and OpenJDK. All of these should be installed with the Unity Hub. You will also need to enable developer options and USB debugging on your phone, as described at https://developer.android.com/studio/debug/dev-options#enable For iOS:You will need to have Unity 2021 LTS or later installed along with the iOS Build Support module. You will also need to install the latest version of Apple's Xcode IDE, which can be found on the Mac App Store. Once you've done that, add your Apple ID account to your Xcode preferences, as described at https://help.apple.com/xcode/mac/current/#/devaf282080a Note that the Xcode IDE is only available on Macs. If you have a Windows computer, you will still be able to develop an AR applications in Unity and export it to an Xcode project, but you will not be able to open that Xcode project and deploy the build to an iOS device for testing

name: Yuri Kochiyama High School Leadership Program 2024
description: The Yuri Kochiyama High School Leadership Program (YKLP) is an annual opportunity for DMV high school students to learn about the history of Asian American activism, strengthen their sense of identity through learning about cross-racial and intersectional community building, and develop peer solidarity and mentorship with other BIPOC-identifying individuals at UMD and other high school students.Hosted by the Asian American Student Union (AASU) at the University of Maryland, College Park (UMCP), YKLP seeks to celebrate the legacy of Japanese American activist, Yuri Kochiyama, by providing community education and mentorship to students interested in Asian American issues--completely free of charge.This year, we are taking applications for a cohort that will meet once a week through a hybrid format over a 5-week session during the spring. Each week, YK participants will come together to learn about Asian American history, identity, and leadership through intersectional community building. YKLP will end with an End-of-Program Celebration on April 13. The hybrid schedule is as follows: WEEK ONE (2/17): in-person WEEK TWO (2/24) : online WEEK THREE (3/02): in-person WEEK FOUR (3/09): online WEEK FIVE (3/16): in-person Graduation (4/13): in-person We hope to raise awareness about Asian Pacific Islander Desi American (APIDA) issues that matter to community members, highlighting APIDA experiences and engaging with each other to better integrate intersectional concepts within our daily lives. YKLP is open to all public high school students within the DMV who are of BIPOC-identifying background to facilitate inter-community building and learning.

name: En'Rage Models Practice
description: Our practice sessions are dynamic and empowering, designed to build confidence, enhance runway skills, and foster creativity in a supportive environment. Each session begins with a warm-up to prepare our models for the physical and mental demands of the runway. Models are then guided through a series of runway walks, where they practice posture, poise, and movement in a variety of styles that challenge traditional norms of fashion and modeling. Throughout the practice, we focus on perfecting choreography for upcoming shows, allowing models to develop their unique flair while staying in sync with the group’s overall performance. Our experienced runway coaches provide individual feedback to ensure that each model feels confident in expressing their own style, aligning with our mission of self-empowerment and diversity. In addition to runway practice, we also incorporate photoshoot preparation, helping models become comfortable in front of the camera, and working on their poses and expressions. Music is played to set the tone, and we regularly rotate different fashion themes to keep practices fresh and engaging. Each session concludes with a debrief, where we emphasize the importance of mutual support and encouragement, celebrating personal growth and teamwork. En'Rage Models practices are more than just rehearsals—they are an opportunity for our members to develop their self-esteem, push creative boundaries, and prepare for the high-energy experience of the runway.

description: The National Hillel Basketball Tournament (NHBT) was founded in 2010 to bring Jewish students together around the inclusive and encompassing game of basketball. Now in its 13th year, the non-profit initiative, annually housed in the University of Maryland’s state-of-the-art facilities, attracts over 1,500 participants from across the United States and Canada. Players and fans also participate in various off-the-court programs such as Shabbat meals, keynote speakers, and an exciting bar night to kick the weekend off. In addition to NHBT’s impressive scale and reach, its impact has reached new heights in recent years. By providing students a chance to meet, socialize, and compete in a positive Jewish environment, NHBT serves as an oasis for students experiencing antisemitism on their respective campuses. By platforming like-minded organizations and starting initiatives, NHBT has provided a beacon of hope and togetherness for Jewish and campus communities far and wide.

name: En'Rage Models Practice
description: Our practice sessions are dynamic and empowering, designed to build confidence, enhance runway skills, and foster creativity in a supportive environment. Each session begins with a warm-up to prepare our models for the physical and mental demands of the runway. Models are then guided through a series of runway walks, where they practice posture, poise, and movement in a variety of styles that challenge traditional norms of fashion and modeling. Throughout the practice, we focus on perfecting choreography for upcoming shows, allowing models to develop their unique flair while staying in sync with the group’s overall performance. Our experienced runway coaches provide individual feedback to ensure that each model feels confident in expressing their own style, aligning with our mission of self-empowerment and diversity. In addition to runway practice, we also incorporate photoshoot preparation, helping models become comfortable in front of the camera, and working on their poses and expressions. Music is played to set the tone, and we regularly rotate different fashion themes to keep practices fresh and engaging. Each session concludes with a debrief, where we emphasize the importance of mutual support and encouragement, celebrating personal growth and teamwork. En'Rage Models practices are more than just rehearsals—they are an opportunity for our members to develop their self-esteem, push creative boundaries, and prepare for the high-energy experience of the runway.

name: How to Prepare For an Interview
organization: University Career Center & The Presidents Promise
description: Interviewing takes practice and interviews do not need to be perfect. You will say "um” at certain points. You will get caught off-guard by an unexpected interview question and will need some time to think through how to best answer it. You may need to ask the interviewer to repeat a question because you want to make sure you understood it correctly. These scenarios are okay! We are human. The key is to be prepared and be yourself throughout the interview process.In this session, we will discuss: The different types of interviews (live phone/virtual, asynchronous, case, technical, etc) and quick tips to prepare for each. Overall, however, this workshop will focus on behavioral-based interviewing tips. What to know about an employer and the position before stepping foot into the interview or joining that Zoom call. How to think through and articulate your “power stories” - the stories you anticipate will come up in an interview and how to share that story in a way an outsider (i.e. the interviewer) will understand and appreciate. Additional ways to prepare for upcoming interviews. This workshop will be conducted virtually on a monthly basis through the University Career Center & The President's Promise. If this date doesn’t work for you, check out Handshake for future offerings.In addition to this workshop, students have access to Big Interview in Handshake to practice interview questions on your own time. You may also schedule a mock interview with a career advisor in Handshake through a career advising appointment. - Register for the Sep 18, 2024, workshop - Register for the Oct 22, 2024, workshop - Register for the Nov 19, 2024, workshop

name: Pride Month Kickoff / TDOV Celebration 2023
description: All of the UMD community is invited to kick off Pride Month 2023! Our theme for this year is "Love me Tender, Love me Queer." Dinner will be served at 7:30pm (catered from Moby's). Those who are keeping fast will be invited in a few minutes early so they can break fast at 7:34pm. There will be a photo booth, and our event playlist will exclusively feature songs by queer and trans artists of color. We are thrilled to have Rayceen Pendarvis as our keynote speaker. Known as the High Priestess of Love, the Queen of the Shameless Plug, the Empress of Pride, and the Goddess of DC, Rayceen is an event host, community advocate, and lifelong Washingtonian. Rayceen hosts various annual and special events by Team Rayceen Productions and has hosted events in conjunction with DC Public Library, DC Department of Aging and Community Living, The DC Center for the LGBT Community, Story District, and other organizations. Rayceen is active on Twitter, Facebook, and Instagram. Please visit Rayceen.com. Following some short introductory remarks from Rayceen, the main program will be a dialogue between Rayceen and Leo Osei, Jr. '25. Launching Pride Month with an intergenerational dialogue between a Black queer elder and a current out Black student reflects our intention to center racial justice, the wisdom of our elders, and the wisdom of our youth. The program will cover topics such as pride across time, the politics of visibility, and the healing power of queer and trans joy. Following their dialogue, Leo will also moderate a Q&A section open to all audience members. If you have any accessibility needs, please contact shabab@umd.edu and we will do our best to accommodate your request. This event is hosted by MICA in partnership with the LGBTQ+ Equity Center, the Office of Graduate Diversity & Inclusion, and SEE.

name: Going Zero Waste & Plastic Free at UMD
description: Join us for an interactive conversation to discuss sustainability issues, share your thoughts, and develop a plan of action to improve your environmental impact! Meet other students who are concerned about the environment and are looking to connect and take action. Our February event will be a discussion about the Campus Race to Zero Waste & Plastics Reductions:- Why waste is an important issue for the well being of people and the ecosystems we share with other species- How to reduce your waste through daily habits, energy efficiency upgrades, renewable energy, and more - How UMD is reducing waste & plastics, by the numbers look at how we compare to other schools- How to raise awareness and advocate effectively to encourage others to join sustainability efforts Our guest speaker is Adrienne Small, UMD's Recycling Coordinator, who will be sharing information and available for Q&A! description: SEE invites you to UMD’s own Hoff Theater to unwind and join us for our first Free Fall Movie Series of the 2019-20 school year! Enjoy and support several of this year’s hottest movies along with some classic cultural milestones in a large theatrical setting all semester long!Iron Man (2008)- August 29th @ 8:00pm(Action/Sci-Fi) "After being held captive in an Afghan cave, billionaire engineer Tony Stark creates a unique weaponized suit of armor to fight evil." (IMDb)Guardians of the Galaxy (2014) - August 30th @ 8:00pm(Action/Comedy) "A group of intergalactic criminals must pull together to stop a fanatical warrior with plans to purge the universe." (IMDb)Avengers: Endgame - August 31st @ 8:00pm(Action/Sci-Fi) "After the devastating events of Avengers: Infinity War (2018), the universe is in ruins. With the help of remaining allies, the Avengers assemble once more in order to reverse Thanos' actions and restore balance to the universe." (IMDb)Detective Pikachu - September 5th & 7th @ 8:00pm(Action/Comedy) "In a world where people collect Pokémon to do battle, a boy comes across an intelligent talking Pikachu who seeks to be a detective." (IMDb)Rocketman - September 11th & 12th @ 8:00pm(Biography/Drama) "A musical fantasy about the fantastical human story of Elton John's breakthrough years." (IMDb)Yesterday - September 13th & 14th @ 8:00pm(Comedy/Fantasy) "A struggling musician realizes he's the only person on Earth who can remember The Beatles after waking up in an alternate timeline where they never existed." (IMDb)John Wick: Chapter 3 - Parabellum - September 17th & 19th @ 8:00pm(Action/Crime/Thriller) "Super-assassin John Wick is on the run after killing a member of the international assassin's guild, and with a $14 million price tag on his head - he is the target of hit men and women everywhere." (IMDb)Bill and Ted’s Excellent Adventure (1989): A Special 30th Anniversary Screening - September 21st @ 10:00pm(Adventure/Comedy) "Two seemingly dumb teens set off on a quest to prepare the ultimate historical presentation with the help of a time machine." (IMDb)Midsommar - September 26th & 27th @ 8:00pm(Drama/Horror/Mystery) "A couple travels to Sweden to visit a rural hometown's fabled mid-summer festival. What begins as an idyllic retreat quickly devolves into an increasingly violent and bizarre competition at the hands of a pagan cult." (IMDb)The Rocky Horror Picture Show (1975) - September 28th @ 10:00pm(Comedy/Musical) "A newly engaged couple have a breakdown in an isolated area and must pay a call to the bizarre residence of Dr. Frank-N-Furter." (IMDb)Toy Story 4 - October 3rd & 4th @ 8:00pm(Animation/Comedy) "When a new toy called "Forky" joins Woody and the gang, a road trip alongside old and new friends reveals how big the world can be for a toy." (IMDb)Each screening will be in Hoff Theatre inside the Stamp Student Union. Each screening is open for anyone to attend and doors will open 30 minutues prior to showtime. Seating will be available on a first-come, first-serve basis.All weekend movies hosted by Terps After Dark.

name: Yuri Kochiyama High School Leadership Program
description: The Yuri Kochiyama High School Leadership Program (YKLP) is an annual opportunity for DMV high school students to learn about the history of Asian American activism, strengthen their sense of identity through learning about cross-racial and intersectional community building, and develop peer solidarity and mentorship with other BIPOC-identifying individuals at UMD and other high school students.Hosted by the Asian American Student Union (AASU) at the University of Maryland, College Park (UMCP), YKLP seeks to celebrate the legacy of Japanese American activist, Yuri Kochiyama, by providing community education and mentorship to students interested in Asian American issues completely free of charge. The hybrid schedule is as followed: WEEK ONE (2/26): in-person WEEK TWO (3/5) : online WEEK THREE (3/12): in-person WEEK FOUR (3/26): online WEEK FIVE (4/2): online CELEBRATION (4/23): in-person We hope to raise awareness about Asian Pacific Islander Desi American (APIDA) issues that matter to community members, highlighting APIDA experiences and engaging with various BIPOC communities to better integrate intersectional concepts within our activism. For the first time ever, YKLP will now be open to all public high school students within the DMV who are of BIPOC-identifying background to facilitate inter-community building and learning.

name: Imagining Fictitious [non] futures: AI and Us
description: Welcome to the age of AI! With machines now capable of producing “art” at the click of a button, it’s easy to feel overwhelmed by the possibilities - and the potential threats - of this new technology to our future. In this workshop, artist Dan Ortiz Leizman invites you to explore the creative potential of AI, using cutting-edge tools such as DALL-E and Chat GPT to mindfully generate imaginative and thought-provoking artworks. But this workshop isn’t just about using machines as tools. We’ll also explore the ways in which AI can be collaborators, helping us to think in new and unexpected ways. Through a series of hands-on activities, we’ll discover how to engage with AI in ways that are both creative and ethical, pushing the boundaries of what’s possible while retaining our human connection to the work we create. No previous experience with AI or art is necessary - just bring a device that can connect to the internet, and an open mind ready to explore the exciting possibilities of this emerging technology. P.S. This blurb was written with the help of AI Dan Ortiz Leizman’s work probes the limits of the body and its capacity for transformation. Their research into the intersections of the body, time, and queer worldbuilding strategies leads them to question the boundaries of identity and the possibilities of fictitious [non] futures. In this exhibition, Ortiz Leizman presents a series of works that imagine a future in which asexual reproduction in humans has become a reality in the aftermath of nuclear catastrophe. Through a combination of writing, drawing, sound, and AI generated “histories from the future,” they invite the viewer to consider what it means to be human when the traditional modes of social navigation are no longer viable. More about Ortiz Leizman’s work is on their website and instagram. This workshop is provided in conjunction with the Stamp Gallery exhibition LIMBSHIFT, and is supported by a grant from the Maryland State Arts Council (msac.org)

name: SEE Presents: Free Fall Movie Series - Rocketman
description: SEE invites you to UMD’s own Hoff Theater to unwind and join us for our first Free Fall Movie Series of the 2019-20 school year! Enjoy and support several of this year’s hottest movies along with some classic cultural milestones in a large theatrical setting all semester long!Iron Man (2008)- August 29th @ 8:00pm(Action/Sci-Fi) "After being held captive in an Afghan cave, billionaire engineer Tony Stark creates a unique weaponized suit of armor to fight evil." (IMDb)Guardians of the Galaxy (2014) - August 30th @ 8:00pm(Action/Comedy) "A group of intergalactic criminals must pull together to stop a fanatical warrior with plans to purge the universe." (IMDb)Avengers: Endgame - August 31st @ 8:00pm(Action/Sci-Fi) "After the devastating events of Avengers: Infinity War (2018), the universe is in ruins. With the help of remaining allies, the Avengers assemble once more in order to reverse Thanos' actions and restore balance to the universe." (IMDb)Detective Pikachu - September 5th & 7th @ 8:00pm(Action/Comedy) "In a world where people collect Pokémon to do battle, a boy comes across an intelligent talking Pikachu who seeks to be a detective." (IMDb)Rocketman - September 11th & 12th @ 8:00pm(Biography/Drama) "A musical fantasy about the fantastical human story of Elton John's breakthrough years." (IMDb)Yesterday - September 13th & 14th @ 8:00pm(Comedy/Fantasy) "A struggling musician realizes he's the only person on Earth who can remember The Beatles after waking up in an alternate timeline where they never existed." (IMDb)John Wick: Chapter 3 - Parabellum - September 17th & 19th @ 8:00pm(Action/Crime/Thriller) "Super-assassin John Wick is on the run after killing a member of the international assassin's guild, and with a $14 million price tag on his head - he is the target of hit men and women everywhere." (IMDb)Bill and Ted’s Excellent Adventure (1989): A Special 30th Anniversary Screening - September 21st @ 10:00pm(Adventure/Comedy) "Two seemingly dumb teens set off on a quest to prepare the ultimate historical presentation with the help of a time machine." (IMDb)Midsommar - September 26th & 27th @ 8:00pm(Drama/Horror/Mystery) "A couple travels to Sweden to visit a rural hometown's fabled mid-summer festival. What begins as an idyllic retreat quickly devolves into an increasingly violent and bizarre competition at the hands of a pagan cult." (IMDb)The Rocky Horror Picture Show (1975) - September 28th @ 10:00pm(Comedy/Musical) "A newly engaged couple have a breakdown in an isolated area and must pay a call to the bizarre residence of Dr. Frank-N-Furter." (IMDb)Toy Story 4 - October 3rd & 4th @ 8:00pm(Animation/Comedy) "When a new toy called "Forky" joins Woody and the gang, a road trip alongside old and new friends reveals how big the world can be for a toy." (IMDb)Each screening will be in Hoff Theatre inside the Stamp Student Union. Each screening is open for anyone to attend and doors will open 30 minutues prior to showtime. Seating will be available on a first-come, first serve basis.All weekend movies hosted by Terps After Dark.

name: Fallapalooza with Chelsea Cutler
description: Fallapalooza with Chelsea Cutler will take place on Friday, October 11, 2019 in Ritchie Coliseum! The show will begin at 8 p.m. with doors opening at 7 p.m. and closing at 9:15 p.m.This event is open to students, staff, faculty and the general public. Tickets are $10 for members of the UMD Community with a valid UMD ID and $20 for the general public.Tickets will be available for purchase online at umdtickets.com and at the Stamp Ticket Office beginning Monday, September 9, 2019. Hailing from Westport, Connecticut, Chelsea Cutler is an indie/pop singer, songwriter and producer. A multi-instrumentalist, she grew up making music but became interested in recording and production at the age of 17. Cutler began uploading covers of artists spanning the Tallest Man on Earth and ODESZA in 2014, and as a freshman at Amherst College, she shared the original song "Anything for You" in late 2015. "Wake Up" followed in 2016 as Cutler started to be featured on songs by indie electronic acts such as Kidswaste, Louis the Child, and Kasbo, garnering millions of streams between them. In 2017, she began releasing more original music beginning with her breakthrough single “Your Shirt,” which led to the release of her debut EP, “Snow in October,” in Fall 2017.She kicked off 2018 by embarking on a 27-city tour supporting frequent collaborator Quinn XCII. That summer she released an 8- song mixtape “Sleeping With Roses,” which led to her first US headline tour beginning in that Fall. Following the tour, she released “Sleeping With Roses II,” the second mixtape of the series, in November 2018. She then announced her first European tour and Part II of her US tour. Both legs of her US tour (Fall 2018 and Spring 2019) were completely sold out in advance.In 2019, she paired with Jeremy Zucker for the “brent” EP and featured on Kygo’s summer smash “Not OK”. She released her latest single “How To Be Human” in August and is gearing up for her debut album set to release soon on Republic Records. She also played major festivals this summer including Lollapalooza, Bonnaroo, and Governors Ball.Please email all media/press questions to: seepublicrelations@umd.edu

name: International Affairs Women of Color
description: Application Due: December 1, 2019Forum Date: December 6, 2019 The German Marshall Fund of the United States (GMF) is seeking young women of color interested in pursuing a career in foreign policy and national security to apply to attend GMF's Third Annual Women of Color in Transatlantic Leadership Forum as a Young Professional Participant. To ensure the next generation of foreign policy and national security professionals are included in the dialogue, we will select fifteen young women with demonstrated interest in global affairs and exceptional leadership experience to participate in this year's forum. Forum Information: Third Annual Women of Color in Transatlantic Leadership Forum:Changing the Face of Foreign Affairs The Third Annual Women of Color in Transatlantic Leadership Forum will convene over 100 distinguished women of color leaders from across sectors to discuss the foreign policy and national security issues most pressing to the transatlantic space, and to create a pipeline to encourage women of color to continue pursuing opportunities to advance the international and transatlantic component of their leadership. The Forum will open with a Congressional Roundtable, featuring Congresswomen of color who serve as leading voices on foreign affairs and national security issues in the U.S. Congress. The roundtable will be followed by three "power panels" in which woman leaders distinguished in government, business, Congress, and think tanks will engage in dialogue on the Forum topic: Changing the Face of Foreign Affairs. Date: December 6, 2019 Time: 8:30 a.m. - 2:30 p.m. Location: Arena Stage, Home of the Mead Center for American Theater 1101 Sixth Street SW, Washington, DC 20024 Young Professionals Application Information: Qualified applicants will be: Current juniors, seniors, graduate students, or young professionals (1-3 years of experience); Women of Color with a desire to pursue a career in international affairs; Willing to network and develop relationships; and Able to attend the full forum program on December 6, 2019. Applications are due by December 1, 2019, at 5:00 pm EST. Applicants will receive notification of their selection by December 2, 2019. To apply, click here. There is no fee to join the Third Annual Women of Color in Transatlantic Leadership Forum. Please direct any questions to Catharine Carstens at congressionalaffairs@gmfus.org or +1 202 683 2683.

name: Camp PALS Volunteer opportunity
description: Volunteer to be a Counselor for the PALS program Camp PALS this summer. PALS is a nonprofit organization that provides one week long summer camp opportunities for teens and young adults with Down syndrome and their peers at 14 college campuses across the country. This is a one-week experience from 9am-5pm. Listed below are some details about Camp PALS: Here are some details about Camp PALS: - They offer 14 week long sleep-away camps across the country, including Camp PALS Georgetown, Chicago, and North Carolina! - Volunteer counselors are paired one-to-one with a camper to provide an opportunity to build -meaningful friendships through trips and activities - Looking for volunteers ages 16-30 who are welcoming, genuine, passionate, supportive, and fun which are all the values of the program. - No experience with Down syndrome or the disability community is necessary! They encourage groups of applicants to apply together to share the camp experience. If you are interested please visit the website at palsprograms.org/volunteer or check out their social media pages on Facebook or YouTube channel to get a look at what the PALS experience is like. PALS is an amazing opportunity to give back to the community, gain invaluable leadership skills, and make friends that will last a lifetime! There are no costs for volunteers at PALS, and applicants can apply for travel costs to be covered as well. We are looking for male applicants at this point in our season. Females are welcome to apply but will likely be placed on a waitlist. The dates for each of our 15 camps is different based on their locations, but the dates for Baltimore are July 7-13 at UMBC, and Georgetown is July 28-August 3 at Georgetown University.

name: Bike & Build Looking for Summer 2020 Volunteers
description: Bike & Build is a nonprofit organization that runs cross country and regional cycling trips to raise money and awareness for affordable housing, while fostering lifelong civic engagement in young adults. Our riders spend about 11 weeks biking from the east coast to the west coast, stopping every 3-5 days to volunteer with different affordable housing organizations. Applications are now open for our summer of 2020 routes and we would love to engage more service minded and adventurous folks in the affordable housing cause, while having a life changing summer. We also offer scholarships to engages young adults from low-income & historically marginalized communities, as well as applicants coming from national service backgrounds to participate in Bike & Build. People of color, immigrant, trans, and gender queer applicants are encouraged to apply. No cycling experience is necessary. To apply, click here. Please reach out to Lily Goldberg lily@bikeandbuild.org with any questions.
