name: GRadulting Workshop Series - Why is my credit score important?
description: Our society is becoming increasingly dependent on credit to make purchases and financial decisions. A good credit score is used for more than just getting a credit card or a loan. Credit scores demonstrate your history of paying your debts to entities that loan you money. Your credit score may be used by everyone from potential employers to landlords to evaluate your stability and financial health. Learn more about this important number including how to how to establish good credit, how to get your credit report for free and how to improve your score. Speakers: Ann Holmes, College of Behavioral and Social Sciences, UMD ... Gradute Student Legal Aid offers the GRadulting Virtual Workshop Series, often in collaboration with other offices on campus. GradTerps (and sometimes undergrads) are welcome to join us virtually on Tuesdays, usually at 12:30pm. Whether you are in the U.S. or in your home country, you can count on us for great information to help you navigate the issues and challenges of the adult world. If you are unable to attend, many of our speakers will give us permission to record the workshop so you can view it at your own convenience. We hope to see you there! What is GRadulting? Gradulting is defined as graduate students who are "adulting" -- (v): to carry out one or more of the duties and responsibilities expected of fully developed individuals, such as financial planning, buying a home, negotiating a salary, or estate planning. GradTerps, join our Google Group to receive a weekly reminder of the upcoming workshops!

name: Profiles of Individual Radicalisation in Australia (PIRA) Dataset: An Introduction to PIRA and an Exploration of Risk and Contextual Factors Linked to Radicalisation in Australia
description: On Monday, December 14 at 6:00 p.m. ET, University of Queensland Professor Adrian Cherney and Senior Research Assistant Emma Belton will provide a virtual talk on “Profiles of Individual Radicalisation in Australia (PIRA) Dataset: An Introduction to PIRA and an Exploration of Risk and Contextual Factors Linked to Radicalisation in Australia.” This event is free and open to the public, but RSVPs are required. If you have any questions, please email the START events team at start-events@umd.edu. The Profiles of Individual Radicalisation in Australia (PIRA) dataset captures 122 different variables relating to background, demographic, group affiliation, and contextual information on individuals who have radicalised to violent extremism in Australia from 1985-2020. PIRA is modelled on START's Profiles of Individual Radicalisation in the United States (PIRUS) dataset. Like PIRUS, PIRA draws on open source materials to identify and code for data on specific individuals identified as having radicalised to extremism. In this presentation we will introduce the PIRA dataset, outline its development and provide an overview of data relating to background characteristics and risk factors for radicalisation amongst the sample, and consider some of our early findings for theory and policy on radicalisation to violent extremism. Adrian Cherney is a Professor in the School of Social Science at the University of Queensland. He is also an Australian Research Council (ARC) Future Fellow. His research focuses on the evaluation of programs aimed at convicted terrorists and individuals identified as at risk of radicalisation. He is also collating data on individual radicalisation in Australia. Projects include evaluations of case managed interventions delivered by the police in Australia. He completed an evaluation of the Proactive Integrated Support Model (PRISM) intervention in New South Wales that targets convicted terrorists and radicalised inmates. He has undertaken research on inmates exiting custody and/or completing a community based order after the completion of a sentence for terrorism. Other funded projects include the development of program integrity guidelines for CVE program design, implementation and evaluation. He is also part of team at UQ being funded to conduct systematic reviews of CVE programs. Emma Belton is a PhD candidate and Senior Research Assistant in the School of Social Science at the University of Queensland. Her research aims to improve understanding relating to the backgrounds and risk factors associated with individuals who have been convicted of a terrorist offence or identified as having radicalised to violent extremism. Her research draws on the Profiles of Individual Radicalisation in Australia (PIRA) dataset. She has also worked on several research projects examining the impact of countering violent extremism interventions, across community and custodial settings.

name: Fearless New Play Festival
description: The Fearless New Play Festival is a four-day celebration of new scripts in development that address urgent issues of today. The festival kicks off on November 19 with a speech by nationally renowned keynote playwright Lauren Yee. The festival features staged readings of new short plays by current TDPS students and alumni from November 19-22. Selected plays for the 2020 Fearless New Play Festival By Grace (Part Two) by Agyeiwaa Asante ’18 A Tea Party by Mariel Berlin-Fischler ’14 All of my Bullies and Where They Are Now by Elizabeth Crino ’18 Ghost Story by Evangelina Hakes ’19 The Ice Room by Liz Maestri ’03 RAPunzel by Jasmine Mitchell ‘20 Tiny Ruins by April Monu ’18 Please Like Me by Jordan Resnick ’22 Loving in the Age of Social Distancing by Amber Smithers ‘20 The Tao Island by Lyra Woods ’17 Announcing Keynote Playwright Lauren Yee The School of Theatre, Dance, and Performance Studies is thrilled to announce that internationally-renowned playwright Lauren Yee will be our 2020 keynote playwright. Lauren Yee is a playwright, screenwriter, and TV writer born and raised in San Francisco. She currently lives in New York City. Her play Cambodian Rock Band, with music by Dengue Fever and others, just had a lauded off-Broadway run at Signature Theatre. Her plays The Great Leap and Cambodian Rock Band led the list of top 10 most produced plays in the country for the 2019-20 season. She is the winner of the 2019 Doris Duke Artist Award for outstanding contributions to theater, the 2019 Steinberg Playwright Award, the Horton Foote Prize, the Kesselring Prize, the ATCA/Steinberg Award, American Academy of Arts and Letters literature award, and the Francesca Primus Prize. She has been a finalist for the Edward M. Kennedy Prize and the Susan Smith Blackburn Prize. Her plays were the #1 and #2 plays on the 2017 Kilroys List. Lauren is a Residency 5 playwright at Signature Theatre in New York, New Dramatists member (class of 2025), Ma-Yi Writers’ Lab member, former Princeton University Hodder fellow, and Playwrights Realm alumni playwright. She earned her BA at Yale and her MFA at UC San Diego, and American Theatre Magazine named her as the second most-produced playwright in the country for the 2019/20 season. For more info, please visit www.laurenyee.com.

name: Arts Citizenship Talks (ACTnow): Revelations by Black Women in the Arts–Theater
description: From themes of racial violence and cultural appropriation to multiculturalism and gender equality, the work of The Clarice's 2020-21 artists is complex, provocative and deeply sensitive. Arts Citizenship Talks (ACTnow) are opportunities to hear from these artists about the issues reflected in their works. These conversations are an invitation to act now! Revelations by Black Women in the Arts is a series of powerful conversations by Black woman scholars, performers, educators and leaders delves into the essence of being a Black female artist in a society ill-equipped to receive and make room for them. Whether they move along the margins or at the center of their fields, these extraordinary women will share their artistry, scholarship, vision and creativity throughout Spring 2021. description: The Maryland Sports Business Conference was created in 2020 by undergraduate students in the Sports Business Society at the University of Maryland. All proceeds will go directly to the foundation! Our goal is to raise $5,000 to fully fund 25 Special Olympic athletes to pay for their yearly training, competitions, and programs. Click here to make a donation! To learn more about Special Olympics Maryland, visit: https://www.somd.org/

name: UMCP TASA Night Market 2021
description: Night markets are one of the most extraordinary aspects of Taiwanese culture. A night market is a street market that is held almost every night in major cities of Taiwan. Every day after the sun sets, hundreds of vendors set up their shops at local street corners in order to sell their wares at the night markets in Taiwanese towns and cities. Within a few hours, the streets bustle with vendors selling food, souvenirs, merchandise, and clothing to potential buyers. Each night market is a unique street bazaar in which locals and tourists stroll, shop, dine, and explore. This year, Night Market will be held virtually over Zoom. In lieu of in-person food and game stalls, we will be having virtual food competitions, play games online, and stream performances by the local Asian cultural performance groups. Every year, we strive to replicate the bustling, lively atmosphere of a traditional night market by offering guests the chance to sample authentic Taiwanese cuisine, play traditional Taiwanese games, and watch performances by local Asian cultural performance groups. Additionally, there will be opportunities to learn about all different aspects of Taiwanese culture, including the language, history, current events, and popular culture of Taiwan. Although this year's Night Market will be different than in the past, we hope that attendees will still leave feeling like they've immersed themselves in Taiwanese culture for the night.

name: Rich Kids: A History of Shopping Malls in Tehran (UK)
description: Around the world, the gap between rich and poor continues to widen. Images of the children of the elite and of post-colonial dictatorships often feature cash and seaside holidays while the working population suffers under sanctions and dictatorships. In this virtual presentation, The Javaad Alipoor Company’s Rich Kids: A History of Shopping Malls in Tehran explores entitlement and greedy consumption, as well as the role of digital technology, in creating this new apartheid and gentrification. As the performance is completely live streamed, audiences can access the performance from the comfort of their own homes with a supplemental experience on Instagram that is not required, but highly recommended! Always taking stories beyond the stage through powerful multi-platform creations, The Javaad Alipoor Company explores the intersection of politics and technology in our ever-changing world. The company is devoted to creating works for diverse audiences and communities, and their 2021-22 virtual visit with The Clarice will include an Arts Citizenship Talk (ACTnow), visits to the UMD School of Theatre, Dance, and Performance Studies and a dynamic partnership with UMD’s Roshan Institute for Persian Studies. In 2017, the company began writing a trilogy that highlights society’s fracturing identities and technology’s impact on the world; Rich Kids is the second installment.

name: RAJAS (India)
description: RAJAS, named after the Sanskrit term that defines the human quality that compels us to act and create, combines improvisation with various musical approaches. Led by University of Maryland anthropology and French language graduate Rajna Swaminathan ’13, RAJAS blends jazz with South Asian harmony and rhythm to create a unique sound. With the group’s own compositions serving merely as points of departure, the ensemble’s collaborative process centers around mutuality and multiplicity. On stage you will hear vocals, the percussive mrudangam, guitar, bass, piano, tenor saxophone and trumpet. While visiting The Clarice, RAJAS will work closely with students in the UMD School of Music and the Asian American studies program on campus. Ensemble members will also host a Concert in the Quad for on-campus student residents in the College Park Scholars program. Health + Safety There may be COVID safety policies such as mask requirements in place when you attend this event. Please see our health & safety page for the most up to date information about attendance!

name: Veterans Yoga
description: Sun Salutations (8/31) Get ready for a class to introduce health and vitality into the semester! This short class includes 20 minutes of cleansing movement fit for yogis of all shapes, sizes, and experience levels. Bonus: Do you not have time to relax and let go for even just a few minutes? Your instructor includes at least five minutes of required shavasana practice at the end of each class to give the mind a break from the rest of the world. Learn a New Pose (9/2) Today’s yoga session will include 18 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out, meaning that yogis of all experience and backgrounds will benefit! Get ready to build strength and resilience with this fun-to learn movement. Relaxation Meditation (9/7) Tuesday’s session will be focused on grounding yourself in this new semester. Just fifteen minutes of passive, yet focused yoga practice will bring you into the moment and out of the stresses of the new semester. Get a Workout in (9/9) After Tuesday’s session focused on relaxation and finding ground in the new semester, it’s time to ramp up the heat. You would never believe what just twenty minutes of poses can do to get that blood pumping and the sweat pouring! Don’t worry, though! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Open the Hips (9/14) We have been in class for a couple of weeks now and our bodies need us to keep moving to stay open and ready for all that life has to offer. Twenty three minutes of opening the hips will keep them from tightening from all the stress and constant sitting motion. Don’t forget! We also include at least five minutes of time to destress and prepare for the rest of the week. Learn a New Pose (9/16) Today’s yoga session will include 24 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out. Yogis of all experience and backgrounds will benefit from this fun practice! Get ready to build some awesome abdominal strength with this sequence. Relaxation Meditation (9/21) Today’s session will be focused on grounding yourself in this new semester. Twenty six minutes of passive, yet focused yoga practice will bring you into the moment and out of the stresses of the semester’s stressors. Getting in a Workout! (9/23) After Tuesday’s session focused on relaxation and finding ground in this awesome in-person semester, it’s time to get that body moving. Just thirty three minutes of poses will get that blood pumping and the sweat pouring! Don’t worry! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Plus, we won’t leave your muscles stiff from the hard work! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for the Booty (9/28) Looking to add cushion and tone to your derriere? Who isn’t?! Today’s session will be devoted to working to add strength to the glutes and hamstrings. Twenty minutes of work will show you some tips and tools to build your important muscle groups that keep your body healthy and moving! Learn a New Pose (9/30) Today’s yoga session will include 25 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out! Even the simplest of poses require detail-orientation! Get ready to build strength and resilience in simple poses. Relaxation Meditation (10/5) Tuesday’s session will be focused on staying sane as the semester continues to pose more difficulties. This is a time for you to take 26 minutes to treat yourself to reduce stress and a little self-care. Get a Workout In (10/7) After Tuesday’s session focused on relaxation and de-stressing, it’s time to move the mind, body, and spirit. Just 34 minutes of yoga flow will get that blood pumping! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in and focused throughout the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Plus, we won’t leave your muscles stiff from the hard work! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for Weak and Tight Shoulders (10/12) We get it. Being an athlete, veteran, human, parent, student, etc. comes with a price. Usually that price is paid in the body. Today we are going to focus on restoring weak and/or tight shoulders. Don’t shy away from class out of fear of injury! There are modifications for all flexibility levels in the shoulders. We are working to improve, not perfect! After all, we only have twenty six minutes! Learn a New Pose (10/14) Today’s yoga session will include 34 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out! Poses that seem difficult from the outside may be a bit simpler than you anticipate! We are focused on safety in strength. So first, we will build strength and confidence. Then we will build upon simple poses to create a beautiful movement to feel proud about. Relaxation Meditation (10/19) We are mid-semester. While it feels like this is the time to be working your butt off with as few breaks as possible, don’t forget about the importance of daily self-care. Today’s class will be nineteen minutes focused on nothing but bringing you back to yourself. This is a time to reclaim the best parts of yourself and create the person you want to be with focused intention. Get a Workout In (10/21) Tuesday got us mentally focused for the week, so now it is time to ramp up the energy to end the week strong! Thirty-one minutes of yoga flow will get that blood pumping! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in and focused. Don’t forget a towel! We will leave your muscles feeling worked, but not too stiff! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for Back Pain (10/26) Is your back constantly feeling stiff? Is the lower back achy and shoulder blades tight? Come to today’s yoga session for the opportunity to release some of that stiffness, and open yourself up to a world of relief! You might be surprised at what a short 33 minutes of stretching and strengthening can do for the body. Learn a New Pose (10/28) Ready to expand your yoga knowledge and experience? Today’s class will revolve around learning a yoga pose through-and-through. There is no reason to worry about the experience level needed for the pose, as all poses learned and performed here can be done at any level! Set aside 33 minutes and get mentally ready to learn reverse warrior so we can add it to your yoga repertoire! Relaxation Meditation (11/2) Meditating on a regular basis has positive effects on the body and mind, such as greater sense of focus, muscle relaxation, and increased creativity. Today’s meditation will be focused on gratitude and increasing happiness. Giving thanks can come in many forms, but have you tried it in the form of meditation?! Getting in a Workout! (11/4) After Tuesday’s session focused on gratitude in this challenging semester, it’s time to get that body moving. Just 34 minutes of sweat-inducing poses will get that blood pumping! This class is fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Plus, we won’t leave your muscles stiff from the hard work! Get ready to build strength and resilience with this fun-to learn movement. Relaxation Meditation (9/7) Tuesday’s session will be focused on grounding yourself in this new semester. Just fifteen minutes of passive, yet focused yoga practice will bring you into the moment and out of the stresses of the new semester. Get a Workout in (9/9) After Tuesday’s session focused on relaxation and finding ground in the new semester, it’s time to ramp up the heat. This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Open the Hips (9/14) We have been in class for a couple of weeks now and our bodies need us to keep moving to stay open and ready for all that life has to offer. We also include at least five minutes of time to destress and prepare for the rest of the week. name: Veterans Yoga
description: Sun Salutations (8/31) Get ready for a class to introduce health and vitality into the semester! This short class includes 20 minutes of cleansing movement fit for yogis of all shapes, sizes, and experience levels. Bonus: Do you not have time to relax and let go for even just a few minutes? Your instructor includes at least five minutes of required shavasana practice at the end of each class to give the mind a break from the rest of the world. Learn a New Pose (9/2) Today’s yoga session will include 18 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out, meaning that yogis of all experience and backgrounds will benefit! Get ready to build strength and resilience with this fun-to learn movement. Relaxation Meditation (9/7) Tuesday’s session will be focused on grounding yourself in this new semester. Just fifteen minutes of passive, yet focused yoga practice will bring you into the moment and out of the stresses of the new semester. Get a Workout in (9/9) After Tuesday’s session focused on relaxation and finding ground in the new semester, it’s time to ramp up the heat. You would never believe what just twenty minutes of poses can do to get that blood pumping and the sweat pouring! Don’t worry, though! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Open the Hips (9/14) We have been in class for a couple of weeks now and our bodies need us to keep moving to stay open and ready for all that life has to offer. Twenty three minutes of opening the hips will keep them from tightening from all the stress and constant sitting motion. Don’t forget! We also include at least five minutes of time to destress and prepare for the rest of the week. Learn a New Pose (9/16) Today’s yoga session will include 24 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out. Yogis of all experience and backgrounds will benefit from this fun practice! Get ready to build some awesome abdominal strength with this sequence. Relaxation Meditation (9/21) Today’s session will be focused on grounding yourself in this new semester. Twenty six minutes of passive, yet focused yoga practice will bring you into the moment and out of the stresses of the semester’s stressors. Getting in a Workout! (9/23) After Tuesday’s session focused on relaxation and finding ground in this awesome in-person semester, it’s time to get that body moving. Just thirty three minutes of poses will get that blood pumping and the sweat pouring! Don’t worry! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Plus, we won’t leave your muscles stiff from the hard work! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for the Booty (9/28) Looking to add cushion and tone to your derriere? Who isn’t?! Today’s session will be devoted to working to add strength to the glutes and hamstrings. Twenty minutes of work will show you some tips and tools to build your important muscle groups that keep your body healthy and moving! Learn a New Pose (9/30) Today’s yoga session will include 25 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out! Even the simplest of poses require detail-orientation! Get ready to build strength and resilience in simple poses. Relaxation Meditation (10/5) Tuesday’s session will be focused on staying sane as the semester continues to pose more difficulties. This is a time for you to take 26 minutes to treat yourself to reduce stress and a little self-care. Get a Workout In (10/7) After Tuesday’s session focused on relaxation and de-stressing, it’s time to move the mind, body, and spirit. Just 34 minutes of yoga flow will get that blood pumping! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in and focused throughout the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Plus, we won’t leave your muscles stiff from the hard work! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for Weak and Tight Shoulders (10/12) We get it. Being an athlete, veteran, human, parent, student, etc. comes with a price. Usually that price is paid in the body. Today we are going to focus on restoring weak and/or tight shoulders. Don’t shy away from class out of fear of injury! There are modifications for all flexibility levels in the shoulders. We are working to improve, not perfect! After all, we only have twenty six minutes! Learn a New Pose (10/14) Today’s yoga session will include 34 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out! Poses that seem difficult from the outside may be a bit simpler than you anticipate! We are focused on safety in strength. So first, we will build strength and confidence. Then we will build upon simple poses to create a beautiful movement to feel proud about. Relaxation Meditation (10/19) We are mid-semester. While it feels like this is the time to be working your butt off with as few breaks as possible, don’t forget about the importance of daily self-care. Today’s class will be nineteen minutes focused on nothing but bringing you back to yourself. This is a time to reclaim the best parts of yourself and create the person you want to be with focused intention. Get a Workout In (10/21) Tuesday got us mentally focused for the week, so now it is time to ramp up the energy to end the week strong! Thirty-one minutes of yoga flow will get that blood pumping! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in and focused. Don’t forget a towel! We will leave your muscles feeling worked, but not too stiff! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for Back Pain (10/26) Is your back constantly feeling stiff? Is the lower back achy and shoulder blades tight? Come to today’s yoga session for the opportunity to release some of that stiffness, and open yourself up to a world of relief! You might be surprised at what a short 33 minutes of stretching and strengthening can do for the body. Learn a New Pose (10/28) Ready to expand your yoga knowledge and experience? Today’s class will revolve around learning a yoga pose through-and-through. There is no reason to worry about the experience level needed for the pose, as all poses learned and performed here can be done at any level! Set aside 33 minutes and get mentally ready to learn reverse warrior so we can add it to your yoga repertoire! Relaxation Meditation (11/2) Meditating on a regular basis has positive effects on the body and mind, such as greater sense of focus, muscle relaxation, and increased creativity. Today’s meditation will be focused on gratitude and increasing happiness. Giving thanks can come in many forms, but have you tried it in the form of meditation?! Getting in a Workout! (11/4) After Tuesday’s session focused on gratitude in this challenging semester, it’s time to get that body moving. Just 34 minutes of sweat-inducing poses will get that blood pumping! This class is fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Plus, we won’t leave your muscles stiff from the hard work! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for a Better Mood (11/9) College is demanding, stressful, and can induce negative feelings! Combat those real-time stresses by moving the body and bonding with fellow veterans. Coming to this thirty minute vinyasa class will open the heart to the positivity you need to get you to the end of the semester. Learn a New Pose (11/11) Ready to expand your yoga knowledge and experience? Today’s class will revolve around learning a yoga pose through-and-through. There is no reason to worry about the experience level needed for the pose, as all poses learned and performed here can be done at any level! Set aside 35 minutes and get mentally ready to learn a new pose to add to your yoga repertoire! Relaxation Meditation (11/16) Today’s meditation practice will be short, sweet, and perfect to regain focus on your workflow. As we near the end of the semester, stress increases, the mind wanders, and we lose focus. We will be going through meditation techniques that can be utilized at home, work, or on the bus. Don’t underestimate the power of this 26 minute session. Come join your fellow veterans and enjoy the feeling of a clear mind. Get a Workout In (11/18) After Tuesday’s session focused on de-stressing and refocusing, it’s time to move that body. Just 34 minutes of yoga flow will get that blood pumping! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in and focused throughout the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Plus, we won’t leave your muscles stiff from the hard work! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for Neck Pain (11/23) After months of looking down at our computer screens, it’s no wonder so many of us have the amount of pain in our necks that we do! Today’s class will be all about de-stressing, communication, and releasing the tension in the neck through yoga practice. Set aside 31 minutes for this perfectly-paced practice.

name: Private Militaries and the Security Industry in Civil Wars: Competition and Market Accountability
description: On Thursday, April 7 at 12:00 p.m. ET, START Associate Research Scientist Elizabeth Radziszewski will provide a virtual talk on her book, Private Militaries and the Security Industry in Civil Wars: Competition and Market Accountability. This event is free and open to the public, but RSVPs are required. If you have any questions, please email the START events team at start-events@umd.edu. Whether they train police forces in Afghanistan or provide military assistance to governments in Africa that are battling rebel groups, private military and security companies (PMSCs), or corporations that provide security and military services for profit, have been present in numerous conflicts around the globe. In 1984 only one international PMSC intervened in a civil war; in 1989 there were 15 international PMSCs present in conflict zones, while from 2003 to 2019 over 120 of such companies provided services during the Iraq war. Why do international PMSCs sometimes help with conflict termination while in other cases their intervention is associated with prolonged wars? And in what ways does market competition affect PMSCs’ military effectiveness? Relying on quantitative analysis of original data on international PMSCs’ involvement in civil wars from 1990 to 2008 and PMSCs’ human rights and fraud violations in Iraq from 2003 to 2019, the book investigates how local and global competition impacts accountability of these non-state actors and their contribution to the termination of major and minor wars. This talk will also explore conditions under which private military and security companies could be effectively utilized by governments to help terminate irregular conflicts. Dr. Elizabeth Radziszewski is an Associate Research Scientist at START where she co-leads the Global Responses to Asymmetric Threats project. Her research focuses on irregular warfare, international rivalries, foreign policy, and creativity/innovation. She is the author of Private Militaries and the Security Industry in Civil Wars: Competition and Market Accountability (Oxford University Press, 2020) and Social Networks and Public Support for the European Union (Routledge, 2013). Her work has been published in several peer-reviewed journals and policy magazines such as the Wilson Quarterly, Journal of Conflict Resolution, Small Wars & Insurgencies, Foreign Policy Analysis, Journal of Global Security Studies, International Interactions, and Political Research Quarterly. Prior to joining START in 2022 she was an Assistant Professor in the Department of Political Science and the Master’s program in Homeland Security at Rider University and a Research Fellow at Stockdale Center for Ethical Leadership at the U.S. Naval Academy. Over the years, Dr. Radziszewski designed and taught over 15 courses in the area of foreign policy, global security, and unconventional warfare at the undergraduate and graduate level. She received her Ph.D. from the University of Illinois, Urbana-Champaign.

description: Robert Law is the Director of Regulatory Affairs and Policy for the Center for Immigration Studies, a Washington, DC-based research institute that examines the impact of immigration on the United States. He is a recognized expert on the legal immigration system, with particular understanding of the impact that employment-based immigrant and nonimmigrant policies affect the wages and opportunities for American workers. Prior to joining the Center, from 2017-2021 Robert was an administration official at U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services, serving first as a senior policy advisor and then as chief of the Office of Policy and Strategy. name: Intro to VR Development (Part I)
description: In this beginner-friendly workshop series, you will learn the basics of developing virtual reality (VR) experiences using the Unity's cross-platform XR Interaction Toolkit as you create a simple Beat Saber VR clone from start to finish. By the end of this workshop, you will have an understanding of how to configure a Unity project for VR, enable HMD and controller tracking in your scene, and build and deploy your apps to the Oculus Quest 2 headset. NOTES: This workshop requires you to bring a computer with Unity 2021.2 installed along with the Android Build Support module and the options for the Android SDK & NDK Tools and OpenJDK. All of these must be installed with the Unity Hub, even if you have other versions on your computer. The Unity Editor could take 30 mins or longer to download and install, so you will not have enough time during the workshop to install the software without falling behind. It is recommended you install the software well in advance of the workshop. It is strongly recommended that you bring a physical mouse since it can be difficult to work in Unity with a laptop trackpad. As per University guidelines, all attendees of this event will be required to wear KN95 masks. Violators will be denied entry into the event.

name: When Far Away is Close to Home: Connecting Media Reports to the Lived Experiences of the Russian War on Ukraine
description: Join an engaging in-person panel in the Grand Ballroom Lounge in the Stamp Student Union on May 9th, 2022 from 4:30-6pm We have seen a lot of news stories and event programming about the Ukrainian crisis, but this panel is something very special. Ukrainian members of our UMD community and students from the region who are allies to the Ukrainian cause will comment on the media reports sharing lived experiences of the war and connecting the reported with the lived. This panel will bridge what you heard about the war with firsthand experience. Abstract: What does the future hold for Ukraine and the world? What role can the academic community play in preventing a global crisis stretching beyond Ukraine’s borders? Does the effects of war reach the UMD community? On February 24, 2022, Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine — a democratic, sovereign country in the heart of Europe. In just one month, the Russian army killed thousands of people, forced millions to leave their homes and seek refuge, and destroyed five thousands of civilians' houses. As the humanitarian crisis caused by the war escalates, the free world united by providing humanitarian assistance, defensive military equipment to Ukraine, and imposing sanctions on Russia. The impact of this war is global. It is not only the war against Ukraine. Global stability and food security worldwide are at risk. With almost 4.8 million people seeking refuge in neighboring countries and 7.1 million people being internally displaced, the humanitarian crisis stretches beyond the borders of Ukraine. These numbers hold countless stories of human suffering, fight for freedom and hope for a brighter future. It is our hope that the discussion will connect the academic expertise with the personal experience forging a path for making a difference. Join the community panel discussion about the global impact of Russia’s war in Ukraine and how it connects to the personal experience of people affected. The panel is organized under the patronage of the Graduate Student Government and the Ukrainian Student Association.
location: Stamp Student Union - Grand Ballroom Lounge

AEES along with alumni, students, campus groups, and faculty are joining together to purchase LEAFhouse and keep it on campus to be used as a resource for student clubs now and in the future. name: Intro to VR Development (Part 2)
description: Now that you understand the basics of virtual-reality development within Unity, it’s time to put those skills to the test! Given the recent release of the highly anticipated virtual-reality game “BONELAB,” we are going to create our own very non-copyright-infringing parody called “FEMUR ARENA”, which is a simple game where you fend off a wave of robotic headcrabs (trust me, it will make more sense once you attend!). In this workshop, we will create “FEMUR ARENA” by utilizing Unity’s XR Interaction Toolkit, OpenXR, Physics, and many other tools that Unity provides. We will also discuss the “do’s and don’ts” of virtual-reality applications, different movement systems like teleportation and smooth locomotion, development tips and tricks, and so much more. No prior experience is necessary, and all majors are welcome! Notes:This workshop requires you to bring a computer with a variety of special software tools installed prior to attending the workshop. These tools could take 30 mins or longer to download and install, so you will not have enough time during the workshop to install the software without falling behind. Additionally, it is strongly recommended that you bring a physical mouse. For Android:You will need to have Unity 2021.3.10 (LTS) or later installed along with the Android Build Support module and the options for the Android SDK & NDK Tools and OpenJDK. All of these should be installed with the Unity Hub. You will also need to enable developer options and USB debugging on your phone, as described at https://developer.android.com/studio/debug/dev-options#enable For iOS:You will need to have Unity 2021.3.10 (LTS) or later installed along with the iOS Build Support module. You will also need to install the latest version of Apple's Xcode IDE, which can be found on the Mac App Store. Once you've done that, add your Apple ID account to your Xcode preferences, as described at https://help.apple.com/xcode/mac/current/#/devaf282080a Note that the Xcode IDE is only available on Macs. If you have a Windows computer, you will still be able to develop an AR applications in Unity and export it to an Xcode project, but you will not be able to open that Xcode project and deploy the build to an iOS device for testing

name: Beekeeping Club Weekly Meeting
description: During the late spring, summer, and early fall, we have meetings to check on our bees. We learn about sustainable beekeeping practices, what to look for and do while taking care of bees. People who show up to this meeting will have to wear bee-safe clothing such as close toed shoes, and preferably pants, though we have full suits and half suits along with gloves provided. Participants will also have to sign a safety waiver which accepts the possibility of bee stings. When it is too cold or rainy, we go to the UMD Greenhouses to complete workshops such as candles, chapstick, and soap using beeswax. Feel free to reach out through our TerpLink page, our email, or the Discord for more information! The Beekeeping Club does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, religion, age, or physical ability. The Mission of The Beekeeping Club is to educate students about bees and beekeeping through hands-on experience and lectures, about harvesting raw products from them in sustainable ways, and about turning those raw products a variety of goods. The Beekeeping Club seeks to offer anyone with a curiosity or passion for bees and beekeeping the ability to participate in beekeeping regardless of their skill level or prior experience and to guide them in learning more about bees and the role beekeeping plays a sustainable world.

name: En'Rage Models Practice
description: Our practice sessions are dynamic and empowering, designed to build confidence, enhance runway skills, and foster creativity in a supportive environment. Each session begins with a warm-up to prepare our models for the physical and mental demands of the runway. Models are then guided through a series of runway walks, where they practice posture, poise, and movement in a variety of styles that challenge traditional norms of fashion and modeling. Throughout the practice, we focus on perfecting choreography for upcoming shows, allowing models to develop their unique flair while staying in sync with the group’s overall performance. Our experienced runway coaches provide individual feedback to ensure that each model feels confident in expressing their own style, aligning with our mission of self-empowerment and diversity. In addition to runway practice, we also incorporate photoshoot preparation, helping models become comfortable in front of the camera, and working on their poses and expressions. Music is played to set the tone, and we regularly rotate different fashion themes to keep practices fresh and engaging. Each session concludes with a debrief, where we emphasize the importance of mutual support and encouragement, celebrating personal growth and teamwork. En'Rage Models practices are more than just rehearsals—they are an opportunity for our members to develop their self-esteem, push creative boundaries, and prepare for the high-energy experience of the runway.

name: Linocut Workshop
description: Studio A offers a valuable and necessary space for the University of Maryland community to connect with one another and themselves through art. In this linocut workshop, participants will have the chance to engage with our creative space and explore the art of printmaking. This experience will be hands-on, allowing participants to create their own unique designs by carving into linoleum blocks, then use ink to bring them to life! Participants can transfer their designs to white/recycled paper provided by Studio A and may bring in their own clothing item to transfer their designs to as well! Studio A hopes to not only convey the techniques of carving and printing but also allow for participants to discover the ways they can foster their own creativity. Participants will be encouraged to get creative, collaborate with others, and seek inspiration from the space in engaging with this linocut workshop experience! This workshop is supported by a Pepsi Grant.

name: National Hillel Basketball Tournament 2025
description: The National Hillel Basketball Tournament (NHBT) was founded in 2010 to bring Jewish students together around the inclusive and encompassing game of basketball. Solely organized by a board of 30 highly motivated students, what began as a small event has quickly developed into one of the largest collegiate gatherings of Jewish students in the country. Now in its 13th year, the non-profit initiative, annually housed in the University of Maryland’s state-of-the-art facilities, attracts over 1,500 participants from across the United States and Canada. This year, we expect over 50 teams from over 30 universities across North America to partake in the weekend-long tournament experience. Players and fans also participate in various off-the-court programs such as Shabbat meals, keynote speakers, and an exciting bar night to kick the weekend off. In addition to NHBT’s impressive scale and reach, its impact has reached new heights in recent years. By providing students a chance to meet, socialize, and compete in a positive Jewish environment, NHBT serves as an oasis for students experiencing antisemitism on their respective campuses. By platforming like-minded organizations and starting initiatives, NHBT has provided a beacon of hope and togetherness for Jewish and campus communities far and wide.

name: En'Rage Models Practice
description: Our practice sessions are dynamic and empowering, designed to build confidence, enhance runway skills, and foster creativity in a supportive environment. Each session begins with a warm-up to prepare our models for the physical and mental demands of the runway. Models are then guided through a series of runway walks, where they practice posture, poise, and movement in a variety of styles that challenge traditional norms of fashion and modeling. Throughout the practice, we focus on perfecting choreography for upcoming shows, allowing models to develop their unique flair while staying in sync with the group’s overall performance. Our experienced runway coaches provide individual feedback to ensure that each model feels confident in expressing their own style, aligning with our mission of self-empowerment and diversity. In addition to runway practice, we also incorporate photoshoot preparation, helping models become comfortable in front of the camera, and working on their poses and expressions. Music is played to set the tone, and we regularly rotate different fashion themes to keep practices fresh and engaging. Each session concludes with a debrief, where we emphasize the importance of mutual support and encouragement, celebrating personal growth and teamwork. En'Rage Models practices are more than just rehearsals—they are an opportunity for our members to develop their self-esteem, push creative boundaries, and prepare for the high-energy experience of the runway.

name: Harvesting the Truth: Colonial Disruptions of Indigenous Food Systems & The Myths of Thanksgiving
description: This event will examine how settler colonialism permanently altered Indigenous food systems and food sovereignty across tribal communities in the United States. Furthermore, we will analyze how settler colonialism influenced anti-Indigenous shifts in policy, the dispossession of Native land, and compromising cultural practices. We will confront the colonial narratives of Thanksgiving by giving voice to Indigenous narratives, which have historically been suppressed. We will showcase how Indigenous communities are working to revitalize their food systems, providing food security in tribes, and their advocacy efforts regarding food sovereignty. It is important to note that while we are focusing on Native experiences in the U.S., food is being used as a mechanism of control to exercise imperial power globally. This is an inhumane act orchestrated by settler colonialism which is still unfolding today. Discussion led by graduate students Kianna L. Big Crow and Vy Thompson.

name: Camp PALS Volunteer opportunity
description: Volunteer to be a Counselor for the PALS program Camp PALS this summer. PALS is a nonprofit organization that provides one week long summer camp opportunities for teens and young adults with Down syndrome and their peers at 14 college campuses across the country. This is a one-week experience from 9am-5pm. Listed below are some details about Camp PALS: Here are some details about Camp PALS: - They offer 14 week long sleep-away camps across the country, including Camp PALS Georgetown, Chicago, and North Carolina! - Volunteer counselors are paired one-to-one with a camper to provide an opportunity to build -meaningful friendships through trips and activities - Looking for volunteers ages 16-30 who are welcoming, genuine, passionate, supportive, and fun which are all the values of the program. - No experience with Down syndrome or the disability community is necessary! They encourage groups of applicants to apply together to share the camp experience. If you are interested please visit the website at palsprograms.org/volunteer or check out their social media pages on Facebook or YouTube channel to get a look at what the PALS experience is like. PALS is an amazing opportunity to give back to the community, gain invaluable leadership skills, and make friends that will last a lifetime! There are no costs for volunteers at PALS, and applicants can apply for travel costs to be covered as well. We are looking for male applicants at this point in our season. Females are welcome to apply but will likely be placed on a waitlist. The dates for each of our 15 camps is different based on their locations, but the dates for Baltimore are July 7-13 at UMBC, and Georgetown is July 28-August 3 at Georgetown University.

description: SEE invites you to UMD’s own Hoff Theater to unwind and join us for our first Free Fall Movie Series of the 2019-20 school year! (IMDb)Guardians of the Galaxy (2014) - August 30th @ 8:00pm(Action/Comedy) "A group of intergalactic criminals must pull together to stop a fanatical warrior with plans to purge the universe." (IMDb)Avengers: Endgame - August 31st @ 8:00pm(Action/Sci-Fi) "After the devastating events of Avengers: Infinity War (2018), the universe is in ruins. With the help of remaining allies, the Avengers assemble once more in order to reverse Thanos' actions and restore balance to the universe." (IMDb)Detective Pikachu - September 5th & 7th @ 8:00pm(Action/Comedy) "In a world where people collect Pokémon to do battle, a boy comes across an intelligent talking Pikachu who seeks to be a detective." (IMDb)Rocketman - September 11th & 12th @ 8:00pm(Biography/Drama) "A musical fantasy about the fantastical human story of Elton John's breakthrough years." (IMDb)Yesterday - September 13th & 14th @ 8:00pm(Comedy/Fantasy) "A struggling musician realizes he's the only person on Earth who can remember The Beatles after waking up in an alternate timeline where they never existed." (IMDb)John Wick: Chapter 3 - Parabellum - September 17th & 19th @ 8:00pm(Action/Crime/Thriller) "Super-assassin John Wick is on the run after killing a member of the international assassin's guild, and with a $14 million price tag on his head - he is the target of hit men and women everywhere." (IMDb)Bill and Ted’s Excellent Adventure (1989): A Special 30th Anniversary Screening - September 21st @ 10:00pm(Adventure/Comedy) "Two seemingly dumb teens set off on a quest to prepare the ultimate historical presentation with the help of a time machine." (IMDb)Midsommar - September 26th & 27th @ 8:00pm(Drama/Horror/Mystery) "A couple travels to Sweden to visit a rural hometown's fabled mid-summer festival. What begins as an idyllic retreat quickly devolves into an increasingly violent and bizarre competition at the hands of a pagan cult." (IMDb)The Rocky Horror Picture Show (1975) - September 28th @ 10:00pm(Comedy/Musical) "A newly engaged couple have a breakdown in an isolated area and must pay a call to the bizarre residence of Dr. Frank-N-Furter." (IMDb)Toy Story 4 - October 3rd & 4th @ 8:00pm(Animation/Comedy) "When a new toy called "Forky" joins Woody and the gang, a road trip alongside old and new friends reveals how big the world can be for a toy." (IMDb)Each screening will be in Hoff Theatre inside the Stamp Student Union. Each screening is open for anyone to attend and doors will open 30 minutues prior to showtime. Seating will be available on a first-come, first serve basis.All weekend movies hosted by Terps After Dark.

name: Camp PALS Volunteer opportunity
description: Volunteer to be a Counselor for the PALS program Camp PALS this summer. PALS is a nonprofit organization that provides one week long summer camp opportunities for teens and young adults with Down syndrome and their peers at 14 college campuses across the country. This is a one-week experience from 9am-5pm. Listed below are some details about Camp PALS: Here are some details about Camp PALS: - They offer 14 week long sleep-away camps across the country, including Camp PALS Georgetown, Chicago, and North Carolina! - Volunteer counselors are paired one-to-one with a camper to provide an opportunity to build -meaningful friendships through trips and activities - Looking for volunteers ages 16-30 who are welcoming, genuine, passionate, supportive, and fun which are all the values of the program. - No experience with Down syndrome or the disability community is necessary! They encourage groups of applicants to apply together to share the camp experience. If you are interested please visit the website at palsprograms.org/volunteer or check out their social media pages on Facebook or YouTube channel to get a look at what the PALS experience is like. PALS is an amazing opportunity to give back to the community, gain invaluable leadership skills, and make friends that will last a lifetime! There are no costs for volunteers at PALS, and applicants can apply for travel costs to be covered as well. We are looking for male applicants at this point in our season. Females are welcome to apply but will likely be placed on a waitlist. The dates for each of our 15 camps is different based on their locations, but the dates for Baltimore are July 7-13 at UMBC, and Georgetown is July 28-August 3 at Georgetown University.

name: Swarms of Mass Destruction: Are Drone Swarms Weapons of Mass Destruction?
description: On Friday, February 19 at 11:00 a.m. ET, WMD Warfare and Drone Swarms Analyst Zachary Kallenborn will provide a virtual talk on “Swarms of Mass Destruction: Are Drone Swarms Weapons of Mass Destruction?” This event is free and open to the public, but RSVPs are required. If you have any questions, please email the START events team at start-events@umd.edu. From the United States to China and Spain, numerous states are developing drone swarms. The technology has the potential to become a new weapon of destruction akin to chemical weapons, non-contagious biological weapons, and potentially low-yield nuclear weapons. Armed, fully autonomous drone swarms can bypass any arbitrary threshold for "mass destruction" and the limits of autonomous decision-making coupled with the complexity of swarms means the weapons cannot effectively discriminate between civilian and military targets. In considering traditional WMD roles, drone swarms could be effective mass casualty weapons, but are not likely to be effective strategic deterrents. Drone swarms could be useful anti-access/ area-denial and assassination weapons, depending on context. Zachary Kallenborn is a Research Affiliate with the Unconventional Weapons and Technology Division of the National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START), U.S. Army Training and Doctrine Command "Mad Scientist," and Senior Consultant at ABS Group. His work has been published in a wide range of peer-reviewed, trade, and popular outlets, including Foreign Policy, Slate, War on the Rocks, and the Nonproliferation Review. Journalists have written about and shared that research in Forbes, Popular Mechanics, Yahoo News!, the National Interest, and MSN. All views expressed here are Kallenborn’s own and do not represent those of any current or former employers, funders, or affiliates.

name: Homegrown: ISIS in America
description: On Tuesday, November 17 at 12:00 p.m. ET, George Washington University Program on Extremism Deputy Director Seamus Hughes and Program on Extremism Research Fellow Bennett Clifford will provide a virtual talk on their new book “Homegrown: ISIS in America.” This event is free and open to the public, but RSVPs are required. If you have any questions, please email the START events team at start-events@umd.edu. How big is the threat posed by American ISIS supporters? How many Americans have joined ISIS and how many want to return to the United States? Compared to participation by Americans in other jihadist groups, the scale of American involvement in jihadist activity today is unprecedented. This book, from one of the leading counter-terror centres, draws on first-hand interviews with former American Islamic State members and law enforcement officials who tracked them, and includes detailed analysis of the court cases against them and their social media presence. Homegrown reveals how and why ISIS was able to radicalize and recruit a new generation of jihadist sympathizers in America. Seamus Hughes is the Deputy Director of the Program on Extremism at George Washington University. He is an expert on terrorism, homegrown violent extremism, and countering violent extremism (CVE). He regularly provides commentary to media outlets, including the New York Times, The Washington Post, the Wall Street Journal, and BBC. Hughes previously worked at the National Counterterrorism Center (NCTC), serving as a lead staffer on U.S. government efforts to implement a national CVE strategy. Hughes created a groundbreaking intervention program to help steer individuals away from violence through non-law enforcement means, and worked closely with the FBI Joint Terrorism Task Force, Fusion Centers, and U.S. Attorney Offices. Bennett Clifford is a Research Fellow at the Program on Extremism. He studies supporters of extremist groups in the United States and in the Caucasus, Central Asia, and the Balkans. In addition, Clifford studies terrorists' adaptation of digital communications technologies for operational and strategic planning. He is the author of the Program on Extremism reports "The Travelers: American Jihadists in Syria and Iraq" and "Encrypted Extremism: Inside the English-Speaking Islamic State Ecosystem on Telegram," and his research is frequently featured in academic and popular publications, including the Atlantic, Lawfare, and the CTC Sentinel. Clifford is a Master of Arts in Law and Diplomacy candidate at the Fletcher School of Law and Diplomacy.

name: Fearless New Play Festival
description: The Fearless New Play Festival is a four-day celebration of new scripts in development that address urgent issues of today. The festival kicks off on November 19 with a speech by nationally renowned keynote playwright Lauren Yee. The festival features staged readings of new short plays by current TDPS students and alumni from November 19-22. Selected plays for the 2020 Fearless New Play Festival By Grace (Part Two) by Agyeiwaa Asante ’18 A Tea Party by Mariel Berlin-Fischler ’14 All of my Bullies and Where They Are Now by Elizabeth Crino ’18 Ghost Story by Evangelina Hakes ’19 The Ice Room by Liz Maestri ’03 RAPunzel by Jasmine Mitchell ‘20 Tiny Ruins by April Monu ’18 Please Like Me by Jordan Resnick ’22 Loving in the Age of Social Distancing by Amber Smithers ‘20 The Tao Island by Lyra Woods ’17 Announcing Keynote Playwright Lauren Yee The School of Theatre, Dance, and Performance Studies is thrilled to announce that internationally-renowned playwright Lauren Yee will be our 2020 keynote playwright. Lauren Yee is a playwright, screenwriter, and TV writer born and raised in San Francisco. She currently lives in New York City. Her play Cambodian Rock Band, with music by Dengue Fever and others, just had a lauded off-Broadway run at Signature Theatre. Her plays The Great Leap and Cambodian Rock Band led the list of top 10 most produced plays in the country for the 2019-20 season. She is the winner of the 2019 Doris Duke Artist Award for outstanding contributions to theater, the 2019 Steinberg Playwright Award, the Horton Foote Prize, the Kesselring Prize, the ATCA/Steinberg Award, American Academy of Arts and Letters literature award, and the Francesca Primus Prize. She has been a finalist for the Edward M. Kennedy Prize and the Susan Smith Blackburn Prize. Her plays were the #1 and #2 plays on the 2017 Kilroys List. Lauren is a Residency 5 playwright at Signature Theatre in New York, New Dramatists member (class of 2025), Ma-Yi Writers’ Lab member, former Princeton University Hodder fellow, and Playwrights Realm alumni playwright. She earned her BA at Yale and her MFA at UC San Diego, and American Theatre Magazine named her as the second most-produced playwright in the country for the 2019/20 season. For more info, please visit www.laurenyee.com.

name: TerpService Days - Community Forklift
description: Community Forklift is no ordinary home improvement or environmental protection center. It's both! The organization provides donated building materials to our College Park community at low prices, helping to reduce the cost of living. Donations from homeowners and contractors allow for environmental preservation in two ways: gently used furniture and other supplies are kept out of landfills and incinerators, and the environmental damage caused by producing new building materials is eliminated. Students will support Community Forklift by sorting, preparing, and stocking green building supplies for community clients. Volunteers should wear "work" clothes that can get dirty or even stained with paint and must wear closed-toed shoes. Volunteers should also dress in layers for the weather and bring a reusable water bottle. Work gloves and extra t-shirts will be provided by TerpService. TerpService Days are one-time days of service targeted at the broad campus community. Students with significant or no experience in service-learning are welcome to participate. Student groups also enjoy participating in the service days. http://thestamp.umd.edu/leadership_community_service-learning/programs/terpservice/terpservice_days

name: Cipher Tech Solutions Workshop & Tech Talk
description: Since 2001 we’ve all heard the media buzz about “nameless U.S. officials” claiming that terrorists and foreign intelligence services have been using steganography applications to facilitate covert communication between their operatives. However, it wasn’t until June of 2010, when the FBI caught a ring of Russian spies in DC, that steganography really entered the limelight. That summer, it was openly confirmed that these spies had, in fact, been communicating with Moscow via covert communication channels afforded to them through custom written Steganography applications. Although equally mysterious, data carving, which is the art of recovering deleted files from unallocated disk space, sees even less media attention than steganography. However, it typically plays a critical role in almost every digital forensic examination. In an interactive session on Tuesday March 4th Cipher Tech will discuss the conceptual fundamentals of both steganography and data carving techniques and will challenge you to put your newfound knowledge to use by implementing the algorithms in the language of your choice. Use your scripts to solve different challenges throughout the talk and unlock some cool swag.

name: ACTnow with Harlem Quartet ft. Ilmar Gavilán & Aldo López Gavilán: Barriers to Entry: Music-Making Across the Geopolitical Divide
description: From themes of racial violence and cultural appropriation to multiculturalism and gender equality, the work of The Clarice's artists is complex, provocative and deeply sensitive. Arts Citizenship Talks (ACTnow) are opportunities to hear from these artists about the issues reflected in their works. These conversations are an invitation to act now! For decades, siblings Aldo López Gavilán and Ilmar Gavilán sat on opposite sides of the US-Cuba feud. Despite their shared heritage and profession, the brothers remained estranged well into their adult lives, unable to traverse the vast geopolitical chasm separating the two nations. In this discussion, the Gavilán brothers and Harlem Quartet investigate musical collaboration between artists of countries with notoriously difficult relations. Featuring excerpts from their documentary Los Hermanos, the presentation will address the human consequences of this decades-old political crisis. Reserve tickets to Harlem Quartet & Aldo López-Gavilán. Health + SafetyThere may be COVID safety policies such as mask requirements in place when you attend this event. Please see our health & safety page for the most up to date information about attendance!

description: Do you want to make a REAL impact on one of NASA's missions? Are you looking to shape the next generation of space technologies? The XR Club is putting together a proposal to participate in the 2022 NASA SUITS Challenge, where teams of college students design and prototype an augmented reality interface for the space helmets that will be used by astronauts on NASA's 2024 Artemis mission to the moon. This interface would assist astronauts with various tasks on their mission, from navigating around and exploring new areas of the Moon to gathering samples of and conduct experiments on the lunar surface. This year's challenge also has a new focus on search and rescue as well as the use of tele-robotics and other peripheral devices that further assist the astronaut. Towards the end of the challenge in May 2022, selected teams will fly out to Houston to test out their prototypes in the simulated lunar environment at NASA's Johnson Space Center. The challenge also includes an outreach component, where teams showcase their achievements through social media, local news outlets, research papers, and K-12 outreach. If you're interested in augmented reality, virtual reality, game development, app development, artificial intelligence, computer vision, cloud computing, robotics, 3D printing, UI/UX design, marketing, teaching, or research, please stop by MTH B0421 on Thursday, September 30 at 6:30 PM to learn more about the challenge, our proposal, and how you can get involved in this real-world project. name: Malpaso Dance Company
description: Join us in person at The Clarice! Please note that this performance will not be livestreamed. Mixing modern Cuban music with contemporary classical and electronic sounds, Malpaso Dance Company has become one of Cuba’s most driven and in-demand touring dance troupes. Since their American debut in 2014, their innovations in the modern dance landscape have led to collaborations with elite international composers and have earned praise as, “an unfailingly open and generous crew” (The New York Times). At The Clarice, Malpaso presents three reflections on the ways an individual interacts with the rest of the world. Indomitable Waltz by Los Angeles choreographer Aszure Barton grippingly explores the emotional range of human relationships through black-clad figures that emerge from the dark to dazzle in the light, moving in and out of groups of ever-shifting sizes. Ocaso, choreographed by Malpaso cofounder Osnel Delgado, is a duet that grapples with the power of young love to animate, support, illuminate and devastate, brazenly set to the sounds of Autechre, Kronos Quartet and Max Richter. A stirring work about identity and self-discovery, Malpaso presents its 2018 re-staging of the acclaimed Tabula Rasa in collaboration with legendary Israeli choreographer Ohad Naharin. During the 2020-21 season, Malpaso artists provided teaching videos for dance classes in the School of Theatre, Dance, and Performance Studies (TDPS). While visiting The Clarice this season, members of Malpaso Dance Company will visit TDPS Dance Technique classes and will lead a post-performance Q & A. Health + Safety There may be COVID safety policies such as mask requirements in place when you attend this event. Please see our health & safety page for the most up to date information about attendance!

name: Veterans Yoga
description: Sun Salutations (8/31) Get ready for a class to introduce health and vitality into the semester! This short class includes 20 minutes of cleansing movement fit for yogis of all shapes, sizes, and experience levels. Bonus: Do you not have time to relax and let go for even just a few minutes? Your instructor includes at least five minutes of required shavasana practice at the end of each class to give the mind a break from the rest of the world. Learn a New Pose (9/2) Today’s yoga session will include 18 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out, meaning that yogis of all experience and backgrounds will benefit! Get ready to build strength and resilience with this fun-to learn movement. Relaxation Meditation (9/7) Tuesday’s session will be focused on grounding yourself in this new semester. Just fifteen minutes of passive, yet focused yoga practice will bring you into the moment and out of the stresses of the new semester. Get a Workout in (9/9) After Tuesday’s session focused on relaxation and finding ground in the new semester, it’s time to ramp up the heat. You would never believe what just twenty minutes of poses can do to get that blood pumping and the sweat pouring! Don’t worry, though! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Open the Hips (9/14) We have been in class for a couple of weeks now and our bodies need us to keep moving to stay open and ready for all that life has to offer. Twenty three minutes of opening the hips will keep them from tightening from all the stress and constant sitting motion. Don’t forget! We also include at least five minutes of time to destress and prepare for the rest of the week. Learn a New Pose (9/16) Today’s yoga session will include 24 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out. Yogis of all experience and backgrounds will benefit from this fun practice! Get ready to build some awesome abdominal strength with this sequence. Relaxation Meditation (9/21) Today’s session will be focused on grounding yourself in this new semester. Twenty six minutes of passive, yet focused yoga practice will bring you into the moment and out of the stresses of the semester’s stressors. Getting in a Workout! (9/23) After Tuesday’s session focused on relaxation and finding ground in this awesome in-person semester, it’s time to get that body moving. Just thirty three minutes of poses will get that blood pumping and the sweat pouring! Don’t worry! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Plus, we won’t leave your muscles stiff from the hard work! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for the Booty (9/28) Looking to add cushion and tone to your derriere? Who isn’t?! Today’s session will be devoted to working to add strength to the glutes and hamstrings. Twenty minutes of work will show you some tips and tools to build your important muscle groups that keep your body healthy and moving! Learn a New Pose (9/30) Today’s yoga session will include 25 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out! Even the simplest of poses require detail-orientation! Get ready to build strength and resilience in simple poses. Relaxation Meditation (10/5) Tuesday’s session will be focused on staying sane as the semester continues to pose more difficulties. This is a time for you to take 26 minutes to treat yourself to reduce stress and a little self-care. Get a Workout In (10/7) After Tuesday’s session focused on relaxation and de-stressing, it’s time to move the mind, body, and spirit. Just 34 minutes of yoga flow will get that blood pumping! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in and focused throughout the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Plus, we won’t leave your muscles stiff from the hard work! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for Weak and Tight Shoulders (10/12) We get it. Being an athlete, veteran, human, parent, student, etc. comes with a price. Usually that price is paid in the body. Today we are going to focus on restoring weak and/or tight shoulders. Don’t shy away from class out of fear of injury! There are modifications for all flexibility levels in the shoulders. We are working to improve, not perfect! After all, we only have twenty six minutes! Learn a New Pose (10/14) Today’s yoga session will include 34 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out! Poses that seem difficult from the outside may be a bit simpler than you anticipate! We are focused on safety in strength. So first, we will build strength and confidence. Then we will build upon simple poses to create a beautiful movement to feel proud about. Relaxation Meditation (10/19) We are mid-semester. While it feels like this is the time to be working your butt off with as few breaks as possible, don’t forget about the importance of daily self-care. Today’s class will be nineteen minutes focused on nothing but bringing you back to yourself. This is a time to reclaim the best parts of yourself and create the person you want to be with focused intention. Get a Workout In (10/21) Tuesday got us mentally focused for the week, so now it is time to ramp up the energy to end the week strong! Thirty-one minutes of yoga flow will get that blood pumping! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in and focused. Don’t forget a towel! We will leave your muscles feeling worked, but not too stiff! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for Back Pain (10/26) Is your back constantly feeling stiff? Is the lower back achy and shoulder blades tight? Come to today’s yoga session for the opportunity to release some of that stiffness, and open yourself up to a world of relief! You might be surprised at what a short 33 minutes of stretching and strengthening can do for the body. Learn a New Pose (10/28) Ready to expand your yoga knowledge and experience? Today’s class will revolve around learning a yoga pose through-and-through. There is no reason to worry about the experience level needed for the pose, as all poses learned and performed here can be done at any level! Set aside 33 minutes and get mentally ready to learn reverse warrior so we can add it to your yoga repertoire! Relaxation Meditation (11/2) Meditating on a regular basis has positive effects on the body and mind, such as greater sense of focus, muscle relaxation, and increased creativity. Today’s meditation will be focused on gratitude and increasing happiness. Giving thanks can come in many forms, but have you tried it in the form of meditation?! Getting in a Workout! (11/4) After Tuesday’s session focused on gratitude in this challenging semester, it’s time to get that body moving. Just 34 minutes of sweat-inducing poses will get that blood pumping! This class is fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Plus, we won’t leave your muscles stiff from the hard work! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for a Better Mood (11/9) College is demanding, stressful, and can induce negative feelings! Combat those real-time stresses by moving the body and bonding with fellow veterans. Coming to this thirty minute vinyasa class will open the heart to the positivity you need to get you to the end of the semester. Learn a New Pose (11/11) Ready to expand your yoga knowledge and experience? Today’s class will revolve around learning a yoga pose through-and-through. There is no reason to worry about the experience level needed for the pose, as all poses learned and performed here can be done at any level! Set aside 35 minutes and get mentally ready to learn a new pose to add to your yoga repertoire! Relaxation Meditation (11/16) Today’s meditation practice will be short, sweet, and perfect to regain focus on your workflow. As we near the end of the semester, stress increases, the mind wanders, and we lose focus. We will be going through meditation techniques that can be utilized at home, work, or on the bus. Don’t underestimate the power of this 26 minute session. Come join your fellow veterans and enjoy the feeling of a clear mind. Get a Workout In (11/18) After Tuesday’s session focused on de-stressing and refocusing, it’s time to move that body. Just 34 minutes of yoga flow will get that blood pumping! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in and focused throughout the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Plus, we won’t leave your muscles stiff from the hard work! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for Neck Pain (11/23) After months of looking down at our computer screens, it’s no wonder so many of us have the amount of pain in our necks that we do! Today’s class will be all about de-stressing, communication, and releasing the tension in the neck through yoga practice. Set aside 31 minutes for this perfectly-paced practice.

NOTES: This workshop requires you to bring a computer with Unity 2021.2 installed. The Unity Editor could take 30 mins or longer to download and install, so you will not have enough time during the workshop to install the software without falling behind. It is recommended you install the software well in advance of the workshop. This workshop will start promptly at 6:30 PM, with the assumption you have Unity installed. We will be in the room 30 minutes prior to the workshop (i.e. 6:00 PM) to assist any attendees with troubleshooting any problems they have with the installation process. You are also encouraged to ask for assistance earlier via our Discord or our Open Lab Hours. It is strongly recommended that you bring a physical mouse, since it can be difficult to work in Unity with a laptop trackpad. As per University guidelines, all attendees of this event will be required to wear KN95 masks. Violators will be denied entry into the event.

description: The John and Stella Graves Makerspace and the Libraries' GIS Team are hosting a student competition highlighting our Augmented Reality Sandbox and its applications across many academic disciplines. Please note that this is a one-way trip: The DC Bike Party leaves our final destination (Dupont Circle) by 8pm, has one midway party stop, and one afterparty stop, which goes on into the late evening.
