name: AR Sandbox: April Topography Competition
description: The John and Stella Graves Makerspace and the Libraries' GIS Team are hosting a student competition highlighting our Augmented Reality Sandbox and its applications across many academic disciplines. There will be a total of 5 topography competitions that will take place in the Fall '23 and Spring '24 semesters. The winner of each monthly competition will receive a $50 Amazon gift card! From April 8th-19th, undergraduate and graduate students are invited to use the AR Sandbox to create and submit a 3D rendering of the provided 2D topographical map. This month's map is of a portion of Iceland. Participants' submissions will be judged based on aesthetics and overall accuracy to the reference map. The GIS team will be hosting an instructional session on Wednesday April 10th from 12:30-1pm to provide additional support for students creating their map submissions. Submissions can be anytime during the Makerspace's hours in these two weeks, but the event is recommended for students who are unfamiliar with reading topography. For full competition rules and submission instructions, see details below. Competition Rules 1. Participants must be currently enrolled undergraduate or graduate students at the University of Maryland, College Park. 2. Each submission should be completed and submitted by one individual student. 3. Each student is allowed only one submission per competition (5 total submissions if a student participates in every iteration of the competition). 4. Each participant will have a maximum of 30 minutes to complete their submission. 5. The winner of the competition will be announced February 19th, 2024 6. The winning submission will be posted to the @umdlibstem Instagram. 7. Before collecting the $50 Amazon gift card prize, the winner will need to provide contact information and a signature for Library documentation. Submission Instructions 1. Book time to use the AR Sandbox here. You will receive an email to confirm your requested time. We may not approve your request if there are conflicting appointments, trainings, or makerspace events. 2. Come to the JSG Makerspace in the STEM Library at your confirmed time. Makerspace staff will help you set up the AR Sandbox to complete your submission. 3. Recreate the 2D topographical map using the AR Sandbox within the 30 minute time limit. 4. Take a picture of both the sandbox itself and the screen projecting your creation's topography. 5. Name your image files in the following format: FirstNameLastName_sandboxsubmission 6. Complete the submission google form, including both photos. 7. Wait to hear if you are our winner!

name: Naloxone Training
description: The University of Maryland Health Center is designated as an Overdose Response Program (ORP) through the Maryland Department of Health. As part of this designation, we offer overdose response resources to the UMD community, free of charge. One of the most popular resources we offer is Naloxone, an opioid overdose reversal medication. Similarly to how an EpiPen temporarily blocks the life-threatening symptoms of an allergic reaction (i.e. inability to breathe) while emergency medical assistance arrives, Naloxone offers this temporary support for those experiencing an opioid overdose. To get your free Naloxone through the Health Center, all you have to do is attend a brief training, which goes over how to recognize signs of an opioid overdose, instructions for using Naloxone, and what to do as emergency medical assistance makes its way to you and the person in crisis. Trainings are all offered in the Sahet Room of the Health Center, just past the main entrance to the building, and are free to any UMD community member interested in attending! Registration is required for attendance.

name: Beekeeping Club Weekly Meeting
description: During the late spring, summer, and early fall, we have meetings to check on our bees. We learn about sustainable beekeeping practices, what to look for and do while taking care of bees. People who show up to this meeting will have to wear bee-safe clothing such as close toed shoes, and preferably pants, though we have full suits and half suits along with gloves provided. Participants will also have to sign a safety waiver which accepts the possibility of bee stings. When it is too cold or rainy, we go to the UMD Greenhouses to complete workshops such as candles, chapstick, and soap using beeswax. Feel free to reach out through our TerpLink page, our email, or the Discord for more information! The Beekeeping Club does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, religion, age, or physical ability. The Mission of The Beekeeping Club is to educate students about bees and beekeeping through hands-on experience and lectures, about harvesting raw products from them in sustainable ways, and about turning those raw products a variety of goods. The Beekeeping Club seeks to offer anyone with a curiosity or passion for bees and beekeeping the ability to participate in beekeeping regardless of their skill level or prior experience and to guide them in learning more about bees and the role beekeeping plays a sustainable world.

name: AR Sandbox: February Topography Competition
description: The John and Stella Graves Makerspace and the Libraries' GIS Team are hosting a student competition highlighting our Augmented Reality Sandbox and its applications across many academic disciplines. There will be a total of 5 topography competitions that will take place in the Fall '23 and Spring '24 semesters. The winner of each monthly competition will receive a $50 Amazon gift card! From February 5th-16th, undergraduate and graduate students are invited to use the AR Sandbox to create and submit a 3D rendering of the provided 2D topographical map. This month's map is of a portion of Lake Tahoe in California. Participants' submissions will be judged based on aesthetics and overall accuracy to the reference map. The GIS team will be hosting open hours on Tuesdays from 1-2pm and Wednesdays from 1-3pm to provide additional support for students creating their map submissions. Submissions can be created outside of these hours, but they are recommended for students who are unfamiliar with reading topography. For full competition rules and submission instructions, see details below. Competition Rules 1. Participants must be currently enrolled undergraduate or graduate students at the University of Maryland, College Park. 2. Each submission should be completed and submitted by one individual student. 3. Each student is allowed only one submission per competition (5 total submissions if a student participates in every iteration of the competition). 4. Each participant will have a maximum of 30 minutes to complete their submission. 5. The winner of the competition will be announced February 19th, 2024 6. The winning submission will be posted to the @umdlibstem Instagram. 7. Before collecting the $50 Amazon gift card prize, the winner will need to provide contact information and a signature for Library documentation. Submission Instructions 1. Book time to use the AR Sandbox here. You will receive an email to confirm your requested time. We may not approve your request if there are conflicting appointments, trainings, or makerspace events. 2. Come to the JSG Makerspace in the STEM Library at your confirmed time. Makerspace staff will help you set up the AR Sandbox to complete your submission. 3. Recreate the 2D topographical map using the AR Sandbox within the 30 minute time limit. 4. Take a picture of both the sandbox itself and the screen projecting your creation's topography. 5. Name your image files in the following format: FirstNameLastName_sandboxsubmission 6. Complete the submission google form, including both photos. 7. Wait to hear if you are our winner! name: En'Rage Models Practice
description: Our practice sessions are dynamic and empowering, designed to build confidence, enhance runway skills, and foster creativity in a supportive environment. Each session begins with a warm-up to prepare our models for the physical and mental demands of the runway. Models are then guided through a series of runway walks, where they practice posture, poise, and movement in a variety of styles that challenge traditional norms of fashion and modeling. Throughout the practice, we focus on perfecting choreography for upcoming shows, allowing models to develop their unique flair while staying in sync with the group’s overall performance. Our experienced runway coaches provide individual feedback to ensure that each model feels confident in expressing their own style, aligning with our mission of self-empowerment and diversity. In addition to runway practice, we also incorporate photoshoot preparation, helping models become comfortable in front of the camera, and working on their poses and expressions. Music is played to set the tone, and we regularly rotate different fashion themes to keep practices fresh and engaging. Each session concludes with a debrief, where we emphasize the importance of mutual support and encouragement, celebrating personal growth and teamwork. En'Rage Models practices are more than just rehearsals—they are an opportunity for our members to develop their self-esteem, push creative boundaries, and prepare for the high-energy experience of the runway.
location: Department of Mathematics, William E. Kirwan Hall

description: During this meeting we will open and inspect our three hives to monitor their health and activity as populations increase with the coming spring. We learn about sustainable beekeeping practices, what to look for and do while taking care of bees. People who show up to this meeting will have to wear bee-safe clothing such as close toed shoes, and preferably pants, though we have full suits and half suits along with gloves provided. Participants will also have to sign a safety waiver which accepts the possibility of bee stings. Join our Discord: https://discord.gg/tR9FyWVm8E for the most up-to-date information and announcements on event details. Also feel free to reach out through our TerpLink page or email for any questions you might have. The Mission of The Beekeeping Club is to educate students about bees and beekeeping through hands-on experience and lectures, about harvesting raw products from them in sustainable ways, and about turning those raw products a variety of goods. The Beekeeping Club seeks to offer anyone with a curiosity or passion for bees and beekeeping the ability to participate in beekeeping regardless of their skill level or prior experience and to guide them in learning more about bees and the role beekeeping plays a sustainable world.

name: New Organization Welcome Meeting | In-Person
description: New Organization Welcome Meetings serve to inform organizations that are new or formerly inactive on the steps of the registration process and are a requirement for registration. While only one organization member (does not have to be in a leadership position) is required to attend, we recommend that more come. If you have already attended a New Organization Welcome Meeting for your organization in the Fall 2024 semester, you will not have to attend another meeting for your organization. If you attended any New Organization Welcome meeting prior to Fall 2024, you will need to attend a meeting this semester. If you are attempting to register multiple new organizations, you only need to attend one meeting. name: SKY Campus Happiness Retreat Online Version
description: At the university level and in competitions, students are subjected to academic, emotional, and physical stress. Effective stress management is useful not only for academic success but even for competitions that students participate in for an enriching university experience. Sudarshan Kriya and Yoga (SKY breath Meditation) have been scientifically validated to not only reduce stress, depression, and anxiety significantly but also enhance well being. SKY Happiness Retreat is a holistic well-being program taught over 3 consecutive days (3 sessions) (in-person). This nine-hour retreat includes: 1. SKY Breath Meditation 2. Evidence-based breathwork techniques 3. Social connection 4. Mindful leadership and light yoga SKY Breath Meditation and the 3-session Retreat have been shown in research to significantly reduce anxiety and depression, lower stress markers, and increase wellbeing, focus, improved sleep, optimism, and social connection. Participants report an increased ability to stay calm, confident, and resilient amidst challenges, increased levels of social connection and feelings of inclusion, and less suicidal feelings. SK&Y will benefit UMD students including those on the SKY at UMD to better manage their stress & loneliness especially during these unprecedented times and have an enriching university experience. Over the last few semesters that this program has been offered on campus, there’s been an astounding amount of positive impact, also chronicled in multiple articles in The Forbes, Lantern, Huffington Post, etc. Here’s one of the articles from studies done at Yale and Harvard: https://www.forbes.com/sites/jessicagold/2020/09/02/how-to-decrease-back-to-college-anxiety-just-breathe/?sh=280d0bd42df1 Also this video snapshots Testimonials from the Yale University: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Vlu3arLc0WE&t=57s Students gain foundational stress management and leadership skills, develop a daily breathing and meditation practice, learn a short personal yoga practice, develop strategies for social connection and team-building and engage in a peer-driven service initiative. The retreat features interactive group processes, experiential learning, emotional intelligence training, breathing techniques, yoga, meditation, leadership and service. We are inviting the SKY campus retreat facilitator from IAHV (https://www.skycampushappiness.org/about) to facilitate this in-person retreat at UMD. After the retreat student leaders introduce some of the mindful practices to students of the campus who didn’t attend the retreat. name: SKY Campus Happiness Retreat Online Version
description: At the university level and in competitions, students are subjected to academic, emotional, and physical stress. Effective stress management is useful not only for academic success but even for competitions that students participate in for an enriching university experience. Sudarshan Kriya and Yoga (SKY breath Meditation) have been scientifically validated to not only reduce stress, depression, and anxiety significantly but also enhance well being. SKY Happiness Retreat is a holistic well-being program taught over 3 consecutive days (3 sessions) (in-person). This nine-hour retreat includes: 1. SKY Breath Meditation 2. Evidence-based breathwork techniques 3. Social connection 4. Mindful leadership and light yoga SKY Breath Meditation and the 3-session Retreat have been shown in research to significantly reduce anxiety and depression, lower stress markers, and increase wellbeing, focus, improved sleep, optimism, and social connection. Participants report an increased ability to stay calm, confident, and resilient amidst challenges, increased levels of social connection and feelings of inclusion, and less suicidal feelings. SK&Y will benefit UMD students including those on the SKY at UMD to better manage their stress & loneliness especially during these unprecedented times and have an enriching university experience. Over the last few semesters that this program has been offered on campus, there’s been an astounding amount of positive impact, also chronicled in multiple articles in The Forbes, Lantern, Huffington Post, etc. Here’s one of the articles from studies done at Yale and Harvard: https://www.forbes.com/sites/jessicagold/2020/09/02/how-to-decrease-back-to-college-anxiety-just-breathe/?sh=280d0bd42df1 Also this video snapshots Testimonials from the Yale University: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Vlu3arLc0WE&t=57s Students gain foundational stress management and leadership skills, develop a daily breathing and meditation practice, learn a short personal yoga practice, develop strategies for social connection and team-building and engage in a peer-driven service initiative. The retreat features interactive group processes, experiential learning, emotional intelligence training, breathing techniques, yoga, meditation, leadership and service. We are inviting the SKY campus retreat facilitator from IAHV (https://www.skycampushappiness.org/about) to facilitate this in-person retreat at UMD. After the retreat student leaders introduce some of the mindful practices to students of the campus who didn’t attend the retreat. Students use this as an opportunity to improve leadership skills, as well as contribute to the overall development of the campus community.

name: Black Prom: Harlem Nights
description: Dress Code: 1920’s Formal Glam About Black Prom: Harlem Nights The Black Prom: Harlem Nights is a glamorous celebration of Black culture, excellence, and community, inspired by the rich history of the Harlem Renaissance. This event serves as a bridge between our shared legacies and the horizons we aspire to reach, offering a night of elegance, empowerment, and joy. Rooted in the theme “Black Legacies and Horizons,” Black Prom: Harlem Nights honors the artistic, intellectual, and cultural contributions of the Harlem Renaissance, a time when Black creatives redefined identity and reshaped the world’s view of Black brilliance. From jazz melodies to the evocative poetries, Harlem’s history reminds us of the power of our heritage to inspire future generations. At its core, Black Prom: Harlem Nights is also a tribute to Black Joy and Celebration, embracing the beauty and diversity of the Black experience. This evening invites attendees to step into the glamour and sophistication of the 1920s while celebrating their own unique paths and the limitless possibilities ahead. Through music, dance, and performances, we reflect on how far we’ve come and look forward to the horizons of creativity, leadership, and resilience yet to be explored. Harlem Nights is more than an event, it’s a statement of pride in where we’ve been and a declaration of hope for where we’re going. Together, we revel in the enduring spirit of Black excellence, honor the legacies that paved the way, and embrace the bright horizons of tomorrow. Doors Open at 6:45 Collaborators: Black Student Union (BSU), Enrage Models, The Caribbean Students Association (CSA), East African Student Union (EASU), The National Pan-Hellenic Council (NPHC) Sponsors : Lavender Lab & African American Studies Department (AASU)

name: En'Rage Models Practice
description: Our practice sessions are dynamic and empowering, designed to build confidence, enhance runway skills, and foster creativity in a supportive environment. Each session begins with a warm-up to prepare our models for the physical and mental demands of the runway. Models are then guided through a series of runway walks, where they practice posture, poise, and movement in a variety of styles that challenge traditional norms of fashion and modeling. Throughout the practice, we focus on perfecting choreography for upcoming shows, allowing models to develop their unique flair while staying in sync with the group’s overall performance. Our experienced runway coaches provide individual feedback to ensure that each model feels confident in expressing their own style, aligning with our mission of self-empowerment and diversity. In addition to runway practice, we also incorporate photoshoot preparation, helping models become comfortable in front of the camera, and working on their poses and expressions. Music is played to set the tone, and we regularly rotate different fashion themes to keep practices fresh and engaging. Each session concludes with a debrief, where we emphasize the importance of mutual support and encouragement, celebrating personal growth and teamwork. En'Rage Models practices are more than just rehearsals—they are an opportunity for our members to develop their self-esteem, push creative boundaries, and prepare for the high-energy experience of the runway.
location: Department of Mathematics, William E. Kirwan Hall

name: National Hillel Basketball Tournament 2025
description: The National Hillel Basketball Tournament (NHBT) was founded in 2010 to bring Jewish students together around the inclusive and encompassing game of basketball. Solely organized by a board of 30 highly motivated students, what began as a small event has quickly developed into one of the largest collegiate gatherings of Jewish students in the country. Now in its 13th year, the non-profit initiative, annually housed in the University of Maryland’s state-of-the-art facilities, attracts over 1,500 participants from across the United States and Canada. This year, we expect over 50 teams from over 30 universities across North America to partake in the weekend-long tournament experience. Players and fans also participate in various off-the-court programs such as Shabbat meals, keynote speakers, and an exciting bar night to kick the weekend off. In addition to NHBT’s impressive scale and reach, its impact has reached new heights in recent years. By providing students a chance to meet, socialize, and compete in a positive Jewish environment, NHBT serves as an oasis for students experiencing antisemitism on their respective campuses. By platforming like-minded organizations and starting initiatives, NHBT has provided a beacon of hope and togetherness for Jewish and campus communities far and wide.

name: Graduate Student Government Special-General Election & Constitutional Referendum
description: This is the online listing for the 2025 Graduate Student Government Special-General Election & Constitutional Referendum. This is not a singular event, but rather an ongoing process beginning on August 25, 2025 and ending on September 15, 2025. This process is being held to perform two primary functions: 1.) To fill vacancies in the 2025-2026 Graduate Student Assembly; and,2.) To hold a referendum on GSG Constitutional amendments proposed by the 2024-2025 GSG Constitution & Bylaws Review Committee after completion of our constitutionally mandated foundational document review process conducted every five years. A call for nominations to fill vacant program Assembly seats well be sent out on August 25, 2025. Nominations will remain open for two weeks, and will close on September 8, 2025. The voting period for the Special-General Election, as well as the constitutional referendum, will open shortly after nominations close on September 8, 2025 and will remain open for one week before closing at 11:59 pm on September 15, 2025. Results will be posted to the GSG website and sent out via email the following day. A constitutional referendum was last held during the May 2025 GSG General Election, and although the amendments received over 90% of votes in favor, the minimum threshold of votes (currently set at 1/20th of the graduate student body) was not reached, rendering the results of the May 2025 referendum invalid. As such, a repeat referendum is behind held during this Special-General Election period.

name: Screening of Bhopali on the 35th Anniversary of the Bhopal Gas Disaster
description: We are hosting a film screening on the occasion of the 35th Anniversary of the Bhopal Gas Disaster in collaboration with the International Campaign for Justice in Bhopal (ICJB), on Dec 3, Tuesday, at 6.00 pm in Room 1201, John S Toll Building at UMD. A short reminder on the history of the Bhopal Gas Disaster - In the night of Dec 3, 1984, the residents of the central Indian city of Bhopal woke up to the toxic fumes of methyl isocyanate, leaking from a Union Carbide pesticide plant nearby. Several thousands passed away on that night itself, while the still continuing impacts have claimed the lives of 20000+ and injury to 100000+. The perpetrators of one of the worst industrial and environmental disasters in the world remain scot-free, while the victims, survivors and even the future generations continue to fight against the apathy of the US based company, and the Indian and US governments. Join us in the screening of "Bhopali", an award winning documentary on the Bhopal disaster, which will be followed by a short interactive session where we can discuss ways to support the survivors of Bhopal. Feel free to invite anybody who might be interested. Hope to see you there! In solidarity, Association for India's Development - UMD

name: Connected Diaspora Keynote with Mauricio E. Ramírez
description: Mauricio E. Ramírez is an artist, curator, and Ph.D. Candidate in the Latin American and Latino Studies Department at UC Santa Cruz with an emphasis in Visual Studies. An expert on Latinx public murals and visual art in the San Francisco Bay Area, Mauricio’s dissertation, “Painting Central America: U.S. Central American Visual Art of San Francisco,” explores the visual expressions and solidarity that emerged in San Francisco’s Mission District as a response to the civil wars in El Salvador, Guatemala, and Nicaragua beginning in the 1980s. His research sheds light on the history of Central American art and activism, the emerging 1.5 and second-generation U.S. Central American artists, and the intersections of Latinx solidarity with Central Americans. Mauricio is currently a University of California President’s Pre-Professoriate Fellow and a SOMArts curatorial resident, co-curating the upcoming exhibition, CARAVANA: Mobilizing Central American Art (1984–Present), in San Francisco, March 2021. This keynote will stream live at stamp.umd.edu/cdkeynote

name: Register for Spring Social Change Writing Class!
description: ENGL292/ ENGL388C Writing for Change This class offers students an opportunity to combine service with scholarship. We will work with ninth grade students at local Northwestern High School to explore the ways writing can be used as a tool for social change. In collaboration with the high school students, we will host a performance event that opens a dialogue surrounding a pressing social issue. In addition to tutoring and mentoring, this class requires a good deal of writing. You will write multiple reflections, a literacy narrative, a creative composition, and publicity materials. You will conduct independent research and will be expected to switch fluidly between academic, creative, professional, and hybrid genres. We will also focus on developing critical self-awareness of our own relationships with literacy, writing, education, and activism. In addition to two weekly 75-minute meetings, this class requires commitment to an off-campus service-learning component for about 75 minutes, once a week (Tuesdays from 2:00-3:15, including transportation time). There will also be a fee collected for paperwork and background checks required for volunteering at NHS. The course has no prerequisites, but completion of ENGL101 is strongly recommended. Individuals interested in taking this class as ENGL388C, the Community Engagement Internship, can do so by signing up through the English Undergraduate Studies Office. The course meets Tuesdays from 2:00-4:45 (including our weekly visit to Northwestern) and Thursdays from 3:30-4:45. It fulfills the Diversity--Understanding Plural Societies and Scholarship-in-Practice General Education requirements and counts towards the Professional Writing and Rhetoric minors. For more questions, please e-mail the course instructor, Justin Lohr, at jlohr@umd.edu. 292 Spring 2019 Preview.docx Click to View

name: Camp PALS Volunteer opportunity
description: Volunteer to be a Counselor for the PALS program Camp PALS this summer. PALS is a nonprofit organization that provides one week long summer camp opportunities for teens and young adults with Down syndrome and their peers at 14 college campuses across the country. This is a one-week experience from 9am-5pm. Listed below are some details about Camp PALS: Here are some details about Camp PALS: - They offer 14 week long sleep-away camps across the country, including Camp PALS Georgetown, Chicago, and North Carolina! - Volunteer counselors are paired one-to-one with a camper to provide an opportunity to build -meaningful friendships through trips and activities - Looking for volunteers ages 16-30 who are welcoming, genuine, passionate, supportive, and fun which are all the values of the program. - No experience with Down syndrome or the disability community is necessary! They encourage groups of applicants to apply together to share the camp experience. If you are interested please visit the website at palsprograms.org/volunteer or check out their social media pages on Facebook or YouTube channel to get a look at what the PALS experience is like. PALS is an amazing opportunity to give back to the community, gain invaluable leadership skills, and make friends that will last a lifetime! There are no costs for volunteers at PALS, and applicants can apply for travel costs to be covered as well. We are looking for male applicants at this point in our season. Females are welcome to apply but will likely be placed on a waitlist. The dates for each of our 15 camps is different based on their locations, but the dates for Baltimore are July 7-13 at UMBC, and Georgetown is July 28-August 3 at Georgetown University.

name: SEE Presents: Free Fall Movie Series - Toy Story 4
description: SEE invites you to UMD’s own Hoff Theater to unwind and join us for our first Free Fall Movie Series of the 2019-20 school year! Enjoy and support several of this year’s hottest movies along with some classic cultural milestones in a large theatrical setting all semester long!Iron Man (2008)- August 29th @ 8:00pm(Action/Sci-Fi) "After being held captive in an Afghan cave, billionaire engineer Tony Stark creates a unique weaponized suit of armor to fight evil." (IMDb)Guardians of the Galaxy (2014) - August 30th @ 8:00pm(Action/Comedy) "A group of intergalactic criminals must pull together to stop a fanatical warrior with plans to purge the universe." (IMDb)Avengers: Endgame - August 31st @ 8:00pm(Action/Sci-Fi) "After the devastating events of Avengers: Infinity War (2018), the universe is in ruins. With the help of remaining allies, the Avengers assemble once more in order to reverse Thanos' actions and restore balance to the universe." (IMDb)Detective Pikachu - September 5th & 7th @ 8:00pm(Action/Comedy) "In a world where people collect Pokémon to do battle, a boy comes across an intelligent talking Pikachu who seeks to be a detective." (IMDb)Rocketman - September 11th & 12th @ 8:00pm(Biography/Drama) "A musical fantasy about the fantastical human story of Elton John's breakthrough years." (IMDb)Yesterday - September 13th & 14th @ 8:00pm(Comedy/Fantasy) "A struggling musician realizes he's the only person on Earth who can remember The Beatles after waking up in an alternate timeline where they never existed." (IMDb)John Wick: Chapter 3 - Parabellum - September 17th & 19th @ 8:00pm(Action/Crime/Thriller) "Super-assassin John Wick is on the run after killing a member of the international assassin's guild, and with a $14 million price tag on his head - he is the target of hit men and women everywhere." (IMDb)Bill and Ted’s Excellent Adventure (1989): A Special 30th Anniversary Screening - September 21st @ 10:00pm(Adventure/Comedy) "Two seemingly dumb teens set off on a quest to prepare the ultimate historical presentation with the help of a time machine." (IMDb)Midsommar - September 26th & 27th @ 8:00pm(Drama/Horror/Mystery) "A couple travels to Sweden to visit a rural hometown's fabled mid-summer festival. What begins as an idyllic retreat quickly devolves into an increasingly violent and bizarre competition at the hands of a pagan cult." (IMDb)The Rocky Horror Picture Show (1975) - September 28th @ 10:00pm(Comedy/Musical) "A newly engaged couple have a breakdown in an isolated area and must pay a call to the bizarre residence of Dr. Frank-N-Furter." (IMDb)Toy Story 4 - October 3rd & 4th @ 8:00pm(Animation/Comedy) "When a new toy called "Forky" joins Woody and the gang, a road trip alongside old and new friends reveals how big the world can be for a toy." (IMDb)Each screening will be in Hoff Theatre inside the Stamp Student Union. Each screening is open for anyone to attend and doors will open 30 minutues prior to showtime. Seating will be available on a first-come, first serve basis.All weekend movies hosted by Terps After Dark.

name: Spring 2021 ODK Drury Bagwell Lecture: Living Virtually, Thinking Globally ft. Van Jones
description: ODK, the premier leadership honors society on campus, is excited to announce their spring lecture in honor of former Faculty Secretary Drury "Dru" Bagwell. We will be hosting Van Jones for our lecture, "Living Virtually, Thinking Globally" on Monday, May 3rd at 7PM in an online setting. This event is also brought to you through partnership with a host of departments and organizations on campus: the Office of Undergraduate Studies, the College of Behavioral & Social Sciences, the Stamp Student Union, the University Career Center & The President's Promise, the Department of Fraternity and Sorority Life, the Smith Center for Social Value Creation, the Counseling Center, the Honors College, and College Park Scholars. Van Jones is the Founder of Dream Corps, a social entrepreneur, a CNN political commentator, Emmy Award-winning producer, and a New York Times best-selling author. Famous for his heart-felt election night coverage, Jones showed up as “the voice of reason” for people in red states and blue throughout the volatile 2016 political season. In 2019, Van and his team at #cut50 succeeded in passing the FIRST STEP Act (a bipartisan Federal bill that the New York Times calls the most substantial breakthrough in criminal justice in a generation). Jones has founded and led numerous social enterprises engaged in social and environmental justice. These include: The Ella Baker Center for Human Rights, which promotes criminal justice reform Color of Change, which works for racial fairness through its over one million members Rebuild The Dream, a 21st Century "think tank" that champions innovative solutions to fix the U.S. economy and uplift the next generation. which promotes innovative policy solutions. The Dream Corps, an organization that brings people together to solve America's toughest problems. The Dream Corps' major initiatives are: Dream Corps TECH, aimed to help 100,000 young women and men from underrepresented backgrounds find success in the tech sector; Dream Corps JUSTICE, an initiative focused on making communities safer while reducing the number of people in our prisons and jails. And Green For All, which advances environmental solutions that prioritize families and workers living on the frontlines of some of the worst pollution in America. REFORM Alliance, which aims to transform probation and parole by changing laws, systems and culture to create real pathways to work and wellbeing. Magic Labs Media, founded by Jones and where he currently serves as its President. Jones is a Yale-educated attorney. He is the author of three New York Times best-selling books, The Green Collar Economy (2008) and Rebuild the Dream (2012) and Beyond the Messy Truth (2017). He was the main advocate for the Green Jobs Act. Signed into law by George W. Bush in 2007, the Green Jobs Act was the first piece of federal legislation to codify the term “green jobs.” During the Obama Administration, the legislation has resulted in $500 million in national funding for green jobs training. In 2009, Jones worked as the green jobs advisor to President Barack Obama. In this role, Jones helped to lead the inter-agency process that oversaw the multi-billion dollar investment in skills training and jobs development within the environmental and green energy sectors. Together with #cut50, Van succeeded in passing the FIRST STEP Act (a bipartisan Federal bill that the New York Times calls the most substantial breakthrough in criminal justice in a generation). Jones has been honored with numerous awards and spotlighted on several lists of high achievers, including: the World Economic Forum’s “Young Global Leader” designation; Rolling Stone’s 2012 “12 Leaders Who Get Things Done”; TIME’s 2009 “100 Most Influential People in The World”; and the Root's 2014 "The Root 100." In 2017, Van Jones signed a management deal with Roc Nation, becoming the first political commentator & activist in their family.

name: Brooklyn Rider: Healing Modes (USA)
description: From the ancient Greeks to modern American neuroscientists, people have long recognized the healing properties of music. In string quartet Brooklyn Rider’s stirring program Healing Modes, we hear a profound exploration of the power of music to help society recover from tumult and suffering. The program features gripping works by trailblazing living composers Caroline Shaw, Gabriela Lena Frank and Reena Esmail along with Ludwig van Beethoven’s fifteenth string quartet—all creating a sonoric testament to resilience and deliverance. Lauded by NPR as “a string quartet of boundless imagination,” Brooklyn Rider has collaborated with the likes of banjo master Béla Fleck, Iranian virtuoso Kayhan Kalhor and Mexican jazz singer Magos Herrera. Brooklyn Rider finds inspiration in diverse musical languages ranging from Persian classical music to Beethoven to the various voices of living composers—including UMD School of Music student composers as part of a Composer Reading on campus. Committed to inclusive programming and deep artistic collaborations, the quartet has also performed in The Clarice’s sensory-friendly series for Prince George’s County children with autism and other disabilities. In 2021-22, Brooklyn Rider will continue working with School of Music students and appear as part of the school’s Renegade series, which features innovative and entrepreneurial artists of various disciplines. For this event the audience is invited to experience the performance from a new vantage point. Audience seating will be on the Dekelboum stage, on risers where the orchestra typically sits. The musicians will perform on the front of the stage, facing the audience. Seating will be general admission. Program: Caroline Shaw: Schisma Gabriela Lena Frank: Kanto Kechua No. 2 Reena Esmail: Zeher (Poison) Ludwig van Beethoven: Quartet No. 15 in A minor, Op. 132 Health + SafetyThere may be COVID safety policies such as mask requirements in place when you attend this event. Please see our health & safety page for the most up to date information about attendance!

name: Resume Workshop - March 27th @ 5:30pm
description: Can your resume pass the 10-second test? 10-seconds are all the time an employer gives your resume in deciding to keep it or pass on it. It is your first impression and it needs to convince an employer that you are worth an interview. Please join us for our first Resume Workshop, March 27th from 5:30pm to 6:55pm, in Room 1111 of the Architecture building. This lively, fast-moving workshop will give students of the Master in Real Estate program a chance to have your resume reviewed by top industry professionals of the real estate industry; including CEOs, HR managers, entrepreneurs, and other top members of this dynamic industry! Working together you will determine if your resume contains the right information to land your ideal job, target your qualifications for a specific job, discuss what experiences are relevant, and explore where they are lacking and how to improve. If you are interested in attending the resume workshop, you must RSVP by following this link. Space is limited for this event, so please register before March 20, 2013. If you have any questions about the workshop, please do not hesitate to contact us at mwalsh9@umd.edu or rmunawar@terpmail.umd.edu . We look forward to seeing you on the 27th! --------------- Event Format Please bring MULTIPLE COPIES of your professional resume to the event (at least 5 copies) for editing. Introduction made by the President of SoRED of the participants and their background and the general format of the workshop. The event format will consists of “stations”—tables with one professional representing their specific area of expertise (leasing, brokerage, acquisition, development consultancy, etc.). Students will rotate between stations providing professionals with a copy of their resume to be reviewed. No more than 3 students will be allowed to sit at a table at one time and students will be given 20 minutes at each table. After 20 minutes they must move to a different table. We will rotate tables three times (totaling 60 minutes). This allows for a 10 minute introduction and for 15 minutes of networking or last minute resume questions at the end. Professionals will aim to spend 7-10 minutes addressing each resume. The idea is to present students with the truth regarding their resume and how it communicates the students strengths to a particular job/industry. Professionals will aim to be very honest with students about where their resumes are weak and how they can go about improving them—that’s the whole purpose of the event. --------- Confirmed Participating Professionals Josh Wooldridge, Senior Development Director - The Bainbridge Companies Jenna K. Polivka, Associate Vice President - Cassidy Turley Emily C. Smith, Senior Associate - CBRE-Global Corporate Services Shawna Jones, President, The Jones Group - The Jones Group Michael Pitchford, President & CEO - Community Preservation & Development Corporation Al Tetrault, Professor, Principal - Tetrault and Associates (formerly)

name: cybergamut Technical Tuesdays - Cyber Security Strategy — Why We’re Losing and What’s Needed to Win by Steve Chabinsky of CrowdStrike
description: cybergamut Technical Tuesday is for cyber professionals to exchange ideas and discuss technical issues of mutual interest. We’ll have a Technical Tuesday event on 22 October 2013 (1600 – 1730 East Coast Time). We’re co-hosting this event with the Maryland Chapter of InfraGard. Topic: Cyber Security Strategy – Why We’re Losing and What’s Needed to Win Everybody seems to be spending more on cybersecurity, but with questionable return on investment. In fact, the problem clearly is getting worse, and current strategies show no indication of reversing that trend. This non-technical presentation explores the typical cyber risk environment, considers the proper balance and likely effectiveness of threat deterrence, vulnerability mitigation, and consequence management to reduce cyber risk, and examines the current and evolving roles of government agencies and the private sector in addressing the problem. Backed by powerful, real-world examples of threat actor tactics, this presentation will help managers develop a better understanding of how their current security approach is most likely to succeed or fail over time, and what strategies are the most likely to shift the advantage to the good guys. Presented by: Steven Chabinsky, CrowdStrike Steve Chabinsky recently returned to the private sector after a distinguished career with the FBI, where he served most recently as Deputy Assistant Director of the Cyber Division. At CrowdStrike, he is Chief Risk Officer and Senior Vice President of Legal Affairs. He also serves as an adjunct faculty member of George Washington University, and as the cyber Columnist for Security magazine. Mr. Chabinsky is the recipient of numerous awards and recognitions, including the National Intelligence Distinguished Service Medal, the Presidential Rank Award for Meritorious Executive, the National Security Agency Bronze Medallion for inspired leadership, and the Financial Services Information Sharing & Analysis Center (FS-ISAC) Public/Private Sector Partnership Award.

name: echoAR: How to Build a Cloud-Connected AR/VR App in 15 Minutes or Less
description: Title: echoAR: How to Build a Cloud-Connected AR/VR App in 15 Minutes or Less Led by: Alon Grinshpoon, Founder & CEO @ echoAR Topic Areas: Augmented Reality (AR), Virtual Reality (VR), Spatial Cloud Computing, Developer Tools Description: The workshop will show how to quickly create augmented and virtual reality (AR/VR) apps with no technical skills or coding required and scale existing apps by connecting them to the cloud. Workshop participants will learn how to create real-time cloud-connected AR/VR apps using the echoAR platform. Participants will also discover how AR/VR are changing the world through the demonstration of different use cases of 3D applications and live demos of AR/VR experiences. Participants are encouraged to bring a laptop and a smartphone. Platforms for experimentation include: Google ARCore, WebXR, Vuforia, Unity-based apps, and more. Participants of the workshop will also be given one month of FREE business tier access to the echoAR platform by registering at https://console.echoar.xyz/#/auth/register-promo?code=UMDXR. Company Description: echoAR (www.echoAR.xyz; Techstars '19) is a cloud platform for augmented and virtual reality (AR/VR) that provides tools and server-side infrastructure to help developers & companies quickly build and deploy AR/VR apps and experiences. We are backed by Remagine Ventures and Techstars, and received grants from Y Combinator, Verizon, and NYC Media Lab. We were named AR/VR finalists for SXSW 2020, won the DevProject Award 2019, named among the 2019 Most Fundable Companies, named one of the Top 25 finalists in Sir Richard Branson's Extreme Tech Challenge (XTC) 2019, and featured on The Hill and Bold TV. CEO Description: Alon Grinshpoon is the CEO and founder of echoAR (www.echoAR.xyz), a cloud platform for augmented reality (AR) and virtual reality (VR) that provides tools and network infrastructure to help developers & companies quickly build and deploy AR/VR apps and content. Alon received his MSc in computer science from Columbia University specializing in computer graphics, virtual and augmented reality, and human-computer interaction. Alon received his BSc in computer science and electrical engineering from Tel Aviv University specializing in software engineering, computer networks and cyber security. Alon is a former Mellanox engineer, graduate researcher at the Computer Graphics and User Interfaces Laboratory of Columbia University, and research and teaching assistant in the fields of computer networks and distributed cloud networks. Alon is a Techstars alum, NYC Media Lab alum, a Startup Leadership Program (SLP) fellow, and member of the Virtual World Society. Alon is a speaker on emerging technologies and has given talks at major AR/VR tech conferences in the US, Canada and Israel.

name: ACTNow: Far From The Norm and TL Collective
description: Two dance companies present intimate short films followed by a live virtual Q&A moderated by Associate Professor of American Studies La Marr Jurelle Bruce, an interdisciplinary humanities scholar, critical theorist and Afromanticist. Far From The Norm’s CAN’T KILL US ALL unravels one man’s mental unrest as he navigates the turbulence of dealing with two global pandemics. This theatrical experience combines hip-hop theatre and film, revealing the deterioration of a man’s emotional sanity and physical stability as he confronts life in lockdown. From reflecting on childhood memories, to reliving trauma experienced by Black bodies, CAN’T KILL US ALL pushes through the darkness to find light, humility and peace. TL Collective’s Tough Skin presents four humans from completely different backgrounds and cultures. The film is a captivating visual representation of what it looks like to stay committed to connection and humanity even in dire circumstances. From themes of racial violence and cultural appropriation to multiculturalism and gender equality, the work of The Clarice's 2020-21 visiting artists is complex, provocative and deeply sensitive. Arts Citizenship Talks (ACTnow) are opportunities to hear from these artists about the issues reflected in their works. These conversations are an invitation to act now! Engagement on Campus and in the Community: Throughout Fall 2020, Botis Seva and members of Far From The Norm will virtually visit students in the School of Theatre, Dance, and Performance Studies to discuss their work and choreographic technique. Micaela Taylor and members of TL Collective will also visit students in the School of Theatre, Dance, and Performance Studies. In addition, Micaela Taylor is participating in The Clarice’s BlackLight Summit as a member of the summit Career Readiness mentorship team. Film Credits: CAN’T KILL US ALL Produced by Far From The Norm, CAN’T KILL US ALL is a collaboration from 3 original voices working in hip-hop theatre: dance artist Botis Seva, filmmaker Ben Williams and composer Torben Lars Sylvest. CAN’T KILL US ALL is co-commissioned by Arts Council England, BBC and The Space.

name: Fearless New Play Festival
description: The Fearless New Play Festival is a four-day celebration of new scripts in development that address urgent issues of today. The festival kicks off on November 19 with a speech by nationally renowned keynote playwright Lauren Yee. The festival features staged readings of new short plays by current TDPS students and alumni from November 19-22. Selected plays for the 2020 Fearless New Play Festival By Grace (Part Two) by Agyeiwaa Asante ’18 A Tea Party by Mariel Berlin-Fischler ’14 All of my Bullies and Where They Are Now by Elizabeth Crino ’18 Ghost Story by Evangelina Hakes ’19 The Ice Room by Liz Maestri ’03 RAPunzel by Jasmine Mitchell ‘20 Tiny Ruins by April Monu ’18 Please Like Me by Jordan Resnick ’22 Loving in the Age of Social Distancing by Amber Smithers ‘20 The Tao Island by Lyra Woods ’17 Announcing Keynote Playwright Lauren Yee The School of Theatre, Dance, and Performance Studies is thrilled to announce that internationally-renowned playwright Lauren Yee will be our 2020 keynote playwright. Lauren Yee is a playwright, screenwriter, and TV writer born and raised in San Francisco. She currently lives in New York City. Her play Cambodian Rock Band, with music by Dengue Fever and others, just had a lauded off-Broadway run at Signature Theatre. Her plays The Great Leap and Cambodian Rock Band led the list of top 10 most produced plays in the country for the 2019-20 season. She is the winner of the 2019 Doris Duke Artist Award for outstanding contributions to theater, the 2019 Steinberg Playwright Award, the Horton Foote Prize, the Kesselring Prize, the ATCA/Steinberg Award, American Academy of Arts and Letters literature award, and the Francesca Primus Prize. She has been a finalist for the Edward M. Kennedy Prize and the Susan Smith Blackburn Prize. Her plays were the #1 and #2 plays on the 2017 Kilroys List. Lauren is a Residency 5 playwright at Signature Theatre in New York, New Dramatists member (class of 2025), Ma-Yi Writers’ Lab member, former Princeton University Hodder fellow, and Playwrights Realm alumni playwright. She earned her BA at Yale and her MFA at UC San Diego, and American Theatre Magazine named her as the second most-produced playwright in the country for the 2019/20 season. For more info, please visit www.laurenyee.com.

name: Guest Speaker: Rabbi Menachem Leibtag
description: At Kedma, we seek to provide the community at UMD with unique opportunities for Jewish education and spirituality. We are able to explore our deep connection to our culture and roots through the learning of Jewish texts. To help with this goal, we would like to host Rabbi Menachem Leibtag for a Torah lecture via Zoom to teach and inspire our organization to become better Torah scholars, as well as improve our character as people. Rabbi Menachem Leibtag, founder of the Tanach (Jewish Bible) Study Center www.tanach.org, is an internationally acclaimed bible scholar and pioneer of Jewish Education on the internet. His essays on Parshat ha’Shavua (weekly Torah portion) reflect his vibrant thematic-analytical approach, blending the methods of modern scholarship with traditional approaches. As a teacher at Yeshivat Har Etzion, he is best known for his ability to teach students how to study the Bible. Rabbi Leibtag also teaches at Yeshivat Shaalavim, Midreshet Lindenbaum, and Matan; and routinely lectures around the globe, primarily as a Scholar in Residence in communities in North America. Rabbi Leibtag will be teaching on matters of Bible and Religion via Zoom to about 40 students.

description: Every week we'll be having a general body meeting focused on a different topic in cybersecurity. These are a great chance to learn a new skill and get some hands-on experience. We'll have different challenges each week based around different skills. Members of all experience levels are welcome to join! Stop by, have some pizza (first come first serve), and learn a new skill or tool that you can add to your resume. We encourage everyone to participate and ask questions. If there are any skills you're interested in, let us know. Here's a rough schedule of some topics that we hope to cover: 2/26 - Forensics, file carving, steganography 3/5 - Threat monitoring & intrusion detection 3/12 - Penetration testing & network security 3/19 - Spring break! 3/26 - Password cracking 4/2 - Web security - SQL injection, XSS, CSRF 4/9 - Reverse engineering/cracking 4/16 - Cryptography - codemaking and codebreaking 4/23 - Software exploitation - smashing the stack 4/30 - Game hacking - godmode plz! 5/7 - OMGLOLBBQ?

name: Veterans Yoga
description: Sun Salutations (8/31) Get ready for a class to introduce health and vitality into the semester! This short class includes 20 minutes of cleansing movement fit for yogis of all shapes, sizes, and experience levels. Bonus: Do you not have time to relax and let go for even just a few minutes? Your instructor includes at least five minutes of required shavasana practice at the end of each class to give the mind a break from the rest of the world. Learn a New Pose (9/2) Today’s yoga session will include 18 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out, meaning that yogis of all experience and backgrounds will benefit! Get ready to build strength and resilience with this fun-to learn movement. Relaxation Meditation (9/7) Tuesday’s session will be focused on grounding yourself in this new semester. Just fifteen minutes of passive, yet focused yoga practice will bring you into the moment and out of the stresses of the new semester. Get a Workout in (9/9) After Tuesday’s session focused on relaxation and finding ground in the new semester, it’s time to ramp up the heat. You would never believe what just twenty minutes of poses can do to get that blood pumping and the sweat pouring! Don’t worry, though! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Open the Hips (9/14) We have been in class for a couple of weeks now and our bodies need us to keep moving to stay open and ready for all that life has to offer. Twenty three minutes of opening the hips will keep them from tightening from all the stress and constant sitting motion. Don’t forget! We also include at least five minutes of time to destress and prepare for the rest of the week. Learn a New Pose (9/16) Today’s yoga session will include 24 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out. Yogis of all experience and backgrounds will benefit from this fun practice! Get ready to build some awesome abdominal strength with this sequence. Relaxation Meditation (9/21) Today’s session will be focused on grounding yourself in this new semester. Twenty six minutes of passive, yet focused yoga practice will bring you into the moment and out of the stresses of the semester’s stressors. Getting in a Workout! (9/23) After Tuesday’s session focused on relaxation and finding ground in this awesome in-person semester, it’s time to get that body moving. Just thirty three minutes of poses will get that blood pumping and the sweat pouring! Don’t worry! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Plus, we won’t leave your muscles stiff from the hard work! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for the Booty (9/28) Looking to add cushion and tone to your derriere? Who isn’t?! Today’s session will be devoted to working to add strength to the glutes and hamstrings. Twenty minutes of work will show you some tips and tools to build your important muscle groups that keep your body healthy and moving! Learn a New Pose (9/30) Today’s yoga session will include 25 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out! Even the simplest of poses require detail-orientation! Get ready to build strength and resilience in simple poses. Relaxation Meditation (10/5) Tuesday’s session will be focused on staying sane as the semester continues to pose more difficulties. Plus, we won’t leave your muscles stiff from the hard work! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. We are working to improve, not perfect! After all, we only have twenty six minutes! Learn a New Pose (10/14) Today’s yoga session will include 34 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out! Poses that seem difficult from the outside may be a bit simpler than you anticipate! We are focused on safety in strength. So first, we will build strength and confidence. Then we will build upon simple poses to create a beautiful movement to feel proud about. Relaxation Meditation (10/19) We are mid-semester. While it feels like this is the time to be working your butt off with as few breaks as possible, don’t forget about the importance of daily self-care. Today’s class will be nineteen minutes focused on nothing but bringing you back to yourself. This is a time to reclaim the best parts of yourself and create the person you want to be with focused intention. Get a Workout In (10/21) Tuesday got us mentally focused for the week, so now it is time to ramp up the energy to end the week strong! Thirty-one minutes of yoga flow will get that blood pumping! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in and focused. Don’t forget a towel! We will leave your muscles feeling worked, but not too stiff! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for Back Pain (10/26) Is your back constantly feeling stiff? Is the lower back achy and shoulder blades tight? Come to today’s yoga session for the opportunity to release some of that stiffness, and open yourself up to a world of relief! You might be surprised at what a short 33 minutes of stretching and strengthening can do for the body. Learn a New Pose (10/28) Ready to expand your yoga knowledge and experience? Today’s class will revolve around learning a yoga pose through-and-through. There is no reason to worry about the experience level needed for the pose, as all poses learned and performed here can be done at any level! Set aside 33 minutes and get mentally ready to learn reverse warrior so we can add it to your yoga repertoire! Relaxation Meditation (11/2) Meditating on a regular basis has positive effects on the body and mind, such as greater sense of focus, muscle relaxation, and increased creativity. Today’s meditation will be focused on gratitude and increasing happiness. Giving thanks can come in many forms, but have you tried it in the form of meditation?! Getting in a Workout! (11/4) After Tuesday’s session focused on gratitude in this challenging semester, it’s time to get that body moving. Just 34 minutes of sweat-inducing poses will get that blood pumping! This class is fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Plus, we won’t leave your muscles stiff from the hard work! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for a Better Mood (11/9) College is demanding, stressful, and can induce negative feelings! Combat those real-time stresses by moving the body and bonding with fellow veterans. Coming to this thirty minute vinyasa class will open the heart to the positivity you need to get you to the end of the semester. Learn a New Pose (11/11) Ready to expand your yoga knowledge and experience? Today’s class will revolve around learning a yoga pose through-and-through. There is no reason to worry about the experience level needed for the pose, as all poses learned and performed here can be done at any level! Set aside 35 minutes and get mentally ready to learn a new pose to add to your yoga repertoire! Relaxation Meditation (11/16) Today’s meditation practice will be short, sweet, and perfect to regain focus on your workflow. As we near the end of the semester, stress increases, the mind wanders, and we lose focus. We will be going through meditation techniques that can be utilized at home, work, or on the bus. Don’t underestimate the power of this 26 minute session. Come join your fellow veterans and enjoy the feeling of a clear mind. Get a Workout In (11/18) After Tuesday’s session focused on de-stressing and refocusing, it’s time to move that body. Just 34 minutes of yoga flow will get that blood pumping! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in and focused throughout the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Plus, we won’t leave your muscles stiff from the hard work! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for Neck Pain (11/23) After months of looking down at our computer screens, it’s no wonder so many of us have the amount of pain in our necks that we do! Today’s class will be all about de-stressing, communication, and releasing the tension in the neck through yoga practice. Set aside 31 minutes for this perfectly-paced practice.

name: Developing Impact and Effectiveness Assessment Tool for Influence Operations
description: On Tuesday, April 26 at 1:00 p.m. ET, Unconventional Weapons and Technology (UWT) Director Steve Sin and UWT researchers Megan Rutter and Rhyner Washburn will provide a virtual talk on the findings from their project Developing Impact and Effectiveness Assessment Tool for Influence Operations. This event is free and open to the public, but RSVPs are required. If you have any questions, please email the START events team at start-events@umd.edu. Strategic adversaries and competitors of the United States have come to view influence operations as an effective, low-cost, and low consequence (for the influencer) means of advancing their goals and agendas. Given our adversaries and competitors’ view of influence operations, and the immense implications and potential consequences of them, there is a need for research that will advance the state of the art in detecting, characterizing, and countering state-sponsored influence operations. While there is a large volume of work that has been done to understand the nature and effects of influence operations, as well as exploring various methods to counter them, there is a dearth of work that examines how one can measure the impact and effectiveness of influence operations. UWT is developing the “Influence to Action Escalation Model” (IAEM) and the “Influence to Action Chain Template” (I-ACT) to anticipate and measure to measure the impact of influence operations by determining an influence operation's likelihood to galvanize the recipients to exhibit outwardly observable behaviors. The model will be the first step in providing the U.S. intelligence, military, and other government stakeholders a new capability to systematically measure the relative impact and effectiveness of influence operations being conducted against the United States. When fully matured, this capability will allow the United States to prepare for, counter, and neutralize nefarious foreign influence operations more effectively. Dr. Steve S. Sin is the Director of the Unconventional Weapons and Technology Division (UWT) of START, where he manages large research projects, explores new avenues for research, and establishes collaborative research relationships. Dr. Sin specializes in a broad range of international security, terrorism, and homeland security challenges. His expertise includes radiological and nuclear (RN) terrorism; illicit trafficking of RN materials; terrorist use of cyber domain; emerging technology; emergency preparedness and management; intelligence/counterintelligence operations, analysis, and exploitation; Northeast Asia regional security; and counter-terrorism training, exercise, and curriculum development. His expertise in Northeast Asia regional security is focused on North Korea, including its nuclear program; cyber capabilities; intelligence apparatus; regime survival; and leadership. His additional regional expertise includes South Korean nuclear program and infrastructure; North-South Korea relations; and Korea-Japan-China trilateral relations. Megan Rutter is a Junior Researcher on the Unconventional Weapons and Technologies team at START. She has worked on projects ranging in topics from CBRN use by violent non-state actors, red-teaming and horizon scanning, and community-based violence prevention. Megan earned her B.S. in Criminal Justice and Psychology at Northeastern University and her M.A. in Security Policy Studies at George Washington University. Rhyner Washburn is a cyber-intelligence researcher at START.

name: Scholar in Residence: Rabbi Hayyim Angel
description: At Kedma, we feel one of our responsibilities involves providing the UMD community with unique opportunities for Jewish education and spirituality. Scholars in Residence, therefore, are crucial to accomplishing our goals. We are bringing Rabbi Hayyim Angel as a Scholar in Residence for the weekend of October 15th. Rabbi aNgel is the National Scholar of the Institute for Jewish Ideas and Ideals (jewishideas.org). He has taught advanced Bible courses to undergraduate, graduate, and rabbinical students at Yeshiva University since 1996. He also lectures widely in synagogues and schools throughout North America, and consults with yeshivot worldwide to improve their Tanakh curricula. He has authored or edited nineteen books, and has published over 130 scholarly articles, primarily in Bible. Rabbi Angel’s scholarship focuses on the interaction between traditional and academic approaches to Bible study. He is editor of Conversations, the journal of the Institute for Jewish Ideas and Ideals. He also serves on the editorial boards of Tradition and Megadim.Rabbi Angel will be speaking multiple times over the weekend about various Jewish topics. Over the course of the weekend, he will speak about the Jewish Bible, rabbinic literature, and Jewish history, as well as how to apply their lessons to our lives. He will speak for 15 minutes during Friday night prayers, for an hour during the communal dinner following prayers, and for an hour during the communal lunch on Saturday. He will speak a final time for an hour before afternoon prayers on Saturday.

name: Technica 2021
description: Technica, hosted by Technica Hacks, is a 36-hour hackathon at the University of Maryland. Technica brings together underrepresented groups of people in a conducive and fun weekend immersed in technology culture and encouraged to exercise their imagination to create interesting and innovative hacks. Our mission is to narrow the vast gender gap in technology and help diversify the technology industry. Throughout Technica, students have the opportunity to attend as hackers, volunteers or mentors. Everyone, regardless of gender, has the opportunity to attend workshops, talks, activities, network with sponsoring companies and receive Technica Hacks’ and sponsors’ swag. We encourage participants that identify as an underrepresented gender to hack, as per our mission statement, but do not discriminate based off of gender. Our organizers, volunteers, and mentors are the backbone of Technica and without them, the event could not be hosted. Attending Technica as an organizer, volunteer, or mentor gives those who choose to do so a way to support our mission of gender diversification in technology, build leadership skills, and an opportunity to learn more about technology. We provide hardware, mentorship, food, assistance, activities, and workshops throughout the weekend. There will be both an in-person and virtual option available to attendees this year. To register for the event, please visit https://gotechnica.org.

name: NextNOW Fest: Opening Night Party!
description: NextNOW Fest 2022 kicks off the festival week with an opening party at The Hall CP, a restaurant and event venue located off-campus in the University of Maryland’s Discovery District. The party will feature a stage of student musicians and bands from Terrapin Record Label, along with local and alumni vendors, a suminagashi-style paper marbling activity by Pyramid Atlantic Art Center and Illegal Art’s interactive Connect the Dots installation. Terrapin Record Label Stage The indoor stage will feature student musicians and bands from the student-run Terrapin Record Label: Peter Kim Aleca Lulu Jameson Sam Loring Nelson Chen Corduroy Muffin Lisztomania Unity for the Outcasts Illegal Art: Connect The Dots For the project Connect the Dots, Illegal Art asks participants to use a colored pencil or marker, all starting from the same circle, marked “Me”, and make a continuous line through a number of choices, indicated by vertically organized circles, such as age, languages spoken, political leanings, dietary preferences or whether they like beverages with ice or at room temperature. This will create a multi-colored stream of lines that will all end up in the same circle, marked “Us”. Connect The Dots has been installed at The Academic College of Rishon Lizion, Israel (2013), Manny Cantor Center, Manhattan, NY (2014), Bunker Hill Community College, Boston, MA (2018) and the Desert Botanical Garden, Phoenix, AZ (2019). Pyramid Atlantic Art Center: Suminagashi Suminagashi-style paper marbling is the centuries-old process of painting on water. name: Fluid Molds & Found Volumes Mold-making Workshop
description: In this workshop, participants will explore mold-makery and casting as a way of creating a series of unique multiples. Shaping various clay bodies into an evolving container (the mold) and filling its mutating void with pigmented plaster (the cast), participants will be introduced to a mold-making and casting method designed by the artist herself in order to celebrate possibilities over precision and productivity. Being guided through such process, participants will be encouraged to think fluidly between the role of a mold vs. a cast (as well as process vs. product) as they create and work with malleable and solid volumes that are to dynamically and repeatedly embrace, shape, and transform one another. For more about the Unspoken Volumes exhibition and artist Hae Won Sohn, please visit https://stamp.umd.edu/articles/stamp_gallery_presents_unspoken_volumes_hae_won_sohn This workshop will be held on Friday, October 7 from 1 - 5 pm in Studio A, B0107 Stamp Union. Attendance for this workshop is limited, please RSVP at https://forms.gle/LNfSRE8LCSvJui786. This workshop is free and open to the public If this workshop is full, please email stampgallery@umd.edu to be placed on the waitlist. All materials will be provided, though participants are encouraged to wear clothes they do not mind getting dirty. This workshop is supported by the Maryland State Arts Council (msac.org) and a Pepsi Grant.

name: Naloxone Training
description: The University of Maryland Health Center is designated as an Overdose Response Program (ORP) through the Maryland Department of Health. As part of this designation, we offer overdose response resources to the UMD community, free of charge. One of the most popular resources we offer is Naloxone, an opioid overdose reversal medication. Similarly to how an EpiPen temporarily blocks the life-threatening symptoms of an allergic reaction (i.e. inability to breathe) while emergency medical assistance arrives, Naloxone offers this temporary support for those experiencing an opioid overdose. To get your free Naloxone through the Health Center, all you have to do is attend a brief training, which goes over how to recognize signs of an opioid overdose, instructions for using Naloxone, and what to do as emergency medical assistance makes its way to you and the person in crisis. Trainings are all offered in the Sahet Room of the Health Center, just past the main entrance to the building, and are free to any UMD community member interested in attending! Registration is required for attendance.

name: Naloxone Training
description: The University of Maryland Health Center is designated as an Overdose Response Program (ORP) through the Maryland Department of Health. As part of this designation, we offer overdose response resources to the UMD community, free of charge. One of the most popular resources we offer is Naloxone, an opioid overdose reversal medication. Similarly to how an EpiPen temporarily blocks the life-threatening symptoms of an allergic reaction (i.e. inability to breathe) while emergency medical assistance arrives, Naloxone offers this temporary support for those experiencing an opioid overdose. To get your free Naloxone through the Health Center, all you have to do is attend a brief training, which goes over how to recognize signs of an opioid overdose, instructions for using Naloxone, and what to do as emergency medical assistance makes its way to you and the person in crisis. Trainings are all offered in the Sahet Room of the Health Center, just past the main entrance to the building, and are free to any UMD community member interested in attending! Registration is required for attendance. --- RSVP URL: https://forms.gle/woguGFjSDnYfHs7VA

name: National Hillel Basketball Tournament 2025
description: The National Hillel Basketball Tournament (NHBT) was founded in 2010 to bring Jewish students together around the inclusive and encompassing game of basketball. Solely organized by a board of 30 highly motivated students, what began as a small event has quickly developed into one of the largest collegiate gatherings of Jewish students in the country. Now in its 13th year, the non-profit initiative, annually housed in the University of Maryland’s state-of-the-art facilities, attracts over 1,500 participants from across the United States and Canada. This year, we expect over 50 teams from over 30 universities across North America to partake in the weekend-long tournament experience. Players and fans also participate in various off-the-court programs such as Shabbat meals, keynote speakers, and an exciting bar night to kick the weekend off. In addition to NHBT’s impressive scale and reach, its impact has reached new heights in recent years. By providing students a chance to meet, socialize, and compete in a positive Jewish environment, NHBT serves as an oasis for students experiencing antisemitism on their respective campuses. By platforming like-minded organizations and starting initiatives, NHBT has provided a beacon of hope and togetherness for Jewish and campus communities far and wide.

name: En'Rage Models Practice
description: Our practice sessions are dynamic and empowering, designed to build confidence, enhance runway skills, and foster creativity in a supportive environment. Each session begins with a warm-up to prepare our models for the physical and mental demands of the runway. Models are then guided through a series of runway walks, where they practice posture, poise, and movement in a variety of styles that challenge traditional norms of fashion and modeling. Throughout the practice, we focus on perfecting choreography for upcoming shows, allowing models to develop their unique flair while staying in sync with the group’s overall performance. Our experienced runway coaches provide individual feedback to ensure that each model feels confident in expressing their own style, aligning with our mission of self-empowerment and diversity. In addition to runway practice, we also incorporate photoshoot preparation, helping models become comfortable in front of the camera, and working on their poses and expressions. Music is played to set the tone, and we regularly rotate different fashion themes to keep practices fresh and engaging. Each session concludes with a debrief, where we emphasize the importance of mutual support and encouragement, celebrating personal growth and teamwork. En'Rage Models practices are more than just rehearsals—they are an opportunity for our members to develop their self-esteem, push creative boundaries, and prepare for the high-energy experience of the runway.

description: The Yuri Kochiyama High School Leadership Program (YKLP) is an annual opportunity for DMV high school students to learn about the history of Asian American activism, strengthen their sense of identity through learning about cross-racial and intersectional community building, and develop peer solidarity and mentorship with other BIPOC-identifying individuals at UMD and other high school students.Hosted by the Asian American Student Union (AASU) at the University of Maryland, College Park (UMCP), YKLP seeks to celebrate the legacy of Japanese American activist, Yuri Kochiyama, by providing community education and mentorship to students interested in Asian American issues--completely free of charge.This year, we are taking applications for a cohort that will meet once a week through a hybrid format over a 5-week session during the spring. Each week, YK participants will come together to learn about Asian American history, identity, and leadership through intersectional community building. YKLP will end with an End-of-Program Celebration on April 13. The hybrid schedule is as follows: WEEK ONE (2/17): in-person WEEK TWO (2/24) : online WEEK THREE (3/02): in-person WEEK FOUR (3/09): online WEEK FIVE (3/16): in-person Graduation (4/13): in-person We hope to raise awareness about Asian Pacific Islander Desi American (APIDA) issues that matter to community members, highlighting APIDA experiences and engaging with each other to better integrate intersectional concepts within our daily lives. YKLP is open to all public high school students within the DMV who are of BIPOC-identifying background to facilitate inter-community building and learning.

name: New Organization Welcome Meeting | In-Person
description: New Organization Welcome Meetings serve to inform organizations that are new or formerly inactive on the steps of the registration process and are a requirement for registration. While only one organization member (does not have to be in a leadership position) is required to attend, we recommend that more come. If you have already attended a New Organization Welcome Meeting for your organization in the fall semester, you will not have to attend another meeting for your organization. If you are attempting to register multiple new organizations, you only need to attend one meeting.
