organization: Association of Latino Professionals For America (ALPFA)
description: Hey ALPFAmilia! Join us on October 2nd at 5 pm in VMH (room TBD) for our Loteria Night. Winners will receive limited edition prizes. Make sure to RSVP on our Instagram bio linktree @alpfa_umd. What is Loteria? Lotería is a traditional Mexican game of chance, similar to bingo, but instead of numbers, it uses images on a deck of cards. Each card features a unique illustration, such as "La Sirena" (The Mermaid) or "El Gallo" (The Rooster). Players mark their game boards (which also feature these images) as the images are called out, and the first to complete a designated pattern wins. It’s a fun, lively game, often accompanied by laughs, music, and celebrations, especially within Latino communities.

Effective stress management is useful not only for academic success but even for competitions that students participate in for an enriching university experience. SKY Happiness Retreat is a holistic well-being program taught over 3 consecutive days (3 sessions) (in-person). This nine-hour retreat includes: 1. SKY Breath Meditation 2. Evidence-based breathwork techniques 3. Social connection 4. Mindful leadership and light yoga SKY Breath Meditation and the 3-session Retreat have been shown in research to significantly reduce anxiety and depression, lower stress markers, and increase wellbeing, focus, improved sleep, optimism, and social connection. Participants report an increased ability to stay calm, confident, and resilient amidst challenges, increased levels of social connection and feelings of inclusion, and less suicidal feelings. SK&Y will benefit UMD students including those on the SKY at UMD to better manage their stress & loneliness especially during these unprecedented times and have an enriching university experience. name: Veterans Intro to Mountain Biking

No previous mountain biking experience necessary, but you should be comfortable riding a bike.

name: Camp PALS Volunteer opportunity
description: Volunteer to be a Counselor for the PALS program Camp PALS this summer. PALS is a nonprofit organization that provides one week long summer camp opportunities for teens and young adults with Down syndrome and their peers at 14 college campuses across the country. This is a one-week experience from 9am-5pm. Listed below are some details about Camp PALS: Here are some details about Camp PALS: - They offer 14 week long sleep-away camps across the country, including Camp PALS Georgetown, Chicago, and North Carolina! - Volunteer counselors are paired one-to-one with a camper to provide an opportunity to build -meaningful friendships through trips and activities - Looking for volunteers ages 16-30 who are welcoming, genuine, passionate, supportive, and fun which are all the values of the program. - No experience with Down syndrome or the disability community is necessary! They encourage groups of applicants to apply together to share the camp experience. If you are interested please visit the website at palsprograms.org/volunteer or check out their social media pages on Facebook or YouTube channel to get a look at what the PALS experience is like. PALS is an amazing opportunity to give back to the community, gain invaluable leadership skills, and make friends that will last a lifetime! There are no costs for volunteers at PALS, and applicants can apply for travel costs to be covered as well. We are looking for male applicants at this point in our season. Females are welcome to apply but will likely be placed on a waitlist. The dates for each of our 15 camps is different based on their locations, but the dates for Baltimore are July 7-13 at UMBC, and Georgetown is July 28-August 3 at Georgetown University.

name: Camp PALS Volunteer opportunity
description: Volunteer to be a Counselor for the PALS program Camp PALS this summer. PALS is a nonprofit organization that provides one week long summer camp opportunities for teens and young adults with Down syndrome and their peers at 14 college campuses across the country. This is a one-week experience from 9am-5pm. Listed below are some details about Camp PALS: Here are some details about Camp PALS: - They offer 14 week long sleep-away camps across the country, including Camp PALS Georgetown, Chicago, and North Carolina! - Volunteer counselors are paired one-to-one with a camper to provide an opportunity to build -meaningful friendships through trips and activities - Looking for volunteers ages 16-30 who are welcoming, genuine, passionate, supportive, and fun which are all the values of the program. - No experience with Down syndrome or the disability community is necessary! They encourage groups of applicants to apply together to share the camp experience. If you are interested please visit the website at palsprograms.org/volunteer or check out their social media pages on Facebook or YouTube channel to get a look at what the PALS experience is like. PALS is an amazing opportunity to give back to the community, gain invaluable leadership skills, and make friends that will last a lifetime! There are no costs for volunteers at PALS, and applicants can apply for travel costs to be covered as well. We are looking for male applicants at this point in our season. name: A discussion session with Pranith Simha - an educationist working in Bastar in India
description: Can the Adivasis of Bastar still dance after getting educated in schools? Bastar region is situated in Chhattisgarh, a central Indian state famous for its rich tribal culture and dense pristine forests of Dandakaranya. The tribal culture of Bastar is known for its sustainable lifestyles, care for the environment around them, gender-equal practices and being happy in the moment. The way they celebrate life events through dance and songs is mesmerizing. In spite of these many amazing things why is Bastar infamous for violence by both left-wing extremists and the state? During this talk, we will try to find the answers to the following questions: What is the purpose and relevance of modern education? Is it really adding the value? What value is it adding to the lives of tribal people? Are schools the only way for getting educated? What roles do teachers play? Is it possible to establish a balance between national interests and local needs while protecting diversity? About Pranith Simha: Pranith founded Bachpan Banao in 2012 with the vision to create just, equal, free and harmonious society. Bachpan Banao has been working in Dantewada in Chhattisgarh, strengthening the public education system via innovative initiatives. He was recently invited to the Harvard India Conference.
location: Rm 1201, John S Toll Building, UMD

name: Female Forward Women in Law Panel
description: Join Female Forward for our Women in Law panel on February 16th at 7:30pm! This event will be a moderated Q&A with Anita Bandy and Jennifer Weiss-Wolf that will be opened up for members to ask questions at the end. There will be a chance to network with other members and our panelists at the end. Read below for our speaker bios! Anita Bandy: Anita Bandy is an Associate Director in the Securities and Exchange Commission’s Division of Enforcement, where she assists in planning and directing the Commission’s enforcement program. Anita joined the Commission in 2004 and then served in several positions of increasing responsibility in the Enforcement program. During her tenure at the Commission, Anita has led multiple enforcement initiatives and has supervised dozens of investigations that resulted in actions spanning a wide range of matters, including financial fraud, offering frauds, market manipulation, the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act, the Jumpstart Our Business Startups Act, and other illegal acts that occur in the mergers & acquisitions, cyber, broker-dealer and investment-adviser space. Prior to joining the SEC, Anita spent several years in private practice at the law firm of Proskauer LLP, where she focused on white collar and SEC defense work. She received her J.D. with honors from American University and her undergraduate degree with honors from the University of Michigan. Jennifer Weiss-Wolf:Jennifer Weiss-Wolf is vice president for development at the Brennan Center for Justice. A frequent writer and advocate on issues of gender, feminism, and politics in America, Weiss-Wolf is also the Brennan Center's inaugural Women and Democracy Fellow. She is the author of Periods Gone Public: Taking a Stand for Menstrual Equity, lauded by Gloria Steinem as “the beginning of liberation for us all.” Her writing has been published in the New York Times, Los Angeles Times, Time, Newsweek, Salon, Bloomberg, Cosmopolitan, Marie Claire, and Harper’s Bazaar, among others. Prior to joining the Brennan Center, Weiss-Wolf was a foundations specialist at Legal Services NYC, vice president for development at the Pro-Choice Resource Center, and grants manager for the American Civil Liberties Union.An entrepreneur at heart, she took a decade-long hiatus from the world of nonprofits to envision and cofound Milk Money, a women-owned company that creates and franchises stores that sell recycled children’s clothing.

name: Guest Speaker: Michelle Cohen Farber
description: At Kedma, we seek to provide the community at UMD with unique opportunities for Jewish education and spirituality. We are able to explore our deep connection to our culture and roots through the learning of Jewish texts. To help with this goal, we would like to host Rabbanit Michelle Cohen Farber for a Torah lecture via Zoom to teach and inspire our organization to become better Torah scholars, as well as improve our character as people. Rabbanit Michelle Cohen Farber is the founder of Hadran: Advancing Talmud Study for Women and Daf Yomi (Talmud page of the day) for Women, the first woman's podcast on the daf yomi. Rabbanit Michelle spearheaded the first international Siyum HaShas (completion of the Talmud) for women. Rabbanit Michelle studied Talmud at Bar Ilan and in Midreshet Lindenbaum's scholar's program. She has taught Talmud and Jewish law in Pelech Jerusalem, Midreshet Lindenbaum and Matan HaSharon. Rabbanit Michelle will be teaching on matters of the Talmud and Jewish law via Zoom to about 40 students.

name: Understanding the Rise and Resilience of Islamic State Khorasan in Afghanistan
description: On Thursday, November 12 at 1:00 p.m. ET, West Point Combating Terrorism Center (CTC) Assistant Professor Dr. Amira Jadoon will provide a virtual talk on “Understanding the Rise and Resilience of Islamic State Khorasan in Afghanistan.” This event is free and open to the public, but RSVPs are required. If you have any questions, please email the START events team at start-events@umd.edu. Despite significant challenges, in the five years since its emergence, the Islamic State Khorasan (ISK) has managed to successfully embed itself within the Afghanistan-Pakistan region, unleash a wave of terrorism, and endure despite intensive counterterrorism efforts. Between 2015 and 2018, counterterrorism efforts against the group resulted in significant leadership losses, amounting to a total of 548 leaders, including four of its emirs. Yet, the group persists; in 2018, ISK made its mark as one of the top four most lethal groups in the world and continues to threaten Afghanistan's security in 2020. This talk delves into the case study of ISK, tracing the evolution of the group's operational capacity, as well as its losses in CT operations over the five years of its existence. The talk provides an overview of ISK's strategies in Afghanistan and Pakistan, and outlines how the group has leveraged important alliances with local groups to remain resilient in difficult circumstances. Dr. Amira Jadoon is an assistant professor at the Combating Terrorism Center and the Department of Social Sciences at the U.S. Military Academy at West Point. She specializes in international security, economic statecraft, political violence, and terrorism. Her research also examines the behavior of non-state actors, especially in South Asia, and the types of environments that exacerbate terrorist activity. Dr. Jadoon is fluent in Urdu, Hindko, and Punjabi and conducted field work in Pakistan for both her masters and doctoral research. She has published in Foreign Policy Analysis, International Interactions, Studies in Conflict and Terrorism, Dynamics of Asymmetric Conflict, Political Science Quarterly, among others, and has two forthcoming books on the global affiliates of Islamic State. Dr. Jadoon holds a Ph.D. in Political Science from the Rockefeller College of Public Affairs and Policy at the University at Albany, an M.Sc. in Economic Development from the London School of Economics, and a B.A. in Economics and in Journalism from the University of Iowa.

GradTerps (and sometimes undergrads) are welcome to join us virtually on Tuesdays, usually at 12:30pm. Whether you are in the U.S. or in your home country, you can count on us for great information to help you navigate the issues and challenges of the adult world. name: NextLOOK ft. Lineage Percussion: Shadows of Lakeland
description: The duty of artists is to reflect and create content that is synonymous with the current world, exposing the downfalls and triumphs of the human spirit. Lineage Percussion is joining forces with renowned composer Carlos Simon to present the world premiere of Shadows of Lakeland. Lakeland, located in College Park, Maryland, is a historical Black community that has proven resilient when distracted by trials and tribulations. name: Fearless New Play Festival
description: The Fearless New Play Festival is a four-day celebration of new scripts in development that address urgent issues of today. The festival kicks off on November 19 with a speech by nationally renowned keynote playwright Lauren Yee. The festival features staged readings of new short plays by current TDPS students and alumni from November 19-22. Selected plays for the 2020 Fearless New Play Festival By Grace (Part Two) by Agyeiwaa Asante ’18 A Tea Party by Mariel Berlin-Fischler ’14 All of my Bullies and Where They Are Now by Elizabeth Crino ’18 Ghost Story by Evangelina Hakes ’19 The Ice Room by Liz Maestri ’03 RAPunzel by Jasmine Mitchell ‘20 Tiny Ruins by April Monu ’18 Please Like Me by Jordan Resnick ’22 Loving in the Age of Social Distancing by Amber Smithers ‘20 The Tao Island by Lyra Woods ’17 Announcing Keynote Playwright Lauren Yee The School of Theatre, Dance, and Performance Studies is thrilled to announce that internationally-renowned playwright Lauren Yee will be our 2020 keynote playwright. Lauren Yee is a playwright, screenwriter, and TV writer born and raised in San Francisco. She currently lives in New York City. Her play Cambodian Rock Band, with music by Dengue Fever and others, just had a lauded off-Broadway run at Signature Theatre. Her plays The Great Leap and Cambodian Rock Band led the list of top 10 most produced plays in the country for the 2019-20 season. She is the winner of the 2019 Doris Duke Artist Award for outstanding contributions to theater, the 2019 Steinberg Playwright Award, the Horton Foote Prize, the Kesselring Prize, the ATCA/Steinberg Award, American Academy of Arts and Letters literature award, and the Francesca Primus Prize. She has been a finalist for the Edward M. Kennedy Prize and the Susan Smith Blackburn Prize. Her plays were the #1 and #2 plays on the 2017 Kilroys List. Lauren is a Residency 5 playwright at Signature Theatre in New York, New Dramatists member (class of 2025), Ma-Yi Writers’ Lab member, former Princeton University Hodder fellow, and Playwrights Realm alumni playwright. She earned her BA at Yale and her MFA at UC San Diego, and American Theatre Magazine named her as the second most-produced playwright in the country for the 2019/20 season. For more info, please visit www.laurenyee.com.

name: ASHRAE UMD Seminar: Case Study- Engineering One of the World’s Largest Net Zero Schools
description: Bio: Mr. Setty is President of Setty and Associates International PLLC, a full-service mechanical, electrical and plumbing consulting engineering firm. Located in Washington DC, Setty and Associates specializes in institutional projects, energy modeling, commissioning and high performance buildings. Mr. Setty is a registered professional mechanical engineer, LEED certified and a commissioning agent. He is member of three ASHRAE technical and research committees and has presented on the national stage at the government energy conference as well as at ASHRAE national meetings. Abstract: This presentation shows how Net Zero Energy Buildings (NZEB) can be realized in a dense urban environment like Washington DC at the example of a 365,000 ft2 high school project. Focus is on real world experience with the planning, approach, design and execution to accurately analyze and then build one of the largest net zero buildings in the world. The building will neither sacrifice usage nor buy “green power” to reach net zero and is located in a city that sees 100 degree hot and humid days as well as subzero, snow filled months. name: CyberGamut Technical Tuesday - Location Based, Context Aware Services for Mobile
description: cybergamut Technical Tuesday is for cyber professionals to exchange innovative ideas and discuss technical issues of mutual interest. We’ll have a Technical Tuesday event on 12 November 2013 (1600 – 1730 East Coast Time). Topic: Location Based, Context Aware Services for Mobile – Today and Tomorrow As we continue to grow our dependence on mobile devices in our daily routine from taking pictures to delivering corporate documents, the contexts in which these devices are acting becomes increasingly important. Mobility today does not only take into account who the user is but where they are, when they are there, why they go there, what they’re interested in, and what they’re going to do. As our smart phones evolve, they are growing into a contextual engine that will not be just our personal assistant, but also our best friend providing us with all our information needs at the right time and in the right place. Presented by: Guy Levy-Yurista, Ph.D. Guy Levy-Yurista, Ph.D. carries a unique mix of skills acquired over 23 years of experience in venture capital, startup and Fortune 500 environments. He holds in-depth knowledge of mobile, internet, cyber-security, social media, telecommunications, and optical communications technologies. In his most previous role Dr. Levy-Yurista served as Vice President, Product Management with TrustDigital. Following the acquisition of TrustDigital by McAfee in 2010 Dr. Levy-Yurista took over the lead product management role for all of McAfee’s Enterprise Mobility. Prior to that Dr. Levy-Yurista served with AOL in various roles in the Safety and Security, Messaging and Mobile groups. Other prior roles for Dr. Levy-Yurista include leadership of teams in several startup companies, and a GP role with an early stage VC. Dr. Levy-Yurista holds a Ph.D. degree in Physics from the Weizmann Institute of Science, and an MBA degree from the Wharton business school in the University of Pennsylvania. To round things off, Dr. Levy-Yurista is an expert of wine having held the position of Professional Editor with a wine and gourmet magazine for over four years.

name: Work with At-Risk Kids: Change Your life!
description: We're gearing up for the best program year yet at the St. Francis Neighborhood Center and we're looking for dedicated volunteers to help in the Power Project, our free after school youth development program that serves the at-risk children of Reservoir Hill. The program starts Monday, Oct. 6 and we're looking for both tutors and program assistants to support staff and help make sure the program is fun for our kids, safe and successful. We know you're busy, but volunteering is important to you, which is why we're flexible and want to make sure your volunteer experience is the very best it can be. If you'd like to volunteer a few hours a week or a few hours a month, we'll make sure your time here is appreciated, valued and FUN! Our youth development program focuses on arts enrichment, academic support, mentoring and tutoring. Positions involve hands-on work with youth ages 5 to 13. Orientation and training are provided. Hours: Monday through Thursday from 3 to 6 pm. Skills: Experience working with children and the ability to volunteer on a regular basis. For more information, please email volunteer@stfranciscenter.org. About Us: St. Francis Neighborhood Center's mission is committed to breaking the cycles of poverty through education, inspiring self-esteem, self-improvement, and strengthening connections. We provide free academic and arts-based learning programs to community children in addition to mentoring, tutoring and meals.

name: University of Maryland Caribbean Students Association 40th Anniversary Gala
description: Founded on September 11, 1974, the Caribbean Students Association of the University of Maryland has played an integral role in the enhancement of Caribbean heritage at the University and in the surrounding community. With programming ranging from philanthropy to social-cultural, the Caribbean Students Association seeks to celebrate Caribbean culture, politics and history and to provide a forum through which Caribbean expression in all its forms can be maintained. It is with great pride and joy that we present to our alumni, supporters, and current members an evening of fine dining, heritage, and entertainment in celebration of 40 years past and in anticipation of forthcoming years. Please join us as we celebrate our longevity at the University and recognize the achievements of our alumni and current members.
location: University of Maryland Caribbean Students Association Friday, November 21, 2014 from 6:30 PM to 9:00 PM (PST) College Park, MD

name: Terp Vets Kayak Football Tournament
description: The second annual Team River Runner Kayak Football tournament is coming up on March 22nd, and you are invited! Held in the safety of an indoor swimming pool just across the street from the famous Wounded Warrior Barracks at Walter Reed Military Hospital, the competition is relaxed, family-friendly, and open to everyone. All student veterans, alumni, friends, and family members are welcome, regardless of fitness level or previous paddling experience. Last year, our team from the University of Maryland made it to the semi-finals of the tournament before being knocked out by the reigning champions. This year we would love to make an even higher run, but we need your help! If you would like to be part of this exciting event, either as a part of the team or by cheering us on please RSVP or send me a personal message. Alex Nielson Team River Runner is a national non-profit organization that promotes health and healing to wounded veterans and their family members through paddlesports. http://www.teamriverrunner.org/

organization: Half the Sky Movement at UMD
description: This spring, the Half the Sky Movement at UMD is participating in the Students Rebuild Water Challenge. The Students Rebuild Water Challenge calls upon students to help villages and schools in Tanzania gain access to safe drinking water by making paper beads. For every paper bead we make and mail in before March 31st, the Bezos Family Foundation will match that number with a monetary donation to fund up to 41 water sanitation projects in Tanzania. With access to clean water, communities can spend less time collecting water from sources that often make them sick and dedicate more time to things like school and family care. Half the Sky at UMD will be hosting a beading party on Monday, February 24th at 7:00pm in Commons 2 as part of this challenge. We would love for any and all to join us. name: Veterans Yoga
description: Sun Salutations (8/31) Get ready for a class to introduce health and vitality into the semester! This short class includes 20 minutes of cleansing movement fit for yogis of all shapes, sizes, and experience levels. Bonus: Do you not have time to relax and let go for even just a few minutes? Your instructor includes at least five minutes of required shavasana practice at the end of each class to give the mind a break from the rest of the world. Learn a New Pose (9/2) Today’s yoga session will include 18 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out, meaning that yogis of all experience and backgrounds will benefit! Get ready to build strength and resilience with this fun-to learn movement. Relaxation Meditation (9/7) Tuesday’s session will be focused on grounding yourself in this new semester. Just fifteen minutes of passive, yet focused yoga practice will bring you into the moment and out of the stresses of the new semester. Get a Workout in (9/9) After Tuesday’s session focused on relaxation and finding ground in the new semester, it’s time to ramp up the heat. You would never believe what just twenty minutes of poses can do to get that blood pumping and the sweat pouring! Don’t worry, though! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Open the Hips (9/14) We have been in class for a couple of weeks now and our bodies need us to keep moving to stay open and ready for all that life has to offer. Twenty three minutes of opening the hips will keep them from tightening from all the stress and constant sitting motion. Don’t forget! We also include at least five minutes of time to destress and prepare for the rest of the week. Learn a New Pose (9/16) Today’s yoga session will include 24 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out. Yogis of all experience and backgrounds will benefit from this fun practice! Get ready to build some awesome abdominal strength with this sequence. Relaxation Meditation (9/21) Today’s session will be focused on grounding yourself in this new semester. Twenty six minutes of passive, yet focused yoga practice will bring you into the moment and out of the stresses of the semester’s stressors. Getting in a Workout! (9/23) After Tuesday’s session focused on relaxation and finding ground in this awesome in-person semester, it’s time to get that body moving. Just thirty three minutes of poses will get that blood pumping and the sweat pouring! Don’t worry! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Plus, we won’t leave your muscles stiff from the hard work! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for the Booty (9/28) Looking to add cushion and tone to your derriere? Who isn’t?! Today’s session will be devoted to working to add strength to the glutes and hamstrings. Twenty minutes of work will show you some tips and tools to build your important muscle groups that keep your body healthy and moving! Learn a New Pose (9/30) Today’s yoga session will include 25 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out! Even the simplest of poses require detail-orientation! Get ready to build strength and resilience in simple poses. Relaxation Meditation (10/5) Tuesday’s session will be focused on staying sane as the semester continues to pose more difficulties. This is a time for you to take 26 minutes to treat yourself to reduce stress and a little self-care. Get a Workout In (10/7) After Tuesday’s session focused on relaxation and de-stressing, it’s time to move the mind, body, and spirit. Just 34 minutes of yoga flow will get that blood pumping! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in and focused throughout the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Plus, we won’t leave your muscles stiff from the hard work! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for Weak and Tight Shoulders (10/12) We get it. Being an athlete, veteran, human, parent, student, etc. comes with a price. Usually that price is paid in the body. Today we are going to focus on restoring weak and/or tight shoulders. Don’t shy away from class out of fear of injury! There are modifications for all flexibility levels in the shoulders. We are working to improve, not perfect! After all, we only have twenty six minutes! Learn a New Pose (10/14) Today’s yoga session will include 34 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out! Poses that seem difficult from the outside may be a bit simpler than you anticipate! We are focused on safety in strength. So first, we will build strength and confidence. Then we will build upon simple poses to create a beautiful movement to feel proud about. Relaxation Meditation (10/19) We are mid-semester. While it feels like this is the time to be working your butt off with as few breaks as possible, don’t forget about the importance of daily self-care. Today’s class will be nineteen minutes focused on nothing but bringing you back to yourself. This is a time to reclaim the best parts of yourself and create the person you want to be with focused intention. Get a Workout In (10/21) Tuesday got us mentally focused for the week, so now it is time to ramp up the energy to end the week strong! Thirty-one minutes of yoga flow will get that blood pumping! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in and focused. Don’t forget a towel! We will leave your muscles feeling worked, but not too stiff! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for Back Pain (10/26) Is your back constantly feeling stiff? Is the lower back achy and shoulder blades tight? Come to today’s yoga session for the opportunity to release some of that stiffness, and open yourself up to a world of relief! You might be surprised at what a short 33 minutes of stretching and strengthening can do for the body. Learn a New Pose (10/28) Ready to expand your yoga knowledge and experience? Today’s class will revolve around learning a yoga pose through-and-through. There is no reason to worry about the experience level needed for the pose, as all poses learned and performed here can be done at any level! Set aside 33 minutes and get mentally ready to learn reverse warrior so we can add it to your yoga repertoire! Relaxation Meditation (11/2) Meditating on a regular basis has positive effects on the body and mind, such as greater sense of focus, muscle relaxation, and increased creativity. Today’s meditation will be focused on gratitude and increasing happiness. Giving thanks can come in many forms, but have you tried it in the form of meditation?! Getting in a Workout! (11/4) After Tuesday’s session focused on gratitude in this challenging semester, it’s time to get that body moving. Just 34 minutes of sweat-inducing poses will get that blood pumping! This class is fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Plus, we won’t leave your muscles stiff from the hard work! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for a Better Mood (11/9) College is demanding, stressful, and can induce negative feelings! Combat those real-time stresses by moving the body and bonding with fellow veterans. Coming to this thirty minute vinyasa class will open the heart to the positivity you need to get you to the end of the semester. Learn a New Pose (11/11) Ready to expand your yoga knowledge and experience? Today’s class will revolve around learning a yoga pose through-and-through. There is no reason to worry about the experience level needed for the pose, as all poses learned and performed here can be done at any level! Set aside 35 minutes and get mentally ready to learn a new pose to add to your yoga repertoire! Relaxation Meditation (11/16) Today’s meditation practice will be short, sweet, and perfect to regain focus on your workflow. As we near the end of the semester, stress increases, the mind wanders, and we lose focus. We will be going through meditation techniques that can be utilized at home, work, or on the bus. Don’t underestimate the power of this 26 minute session. Come join your fellow veterans and enjoy the feeling of a clear mind. Get a Workout In (11/18) After Tuesday’s session focused on de-stressing and refocusing, it’s time to move that body. Just 34 minutes of yoga flow will get that blood pumping! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in and focused throughout the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Plus, we won’t leave your muscles stiff from the hard work! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for Neck Pain (11/23) After months of looking down at our computer screens, it’s no wonder so many of us have the amount of pain in our necks that we do! Today’s class will be all about de-stressing, communication, and releasing the tension in the neck through yoga practice. Set aside 31 minutes for this perfectly-paced practice.

name: Insurgent Terrorism: Intergroup Relationships and the Killing of Civilians
description: On Wednesday, February 23 at 10:00 a.m. ET, Victor Asal, Brian Phillips and R. Karl Rethemeyer will provide a virtual talk on their new START-Oxford University Press book, “Insurgent Terrorism: Intergroup Relationships and the Killing of Civilians.” This event is free and open to the public, but RSVPs are required. If you have any questions, please email the START events team at start-events@umd.edu. Insurgent groups consist of individuals willing to organize and commit acts of terror to achieve their goals. By nature, they depend on public support, yet they sometimes target private civilians in addition to military personnel and government officials. This book examines insurgent embeddedness--the extent to which an insurgent group is enmeshed in relationships with the state, other insurgents, and the public--in order to understand why they attack civilians. Using Big Allied and Dangerous (BAAD) as the dataset, this book drills into civilian attacks in specific contexts, including schools, news media, and nonmilitary/nongovernment spaces designed for the general public. This book goes one step further, presenting in-depth analyses of intergroup alliances and rivalries, their changes and determinants over time, and the implications for several types of bloodshed against civilians. Insurgent Terrorism offers a comprehensive, modern approach for academics, students, and policy practitioners who seek to understand interorganizational relationships between insurgent organizations. Victor Asal is the Director of the Center for Policy Research and a Professor of Political Science at the University at Albany, SUNY. His research focuses on violent nonstate actors (VNSAs), pedagogy and political discrimination related to ethnicity, gender and sexuality. He has been involved in research projects funded by the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency, Defense Threat Reduction Agency, The Department of Homeland Security, The National Science Foundation, and The Office of Naval Research. Brian J. Phillips is a Reader in the Department of Government at the University of Essex, and an Affiliated Professor at the Center for Research and Teaching in Economics (CIDE) in Mexico City. His research focuses on subnational violence including terrorism, civil conflict, organized crime, and dynamics of violent groups. His research has been funded by the Department of Homeland Security, the National Science Foundation, and the Mexican Presidency. R. Karl Rethemeyer is the Dean of the College of Social and Behavioral Sciences (SBS) at the University of Massachusetts Amherst and a faculty member in SBS's School of Public Policy. His research spans terrorism, terrorist organizations, terrorist networks, counterinsurgency/stabilization operations, and the structure and operation of collaborative and policy networks in the public sector. The START-Oxford University Press Book Series is edited by Laura Dugan (START Affiliate, The Ohio State University), Gary Ackerman (START Affiliate, University at Albany) and Anthony Lemieux (START Affiliate, Georgia State University). The series will approach terrorism conceptually as having a developmental “life-cycle.” Within this perspective, the series will treat terrorism as a phenomenon that has a set of interdependent phases: (1) the origins of extremism and the formation of terrorist groups; (2) terrorist dynamics and persistence; and (3) societal responses to terrorism.

name: Miguel Zenon Quartet
description: From bubbling rhythms and engrossing tunes to traditionally-rooted subjects and musical forms, the music of Puerto Rico native Miguel Zenón is the height of Latin jazz. Composer, improviser, saxophonist and MacArthur Foundation Fellow, Zenón combines the sounds of his homeland with contemporary complexity and innovation to create “an entirely new jazz language for the 21st century” (MacArthur Foundation). His records are an immersive experience, animating cultural soundtracks such as the intoxicating plena tradition and the centuries-old jíbara. Zenón collaborates with long-standing quartet members Austrian bassist Hans Glawischnig, Venezuelan pianist Luis Perdomo and Puerto Rican drummer Henry Cole. A lover of complex mathematical systems, Zenón has developed a highly specialized compositional approach shared now between the members of this incomparable band. Their music is as approachable and kinetic as it is erudite and exploratory, a relic of the social history that inspires so many of Zenón’s touchstones. On the new album “Sonero,” Zenón’s liquid alto tone and his quartet’s seamless ensemble playing brings to life the songs of salsa singer and songwriter Ismael Rivera, again pulling regional influences into a worldwide exchange. While visiting The Clarice, Miguel Zenón will lead a Jazz Clinic and Ethnomusicology Colloquium with students of the School of Music. Health + Safety There may be COVID safety policies such as mask requirements in place when you attend this event. Please see our health & safety page for the most up to date information about attendance!

name: Veterans Yoga
description: Sun Salutations (8/31) Get ready for a class to introduce health and vitality into the semester! This short class includes 20 minutes of cleansing movement fit for yogis of all shapes, sizes, and experience levels. Bonus: Do you not have time to relax and let go for even just a few minutes? Your instructor includes at least five minutes of required shavasana practice at the end of each class to give the mind a break from the rest of the world. Learn a New Pose (9/2) Today’s yoga session will include 18 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out, meaning that yogis of all experience and backgrounds will benefit! Get ready to build strength and resilience with this fun-to learn movement. Relaxation Meditation (9/7) Tuesday’s session will be focused on grounding yourself in this new semester. Just fifteen minutes of passive, yet focused yoga practice will bring you into the moment and out of the stresses of the new semester. Get a Workout in (9/9) After Tuesday’s session focused on relaxation and finding ground in the new semester, it’s time to ramp up the heat. You would never believe what just twenty minutes of poses can do to get that blood pumping and the sweat pouring! Don’t worry, though! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Open the Hips (9/14) We have been in class for a couple of weeks now and our bodies need us to keep moving to stay open and ready for all that life has to offer. Twenty three minutes of opening the hips will keep them from tightening from all the stress and constant sitting motion. Don’t forget! We also include at least five minutes of time to destress and prepare for the rest of the week. Learn a New Pose (9/16) Today’s yoga session will include 24 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out. Yogis of all experience and backgrounds will benefit from this fun practice! Get ready to build some awesome abdominal strength with this sequence. Relaxation Meditation (9/21) Today’s session will be focused on grounding yourself in this new semester. Twenty six minutes of passive, yet focused yoga practice will bring you into the moment and out of the stresses of the semester’s stressors. Getting in a Workout! Just thirty three minutes of poses will get that blood pumping and the sweat pouring! Don’t worry! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Plus, we won’t leave your muscles stiff from the hard work! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for the Booty (9/28) Looking to add cushion and tone to your derriere? Who isn’t?! Today’s session will be devoted to working to add strength to the glutes and hamstrings. Twenty minutes of work will show you some tips and tools to build your important muscle groups that keep your body healthy and moving! Learn a New Pose (9/30) Today’s yoga session will include 25 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out! Even the simplest of poses require detail-orientation! Yoga for Weak and Tight Shoulders (10/12) We get it. Being an athlete, veteran, human, parent, student, etc. comes with a price. Usually that price is paid in the body. Today we are going to focus on restoring weak and/or tight shoulders. Don’t shy away from class out of fear of injury! There are modifications for all flexibility levels in the shoulders. We are working to improve, not perfect! After all, we only have twenty six minutes! Learn a New Pose (10/14) Today’s yoga session will include 34 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out! Poses that seem difficult from the outside may be a bit simpler than you anticipate! We are focused on safety in strength. So first, we will build strength and confidence. Today’s class will be nineteen minutes focused on nothing but bringing you back to yourself. This is a time to reclaim the best parts of yourself and create the person you want to be with focused intention. This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in and focused. Don’t forget a towel! We will leave your muscles feeling worked, but not too stiff! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for Back Pain (10/26) Is your back constantly feeling stiff? Is the lower back achy and shoulder blades tight? Today’s class will revolve around learning a yoga pose through-and-through. There is no reason to worry about the experience level needed for the pose, as all poses learned and performed here can be done at any level! Set aside 33 minutes and get mentally ready to learn reverse warrior so we can add it to your yoga repertoire! Relaxation Meditation (11/2) Meditating on a regular basis has positive effects on the body and mind, such as greater sense of focus, muscle relaxation, and increased creativity. A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for a Better Mood (11/9) College is demanding, stressful, and can induce negative feelings! Combat those real-time stresses by moving the body and bonding with fellow veterans. Coming to this thirty minute vinyasa class will open the heart to the positivity you need to get you to the end of the semester. Set aside 35 minutes and get mentally ready to learn a new pose to add to your yoga repertoire! Relaxation Meditation (11/16) Today’s meditation practice will be short, sweet, and perfect to regain focus on your workflow. As we near the end of the semester, stress increases, the mind wanders, and we lose focus. We will be going through meditation techniques that can be utilized at home, work, or on the bus. Don’t underestimate the power of this 26 minute session. Come join your fellow veterans and enjoy the feeling of a clear mind. This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in and focused throughout the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Plus, we won’t leave your muscles stiff from the hard work! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for Neck Pain (11/23) After months of looking down at our computer screens, it’s no wonder so many of us have the amount of pain in our necks that we do! Today’s class will be all about de-stressing, communication, and releasing the tension in the neck through yoga practice. Set aside 31 minutes for this perfectly-paced practice.

The minor is designed to train the next generation of terrorism analysts, including students who plan to pursue graduate study related to terrorism as well as employment in the federal, state, local, non-profit, and/or private sectors. The program is part of the University of Maryland’s Global Studies program, alongside the minors in International Development and Conflict Management, Global Poverty, and Global Engineering Leadership. We will be offering two info sessions this spring, the first to take place in-person on Tuesday, April 12th at Tydings Hall, Classroom 0101, the second virtually on Thursday, April 21st, 2022. The info session will be led by START’s Director of Undergraduate Studies, Dr. Thomas Guarrieri, and START's Education Coordinator, who will discuss how the Global Terrorism Studies Minor Program currently works, what students have to gain from their experience in the program, application requirements, and any other questions attendees may have.

name: Intro to AR Development (Part I - Sensing the Environment)
description: Movies like Iron Man, Terminator, and Black Panther have long depicted the power of augmented reality. You may have even experienced it for yourself, with apps like Pokemon Go and Snapchat filters. But what if you wanted to make your own AR experience? Surely it must be way too complex for a beginner college student to handle! Wrong! Join the XR Club this Tuesday as we show you just how easy it is to build your own smartphone AR experience from scratch! We'll be using Unity's AR Foundation, a multi-platform framework that connects you to the core underlying capabilities of both smartphones- and headset-based AR platforms. In the first part of this workshop series, you'll learn how to get the camera stream to show up in your application, how to track and visualize features of the environment, like planes and point clouds, and how to deploy an AR application to your phone. No prior experience is necessary; all majors welcome! Notes:This workshop requires you to bring a computer with a variety of special software tools installed prior to attending the workshop. These tools could take 30 mins or longer to download and install, so you will not have enough time during the workshop to install the software without falling behind. Additionally, it is strongly recommended that you bring a physical mouse. For Android:You will need to have Unity 2021.2 (LTS) or later installed along with the Android Build Support module and the options for the Android SDK & NDK Tools and OpenJDK. All of these should be installed with the Unity Hub. You will also need to enable developer options and USB debugging on your phone, as described at https://developer.android.com/studio/debug/dev-options#enable For iOS:You will need to have Unity 2021.2 (LTS) or later installed along with the iOS Build Support module. You will also need to install the latest version of Apple's Xcode IDE, which can be found on the Mac App Store. Once you've done that, add your Apple ID account to your Xcode preferences, as described at https://help.apple.com/xcode/mac/current/#/devaf282080a Note that the Xcode IDE is only available on Macs. If you have a Windows computer, you will still be able to develop an AR applications in Unity and export it to an Xcode project, but you will not be able to open that Xcode project and deploy the build to an iOS device for testing As per University guidelines, all attendees of this event will be required to wear KN95 masks. Violators will be denied entry into the event.

name: Political Violence Across Ideological Categories
description: On Thursday, November 3 at 11:00 a.m. ET, START Founding Director and current University of Maryland Department of Criminology and Criminal Justice Chair Dr. Gary LaFree will provide a virtual talk on his recent co-authored article, “A Comparison of Political Violence by Left-wing, Right-wing and Islamist Extremists in the United States and the World.” This event is free and open to the public, but RSVPs are required. If you have any questions, please email the START events team at start-events@umd.edu. Although political violence has been perpetrated on behalf of a wide range of political ideologies, it is unclear whether there are systematic differences between ideologies in the use of violence to pursue a political cause. Prior research on this topic is scarce and mostly restricted to self-reported measures or less extreme forms of political aggression. Moreover, it has generally focused on respondents in Western countries and has been limited to either comparisons of the supporters of left-wing and right-wing causes or examinations of only Islamist extremism. In this research we address these gaps by comparing the use of political violence by left-wing, right-wing, and Islamist extremists in the United States and worldwide using two unique datasets that cover real-world examples of politically motivated, violent behaviors. Across both datasets, we find that radical acts perpetrated by individuals associated with left-wing causes are less likely to be violent. In the United States, we find no difference between the level of violence perpetrated by right-wing and Islamist extremists. However, differences in violence emerge on the global level, with Islamist extremists being more likely than right-wing extremists to engage in more violent acts. Dr. Gary LaFree was the Founding Director of START and is currently the Chair of the Department of Criminology and Criminal Justice at the University of Maryland. He was recently awarded the title of Distinguished University Professor, which is the highest academic honor conferred upon University of Maryland faculty members.

Along the way, you'll learn how to interact with Unity's physics system and create your own user interfaces (UIs). NOTES: This workshop requires you to bring a computer with Unity 2021.3.9 installed. It is recommended you install the software well in advance of the workshop. It is strongly recommended that you bring a physical mouse since it can be difficult to work in Unity with a laptop trackpad.

name: Naloxone Training
description: The University of Maryland Health Center is designated as an Overdose Response Program (ORP) through the Maryland Department of Health. As part of this designation, we offer overdose response resources to the UMD community, free of charge. One of the most popular resources we offer is Naloxone, an opioid overdose reversal medication. Similarly to how an EpiPen temporarily blocks the life-threatening symptoms of an allergic reaction (i.e. inability to breathe) while emergency medical assistance arrives, Naloxone offers this temporary support for those experiencing an opioid overdose. To get your free Naloxone through the Health Center, all you have to do is attend a brief training, which goes over how to recognize signs of an opioid overdose, instructions for using Naloxone, and what to do as emergency medical assistance makes its way to you and the person in crisis. Trainings are all offered in the Sahet Room of the Health Center, just past the main entrance to the building, and are free to any UMD community member interested in attending! Registration is required for attendance. --- RSVP URL: https://forms.gle/woguGFjSDnYfHs7VA

name: Ganesh Chaturthi Celebration by Hindu YUVA
description: This event is being hosted by Hindu YUVA, a student organization that aims to celebrate Hindu culture. Ganesh Chathurthi is a very popular Hindu festival celebrated annually around the world to mark the birthday of the god Ganesh, who is the remover of obstacles and the bringer of good luck. In this event, participants will be invited to take part in the main aspects of Ganesh Chathurthi: idol making, pooja, and visarjan. First, participants will make a small idol of Ganesh out of modeling clay. Next they will perform a pooja, or ceremony, to evoke the presence of the god in the idol by offering flowers, fruits, and sweets. Participants will then take their idol on a procession around the venue to signify Ganesh's travel back to his home in the Himalayas. Finally, participants will return to the venue and immerse their clay idols in water, which represents Ganesh's return. Hindu YUVA members will assist participants throughout the event, including leading step-by-step instructions for crafting the idol and performing the pooja correctly. Materials for the idol and pooja will be provided at the cost of a small materials fee and for those that RSVP. Participants can RSVP through a link that will be shared on social media platforms and by email.

name: AR Sandbox: December Topography Competition
description: The John and Stella Graves Makerspace and the Libraries' GIS Team are hosting a student competition highlighting our Augmented Reality Sandbox and its applications across many academic disciplines. There will be a total of 5 topography competitions that will take place in the Fall '23 and Spring '24 semesters. The winner of each monthly competition will receive a $50 Amazon gift card! From December 3rd-15th, undergraduate and graduate students are invited to use the AR Sandbox to create and submit a 3D rendering of the provided 2D topographical map. This month's map is of Deep Creek Lake in Maryland. Participants' submissions will be judged based on aesthetics and overall accuracy to the reference map. The GIS team will be hosting open hours on Tuesdays from 1-2pm and Wednesdays from 1-3pm to provide additional support for students creating their map submissions. Submissions can be created outside of these hours, but they are recommended for students who are unfamiliar with reading topography. Each submission should be completed and submitted by one individual student. 3. Each student is allowed only one submission per competition (5 total submissions if a student participates in every iteration of the competition). 4. Each participant will have a maximum of 30 minutes to complete their submission. 5. The winner of the competition will be announced November 20th, 2023 6. The winning submission will be posted to the @umdlibstem Instagram. 7. name: Beekeeping Club Weekly Meeting
description: During the late spring, summer, and early fall, we have meetings to check on our bees. We learn about sustainable beekeeping practices, what to look for and do while taking care of bees. People who show up to this meeting will have to wear bee-safe clothing such as close toed shoes, and preferably pants, though we have full suits and half suits along with gloves provided. Participants will also have to sign a safety waiver which accepts the possibility of bee stings. description: Imagine yourself completely immersed in your very own virtual world. You can bring anything to life: that cool game idea you’ve been sitting on, a breath-taking surreal experience through a mystical forest, or maybe even an interactive simulator that helps people learn something new. What will you create when the limit is your imagination? In this workshop, we will begin your journey to mastering virtual-reality development by introducing you to virtual reality and its design challenges, the features and tools of Unity that solve those challenges and allow us to create immersive experiences, and some examples of virtual-reality projects made within Unity. We welcome everyone no matter their previous experience or skill set, and we are always more than eager to answer your questions! Notes:This workshop requires you to bring a computer with a variety of special software tools installed prior to attending the workshop. These tools could take 30 mins or longer to download and install, so you will not have enough time during the workshop to install the software without falling behind. Additionally, it is strongly recommended that you bring a physical mouse. For Android:You will need to have Unity 2021 LTS or later installed along with the Android Build Support module and the options for the Android SDK & NDK Tools and OpenJDK. All of these should be installed with the Unity Hub. You will also need to enable developer options and USB debugging on your phone, as described at https://developer.android.com/studio/debug/dev-options#enable For iOS:You will need to have Unity 2021 LTS or later installed along with the iOS Build Support module. You will also need to install the latest version of Apple's Xcode IDE, which can be found on the Mac App Store. Once you've done that, add your Apple ID account to your Xcode preferences, as described at https://help.apple.com/xcode/mac/current/#/devaf282080a Note that the Xcode IDE is only available on Macs. If you have a Windows computer, you will still be able to develop an AR applications in Unity and export it to an Xcode project, but you will not be able to open that Xcode project and deploy the build to an iOS device for testing

name: Naloxone Training
description: The University of Maryland Health Center is designated as an Overdose Response Program (ORP) through the Maryland Department of Health. As part of this designation, we offer overdose response resources to the UMD community, free of charge. One of the most popular resources we offer is Naloxone, an opioid overdose reversal medication. Similarly to how an EpiPen temporarily blocks the life-threatening symptoms of an allergic reaction (i.e. inability to breathe) while emergency medical assistance arrives, Naloxone offers this temporary support for those experiencing an opioid overdose. To get your free Naloxone through the Health Center, all you have to do is attend a brief training, which goes over how to recognize signs of an opioid overdose, instructions for using Naloxone, and what to do as emergency medical assistance makes its way to you and the person in crisis. Trainings are all offered in the Sahet Room of the Health Center, just past the main entrance to the building, and are free to any UMD community member interested in attending! Registration is required for attendance.

name: Minority Males in Medicine Symposium
description: The event’s theme will center around “Quiet but Mighty” as minority males in the medical field. We have seen how history is told through a restrictive lens, and we would like to highlight male minority contributions to the health field. By doing so, we can increase awareness as well as show future generations that advancements in the medical field would not have happened without us. The tentative layout of the event will include question-guided discussion among the panelists, breakout rooms to allow student guests to ask follow up questions, a 30 minute lunch break, and advice session. We hope to have open, honest, and moving conversations about the path to a career in medicine/healthcare, the experience as a minority male in medicine/healthcare, and how to advocate for Men's Health and decrease health disparities. Everyone, regardless of gender, has the opportunity to attend workshops, talks, activities, network with sponsoring companies and receive Technica Hacks’ and sponsors’ swag. We encourage participants that identify as an underrepresented gender to hack, as per our mission statement, but do not discriminate based off of gender. Our organizers, volunteers, and mentors are the backbone of Technica and without them, the event could not be hosted. Attending Technica as an organizer, volunteer, or mentor gives those who choose to do so a way to support our mission of gender diversification in technology, build leadership skills, and an opportunity to learn more about technology. name: En'Rage Models Practice
description: Our practice sessions are dynamic and empowering, designed to build confidence, enhance runway skills, and foster creativity in a supportive environment. Each session begins with a warm-up to prepare our models for the physical and mental demands of the runway. Models are then guided through a series of runway walks, where they practice posture, poise, and movement in a variety of styles that challenge traditional norms of fashion and modeling. Throughout the practice, we focus on perfecting choreography for upcoming shows, allowing models to develop their unique flair while staying in sync with the group’s overall performance. Our experienced runway coaches provide individual feedback to ensure that each model feels confident in expressing their own style, aligning with our mission of self-empowerment and diversity. In addition to runway practice, we also incorporate photoshoot preparation, helping models become comfortable in front of the camera, and working on their poses and expressions. Music is played to set the tone, and we regularly rotate different fashion themes to keep practices fresh and engaging. Each session concludes with a debrief, where we emphasize the importance of mutual support and encouragement, celebrating personal growth and teamwork. En'Rage Models practices are more than just rehearsals—they are an opportunity for our members to develop their self-esteem, push creative boundaries, and prepare for the high-energy experience of the runway.

name: New Year, New Knowledge:  Pathways to Progress
description: Get ready for the spring semester with the Graduate School! Join us for a day of discussions and learning. Agenda 10am-10:30am Check-in 10:30am-11:45am Looking Forward in Higher Education: A Panel Discussion Universities are sites of discovery and innovation, but change in higher education itself can be slow and challenging. A range of factors–from budgets to politics to technology–will likely create ripples of change at institutions such as the University of Maryland in the near future. What might those changes be and how will they impact us? Join us to hear perspectives from faculty and researchers across campus. 11:45am-12:30pm Lunch 12:30-2:00pm "So Tell Me About Yourself": Harness the Power of Your Stories Most of us know how important interviews and networking are to our careers – but we still feel a sense of dread about them. After all, people can only get to know us through the stories we are willing to share. And yes, our stories hold power and are important to our personal and professional identities. In this 90-minute workshop, you will have time to reflect on your past experiences and share stories in a way that highlights your skills, accomplishments, and values. You will grow awareness of your strengths and increase your confidence in talking to others. 2:15-3:30pm Prioritizing You: Building a Personalized Self-Care Plan Navigating the demands of graduate school and postdoctoral training can be overwhelming, but prioritizing wellness is key to thriving both personally and professionally. In this 60-minute interactive workshop, you will learn how to develop a personalized wellness plan that incorporates meaningful self-care practices and practical strategies for maintaining balance and resilience. We’ll explore tools for managing stress, fostering mental and emotional well-being, and integrating small but impactful habits into your daily routine. Tailored specifically for the unique challenges faced by graduate students and postdocs, this session will empower you with actionable insights and resources to support your wellness journey. Leave feeling equipped to take proactive steps toward a more balanced, fulfilling, and sustainable academic and personal life. For information regarding accessibility and to request accommodations, contact Dr. Linda Macri in advance of the event at lmacri@umd.edu.

name: National Hillel Basketball Tournament 2025
description: The National Hillel Basketball Tournament (NHBT) was founded in 2010 to bring Jewish students together around the inclusive and encompassing game of basketball. Solely organized by a board of 30 highly motivated students, what began as a small event has quickly developed into one of the largest collegiate gatherings of Jewish students in the country. Now in its 13th year, the non-profit initiative, annually housed in the University of Maryland’s state-of-the-art facilities, attracts over 1,500 participants from across the United States and Canada. This year, we expect over 50 teams from over 30 universities across North America to partake in the weekend-long tournament experience. How to develop and effectively communicate your 'power stories'—the stories you anticipate sharing during an interview, crafted in a way that resonates with the interviewer. name: Miguel Zenon Quartet
description: From bubbling rhythms and engrossing tunes to traditionally-rooted subjects and musical forms, the music of Puerto Rico native Miguel Zenón is the height of Latin jazz. Composer, improviser, saxophonist and MacArthur Foundation Fellow, Zenón combines the sounds of his homeland with contemporary complexity and innovation to create “an entirely new jazz language for the 21st century” (MacArthur Foundation). His records are an immersive experience, animating cultural soundtracks such as the intoxicating plena tradition and the centuries-old jíbara. Zenón collaborates with long-standing quartet members Austrian bassist Hans Glawischnig, Venezuelan pianist Luis Perdomo and Puerto Rican drummer Henry Cole. A lover of complex mathematical systems, Zenón has developed a highly specialized compositional approach shared now between the members of this incomparable band. Their music is as approachable and kinetic as it is erudite and exploratory, a relic of the social history that inspires so many of Zenón’s touchstones. On the new album “Sonero,” Zenón’s liquid alto tone and his quartet’s seamless ensemble playing brings to life the songs of salsa singer and songwriter Ismael Rivera, again pulling regional influences into a worldwide exchange. While visiting The Clarice, Miguel Zenón will lead a Jazz Clinic and Ethnomusicology Colloquium with students of the School of Music. Health + Safety There may be COVID safety policies such as mask requirements in place when you attend this event. Please see our health & safety page for the most up to date information about attendance!
location: The Clarice Smith Performing Arts Center

name: Veterans Yoga
description: Sun Salutations (8/31) Get ready for a class to introduce health and vitality into the semester! This short class includes 20 minutes of cleansing movement fit for yogis of all shapes, sizes, and experience levels. Bonus: Do you not have time to relax and let go for even just a few minutes? Your instructor includes at least five minutes of required shavasana practice at the end of each class to give the mind a break from the rest of the world. Learn a New Pose (9/2) Today’s yoga session will include 18 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out, meaning that yogis of all experience and backgrounds will benefit! Get ready to build strength and resilience with this fun-to learn movement. Relaxation Meditation (9/7) Tuesday’s session will be focused on grounding yourself in this new semester. Just fifteen minutes of passive, yet focused yoga practice will bring you into the moment and out of the stresses of the new semester. Get a Workout in (9/9) After Tuesday’s session focused on relaxation and finding ground in the new semester, it’s time to ramp up the heat. You would never believe what just twenty minutes of poses can do to get that blood pumping and the sweat pouring! Don’t worry, though! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Open the Hips (9/14) We have been in class for a couple of weeks now and our bodies need us to keep moving to stay open and ready for all that life has to offer. Twenty three minutes of opening the hips will keep them from tightening from all the stress and constant sitting motion. Don’t forget! We also include at least five minutes of time to destress and prepare for the rest of the week. Learn a New Pose (9/16) Today’s yoga session will include 24 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out. Yogis of all experience and backgrounds will benefit from this fun practice! Get ready to build some awesome abdominal strength with this sequence. Relaxation Meditation (9/21) Today’s session will be focused on grounding yourself in this new semester. Twenty six minutes of passive, yet focused yoga practice will bring you into the moment and out of the stresses of the semester’s stressors. Getting in a Workout! (9/23) After Tuesday’s session focused on relaxation and finding ground in this awesome in-person semester, it’s time to get that body moving. Just thirty three minutes of poses will get that blood pumping and the sweat pouring! Don’t worry! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Plus, we won’t leave your muscles stiff from the hard work! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for the Booty (9/28) Looking to add cushion and tone to your derriere? Who isn’t?! Today’s session will be devoted to working to add strength to the glutes and hamstrings. Twenty minutes of work will show you some tips and tools to build your important muscle groups that keep your body healthy and moving! Learn a New Pose (9/30) Today’s yoga session will include 25 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out! Even the simplest of poses require detail-orientation! Get ready to build strength and resilience in simple poses. Relaxation Meditation (10/5) Tuesday’s session will be focused on staying sane as the semester continues to pose more difficulties. This is a time for you to take 26 minutes to treat yourself to reduce stress and a little self-care. Get a Workout In (10/7) After Tuesday’s session focused on relaxation and de-stressing, it’s time to move the mind, body, and spirit. Just 34 minutes of yoga flow will get that blood pumping! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in and focused throughout the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Plus, we won’t leave your muscles stiff from the hard work! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for Weak and Tight Shoulders (10/12) We get it. Being an athlete, veteran, human, parent, student, etc. comes with a price. Usually that price is paid in the body. Today we are going to focus on restoring weak and/or tight shoulders. Don’t shy away from class out of fear of injury! There are modifications for all flexibility levels in the shoulders. We are working to improve, not perfect! After all, we only have twenty six minutes! Learn a New Pose (10/14) Today’s yoga session will include 34 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out! Poses that seem difficult from the outside may be a bit simpler than you anticipate! We are focused on safety in strength. So first, we will build strength and confidence. Then we will build upon simple poses to create a beautiful movement to feel proud about. Relaxation Meditation (10/19) We are mid-semester. While it feels like this is the time to be working your butt off with as few breaks as possible, don’t forget about the importance of daily self-care. Today’s class will be nineteen minutes focused on nothing but bringing you back to yourself. This is a time to reclaim the best parts of yourself and create the person you want to be with focused intention. Get a Workout In (10/21) Tuesday got us mentally focused for the week, so now it is time to ramp up the energy to end the week strong! Thirty-one minutes of yoga flow will get that blood pumping! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in and focused. Don’t forget a towel! We will leave your muscles feeling worked, but not too stiff! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for Back Pain (10/26) Is your back constantly feeling stiff? Is the lower back achy and shoulder blades tight? Come to today’s yoga session for the opportunity to release some of that stiffness, and open yourself up to a world of relief! You might be surprised at what a short 33 minutes of stretching and strengthening can do for the body. Learn a New Pose (10/28) Ready to expand your yoga knowledge and experience? Today’s class will revolve around learning a yoga pose through-and-through. There is no reason to worry about the experience level needed for the pose, as all poses learned and performed here can be done at any level! Set aside 33 minutes and get mentally ready to learn reverse warrior so we can add it to your yoga repertoire! Relaxation Meditation (11/2) Meditating on a regular basis has positive effects on the body and mind, such as greater sense of focus, muscle relaxation, and increased creativity. Today’s meditation will be focused on gratitude and increasing happiness. Giving thanks can come in many forms, but have you tried it in the form of meditation?! Getting in a Workout! (11/4) After Tuesday’s session focused on gratitude in this challenging semester, it’s time to get that body moving. Just 34 minutes of sweat-inducing poses will get that blood pumping! This class is fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Plus, we won’t leave your muscles stiff from the hard work! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for a Better Mood (11/9) College is demanding, stressful, and can induce negative feelings! Combat those real-time stresses by moving the body and bonding with fellow veterans. Coming to this thirty minute vinyasa class will open the heart to the positivity you need to get you to the end of the semester. Learn a New Pose (11/11) Ready to expand your yoga knowledge and experience? Today’s class will revolve around learning a yoga pose through-and-through. There is no reason to worry about the experience level needed for the pose, as all poses learned and performed here can be done at any level! Set aside 35 minutes and get mentally ready to learn a new pose to add to your yoga repertoire! Relaxation Meditation (11/16) Today’s meditation practice will be short, sweet, and perfect to regain focus on your workflow. As we near the end of the semester, stress increases, the mind wanders, and we lose focus. We will be going through meditation techniques that can be utilized at home, work, or on the bus. Don’t underestimate the power of this 26 minute session. Come join your fellow veterans and enjoy the feeling of a clear mind. Get a Workout In (11/18) After Tuesday’s session focused on de-stressing and refocusing, it’s time to move that body. Just 34 minutes of yoga flow will get that blood pumping! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in and focused throughout the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Plus, we won’t leave your muscles stiff from the hard work! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for Neck Pain (11/23) After months of looking down at our computer screens, it’s no wonder so many of us have the amount of pain in our necks that we do! Today’s class will be all about de-stressing, communication, and releasing the tension in the neck through yoga practice. Set aside 31 minutes for this perfectly-paced practice.

name: Edgar Reyes Artist Talk
description: Edgar Reyes is a multimedia artist based in the Baltimore and Washington D.C. area. Reyes earned his MFA from Maryland Institute College of Art and has taught at non-profit organizations, schools, and museums. Many of his projects are autobiographical and a reflection of his personal journey as an undocumented youth in the United States. His work highlights the adversities his family has faced when divided by deportations, the loss of loved ones, and racially motivated crimes.Reyes is driven by the desire to raise an awareness and question the ongoing displacement of his community and their native rituals that transcend our current national borders. He explores how the blending of Indigenous and European traditions is an ongoing process of conquest and resistance.Through his creative programming interests and abilities, he nurtures the development of youth-driven arts-based leadership initiatives, that advocate how art and design can assist in self-expression and easing of cultural tensions. Reyes also creates some of his pieces in a collaborative platform as an act of healing and as a resource to creatively engage others in their connection to the land and their shared narratives of survival.His art practice highlights the beauty of being Mexican American, yet questions his national and cultural traditions. He challenges social norms to express what it means for him to be labeled Latino. His art making is centered around building compassion and understanding regarding the complex history of forced and voluntary resettlement throughout the Americas. Participants can join this talk virtually at https://go.umd.edu/edgarreyestalk or in person at the Michelle Smith Collaboratory for Visual Culture. This talk is presented in conjunction with New Arrivals 2021 in the Stamp Gallery and is supported in part by the Maryland State Arts Council (msac.org) This fall the Stamp Gallery at the University of Maryland, College Park, presents New Arrivals 2021, an exhibition of artwork acquired this year by the University’s Contemporary Art Purchasing Program (CAPP). On view August 30 through October 16, 2021, the exhibition features seven artworks by five emerging and mid-career artists. All completed within the two years, the works come from artists connected to the Baltimore-Washington area. The 2020-2021 CAPP Committee (Thomas Boland-Reeves, Emily Gilman, Katherine Jackson, Daniela Ruiz Perez) spent a year researching, writing, discussing and conducting virtual studio and gallery visits. The result of this work is a collection of artworks around their interests and concerns as University of Maryland students and global citizens in 2021. Of their selections, the Committee wrote “Art is fundamental to everyday life, and is essential in providing a medium of catharsis for both suffering and celebration. We strive to showcase works that prioritize inclusivity and diversity by uplifting marginalized voices, such as BIPOC, LGBTQ+, and female communities. The 2020-2021 selections will offer opportunities for both conversation and education that cultivate threads of connection within the UMD community.” For more information visit stamp.umd.edu/gallery
location: Michelle Smith Collaboratory for Visual Culture
