name: The Crossing: Carols After a Plague (USA)
description: Dedicated to the commissioning and performance of music by living composers, professional chamber choir The Crossing explores ways in which to expand choral writing. With more than 100 commissions, the ensemble has received two Grammy awards for “Best Choral Performance” for recordings of works that elevate dynamic compositional voices. Many of The Crossing’s commissions often address issues of our society, environment and politics. In this special project, “Carols After A Plague,” The Crossing will premiere new works that honor the resilience of emerging from a global pandemic and acknowledge the healing much needed in our world. While at The Clarice, members of The Crossing will lead a clinic with choral singers in the UMD School of Music. New commissions for “Carols After A Plague” will be written by: Leila Adu Ambrose Akinmusire Alex Berko Samantha Fernando Mary Jane Leach Shara Nova Joseph C. Unfortunately, the local organization that owns LEAFhouse has plans to sell it and move it off campus. This would be a big loss to sustainability on campus and to all the student groups who use it. So what are we doing about it? We are planning on buying it. Come help us as we coordinate with other groups, apply to grants, petition the university, and plan funding and maintenance plans to procure the building! Any assistance is welcome! name: 2022 APIDAHM Wellness Series: Reflect, Reconnect, and Renew
description: We each take on different roles in our lives– friend, mentor, supporter, leader– but we often forget that we are, above all, human. As we move through APIDA Heritage Month, join us in weekly sessions where we create a space to simply exist and celebrate our humanity. We hope to take time to pause and reflect, connecting our own lived experiences to the larger themes of APIDA Heritage Month and exploring how we can use these insights moving forward. From body movement to workshops to journaling, join our community in uplifting ourselves and one another. Healing the Inner ChildWednesday, April 13, 6PM @ MICA Cozy Corner (Basement level - across from Studio A)This session provides a space for folks to get to know their inner child. We will explore questions like: what is our inner child; how can we nurture them; what makes our inner child feel safe and loved; how can we use our inner child to fuel our advocacy and activism? Nurture your inner child through interactive and collaborative activities and discussion. Diaspora, Distance, and DisconnectThursday, April 21, 5PM @ MICA Cozy Corner (Basement level - across from Studio A)This session focuses on the Asian diaspora and distance and disconnect from extended family and broader communities, not only due to physical distance but also cultural and lingual challenges. We will discuss and reflect on our experiences as a form of self-care and healing. BodyCombat Fitness EventThursday, April 28, 7:00-8:15pm @ Eppley Recreation Centre - Fitness StudioDescription - In honor of APIDA Heritage Month, join our special BodyCombat fitness event. In addition to getting a great workout in, we will discuss things related to APIDA heritage and fixed versus growth mindsets in the fitness environment. All are welcome and no previous experience is necessary. Register here.

name: Camp PALS Volunteer opportunity
description: Volunteer to be a Counselor for the PALS program Camp PALS this summer. PALS is a nonprofit organization that provides one week long summer camp opportunities for teens and young adults with Down syndrome and their peers at 14 college campuses across the country. This is a one-week experience from 9am-5pm. Listed below are some details about Camp PALS: Here are some details about Camp PALS: - They offer 14 week long sleep-away camps across the country, including Camp PALS Georgetown, Chicago, and North Carolina! - Volunteer counselors are paired one-to-one with a camper to provide an opportunity to build -meaningful friendships through trips and activities - Looking for volunteers ages 16-30 who are welcoming, genuine, passionate, supportive, and fun which are all the values of the program. - No experience with Down syndrome or the disability community is necessary! They encourage groups of applicants to apply together to share the camp experience. If you are interested please visit the website at palsprograms.org/volunteer or check out their social media pages on Facebook or YouTube channel to get a look at what the PALS experience is like. PALS is an amazing opportunity to give back to the community, gain invaluable leadership skills, and make friends that will last a lifetime! There are no costs for volunteers at PALS, and applicants can apply for travel costs to be covered as well. We are looking for male applicants at this point in our season. Females are welcome to apply but will likely be placed on a waitlist. The dates for each of our 15 camps is different based on their locations, but the dates for Baltimore are July 7-13 at UMBC, and Georgetown is July 28-August 3 at Georgetown University.

name: SEE Presents: Free Fall Movie Series - Midsommar
description: SEE invites you to UMD’s own Hoff Theater to unwind and join us for our first Free Fall Movie Series of the 2019-20 school year! Enjoy and support several of this year’s hottest movies along with some classic cultural milestones in a large theatrical setting all semester long!Iron Man (2008)- August 29th @ 8:00pm(Action/Sci-Fi) "After being held captive in an Afghan cave, billionaire engineer Tony Stark creates a unique weaponized suit of armor to fight evil." (IMDb)Guardians of the Galaxy (2014) - August 30th @ 8:00pm(Action/Comedy) "A group of intergalactic criminals must pull together to stop a fanatical warrior with plans to purge the universe." (IMDb)Avengers: Endgame - August 31st @ 8:00pm(Action/Sci-Fi) "After the devastating events of Avengers: Infinity War (2018), the universe is in ruins. With the help of remaining allies, the Avengers assemble once more in order to reverse Thanos' actions and restore balance to the universe." (IMDb)Detective Pikachu - September 5th & 7th @ 8:00pm(Action/Comedy) "In a world where people collect Pokémon to do battle, a boy comes across an intelligent talking Pikachu who seeks to be a detective." (IMDb)Rocketman - September 11th & 12th @ 8:00pm(Biography/Drama) "A musical fantasy about the fantastical human story of Elton John's breakthrough years." (IMDb)Yesterday - September 13th & 14th @ 8:00pm(Comedy/Fantasy) "A struggling musician realizes he's the only person on Earth who can remember The Beatles after waking up in an alternate timeline where they never existed." (IMDb)John Wick: Chapter 3 - Parabellum - September 17th & 19th @ 8:00pm(Action/Crime/Thriller) "Super-assassin John Wick is on the run after killing a member of the international assassin's guild, and with a $14 million price tag on his head - he is the target of hit men and women everywhere." (IMDb)Bill and Ted’s Excellent Adventure (1989): A Special 30th Anniversary Screening - September 21st @ 10:00pm(Adventure/Comedy) "Two seemingly dumb teens set off on a quest to prepare the ultimate historical presentation with the help of a time machine." (IMDb)Midsommar - September 26th & 27th @ 8:00pm(Drama/Horror/Mystery) "A couple travels to Sweden to visit a rural hometown's fabled mid-summer festival. What begins as an idyllic retreat quickly devolves into an increasingly violent and bizarre competition at the hands of a pagan cult." (IMDb)The Rocky Horror Picture Show (1975) - September 28th @ 10:00pm(Comedy/Musical) "A newly engaged couple have a breakdown in an isolated area and must pay a call to the bizarre residence of Dr. Frank-N-Furter." (IMDb)Toy Story 4 - October 3rd & 4th @ 8:00pm(Animation/Comedy) "When a new toy called "Forky" joins Woody and the gang, a road trip alongside old and new friends reveals how big the world can be for a toy." (IMDb)Each screening will be in Hoff Theatre inside the Stamp Student Union. Each screening is open for anyone to attend and doors will open 30 minutues prior to showtime. Seating will be available on a first-come, first serve basis.All weekend movies hosted by Terps After Dark.

(Letterboxd)Written and Directed by Quentin TarantinoStarring Leonardo DiCaprio, Brad Pitt, Margot RobbieRuntime: 2 hr 41 minMPAA Rating: RWaves - February 12th, 13th - 8:00p“Let it rush over you…”The epic emotional journey of a suburban African-American family — led by a well-intentioned but domineering father — as they navigate love, forgiveness and coming together in the aftermath of a loss. (Letterboxd)Written and Directed by Trey Edward SchultsStarring Kelvin Harrison Jr., Lucas Hedges, Sterling K. BrownRuntime: 2 hr 15 minMPAA Rating: RKnives Out - February 19th, 20th - 8:00p“Hell, any of them could have done it…”A detective investigates the death of a patriarch of an eccentric, combative family. (IMDB)Written and Directed by Rian JohnsonStarring Daniel Craig, Ana de Armas, Chris EvansRuntime: 2 hr 10 minMPAA Rating: PG-13Parasite (기생충) - February 26th, 27th - 8:00p“Act like you own the place…”All unemployed, Ki-taek’s family takes peculiar interest in the wealthy and glamorous Parks for their livelihood until they get entangled in an unexpected incident. (Letterboxd)Directed by Bong Joon-hoStarring Song Kang-ho, Lee Sun-kyun, Cho Yeo-jeongRuntime: 2 hr 12 minMPAA Rating: RUncut Gems - March 4th, 5th - 8:00p“This is how I win…”Howard Ratner, a charismatic New York City jeweler always on the lookout for the next big score, makes a series of high-stakes bets that could lead to the windfall of a lifetime. name: Zine Making Workshop with La Horchata Zine via Zoom
description: Q: What is a zine? A: A zine is a small-circulation self-published work of original or appropriated texts and images, usually reproduced via photocopier. Zines are the product of either a single person or of a very small group. Join us on this day to learn about zine making, art, and the connection of social media and the Central American diaspora from artists, cultural historians, and others skilled in this 21st century, grassroots level activism and artistry.

name: Camp PALS Volunteer opportunity
description: Volunteer to be a Counselor for the PALS program Camp PALS this summer. PALS is a nonprofit organization that provides one week long summer camp opportunities for teens and young adults with Down syndrome and their peers at 14 college campuses across the country. This is a one-week experience from 9am-5pm. Listed below are some details about Camp PALS: Here are some details about Camp PALS: - They offer 14 week long sleep-away camps across the country, including Camp PALS Georgetown, Chicago, and North Carolina! - Volunteer counselors are paired one-to-one with a camper to provide an opportunity to build -meaningful friendships through trips and activities - Looking for volunteers ages 16-30 who are welcoming, genuine, passionate, supportive, and fun which are all the values of the program. - No experience with Down syndrome or the disability community is necessary! They encourage groups of applicants to apply together to share the camp experience. If you are interested please visit the website at palsprograms.org/volunteer or check out their social media pages on Facebook or YouTube channel to get a look at what the PALS experience is like. PALS is an amazing opportunity to give back to the community, gain invaluable leadership skills, and make friends that will last a lifetime! There are no costs for volunteers at PALS, and applicants can apply for travel costs to be covered as well. We are looking for male applicants at this point in our season. Females are welcome to apply but will likely be placed on a waitlist. The dates for each of our 15 camps is different based on their locations, but the dates for Baltimore are July 7-13 at UMBC, and Georgetown is July 28-August 3 at Georgetown University.

name: Meet the Faculty: Master of Professional Studies in Security & Terrorism Studies (12/6)
description: Come meet our faculty! On Monday, December 6 at 12:00 p.m. ET, Radicalization and Disengagement (RaD) researcher Dr. Elizabeth Yates will provide a virtual talk on her teaching style, learning objectives and course themes in the classes she teaches for START’s MPS in Security & Terrorism Studies. This event is free and open to the public, but RSVPs are required. If you have any questions, please email the START events team at start-events@umd.edu. Dr. Elizabeth Yates is a Senior Researcher on the domestic radicalization team at START. She works primarily on the suite of datasets associated with PIRUS (Profiles of Individual Radicalization in the United States) and BIAS (Bias Incidents and Actors Study), with a special focus on far-right violence, extremism, and hate crimes. She is also a co-Principal Investigator on a multi-year NIJ-funded project studying extremist offender reintegration. In addition, Dr. Yates has taught undergraduate classes in Terrorism Studies and Sociology at the University of Maryland and the University of Pittsburgh, respectively. She earned a doctorate in Sociology at the University of Pittsburgh, and a BA in International Relations at Tufts University. START’s MPS in Security & Terrorism Studies is a 36-credit, fully online graduate program which prepares students to examine the complex social, political, economic, and psychological underpinnings of terrorist and other asymmetric security threats. Students can take classes full- or part-time, and small class sizes enable students to receive the full attention of some of the top experts in the fields of intelligence analysis, national security and terrorism studies. Apply for the Spring 2022 semester by January 7, 2022.

name: How Did This *Monster* Get Elected?
description: The unbelievable has happened. The man who called for deporting all 12 million undocumented immigrants and banning Muslims from entering the country, and who bragged about getting away with sexual assault, has just been elected to be President of the United States. But his election has been met with resistance from the very beginning - with tens of thousands taking to the streets to protest and to stand in solidarity with all those who he would target with his bigotry and hatred. And it also remains true that millions of people in this country, suffering under the impact of a deep social and economic crisis that has gone unaddressed by the elites of both parties, are looking for an alternative. It was only in this last year that 12 million people cast a vote for a self-described socialist. And movements like the courageous struggle of indigenous activists and supporters at Standing Rock, and Black Lives Matter, and a series of smaller actions have shown a desire for change. This election has shown that there is a deep anger at a political establishment that is out of touch with ordinary people's lives and has little to offer. While large numbers of Trump's supporters were driven by racism, that alone does not explain our situation. Economic decline and insecurity clearly drove a vote against the status quo. Trump exploited this sentiment with his false promises. For millions of people at their end of their rope financially, Clinton had nothing to offer besides not being Trump. In the end, that was not enough. Not for those who swung to Trump - or, even more significantly, the millions of people who stayed home because they felt like they had nothing to vote for. This election shows what socialists have been saying all along: we need a socialist alternative to the horror that capitalism has produced. And if we don't seize this moment to build that alternative, then that space will be filled by a right-wing that will offer scapegoating and fear. Join us Thursday as we try to make sense of the election and what it means for our efforts to build and rebuild the grassroots struggles for justice that MUST define the new era of Trump.

name: The March for Racial Justice: Panel Discussion
description: At UMD and Across the US: The March for Racial Justice Meeting Thurs., Sept. 28 at 7 PM Margaret Brent Room 2112 -- Stamp Student Union UMD, College Park Thursday, Sept. 28 at 7 PM at Margaret Brent Room 2112, Stamp Student Union on UMD, College Park join local and national activists to discuss this Saturday's MARCH FOR RACIAL JUSTICE (Sept. 30, M4RJ.com) in DC. The need for a unified, mass movement for racial equality and justice has never been more urgent. Donald Trump's attacks on women, immigrants, and minorities threatens the lives and well-being of millions while his ugly rhetoric emboldens the violent racists of the extreme Right. Here at UMD, we mourne the loss of Lt. Richard Collins III who wasmurdered in May by a white supremicist. We must also continue the struggle to confront and eliminate the institutions of oppression and hate that lead to Lt. Collins tragic death. Confirmed speakers include: * Maurice Cooke, March for Racial Justice (DC) and DC activist * Shujaa Graham, exonerated death row prisoner and Civil Rights activist * Dave Zirin, Sports Editor, The Nation * Akua Ofori, March for Racial Justice (Oakland) and Int. Socialist Org. (ISO) From the "March for Racial Justice" website (M4RJ.com): "The March for Racial Justice is a black and indigenous led multi-community movement united in our demands for racial equity and justice. We are calling for a reversal of laws, policies and practices that hasten inequality, dehumanize people of color and maintain white supremacy. We march because as long as U.S. laws, policies, and practices remain steeped in white supremacy, basic human rights and civil rights for all—our universal and constitutional rights—will never be fully realized. It is our duty to dismantle oppression, as well as, challenge and put an end to racist laws, policies, and practices that dehumanize people of color while sustaining white supremacy. Our mission is to harness the national unrest and dissatisfaction with racial injustice into a national mobilization that strengthens local and nationwide efforts for racial equity and justice." The March for Racial Justice is Saturday, Sept. 30th, 10 AM at DC's Lincoln Park. UMD Students will gather at College Park Metro at 8:30 AM! Sponsored by: March for Racial Justice (M4RJ), International Socialist Org. (ISO), UMD Branch, and Students for Justice in Palestine (SJP), UMD Chapter (list in formation).

name: The Revolutionists
description: Juxtaposed against the background of the French Revolution’s Reign of Terror, this raucous comedy portrays a sisterhood of four women: a playwright, an assassin, a former queen and a rebel. The play touches on themes of legacy, activism, terrorism and feminism to suggest how women can change the world. Though set in 1793, this production uses language, culture and references to contemporary culture to highlight the relevance of such themes today. “…a sassy, hold-on-to-your-seats theatrical adventure…[Gunderson] has created a play that is wonderfully wild and raucous…It’s a wild ride, filled with verbal gymnastics that come racing at you so quickly it’s occasionally hard to keep up. Listen closely, though, and hang on tight. name: Guest Speaker: Rabbi Judah Dardik
description: At Kedma, we seek to provide the community at UMD with unique opportunities for Jewish education and spirituality. We are able to explore our deep connection to our culture and roots through the learning of Jewish texts. To help with this goal, we would like to host Rabbi Judah Dardik for a Torah lecture via Zoom to teach and inspire our organization to become better Torah scholars, as well as improve our character as people. Rabbi Judah Dardik is a Sgan Rosh Yeshiva (Assistant Dean) at Yeshivat Orayta, teaches Talmud, Jewish law, Jewish Philosophy, and Personal Growth, and oversees student welfare. He is also the Dean of the JLE, the Orayta Center for Jewish Leadership and Engagement, where he runs adult education and rabbinic educational missions and directs Orayta’s larger effort to inspire the broader Jewish community and help train its leadership. He completed thirteen years as the spiritual and community leader of Beth Jacob Congregation, in Oakland, California. Under his leadership, it became a vibrant and fast-growing community and educational center for families from a wide range of backgrounds and beliefs and practices. An award-winning teacher, he has lectured widely across the United States and Israel, taught and consulted at multiple schools, wrote a regular Torah column that was turned into a book available on Amazon, and helped to train rabbinical students at Yeshiva University’s RIETS program. Rabbi Dardik is also certified as a couple's educator and served in national leadership positions with AIPAC and the Rabbinical Council of America. He received his BA from Yeshiva University's Sy Syms School of Business, his Master's degree from the Azrielli Graduate School of Jewish Education, and his ordination from the Rabbi Isaac Elchanan Theological Seminary (RIETS) of Yeshiva. He is passionate about Jewish education and welcomes the opportunity to learn with people of all backgrounds and perspectives. Rabbi Dardik will be teaching on matters of Jewish law and philosophy via Zoom to about 40 students.

About Us: St. Francis Neighborhood Center's mission is committed to breaking the cycles of poverty through education, inspiring self-esteem, self-improvement, and strengthening connections. name: Tutor/Mentor 6th - 8th grade Students
description: Do you enjoy giving back to the community through support in literacy - reading, writing, math? Are you interested in helping students gain an appreciation for Science, Technology, Engineering, & Mathematics through hands on activities? If you answered yes, then iL.E.A.D. Success Tutoring & Mentoring is an excellent way to support the Prince George's community. name: Love Island 2024
description: Based loosely on the title of a UK hit reality series, the African Student Association is an event centered around Black love in honor of Black History Month. The topic of Black love involves celebrating and cherishing oneself and the community despite the systemic oppression that negatively impacts one’s experiences. Community and social belonging are significant in many African cultures. With this event, we would like to create a space or “villa” where different members of the UMD community can come together to interact with each other and to learn more about African cultures and current events. With this event “contestants” will be able to make well thought personal decisions impacting the outcome of their experience. This event is similar to the Charity Volunteer Auction events we have hosted in previous years but with a twist. The African Students Association (ASA) at the University of Maryland, College Park began in 1981 with the purpose of encouraging the spirit of unity, togetherness, and humanity amongst its members and the campus community. This event gives our organization the opportunity to showcase important aspects of the mission statement by educating the UMD community about the history of African, exigent issues within the continent, and how its culture, art, music, etc have influenced today's African cultures as well as Western culture while also giving UMD affiliates the chance to participate in a program that gives back to those in need. This event will help us increase interaction between ASA members and those of other backgrounds as well as broaden our community service sphere. A newcomer would be able to learn about African history, especially the artistic side of it, as well as get a taste of African culture through the different elements of the event such as music, host, and art. This event also aids social exchange throughout guests. Guests are able to communicate with each other and hash out their opinions on various voting portions of the show. In addition there are sections in the program where we directly involve the audience and give them a chance to represent what Black love would mean to them.

We go to the three diners on campus and eat as much as we want, or we head to the Stamp student center with more options for food. The point of food insecurity is to allow students to speak with Dr. Psyche about her research andbackground in food insecurity at a local, regional, and national scale. Dorothy’s TableTalk introduces the concept of food desserts, food programs, and international causesthat work to decrease food insecurity around the world. name: Walk with an Arborist & Your Baby
organization: University of Maryland Arboretum & Botanical Gardens
description: Walk with an Arborist & Your Baby encourages new parents to connect with each other and with the outdoors in a safe space, both physically and emotionally. Based in the Garden of Reflection & Remembrance at the Memorial Chapel, participants learn about trees and plants while having their newborns along. Parental leave and the welcoming of a new child can be lonely and stressful. By offering a tour specifically for new parents and caregivers, participants can interact as much (or as little) as they wish with other adults and have a focus in order to leave the house. According to the National Institutes of Health, one in seven women will develop postpartum depression and many others will still experience feelings of loneliness and isolation during parental leave. These symptoms can affect all genders, adoptive parents, and all caregivers, not just the birth parent. Things like cost, transportation, and child care can hinder access to alleviating symptoms. The Arboretum aims to make the outdoors and public gardens more accessible to everyone, regardless of where they are in life's journey. Registration is required on the Arboretum website: https://arboretum.umd.edu/maps-tours/walk-arborist-your-baby

name: Weed Warriors on Campus
organization: University of Maryland Arboretum & Botanical Gardens
description: Weed Warriors on Campus is a volunteer event for UMD students, faculty, staff, and community members that hosts educational invasive species removal events. We meet from March to October, weather permitting. During cold months, please wear appropriate warm outdoor clothing. During hot months, please wear light-colored, loose-fitting clothing and bring water to drink. Hats are always a good idea. There is poison ivy at the work site. Ticks may be present as well. SSL hours are available for students in high school, please bring appropriate forms with you to the event. Registration is Required so we can inform you of weather-related cancellations: October 5, 10am - 12pm: CLICK HERE TO REGISTER Invasive species are non-native organisms that cause harm to the environment, economy, or human health (UMD Extension). Each event includes an explanation of invasive species in Maryland, a demonstration of which invasive species we will be targeting, and group removal of target plants. Removing these species will improve the health of our native trees and plants, as well as the insects, birds, and animals that our native plants support. Weed Warriors on Campus is a great way to get outdoors on campus and meet other people that care about the environment!

name: Maryland Mentor Corps Celebration Days
description: REGISTER TO VOLUNTEER HERE: https://umd.givepulse.com/event/410881-maryland-mentor-corps-2024-celebration-days Maryland Reading Celebration Day (April 19) The Maryland Reading Program (formerly America Reads) is a literacy tutoring program for first and second grade students in Prince George's County Public Schools. University of Maryland mentors work one-on-one with students twice a week, providing extra instruction and support in reading and writing. All mentors receive extensive training in Reading Recovery and general tutoring methods. This year, Maryland Reading Day is on April 19th in the Stamp Student Union. Volunteers have the opportunity to participate in small group reading and facilitate afternoon literacy activities. A book is selected as the theme of the day and students engage in literacy and creative activities that reflect the content or message of the book. This year's book is Strictly No Elephants by Lisa Mantchev. Past books have included The Good Egg by Jory John, Last Stop on Market Street by Matt de la Peña, Click, Clack, Moo: Cows That Type by Doreen Cronin. Maryland Math Celebration Day (May 3) Maryland Math Program (formerly America Counts) is a University of Maryland based program whose goal is to make sure that every child in the United States is able to read independently and well as well as solve and understand the basis of mathematical concepts by the end of fourth grade. The program was established in 1996 with the help of former University of Maryland President William E. Kirwan. In an attempt to achieve this objective, we at Maryland Math host an annual Maryland Math Celebration Day. This year, Maryland Math Celebration Day is on May 3rd. Various students from selected Prince George’s County elementary schools affiliated with this program are invited to the University of Maryland to participate in a tour that not only engages them in mathematical activities but also shows them some of the college experience.

description: Teach-In Session on Cervical Cancer with Professor Jenna Mueller, Assistant Professor, Fischell Department of Bioengineering Dr. Jenna Mueller, who joined the University of Maryland in August 2020, brings extensive expertise in cervical cancer management. Her research focuses on creating low-cost diagnostic and therapeutic technologies to improve cervical cancer care, especially in low and middle-income countries (LMICs). Before joining UMD, she was a Postdoctoral Associate at Duke University, where she helped develop the Pocket colposcope—a commercially available, low-cost device for screening cervical dysplasia. name: En'Rage Models Practice
description: Our practice sessions are dynamic and empowering, designed to build confidence, enhance runway skills, and foster creativity in a supportive environment. Each session begins with a warm-up to prepare our models for the physical and mental demands of the runway. Models are then guided through a series of runway walks, where they practice posture, poise, and movement in a variety of styles that challenge traditional norms of fashion and modeling. Throughout the practice, we focus on perfecting choreography for upcoming shows, allowing models to develop their unique flair while staying in sync with the group’s overall performance. Our experienced runway coaches provide individual feedback to ensure that each model feels confident in expressing their own style, aligning with our mission of self-empowerment and diversity. In addition to runway practice, we also incorporate photoshoot preparation, helping models become comfortable in front of the camera, and working on their poses and expressions. Music is played to set the tone, and we regularly rotate different fashion themes to keep practices fresh and engaging. Each session concludes with a debrief, where we emphasize the importance of mutual support and encouragement, celebrating personal growth and teamwork. En'Rage Models practices are more than just rehearsals—they are an opportunity for our members to develop their self-esteem, push creative boundaries, and prepare for the high-energy experience of the runway.

name: Yuri Kochiyama High School Leadership Program 2024
description: The Yuri Kochiyama High School Leadership Program (YKLP) is an annual opportunity for DMV high school students to learn about the history of Asian American activism, strengthen their sense of identity through learning about cross-racial and intersectional community building, and develop peer solidarity and mentorship with other BIPOC-identifying individuals at UMD and other high school students.Hosted by the Asian American Student Union (AASU) at the University of Maryland, College Park (UMCP), YKLP seeks to celebrate the legacy of Japanese American activist, Yuri Kochiyama, by providing community education and mentorship to students interested in Asian American issues--completely free of charge.This year, we are taking applications for a cohort that will meet once a week through a hybrid format over a 5-week session during the spring. Each week, YK participants will come together to learn about Asian American history, identity, and leadership through intersectional community building. YKLP will end with an End-of-Program Celebration on April 13. name: En'Rage Models Practice
description: Our practice sessions are dynamic and empowering, designed to build confidence, enhance runway skills, and foster creativity in a supportive environment. Each session begins with a warm-up to prepare our models for the physical and mental demands of the runway. Models are then guided through a series of runway walks, where they practice posture, poise, and movement in a variety of styles that challenge traditional norms of fashion and modeling. Throughout the practice, we focus on perfecting choreography for upcoming shows, allowing models to develop their unique flair while staying in sync with the group’s overall performance. Our experienced runway coaches provide individual feedback to ensure that each model feels confident in expressing their own style, aligning with our mission of self-empowerment and diversity. In addition to runway practice, we also incorporate photoshoot preparation, helping models become comfortable in front of the camera, and working on their poses and expressions. Music is played to set the tone, and we regularly rotate different fashion themes to keep practices fresh and engaging. Each session concludes with a debrief, where we emphasize the importance of mutual support and encouragement, celebrating personal growth and teamwork. En'Rage Models practices are more than just rehearsals—they are an opportunity for our members to develop their self-esteem, push creative boundaries, and prepare for the high-energy experience of the runway.

name: DOTS Mobility Audit
description: The DOTS Mobility Audit is a campus community data collection effort for the Bikeways Feasibility Study. As we embark on the creation of UMD’s first on-campus network of dedicated bicycle paths, we are inviting students, faculty, and staff to join us for a behind-the-handlebar tour of our study area. We greatly value the ideas and experiences of micromobility users of all skill levels, and are seeking participation from beginners as well as seasoned cyclists. The feedback and opinions gathered in this audit will be shared with the project team during the feasibility study and preliminary design phase. We are hosting two mobility audits, each covering a different area of campus. We expect for each audit to take 2 to 2.5 hours, including the ride, small-group discussions throughout the audit, and a post-ride lunch/feedback session. A complimentary lunch will be provided by DOTS at the end of each session. Thursday, October 12th (1:00 PM - 3:30 PM) - Eastern Campus Wednesday, October 18 (10:00 AM - 12:30 PM) - Western Campus Prior to the Mobility Audits, DOTS will host a Pre-ride virtual briefing on Monday, October 9 (12:00 PM - 1:00 PM). This briefing will be recorded and will cover the purpose of the Bikeways Feasibility Study, what to expect while on the ride, and our goals in hosting these audits. Each audit is capped at 20 participants. To ensure we get feedback from as many voices as possible, please only register for one session. If you are interested in attending both sessions, please note this under the comments of this form. Leading up to the event, if we have spaces available, we will reach out with more information! E-bikes and E-scooters are welcome to join either session, but please be sure to maintain a slow pace that matches the pace of the larger group. The Beekeeping Club does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, religion, age, or physical ability. The Mission of The Beekeeping Club is to educate students about bees and beekeeping through hands-on experience and lectures, about harvesting raw products from them in sustainable ways, and about turning those raw products a variety of goods. name: Unity Gala 2023
description: This year’s Unity Gala is tied to the Asian Pacific Islander Desi American (APIDA) Heritage Month’s theme of Memories in Motion: Memories seemingly live in our past. Yet, they inform so much of our present and shape so much of our future. They aren’t just the makeup of our individual experiences, but a confluence of our collective identity—they are our ancestors, our stories, our traditions. Memories can evoke so many different feelings for each of us. At times, they bring us joy and laughter, and other recollections might bring pain and sadness. But what is constant is that they move us to think, reflect, and act. To honor our past and how it shapes us. To heal what has yet to be explored. To remember what has been forgotten in service to the broken promises of the American dream. To transform what weighs us down to what lifts us up. And to work in solidarity towards liberation, as all our histories are interconnected. Memories have power. Let them move us to action. Unity Gala is the culminating celebration of the University of Maryland’s recognition of APIDA Heritage Month in April. The mission of the annual Unity Gala is to eliminate cultural barriers between different APIDA student groups on campus to mark the end of Asian Pacific Islander Desi American Heritage Month at UMCP. On campus, Asian American student organizations host their own events within the wider AAPI circle, such as KSA’s KExpo, TASA’s Tour of Taiwan, and VSA’s Family Night. However, student organizations rarely interact with cultural organizations beyond the Asian American/Pacific Islander sphere. The Asian American Student Union strives to extend the sphere of APIDA Organizations through this gala. In the wake of troubling and hostile events, the gala is meant to create a space for a safe exchange of ideas, identities and cultures.

name: Naloxone Training
description: The University of Maryland Health Center is designated as an Overdose Response Program (ORP) through the Maryland Department of Health. As part of this designation, we offer overdose response resources to the UMD community, free of charge. One of the most popular resources we offer is Naloxone, an opioid overdose reversal medication. Similarly to how an EpiPen temporarily blocks the life-threatening symptoms of an allergic reaction (i.e. inability to breathe) while emergency medical assistance arrives, Naloxone offers this temporary support for those experiencing an opioid overdose. To get your free Naloxone through the Health Center, all you have to do is attend a brief training, which goes over how to recognize signs of an opioid overdose, instructions for using Naloxone, and what to do as emergency medical assistance makes its way to you and the person in crisis. Trainings are all offered in the Sahet Room of the Health Center, just past the main entrance to the building, and are free to any UMD community member interested in attending! Registration is required for attendance.

name: Intro to AR Development (Part 1)
description: Movies like Iron Man, Terminator, and Black Panther have long depicted the power of augmented reality. You may have even experienced it for yourself, with apps like Pokemon Go and Snapchat filters. But what if you wanted to make your own AR experience? Surely it must be way too complex for a beginner college student to handle! Wrong! Join the XR Club this Tuesday as we show you just how easy it is to build your own smartphone AR experience from scratch! We'll be using Unity's AR Foundation, a multi-platform framework that connects you to the core underlying capabilities of both smartphones- and headset-based AR platforms. In the first part of this workshop series, you'll learn how to get the camera stream to show up in your application, how to track and visualize features of the environment, like planes and point clouds, and how to deploy an AR application to your phone. No prior experience is necessary; all majors welcome! Notes:This workshop requires you to bring a computer with a variety of special software tools installed prior to attending the workshop. These tools could take 30 mins or longer to download and install, so you will not have enough time during the workshop to install the software without falling behind. Additionally, it is strongly recommended that you bring a physical mouse. For Android:You will need to have Unity 2021.3.10 (LTS) or later installed along with the Android Build Support module and the options for the Android SDK & NDK Tools and OpenJDK. All of these should be installed with the Unity Hub. You will also need to enable developer options and USB debugging on your phone, as described at https://developer.android.com/studio/debug/dev-options#enable For iOS:You will need to have Unity 2021.3.10 (LTS) or later installed along with the iOS Build Support module. You will also need to install the latest version of Apple's Xcode IDE, which can be found on the Mac App Store. Once you've done that, add your Apple ID account to your Xcode preferences, as described at https://help.apple.com/xcode/mac/current/#/devaf282080a Note that the Xcode IDE is only available on Macs. If you have a Windows computer, you will still be able to develop an AR applications in Unity and export it to an Xcode project, but you will not be able to open that Xcode project and deploy the build to an iOS device for testing

name: CARing
description: The Thursday CARing Kids program is a weekly service opportunity for University of Maryland students. The program seeks to provide role models to the elementary school children of Langley Park. This program pairs each child one-on-one with a university student, who is their buddy for the semester. CARing buddies focus on developing the children's language, reading, and math as well as their self image and social abilities which includes playing gamesand other recreational activities. The funds would go towards transporting UMD students and the elementary school students that we partner with. As Lutherans, we do the Thursday CARing Kids Program because of a deep sense of God’s Call to love and serve our neighbor. While the program is put on by Lutheran Student Association, there is no religious instruction involved in the program, and volunteers do not need to have a certain religious orientation toparticipate or contribute to the program.

name: Alternatives in Mobilization: Ethnicity, Religion, and Political Conflict
description: On Wednesday, November 30 at 12:00 p.m. ET, University of Maryland Professor of Government and Politics Dr. Jóhanna Birnir will provide a virtual talk on her co-authored book, Alternatives in Mobilization: Ethnicity, Religion, and Political Conflict. This event is free and open to the public, but RSVPs are required. If you have any questions, please email the START events team at start-events@umd.edu. What determines which identity cleavage, ethnicity or religion, is mobilized in political contestation, be it peaceful or violent? In contrast to common predictions that the greatest contention occurs where identities are fully segmented, most identity conflicts in the world are between ethnic groups that share religion. Alternatives in Mobilization builds on the literature about political demography to address this seeming contradiction. The book proposes that variation in relative group size and intersection of cleavages help explain conundrums in the mobilization of identity, across transgressive and contained political settings. This theory is tested cross-nationally on identity mobilization in civil war and across violent conflict in Pakistan, Uganda, Nepal and Turkey, and peaceful electoral politics in Indonesia. This book helps illustrate a more accurate and improved picture of the ethnic and religious tapestry of the world and addresses an increasing need for a better understanding of how religion contributes to conflict. Dr. Jóhanna Birnir is a Professor in the department of Government and Politics and the director of GVPT Global Learning. Jóhanna studies the effect of identity (ethnicity, religion, gender) on contentious political outcomes (elections and violence), and has done extensive fieldwork in the Andes, South-East Europe and Indonesia. Birnir’s first book "Ethnic Electoral Politics" (Cambridge University Press) examines the relationship between political access and minority strategic choice of peaceful electoral participation, protest or violence against the state. Birnir’s articles on identity and politics are published in numerous academic journals including the American Journal of Political Science, Comparative Political Studies, Journal of Peace Research, Journal of Conflict Resolution, Party Politics, Latin American Research Review, Studies in Comparative International Development, and Journal of Global Security Studies. name: How to Prepare For an Interview
organization: University Career Center & The Presidents Promise
description: Interviewing takes practice and interviews do not need to be perfect. It's normal to say 'um' occasionally, to be surprised by unexpected questions, or to ask for clarification to ensure you understand a question correctly. These scenarios are perfectly okay because we're all human. The key is to be well-prepared and authentic throughout the interview process. Learn more and register on Handshake!Join us for an insightful session where we will explore: The various types of interviews, including live phone/virtual, asynchronous, case, and technical interviews, along with quick tips for each. This workshop will primarily focus on strategies for behavioral-based interviews. Essential information to gather about an employer and the position before attending an interview or joining a Zoom call. How to develop and effectively communicate your 'power stories'—the stories you anticipate sharing during an interview, crafted in a way that resonates with the interviewer. name: Creating Beautiful Trouble: A workshop for activists
description: facilitated by Mora Fernández and Hannah Brancato Co-hosted by the Stamp Gallery and CARE November 12, 5:30-7:30 p.m. Free and Open to the Public. Creating Beautiful Trouble is a workshop that draws from an open-source toolkit of the same name. After viewing examples of “artivism” from the toolkit, and Mora Fernández’s research in Latin America, the facilitators will lead students in ideation about their own artistic strategies to resist sexual violence. The workshop will invite students to reflect on their lived experiences, analyzing the problems and possibilities that they face in constructing a supportive culture for survivors and in building consent culture. About the facilitators: Mora Fernández is an author for the We Will Not Be Silent catalogue, where she is writing about how activism is remembered. She is a Mexican ARTivist, consultant, human rights defender, survivor, and advocate for victims of child sexual abuse with 25 years of international experience. She is the Founder and CEO of La Casa Mandarina AC (LCM), and co-director of FORCE: upsetting rape culture. She became involved with the Monument Quilt when LCM led the Mexican branch and focused primarily on the experiences of undocumented migrants and Latinx survivors. Mora is the co-investigator of a research project between LCM and the University of York, UK: “From feeling to resisting: artivist impact, resistance and knowledge on sexual and gender violence in Mexico.” Hannah Brancato is the curator of the exhibition, a current PhD student in American Studies at the University of Maryland, and an artist. Her research focuses on memory work and the role of art in anti-sexual violence movements, and is informed by her role as co-founder FORCE: Upsetting Rape Culture, an art/organizing collective active from 2010-2020, that produced a range of creative interventions to create a culture of consent. FORCE is best known for the Monument Quilt, a collection of 3,000 stories from survivors of sexual violence, written, painted and stitched onto red fabric. Her current collaborative artwork, Dreamseeds, is currently on view at the Baltimore Museum of Art. This workshop is in conjunction with the current exhibition at the Stamp Gallery, We Will Not Be Silent: Art Transforming Rape Culture, on view from October 30 to December 15, 2025. This exhibition is supported by a Do Good Institute Campus Fund Grant, Arts For All, and the Maryland State Arts Council. Programming is supported by the LGBTQ+ Equity Center and CARE to Stop Violence. ASL interpretation is available. Accessibility for this exhibition includes content warnings, sensory objects, tactile artworks, seating, braille labels, and visual descriptions of artworks. Visitors are encouraged to wear a mask while visiting the opening. A full statement of accessibility is available here. The exhibition flier features large, capitalised, bold font in brown, against a beige background. The bold brown text spells the title: "We Will Not Be Silent: Art Transforming Rape Culture." Below the title are two images of artworks: one on the left shows a raised fist outlined in gold on a magenta background with circular patterns, while the other on the right is an aerial view of a large outdoor installation spelling out "YOU ARE NOT ALONE" in red fabric panels arranged across a grassy field. Additional text announces: "Jadelynn St Dre, Creating Beautiful Trouble: A Workshop for Activists Facilitated by Mora Fernández and Hannah Brancato, November 12, 5:30 PM – 7:30 PM." The flyer notes that the event is free and open to the public and hosted by the Adele H. Stamp Student Union Center for Campus Life’s Stamp Gallery at the University of Maryland. Logos of supporting organizations are displayed along the bottom. ABOUT THE GALLERY Located on the first floor of the Adele H. Stamp Student Union—Center for Campus Life at the University of Maryland, College Park, the Stamp Gallery is dedicated to exhibiting contemporary art, especially the work of emerging and mid-career artists. The Stamp Gallery supports contemporary art that is challenging, academically engaging, and attuned to broad community and social issues. Through meaningful exhibitions and programming, the Gallery offers outside-of-the-classroom experiential learning opportunities. It functions as a laboratory where emerging artists and curators experiment and refine their ideas. The Gallery’s programming aims to emphasize the importance of process to contemporary artistic practice and to provide a forum for dialogue. FREE and open to the public. Gallery hours: Mondays–Thursdays: 10 a.m. – 8 p.m., Fridays: 10 a.m. – 5 p.m., Saturdays: 11 a.m. – 5 p.m., Sundays: Closed. More information: stamp.umd.edu/gallery. Espanol: Creando problemas hermosos: un taller para activistas facilitado por Mora Fernández y Hannah Brancato en el Studio A, B0107 Stamp Union Coorganizado por la Stamp Gallery y CARE 12 de noviembre, 17:30-19:30 hrs “Creando problemas hermosos” es un taller que se basa en un toolkit del mismo nombre. Después de ver ejemplos de "artivismo" del toolkit y la investigación de Mora Fernández en Latinoamérica, las facilitadoras guiarán a lxs estudiantes a idear sus propias estrategias artísticas para resistir la violencia sexual. El taller invitará a lxs estudiantes a reflexionar sobre sus experiencias vividas, analizando los problemas y las posibilidades que enfrentan al construir una cultura que apoye a lxs sobrevivientes y promueva la cultura del consentimiento. Este taller se realiza en conjunto con la exposición actual en la Stamp Gallery: No guardaremos silencio: el arte transformando la cultura de violación, del 30 de octubre al 15 de diciembre de 2025. Sobre las facilitadoras: Mora Fernández (ella) es autora del catálogo “No guardaremos silencio”, donde escribe sobre cómo se recuerda y se construye memoria sobre el activismo. Es una ARTivista mexicana, consultora, defensora de derechos humanos, sobreviviente y acompañante de víctimas de abuso sexual infantil con veinticinco años de experiencia internacional creando proyectos innovadores, disruptivos y radicales para luchar contra la violencia sexual, sanar el trauma, reclamar la alegría y el placer y cambiar las políticas públicas. Es la fundadora y directora ejecutiva de La Casa Mandarina AC (LCM) y codirectora de FORCE: Upsetting Rape Culture. Se involucró con el Monumento de Historias cuando LCM dirigía la parte mexicana y se centró principalmente en las experiencias de migrantes indocumentadxs y sobrevivientes latinxs. Mora es coinvestigadora de un proyecto de investigación entre LCM y la Universidad de York, Reino Unido: Del sentir al resistir: impactos y conocimientos artivistas sobre la violencia sexual y de género en México. Hannah Brancato (ella) es la curadora de la exposición, estudiante de doctorado en Estudios Estadounidenses en la Universidad de Maryland y artista. Su investigación se centra en el trabajo de la memoria y el papel del arte en los movimientos contra la violencia sexual, y está influenciada por su rol como cofundadora de FORCE: Upsetting Rape Culture, un colectivo artístico activo entre 2010 y 2020, que produjo una serie de intervenciones creativas para crear una cultura del consentimiento. FORCE es conocida por el Monumento de Historias, una colección de 3000 historias de sobrevivientes de violencia sexual, escritas, pintadas y bordadas sobre tela roja. Su obra colaborativa actual, “Dreamseeds”, se exhibe actualmente en el Museo de Arte de Baltimore. Esta exposición fue posible gracias al apoyo del Do Good Institute Campus Fund Grant, Arts For All y el Maryland State Arts Council. La programación cuenta con el apoyo del LGBTQ+ Equity Center y CARE to Stop Violence. La accesibilidad es una prioridad para la exposición. Las prácticas de accesibilidad de esta exposición incluyen advertencias sobre el contenido, objetos sensoriales, obras de arte táctiles, descripciones visuales, lugares para sentarse, etiquetas en braille, espacios tranquilos para el descanso y descripciones visuales de las obras de arte. Se recomienda a lxs visitantes usar un tapabocas durante la inauguración y leer las advertencias sobre el contenido antes de entrar. El material de esta exposición estará disponible en inglés, español y braille. El documento completo sobre accesibilidad está disponible aquí y también lo encontrarás más adelante. Advertencia de contenido Se recomienda a lxs visitantes que lean con anticipación las advertencias sobre el contenido de esta exposición. También estarán disponibles en la StampGallery. SOBRE LA STAMP GALLERY Ubicada en la primera planta del Adele H. Stamp Student Union—Center for Campus Life at the University of Maryland, College Park, la Stamp Gallery se dedica a exhibir arte contemporáneo, especialmente la obra de artistas emergentes y a la mitad de su carrera profesional. La Stamp Gallery apoya el arte contemporáneo provocador, académicamente atractivo y en sintonía con las problemáticas comunitarias y sociales. A través de exposiciones y una programación significativa, la Stamp Gallery ofrece oportunidades de aprendizaje experiencial fuera del salón de clases. Asimismo, funciona como un laboratorio donde artistas y curadorxs emergentes experimentan y perfeccionan sus ideas. La programación de la Stamp Gallery busca enfatizar la importancia del proceso para la práctica artística contemporánea y brindar un foro para el diálogo. ENTRADA GRATUITA y abierta al público. Horario de la Stamp Gallery: lunes a jueves: 10:00 a. m. a 8:00 p. m., viernes: 10:00 a. m. a 5:00 p. m., sábados: 11:00 a. m. a 5:00 p. m., domingos: cerrado. Más información: stamp.umd.edu/gallery.

name: Barrio 2025
description: 𝐁𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐢𝐨 is one of FCA’s most cherished traditions—a vibrant celebration of Filipino culture and community at UMD. 🇵🇭✨ More than just a festival, 𝐁𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐢𝐨 honors the creation of the 𝐅𝐢𝐥𝐢𝐩𝐢𝐧𝐨 𝐀𝐦𝐞𝐫𝐢𝐜𝐚𝐧 𝐇𝐢𝐬𝐭𝐨𝐫𝐲 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐁𝐢𝐨𝐠𝐫𝐚𝐩𝐡𝐲 𝐜𝐥𝐚𝐬𝐬 (𝐅𝐀𝐒𝐓), 𝐜𝐮𝐫𝐫𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐥𝐲 𝐚𝐥𝐬𝐨 𝐤𝐧𝐨𝐰𝐧 𝐚𝐬 𝐀𝐀𝐒𝐓𝟑𝟔𝟑, a course that ensures Filipino voices and history are represented in academic spaces. Through Barrio, we carry this milestone beyond the classroom, turning lessons into lived experiences of culture, music, and togetherness. 📚❤️This year’s theme, “𝑲𝒖𝒏𝒈 𝑺𝒂𝒂𝒏 𝑴𝒂𝒚 𝑷𝒖𝒔𝒐, 𝑴𝒂𝒚 𝑳𝒊𝒘𝒂𝒏𝒂𝒈” (𝑾𝒉𝒆𝒓𝒆 𝒕𝒉𝒆𝒓𝒆 𝒊𝒔 𝒉𝒆𝒂𝒓𝒕, 𝒕𝒉𝒆𝒓𝒆 𝒊𝒔 𝒍𝒊𝒈𝒉𝒕), draws inspiration from Philippine history, where the love, courage, and sacrifices of the people have always served as a guiding light. That light symbolizes 𝐤𝐧𝐨𝐰𝐥𝐞𝐝𝐠𝐞, 𝐭𝐫𝐮𝐭𝐡, 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐮𝐧𝐢𝐭𝐲—illuminating not just individuals but entire communities across generations. Through 𝐜𝐮𝐥𝐭𝐮𝐫𝐚𝐥 𝐩𝐞𝐫𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐦𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞𝐬, 𝐭𝐫𝐚𝐝𝐢𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐚𝐥 𝐝𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞𝐬, 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐯𝐢𝐛𝐫𝐚𝐧𝐭 𝐦𝐮𝐬𝐢𝐜, 𝐁𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐢𝐨 will shine a spotlight on our shared heritage and the community we continue to build together. 𝐁𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐢𝐨 serves as a reminder that the warmth and joy of our people radiate brightest when we gather.✨🎶🎤 Expect an evening filled with traditional and contemporary Filipino music, dance, and cultural activities—showcasing the 𝐫𝐢𝐜𝐡𝐧𝐞𝐬𝐬 of the Philippines and the spirit of home that music and community create. 🇵🇭🤩

name: Maryland Leadership Conference Spring 2022
description: Participants must register via Terplink! Find registration information at stamp.umd.edu/MLC22 The Maryland Leadership Conference is a developmental day-long experience for new and intermediate leaders. Designed to enhance your group leadership skills and provide networking opportunities with fellow leaders at UMD, this retreat will develop participants efficacy in leading others through their formal and informal leadership roles. Still wondering if MLC is right for you? Here's some more information to help you make your decision! Who should attend MLC? Student organization members and leadership position holders (or those who hope to hold a leadership position in a student org) Any current UMD student, graduate or undergraduate, interested in getting more engaged in leadership Students who want to reflect on their own leadership within a group How do I benefit from attending MLC? Create meaningful relationships and networks with driven individuals Engaging hands-on activities with real world applications Gain experience and leadership to demonstrate in professional and academic settings Logistics Here are the basics of what you need to know! Dates: April 9th Location: Adele Stamp Student Union Cost: Free* The MLC has a strict cancellation policy. Due to the nature of planning and financial resources invested, we ask that students are responsible and professional in their communication and commitment. In the event a student cannot attend, this requires the student to email a notice of their cancellation by April 4th to mlead@umd.edu. In the event a student does not cancel or attend, the student is charged a $50 cancellation fee.

name: Trash Pick Up
description: Since its inception in 1989, AWS staff and volunteers have removed tons of trash from the Anacostia River each year. Our River Terrace Trash Trap cleanups have been a huge success in helping us to make progress towards our goal for a trash free Anacostia River. This trash trap catches trash before it ends up in the River! But our staff can’t manage this trap alone. Volunteers are critical to our plan to collect trash and monitor this trash trap. This is an excellent opportunity to learn about the trash challenges of the Anacostia and what is being done to address them! Physical Requirements: The task requires squatting down for a relatively long time, and may be physically demanding. It is not suitable for young children. Registration is required. Please register at least 2 days prior to the event date you chose to volunteer. This event may be canceled suddenly due to the weather. What to Wear/Bring: Volunteers should dress appropriately for the weather on the day of the event. We recommend dressing in layers and wearing long socks and pants. Volunteers are required to wear closed-toed shoes. Volunteers should bring a reusable water bottle with them to the event. We will have water coolers where they will be able to refill their bottles. We will provide all other necessary tools and supplies. For more information before the event, contact Emily Castelli at ecastelli2@anacostiaws.org or call 301-699-6204 x103.

name: ASHRAE Seminar Series with Glenn Grant this Friday (April 14, 2017)
description: New Solid State Joining and Processing Technologies for Advanced Materials at Pacific Northwest National Laboratory Mr. Glenn Grant Chief Scientist at the Pacific Northwest National Laboratory Team Lead for Materials Processing within the Applied Materials and Performance Group Friday, April 14th | 11:00 AM DeWalt Seminar Room #2164 | Glenn L. Martin Hall #88 All students welcome | Free pizza and soda will be provided Bio: Glenn Grant is a Chief Scientist at the Pacific Northwest National Laboratory (PNNL) and Team Lead for Materials Processing within the Applied Materials and Performance Group. His research focus is on the formability, joining, and manufacturing of materials for industrial applications, and in the development of new solid state joining and processing technologies for advanced materials for future energy applications. Mr. Grant has been researching and developing Friction Stir Welding and Processing at the lab since 1997. He also leads programs in solid phase processing of new materials for high temperature and high performance applications. Mr. Grant has over 25 publications on solid state joining and processing and over 30 years’ experience in the microstructural and mechanical characterization of materials, and in the exploration of process/property relationships. Abstract: Excellent mechanical, magnetic or electric performance has been demonstrated in tests on small-scale specimens in a wide range of nanostructured materials. For many nanostructured materials the barrier to their implementation is a lack of scalable, high-volume manufacturing methods that retain the high performance microstructures. Recent research at PNNL has demonstrated a high-shear, solidstate processing method that can fabricate bulk materials from nano-powders, or solid billets of nanostructured, or non-equilibrium compositions. The process is called Shear-Assisted Extrusion. This presentation will outline the methods, equipment and performance of extrusions made by the process in several different materials: magnesium for vehicle applications, magnetic materials for electric motors and Ferritic ODS alloys for extreme environments. This presentation will also touch on the process control methodologies needed to produce a thermomechanically controlled shear-assisted extrusion.

name: Work with At-Risk Kids: Change Your life!
description: We're gearing up for the best program year yet at the St. Francis Neighborhood Center and we're looking for dedicated volunteers to help in the Power Project, our free after school youth development program that serves the at-risk children of Reservoir Hill. The program starts Monday, Oct. 6 and we're looking for both tutors and program assistants to support staff and help make sure the program is fun for our kids, safe and successful. We know you're busy, but volunteering is important to you, which is why we're flexible and want to make sure your volunteer experience is the very best it can be. If you'd like to volunteer a few hours a week or a few hours a month, we'll make sure your time here is appreciated, valued and FUN! Our youth development program focuses on arts enrichment, academic support, mentoring and tutoring. Positions involve hands-on work with youth ages 5 to 13. Orientation and training are provided. Hours: Monday through Thursday from 3 to 6 pm. Skills: Experience working with children and the ability to volunteer on a regular basis. For more information, please email volunteer@stfranciscenter.org. About Us: St. Francis Neighborhood Center's mission is committed to breaking the cycles of poverty through education, inspiring self-esteem, self-improvement, and strengthening connections. We provide free academic and arts-based learning programs to community children in addition to mentoring, tutoring and meals.

name: BOILING OF DILUTE EMULSIONS: A NEW HEAT TRANSFER STRATEGY
description: Abstract: This seminar we focus on emulsions in which the dispersed component has a lower boiling point than the carrier fluid. The unusual behavior of boiling dilute emulsions makes them potentially useful cooling of power electronics and other small scale thermal systems. An emulsion of a non-soluble dispersed phase component in water would be well-suited to this application. The emulsion retains the high specific heat and thermal conductivity of water, while boiling of the refrigerant enhances the heat transfer coefficient at temperatures below the saturation temperature of water. Recent measurements of boiling on a thin wire and flat vertical plate will be described that give a better understanding of boiling process. The range of the experiments is extended to include enhanced boiling of the continuous component, which has not previously been observed, in addition to boiling of the dispersed component. In both regimes the heat transfer coefficient is enhanced compared to that of water. Observations reveal the presence of large attached bubbles on the heated wire, the formation of which coincides with the inception of boiling in the heat transfer data. The large attached bubbles represent a new boiling mode that has not been reported in previous studies and is, under some circumstances, the dominant mode of boiling heat transfer. Recently obtained measurements for flow boiling in narrow gap channels are also presented. We find that a twenty percent enhancement of heat transfer coefficients can be obtained in certain situations. A model of boiling is developed based upon the Euler-Euler model of multiphase flows, and the general balance equations provide a rigorous and physically consistent framework. The model contains three phases that represent the continuous component, liquid droplets of the dispersed component, and bubbles that result from boiling of individual droplets. Mass, momentum, and energy transfer between the phases are modeled based upon the behavior of and interaction between individual elements of the dispersed phases. One-dimensional simulations of a single boiling droplet in superheated liquid are also performed, and the results are used to develop the closure equations of the larger model. Simulations of boiling match several trends observed in the experiments. The model thus provides a physically consistent and partially validated platform for future analytical and numerical work. Bio: Frank Kulacki received his education in mechanical engineering at the Illinois Institute of Technology and the University of Minnesota. His current research and scholarly interests include coupled heat and mass transfer in porous media, two-phase flow in micro-channels, natural convection heat transfer, heat transfer in metal foams, hybrid renewable energy systems, thermal energy storage technology, energy policy, management of technology, and the adaptation of computer-based technologies in engineering education. He has published 200 articles and 14 book chapters and has given 200 seminars and invited lectures. Eight of his 21 doctoral students now hold academic positions. He is Editor of the SpringerBriefs in Thermal Engineering and Applied Science which has 30 titles in the past two years and Editor in Chief of the forthcoming Springer Handbook of Thermal Science and Engineering. He has served as department chair at the University of Delaware and dean of engineering at Colorado State University and the University of Minnesota. He has served as Chair of the Heat Transfer Division of the American Society of Mechanical Engineers and was member of the ASME Board on Professional Development, Board on Engineering Education, and Board of the Center for Education. He chaired an ASME Task Force on Graduate Education and was a member of the ASME Vision 2030 project which addresses the body of knowledge for mechanical engineers in the 21St Century. Dr. Kulacki is a Fellow of ASME and the AAAS.

The Maryland Leadership Summit is targeted to emerging leaders who are looking for a launching point into leadership development at University of Maryland. The Maryland Leadership Summit is facilitated by a cohort of trained peer-to-peer leadership educators at the University of Maryland. The sessions are interactive and designed so that participants not only get to know one another throughout the weekend but also have a chance to practice what they are learning in the workshops.

About Us: St. Francis Neighborhood Center's mission is committed to breaking the cycles of poverty through education, inspiring self-esteem, self-improvement, and strengthening connections. About Us: St. Francis Neighborhood Center's mission is committed to breaking the cycles of poverty through education, inspiring self-esteem, self-improvement, and strengthening connections. name: Chuck Wilt/UNA Productions: Grass Is Green
description: Chuck Wilt is the Artistic Director of UNA Productions, a bi-coastal dance company working in California and NYC. An NYU Tisch School of the Arts alumnus, Chuck has been a choreographic fellow for the Alvin Ailey Dance Foundation NDCL, a Dance Initiative Artist In Residence, a recipient of the Rainin Opportunity Fund and an Artist in Residence at the 92nd St. Y, CUNY Dance Initiative, Fusion Japan and Berkeley Ballet Theatre. Wilt’s work has been described as showcasing, “...radical vulnerability [and] eloquent sincerity" with company members that, “... hold our attention with their sensitivity to each other and their meditative focus” (Dance Enthusiast, NYC). The company’s dedication to celebrating individuality and embodying human existence has led to collaborations that honor and explore sexuality and gender and juxtapose connection and isolation. During the 2020-21 season, Wilt zoomed into several dance technique classes in the School of Theatre, Dance, and Performance Studies (TDPS). He also created a new work, Mural, with TDPS students which The Clarice commissioned and premiered during the TDPS Spring Dance Concert. Please see our health & safety page for the most up to date information about attendance!

name: Xênia França
description: Brazilian singer Xênia França mixes tenderness and grit, resolve and romance in songs that sprint through samba and drift through soul, nod to electronica and nestle into balladry. Latin Grammy-nominated Xênia is personally and politically charged with songs that demand respect for her and for her time. Backed by a band as deep and dynamic as her voice, França is a live powerhouse, able to challenge and thrill in the space of a single song. Born in the coastal state of Bahia, França relocated to São Paulo to be, as she remembers, her country’s Gisele Bündchen. She discovered her leadership and voice for black roots pride as lead singer of Aláfia, a kaleidoscopic big band that channeled funk, hip-hop and traditional Brazilian sounds into vibrant anthems. Over the years, França has become a beacon of female empowerment, especially among black women. The Clarice's Visiting Artist Series is committed to providing extensive campus and community engagement opportunities that extend academic learning and cultural opportunities. As part of the 2020-21 season, França co-hosted an Arts Citizenship Talk (ACTnow) and presented an artist talk about their new work. Health + Safety There may be COVID safety policies such as mask requirements in place when you attend this event. Please see our health & safety page for the most up to date information about attendance!

name: Veterans Yoga
description: Sun Salutations (8/31) Get ready for a class to introduce health and vitality into the semester! This short class includes 20 minutes of cleansing movement fit for yogis of all shapes, sizes, and experience levels. Bonus: Do you not have time to relax and let go for even just a few minutes? Your instructor includes at least five minutes of required shavasana practice at the end of each class to give the mind a break from the rest of the world. Learn a New Pose (9/2) Today’s yoga session will include 18 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out, meaning that yogis of all experience and backgrounds will benefit! Get ready to build strength and resilience with this fun-to learn movement. Relaxation Meditation (9/7) Tuesday’s session will be focused on grounding yourself in this new semester. Just fifteen minutes of passive, yet focused yoga practice will bring you into the moment and out of the stresses of the new semester. Get a Workout in (9/9) After Tuesday’s session focused on relaxation and finding ground in the new semester, it’s time to ramp up the heat. You would never believe what just twenty minutes of poses can do to get that blood pumping and the sweat pouring! Don’t worry, though! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Open the Hips (9/14) We have been in class for a couple of weeks now and our bodies need us to keep moving to stay open and ready for all that life has to offer. Twenty three minutes of opening the hips will keep them from tightening from all the stress and constant sitting motion. Don’t forget! We also include at least five minutes of time to destress and prepare for the rest of the week. Learn a New Pose (9/16) Today’s yoga session will include 24 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out. Yogis of all experience and backgrounds will benefit from this fun practice! Get ready to build some awesome abdominal strength with this sequence. Relaxation Meditation (9/21) Today’s session will be focused on grounding yourself in this new semester. Twenty six minutes of passive, yet focused yoga practice will bring you into the moment and out of the stresses of the semester’s stressors. Getting in a Workout! (9/23) After Tuesday’s session focused on relaxation and finding ground in this awesome in-person semester, it’s time to get that body moving. Just thirty three minutes of poses will get that blood pumping and the sweat pouring! Don’t worry! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Plus, we won’t leave your muscles stiff from the hard work! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for the Booty (9/28) Looking to add cushion and tone to your derriere? Who isn’t?! Today’s session will be devoted to working to add strength to the glutes and hamstrings. Twenty minutes of work will show you some tips and tools to build your important muscle groups that keep your body healthy and moving! Learn a New Pose (9/30) Today’s yoga session will include 25 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out! Even the simplest of poses require detail-orientation! Get ready to build strength and resilience in simple poses. Relaxation Meditation (10/5) Tuesday’s session will be focused on staying sane as the semester continues to pose more difficulties. This is a time for you to take 26 minutes to treat yourself to reduce stress and a little self-care. Get a Workout In (10/7) After Tuesday’s session focused on relaxation and de-stressing, it’s time to move the mind, body, and spirit. Just 34 minutes of yoga flow will get that blood pumping! This class is still fit for all levels of experience and will provide the workout you need to stay engaged in and focused throughout the day. Just don’t forget a towel! Plus, we won’t leave your muscles stiff from the hard work! A cool-down and shavasana will transition your body into the rest of the day with ease. Yoga for Weak and Tight Shoulders (10/12) We get it. Being an athlete, veteran, human, parent, student, etc. comes with a price. Usually that price is paid in the body. Today we are going to focus on restoring weak and/or tight shoulders. Don’t shy away from class out of fear of injury! There are modifications for all flexibility levels in the shoulders. We are working to improve, not perfect! After all, we only have twenty six minutes! Learn a New Pose (10/14) Today’s yoga session will include 34 minutes of learning a pose from the inside out! Poses that seem difficult from the outside may be a bit simpler than you anticipate! We are focused on safety in strength. So first, we will build strength and confidence. Then we will build upon simple poses to create a beautiful movement to feel proud about. Relaxation Meditation (10/19) We are mid-semester. She recently appeared on the AwesomenessTV/FUSE series, WTF BARON DAVIS. Prior to that, she appeared in ABC's REVENGE and starred in the ABC Diversity Showcase. He is currently on a Talent Residency at Buzzfeed's Pero Like Channel where his videos have garnered over 30 million views on YouTube alone. He most recently guest starred on the YouTube/BF Pilot series, UNFORTUNATLY ASHLY. He can also be seen around town performing standup at places like The Comedy Store and The Ice House just to name a few. For more information, including the full All Niter schedule, please visit: https://thestamp.umd.edu/Special_Events_Programs/All_Niter
